# Pepe Unchained Developer Docs

Developer documentation for building on Pepe Unchained V2 (Arbitrum Orbit, mainnet chain ID `97741`). The published site is [docs.pepeunchained.com](https://docs.pepeunchained.com); the same pages live here as Markdown. You do not need to clone this repository to build on PEPU:

![PEPU Developer Kit: the PEPU mark, the tagline Consumer first, Google sign-in, no popups, no gas, and chips for SDK, MCP, Skills, Plugin, CLI and Templates](.gitbook/assets/hero.png)

*The PEPU developer kit: SDK, MCP, skills, plugin, CLI and templates.*

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest          # scaffold a Next.js + Privy app
npm i @pepu-chain/sdk viem          # chain definitions, contracts, ABIs, helpers
npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp              # MCP server for coding agents
```

For Claude Code, install the plugin (skills plus the MCP server):

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

## The shortest path

1. [What is Pepe Unchained V2](get-started/introduction.md): the chain in one page.
2. [The Three Pillars](get-started/pillars.md): login, sessions, sponsored gas, and how they combine.
3. [Smart Account Paths](concepts/smart-account-paths.md): which setup to start from.
4. [Quickstart](get-started/quickstart-app.md): `npx create-pepu-app@latest`, fill `.env.local`, click the Privy dashboard settings, `npm run doctor`, `npm run dev`, first sponsored transaction. With an AI agent: [Build with an AI Coding Agent](get-started/ai-assisted.md).

## The nine deliverables

The dev kit is SDK-first: every other deliverable uses the SDK instead of re-implementing it.

| # | Deliverable | What it is | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SDKs | `@pepu-chain/sdk`: chain, contracts registry, Privy, sessions, account abstraction, paymaster, combined flow, doctor | [SDK](sdk/reference.md) |
| 2 | MCP + agentic skills | `@pepu-chain/mcp` (33 tools, 6 prompts) and 12 agent skills that call the SDK and MCP | [MCP](mcp/index.md), [Skills](agent-tooling/skills.md) |
| 3 | Plugins | The `pepu-devkit` Claude Code plugin: MCP server, skills, 6 commands and a builder subagent | [Plugin](agent-tooling/plugin.md) |
| 4 | Starter templates | Six templates, from a consumer app to the full sponsored session | [Templates](templates/index.md) |
| 5 | CLI scaffolding | `create-pepu-app` scaffolds a Next.js app with a chosen template | [CLI](cli/create-pepu-app.md) |
| 6 | Developer docs | This site, one source of truth for all of the above | [Style guide](CONTRIBUTING-DOCS.md) |
| 7 | Our own bundler | The ERC-4337 bundler (Alto) for PEPU, hosted at `bundler.pepeunchained.com` | [Bundler](infra/bundler/overview.md) |
| 8 | Paymaster infrastructure | The verifying paymaster, its policy service and REST APIs, hosted at `paymaster.pepeunchained.com` | [Paymaster](infra/paymaster/overview.md) |
| 9 | Multicall3 and supporting infrastructure | Multicall3, Permit2, EntryPoints, Kernel, with every address | [Contracts](contracts/address-map.md) |

## The three pillars

1. **Google to wallet.** Sign in with Google and get an embedded wallet on PEPU.
2. **Session keys.** Approve once, then act with no wallet popup. Two modes: Privy session signers and Kernel on-chain session keys.
3. **Sponsored transactions.** The user pays no gas. Available on mainnet through the hosted bundler and paymaster.

Their combination is the headline flow: [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md). Start with [The Three Pillars](get-started/pillars.md).

## Hosted bundler and paymaster

The hosted endpoints are: bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. They are the SDK defaults; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` override them. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`). Operators who want to run their own can use the source in [`services/bundler`](../services/bundler) and [`services/paymaster`](../services/paymaster).

## Maintainer notes

This folder syncs to GitBook through bi-directional Git Sync: merging Markdown to the synced branch publishes it, and edits made in GitBook's editor are committed back here.

- **`SUMMARY.md` is load-bearing.** GitBook builds the table of contents from it, so add every new page there in the same change that adds the file.
- **`llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`** follow the llmstxt.org format and are generated by `node scripts/gen-docs.mjs` (CI runs it with `--check`). They assume each page's published URL mirrors its path here. The same script generates `reference/errors.md`, `reference/endpoints.md` and `sdk/errors.md`; do not edit those by hand. `node scripts/check-docs-parity.mjs` keeps counts, names and addresses on the pages equal to the code.
- **Voice.** Plain, sober, friction-focused. No hype words, no emoji. The test for every page: does it make it easier to build or to use?
- **Writing pages.** Read [`CONTRIBUTING-DOCS.md`](CONTRIBUTING-DOCS.md) first. No page should contain a stub marker; `check-docs-parity.mjs` fails on one.

# What is Pepe Unchained V2

Pepe Unchained V2 is an Arbitrum Orbit (Nitro) chain, operated by Conduit, settling to Ethereum L1. It is a standard EVM chain — if you already know how to deploy and verify a Solidity contract on any Arbitrum Orbit chain, you already know how to do it here. Nothing about the execution environment is bespoke.

![The live sponsored-session demo sign-in screen on desktop and mobile: Grant once, then act, with no popups and no gas](../.gitbook/assets/demo.png)

*Built with the dev kit: the live sponsored-session demo. [Try the live demo](https://roadmap-demo.pepeunchained.com).*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Mainnet chain ID** | `97741` |
| **Testnet chain ID** | `97740` (out of scope for development: no faucet, no indexed explorer, no deployed infrastructure) |
| **Stack** | Arbitrum Orbit / Nitro, ArbOS 51 |
| **Settles to** | Ethereum L1 (AnyTrust/Optimium DA — see [Network Properties](network-properties.md)) |
| **Native gas token** | PEPU, 18 decimals |
| **Operator** | Conduit |

Full copy-pasteable RPC URLs, explorers, and currency details are on the [Network Reference](network-reference.md) page. The deeper architectural picture — DA mode, precompiles, and an honest read of the chain's current L2BEAT rating — is on [Network Properties](network-properties.md).

Terms used on this page: [EntryPoint](../reference/glossary.md), [bundler](../reference/glossary.md), [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md), [Kernel](../reference/glossary.md), [session key](../reference/glossary.md), [project](../reference/glossary.md), [free tier](../reference/glossary.md). All are defined in the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md).

## There is an old chain. This is not it.

If you've found a chain ID `3409`, an OP Stack reference, or a Celestia data-availability mention anywhere claiming to be "Pepe Unchained," that's the legacy V1 chain. It is dead. See [V1 vs V2](v1-vs-v2.md) before you configure anything.

## What you can build on today

The goal is a consumer app deployed quickly, without a founder spending weeks learning the chain. The dev kit covers three pillars; see [The Three Pillars](pillars.md).

| Pillar | What a builder can use today |
|---|---|
| Google login to an embedded wallet | Yes. [Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md), [Privy Setup](../onboarding/privy-setup.md). |
| Session keys, no popup per action | Privy mode: yes, the user pays gas. Kernel on-chain mode: yes, uses the hosted bundler and a funded project. [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md). |
| Sponsored transactions | Yes, through the **hosted** bundler and paymaster; you bring a funded project. [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md). |
| All three combined | Yes. [End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md). |

A tiered sponsorship model (a daily free allowance for PEPU's own apps plus project deposits) is live on mainnet; see [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md).

## Endpoints at a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| RPC | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Explorer | `https://pepuscan.com` |
| Bundler | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` overrides; local `http://localhost:4337`) |
| Paymaster | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; ERC-7677 URL `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` overrides; local `http://localhost:8788`) |

Full list: [Network Reference](network-reference.md) and [Endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md).

## What this section covers

This is the developer-facing documentation for building on Pepe Unchained V2: network parameters, contract deployment, verification, wallet and account onboarding (Privy setup, session signers, sponsored transactions, smart accounts), an SDK reference, copy-pasteable recipes, and agent tooling (an MCP server and coding-agent skills). It assumes you already know Solidity and standard EVM tooling (Hardhat, Foundry) — it does not re-teach those tools, only how they apply here.

If you want a running app (and, with a funded project, a sponsored transaction) in about ten minutes, go to [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](quickstart-app.md). If you specifically want to deploy a Solidity contract, go to [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md).

## Scope decisions

Two things are deliberately not part of the dev kit today:

- **No Telegram Mini App template.** Telegram restricts Mini Apps to the TON blockchain, so a PEPU Mini App template would not be accepted there. It is excluded, not postponed.
- **Global Wallet (a cross-app wallet) is deferred.** Each app provisions its own Privy embedded wallet. A shared wallet that follows a user between apps is not built.

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/get-started/v1-vs-v2

# V1 vs V2: Which Chain Are You On

**Short answer: if you are building today, you are building on V2 — chain ID `97741` (mainnet) / `97740` (testnet), Arbitrum Orbit. There is an older chain, V1 — chain ID `3409`, OP Stack — and it is dead. Do not configure your tools against chain ID `3409`.**

This page exists because search results, older third-party chain listings, and cached AI answers still surface V1 details under the name "Pepe Unchained." Getting this wrong costs real time: a wrong chain ID means your wallet, RPC, and deploy scripts silently point at a chain that no longer accepts new activity.

## The two chains

| | V1 (legacy, dead) | V2 (current) |
|---|---|---|
| Chain ID | `3409` | `97741` (mainnet), `97740` (testnet) |
| Stack | OP Stack / Optimium | Arbitrum Orbit / Nitro |
| Data availability | Custom Gas Token setup via Celestia-adjacent configuration | AnyTrust/Optimium, 1-of-1 committee — see [Network Properties](network-properties.md) |
| Status | **Dead.** Legacy migration/claims portal closed **2026-01-31, 23:59 UTC**. No new deployments, no supported RPC. | **Live.** This is the chain the rest of these docs cover. |
| RPC | Not documented here — do not use | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` (mainnet), `https://rpc-pepu-v2-testnet-vn4qxxp9og.t.conduit.xyz` (testnet) |

The migration from V1 to V2 happened because Conduit deprecated the Custom Gas Token feature V1 depended on. V2 is a separate chain, not an upgrade in place — different chain ID, different stack, different RPC, no shared state.

## Where the confusion comes from

- **Third-party chain-list and SDK pages have been observed showing incorrect V2 testnet data** — including a wrong chain ID and a wrong gas-token currency for testnet `97740`. Always verify against this page or a direct `eth_chainId` call against the RPC URLs above rather than trusting a third-party listing.
- Generic "Pepe Unchained" search results and some cached AI answers may still describe the V1 chain's architecture (OP Stack, Celestia-style DA) as if it were current. If you see chain ID `3409` mentioned anywhere in the same breath as architectural claims about Pepe Unchained, that content is describing the dead chain.
- A separate, unrelated chain called "Pepe Chain Mainnet" also exists on some chain-list sites under a different chain ID. It is not related to Pepe Unchained at all — don't confuse the two by name alone.

## What to do

- Configure your wallet, Hardhat/Foundry, and any chain-definition objects against chain ID `97741` (mainnet) or `97740` (testnet) only. See [Network Reference](network-reference.md) for the full, copy-pasteable parameters.
- If you're citing an architectural fact about "Pepe Unchained" from a source you didn't get from this docs set, check whether it's talking about chain `3409` before you rely on it.

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/get-started/pillars

# The Three Pillars and How They Combine

The PEPU dev kit is built around three capabilities that make an app feel like a normal consumer app: Google login to a wallet, session keys, and sponsored transactions. This page defines each pillar, describes what it needs, and gives the decision table for choosing a combination. Read it first; every other page in Onboarding, Privy and the SDK section hangs off it.

![The three pillars (Google to wallet, session keys, sponsored transactions) and the combination: Google login, one signature, no popups, no user gas](../.gitbook/assets/pillars.png)

*The three pillars, and what you get when you combine them.*

Pillars 1 and 2 use Privy mode. Pillar 3 and the combination use the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`), which you use with a funded project.

Terms used on this page: [UserOperation](../reference/glossary.md), [bundler](../reference/glossary.md), [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md), [EntryPoint](../reference/glossary.md), [Kernel](../reference/glossary.md), [session key](../reference/glossary.md), [project](../reference/glossary.md), [free tier](../reference/glossary.md). All are defined in the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md).

## Prerequisites

- Mainnet only: chain ID `97741`. Testnet `97740` is out of scope.
- A Privy app (App ID and App Secret). See [Privy Configuration Overview](../privy/index.md).
- For pillar 3 and the combination: a bundler and a paymaster. Write them as `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`. Local development defaults are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`. See [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## The pillars

### Pillar 1: Google login to an embedded wallet

| | |
|---|---|
| What it gives | A user clicks "Sign in with Google" and gets a self-custodial Privy embedded wallet on chain 97741. No seed phrase, no extension. |
| What it needs | A Privy app with Google enabled, the exact origin (with port) in Allowed origins, embedded wallets on for Ethereum, and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` on the server for the ensure-wallet route. No bundler, no paymaster. |
| SDK | `/privy` (config, requirements), `/privy/react` (`PepuPrivyProvider`, `WalletGate`, `useEmbeddedWallet`), `/privy/wagmi` (`PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`), `/privy/server` (`createEnsureWalletRoute`, `requireUser`) |
| Template | `consumer-app` |
| Page | [Social Login and Embedded Wallets (Privy)](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) |

### Pillar 2: Session keys, with no popup per transaction

There are two modes. They differ in who enforces the limits and in who pays gas.

| | Privy session signers | Kernel on-chain session keys |
|---|---|---|
| Account | The plain embedded EOA | A ZeroDev Kernel v3.1 smart account owned by the embedded wallet |
| Who signs actions | Privy, on your server's request (`eth_signTransaction`), then your server broadcasts | A session key your server holds, signing UserOperations |
| Where the scope is enforced | Privy's backend policy engine (off-chain) | Call policy and timestamp policy contracts, during UserOperation validation (on-chain) |
| What you trust | Privy's policy engine and your policy configuration | The chain. A compromised server can only do what the permission allows until it expires |
| Who pays gas | The user, from the embedded wallet | Whoever sponsors it: pair it with a paymaster (the combination) |
| Needs | An authorization key and a key quorum in the Privy dashboard | A bundler, a paymaster and a session store. No authorization key |
| SDK | `/session` (policy), `/session/server` (routes), `/session/react` (hooks) | `/session/kernel` (policies, approve, load), plus `/combo` for the routes |
| Template | `game-app` | `sponsored-session-app` |
| Page | [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md) | [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md), [Sponsored Session](../onboarding/sponsored-session.md) |

### Pillar 3: Sponsored transactions

| | |
|---|---|
| What it gives | The user pays no gas. A Kernel smart account holding 0 PEPU sends a transaction and a paymaster pays. |
| Who pays | The paymaster contract, from its own EntryPoint deposit, after an off-chain policy service approves the UserOperation. Today that is the v2 paymaster `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` paid from your project's deposit or, for PEPU's own apps, the free tier. The v1 paymaster is retired. |
| What it needs | A bundler (ERC-4337, EntryPoint v0.7), a paymaster (ERC-7677), and your contract on the paymaster's allowlist. |
| SDK | `/aa` (probes, errors), `/aa/kernel` (`toPepuKernelAccount`, `createPepuSponsoredClient`, `sendSponsored`), `/aa/react` (`useSponsoredSend`, `usePepuSmartAccount`, `usePepuSponsorship`), `/aa/react-direct` (`useDirectSponsoredSend`, `useDirectSmartAccount`), `/paymaster` (v2 project helpers) |
| Template | `sponsored-demo` |
| Page | [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md) |

### The combination: Google login, one signature, no popups, no user gas

Sign in with Google (pillar 1), approve one scoped session with one owner signature (the Kernel mode of pillar 2), and every later action is a sponsored UserOperation (pillar 3). The limits live on-chain in the user's smart account.

| | |
|---|---|
| SDK | `/combo` (`createSponsoredSessionRoutes`), `/combo/react` (`useSponsoredSession`), on top of `/session/kernel`, `/aa/kernel`, `/privy/*` |
| Template | `sponsored-session-app` |
| Page | [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md) |

## Decision table

| I want | Choose | Dashboard needs | Template |
|---|---|---|---|
| Login and a wallet, user pays gas, user approves each send | Pillar 1 only | Allowed origins, login methods, embedded wallets | `consumer-app` |
| Popup-free actions, user pays gas, simplest setup, no bundler | Privy session signers | Pillar 1 plus an authorization key and key quorum | `game-app` |
| Gasless sends, user still signs each one | Sponsored transactions, `privy-smart-wallets` transport | Pillar 1 plus Smart Wallets: Kernel, chain 97741, bundler URL, paymaster URL | `sponsored-demo` |
| Gasless sends, URLs kept in your env, no Privy Smart Wallets | Sponsored transactions, `direct` transport | Pillar 1 only | none (use `useDirectSponsoredSend` from `/aa/react-direct`) |
| No popup and no gas, limits enforced on-chain | The combination | Pillar 1 only. Smart Wallets and authorization keys are not needed | `sponsored-session-app` |

Not sure which smart-account setup you need? [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md) compares the plain wallet, the ZeroDev-native path (the SDK builds the Kernel account) and Privy Smart Wallets (Privy builds it) side by side, with a "pick this if" list.

Two choices inside the sponsorship rows:

- **`privy-smart-wallets` versus `direct`.** With `privy-smart-wallets`, Privy's smart-wallet client calls the bundler and paymaster URLs you entered in the dashboard (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project token>`). A paymaster URL embeds a token, so entering it in the dashboard stores a credential there, and the free tier is not reachable from it. With `direct`, the SDK builds the Kernel account itself and your env supplies the URLs. `direct` is what the combination uses. See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md).
- **Privy session versus Kernel session.** Choose Privy mode when users pay their own gas and you accept that Privy's policy engine enforces the scope. Choose Kernel mode when you want the chain to enforce it, which in practice means you also sponsor gas. A Kernel session does not use Privy session signers, so no authorization key is involved.

## What to expect

- Pillar 1 needs nothing but a Privy app.
- Pillar 2 in Privy mode needs no bundler or paymaster. The user pays gas, a fraction of a cent.
- Gas sponsorship needs a claimed and funded project (the free tier is only for PEPU's own Privy app). Only describe a transaction as "gasless" once sponsorship is configured and tested for your project. Use `usePepuSponsorship` or the `pepu_sponsorship_status` MCP tool to check live.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login fails or the iframe is blocked | The origin, including the port, is not in Allowed origins | [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md) |
| "Creating your wallet..." never ends | Privy's client-side creation hangs when the dashboard setting is off | Use `WalletGate` and `createEnsureWalletRoute`; see Pillar 1 page |
| Session grant returns 401 "No valid authorization keys" | Key quorum mismatch (Privy mode) | [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md) |
| Sponsored send denied | Destination not allowlisted, cap hit, or no deposit | [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md) |
| A page spins on "Setting up your smart wallet..." | Smart Wallets not configured for chain 97741 (Privy transport only) | [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md) |

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: which one to use](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Architecture: Who Calls What](../concepts/architecture.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md)

# Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes

Copy-paste path from nothing to a running Next.js app on Pepe Unchained V2 that sends a real transaction whose gas someone else pays. You choose a template, scaffold it, fill two Privy values, click through the Privy dashboard once, get a paymaster project (for the sponsored templates), run `npm run doctor`, run the app and send. If you only want login and a wallet, the first six steps are the whole job and take about five minutes. To let an AI agent do it, see [Build with an AI Coding Agent](ai-assisted.md). To deploy only a Solidity contract, see [Deploy and Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md).

![Quickstart steps: npx create-pepu-app, fill .env.local, Privy dashboard, npm run doctor, npm run dev, first sponsored transaction](../.gitbook/assets/quickstart-steps.png)

*Six steps to your first sponsored transaction.*

The two sponsored templates use the hosted [bundler](../reference/glossary.md) (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md) (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`). They need a [project](../reference/glossary.md) of yours (claim, deposit, token), because the [free tier](../reference/glossary.md) is only for PEPU's own Privy app. Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18.17 or newer and npm. You do not clone this repository.
- A Privy account (free): [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io).
- For a sponsored template only: a wallet holding a little PEPU (for the one-time project setup and the deposit). Buy PEPU on an exchange or bridge via [pepubridge.com](https://pepubridge.com). A transaction costs a fraction of a cent.

## 1. Pick a template

Answer one question: **who pays gas, and does the user approve each action?**

| You want | Template | Smart account path | Extra setup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Login, a wallet, a real PEPU send. Users pay gas | `consumer-app` (default) | none (plain wallet) | none |
| Unlock content by holding a token or NFT | `token-gated-app` | none | a gate token address |
| An NFT mint page | `nft-mint` | none | deploy the contract |
| Popup-free play, user pays gas, limits enforced by Privy | `game-app` | none (Privy session signers) | authorization key, key quorum, a deployed contract |
| One gasless button, client only | `sponsored-demo` | Privy Smart Wallets | Smart Wallets in the dashboard, a project **client** token |
| One signature, then no popups and no user gas, limits enforced on-chain | `sponsored-session-app` | ZeroDev-native | a project **server** key |

Not sure? Take `consumer-app` to see login work, or `sponsored-session-app` for the full experience. The difference between the two smart-account paths is explained in [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md); the template list with more detail is the [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md).

## 2. Scaffold

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template sponsored-session-app
cd my-app
```

Swap the template name for the one you picked. With no `--template` it asks. The CLI copies the template, creates `.env.local` from `.env.example`, adds `.mcp.json` and agent files, installs dependencies and prints the next steps. If it did not install, run `npm install`. Flags (`--yes`, `--pm`, `--no-install`, `--json`) are in [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md).

## 3. Get your Privy values

1. Open [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io), create an app, and open Settings, Basics.
2. Copy the **App ID** and create an **App Secret**.
3. Put them in `.env.local`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID=<your App ID>
PRIVY_APP_SECRET=<your App Secret>
```

The App ID is public. The secret is server only: never prefix it `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, never commit it.

## 4. Click through the Privy dashboard

Four settings decide whether login works. Do them now; the exact menu paths and failure symptoms are in [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

| # | Setting | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Allowed origins (Configuration, App settings) | `http://localhost:3000`, with the port. Add your production origin later |
| 2 | Login methods (User management, Authentication) | Enable Google and email |
| 3 | Embedded wallets (Wallets) | On for Ethereum, create wallets on login |
| 4 | Smart Wallets (Wallets, Smart wallets) | **Only for `sponsored-demo`**: provider Kernel v3.1, chain 97741, bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, paymaster URL from step 5. Every other template: leave it alone |

Port 3000 must be free. If it is taken, Next.js silently starts on 3001 and login fails with errors that never mention the port. Free 3000 rather than working around it.

## 5. Get a paymaster project (sponsored templates only)

Skip this step for `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint` and `game-app`.

A sponsored transaction is paid from a project budget that you own. Getting one is claim, configure, deposit, register; it takes a script about two minutes. Follow [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md): it has the SDK code, the runnable recipe ([Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](../recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md)), and an MCP and agent route for the parts a tool can encode. At the end you hold two credentials, shown once:

| Credential | Looks like | Use it in |
|---|---|---|
| Server key | `ppk_...` (secret) | `sponsored-session-app`: `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>` in `.env.local` |
| Client token | `ppt_...` (publishable, works only from your allowed origins) | `sponsored-demo`: the paymaster URL in the Privy dashboard (step 4, row 4) |

Make sure your project's targets include the contract the template calls: both sponsored templates call `TapScore` (`0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`), and the per-wallet daily limit must be above about 21 PEPU, with a project balance of at least about 25 PEPU, or a new user's first action (which deploys their account) is denied.

For `sponsored-session-app` your `.env.local` now also has:

```
PEPU_BUNDLER_URL=https://bundler.pepeunchained.com
PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>
```

Never commit it. Template-specific variables are in [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md).

## 6. Run the doctor

```bash
npm run doctor
```

It checks `.env.local` against your template, the chain RPC, the bundler and paymaster, and your Privy dashboard settings (including that `http://localhost:3000` is an allowed origin). It never prints values. **Success looks like** lines starting `ok` and a final `ok   no failing checks`:

```text
ok   privy.app-id: Privy app id format looks right.
ok   chain.rpc: RPC reachable, chainId 97741.
ok   sponsorship.bundler: Bundler reachable and reports supported entry points.
ok   sponsorship.paymaster: Paymaster endpoint reachable.
ok   privy.allowed-origins: The page origin (including the port) is in Allowed origins: http://localhost:3000 is allowed.
ok   privy.embedded-wallets: Embedded wallets are enabled for Ethereum ...
ok   no failing checks
```

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `FAIL` | Fix it before you run the app; the message names the variable or setting |
| `WARN ... could not be verified` | Privy's public config did not report that setting. Not a failure: check the dashboard row by hand |
| `skip` | The check does not apply to this template, or you passed `--offline` |

Running on another port: `PEPU_APP_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3001 npm run doctor`, after adding that origin in the dashboard.

## 7. Run the app and send your first sponsored transaction

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000` and check the terminal says port 3000. Then:

| Template | Click | You should see |
|---|---|---|
| `consumer-app` | Sign in, send a small PEPU amount (the wallet needs PEPU) | Your address and balance, then a transaction link. Gas is not sponsored; a permanent notice says so |
| `sponsored-session-app` | Sign in with Google, **Start session**, **Approve**, sign once in Privy, then **Tap** | No popup on Tap. After a few seconds an evidence panel shows a pepuscan link, the sender (your smart account, not your wallet), "Gas paid by paymaster" and a cost. The smart account holds 0 PEPU |
| `sponsored-demo` | Sign in, **Sponsor a tap** | The Kernel smart account (0 PEPU), a transaction link, and the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit dropping. Confirm sponsorship by that drop, not the hash |

Wallet creation shows "Setting up your wallet..." for a moment on first login. A brand-new account's first sponsored operation also deploys the account, so it takes longer and costs more than the next one.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login fails, iframe blocked, OAuth 403 | Origin or port missing from Allowed origins | Step 4, row 1 |
| Setup screen on load | A required env key is missing | Run `npm run doctor`, set the key, restart `npm run dev` |
| `/api/wallet/ensure` returns 500 | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` unset, or the dev server was not restarted | Set it and restart |
| No "Continue with Google" button | Google is off in the dashboard | Step 4, row 2 |
| Page spins on "Setting up your smart wallet..." | `sponsored-demo` without Smart Wallets for chain 97741 | Step 4, row 4 |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | A client token with no allowed origins, or a client token used from a server | Set allowed origins on the project, or use the server key from the server |
| `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | The project's targets do not include `TapScore` | Run the `configure` step again with the contract |
| `trailing-hour spend ... would exceed cap` after the first tap | The per-wallet limit is below the first-operation reservation | Raise the per-wallet limit above about 21 PEPU |
| Privy refuses a send you can afford | Its conservative gas estimate at PEPU's roughly 12,500 gwei base fee | See [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) |

## Next steps

- [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md): why the two sponsored templates differ and which to ship
- [The Three Pillars](pillars.md)
- [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md) and [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)
- [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md)
- [Recipes](../recipes/read-a-contract.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)
- [Build with an AI Coding Agent](ai-assisted.md)

# Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes

The fastest path for agent users: install the MCP server, the plugin and the skills, then scaffold and verify an app without leaving the agent. The agent does the code and config; you provide the Privy credentials. This page is the short path; detail is in the agent-tooling and MCP sections.

![Dev kit map: the SDK at the base; the MCP server with 33 tools, 12 skills, the Claude Code plugin, the create-pepu-app CLI and 6 templates all build on it](../.gitbook/assets/devkit-map.png)

*Everything builds on the SDK.*

The MCP server (`@pepu-chain/mcp`: 33 tools, 6 prompts), 12 skills, 6 commands and the builder subagent (plugin 0.4.4) cover the whole dev kit. Gas sponsorship uses PEPU's hosted bundler and paymaster and needs a funded project of yours.

## Use it with an AI agent: the fast path (Claude Code)

Three steps, about three minutes of your time.

1. Install the plugin (once):

   ```text
   /plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
   /plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
   ```

2. In an empty folder, run the command with your idea:

   ```text
   /pepu-new-app a tap game where players pay no gas and approve once
   ```

3. Answer the agent when it asks for the few things only you have (below), then run what it tells you: `npm run dev`.

What `/pepu-new-app` does, in order:

| Step | What the agent does | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lists the templates and picks one by what you described, saying why in one line. For the idea above: `sponsored-session-app` | `pepu_list_templates` |
| 2 | Scaffolds the app into a new folder (the same as `npx create-pepu-app`), then installs dependencies | `pepu_scaffold_app` |
| 3 | Reads `.env.local`, fills what it can, and asks you for the rest by name without echoing secrets | `pepu_check_env` |
| 4 | Checks your Privy dashboard for the dev origin and tells you which rows to change | `pepu_check_privy_config` |
| 5 | For a sponsored template, checks the hosted bundler and paymaster live and says what is missing (your project's key) | `pepu_sponsorship_status` |
| 6 | Runs typecheck and build and ends with the three commands to run | |

What only you do:

1. Create the Privy app at [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io) and give the agent the App ID and App Secret (or paste them into `.env.local` yourself).
2. Click the dashboard settings the agent lists: Allowed origins `http://localhost:3000`, Google on, embedded wallets on, and Smart Wallets only if it picked `sponsored-demo`. The exact clicks are in [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).
3. For a sponsored template, get a paymaster project with its key. Ask: "Walk me through claiming and funding a paymaster project for my Privy app." The agent encodes the transactions with `pepu_prepare_project_tx`; you sign them with the owner wallet and run the SIWE and attestation script, which needs your wallet and your Privy secret. See [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md).
4. Run `npm run doctor`, then `npm run dev`, and click through the flow. When it looks right, the agent can re-run `/pepu-doctor` for a readiness report.

Other clients (Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Cline) get the MCP server only, no slash commands: use the first prompt below. The rest of this page is the manual route.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18.17 or newer and an MCP-capable agent client.
- A Privy account (you create the app and copy two values).

## 1. Install the MCP server

Every client takes the same stdio server:

```bash
npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp
```

Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Claude Desktop and Cline each have their own config file shape. The shared entry is:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "pepu": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"] } } }
```

Exact per-client steps: [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md). Scaffolded templates already ship a `.mcp.json`. No API key is needed. Optional env: `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, `PEPU_RPC_URL`.

## 2. Claude Code plugin

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

It adds the MCP server, 12 skills, a builder subagent and six commands:

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `/pepu-new-app` | Scaffolds an app, choosing the template by pillar |
| `/pepu-add-login` | Google login and an embedded wallet |
| `/pepu-add-session` | Privy session keys |
| `/pepu-add-sponsorship` | Sponsored transactions, after a live availability check |
| `/pepu-add-sponsored-session` | The full combination |
| `/pepu-doctor` | Env, Privy dashboard and sponsorship readiness |

See [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md) and [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md).

## What the agent does unattended, and what needs you

| Agent can | Needs a human |
|---|---|
| Scaffold the app (`pepu_scaffold_app`) | Create the Privy app at dashboard.privy.io |
| Write SDK code, routes and hooks | Copy the App ID and App Secret into `.env.local` (or paste them to the agent; the tools never echo secrets) |
| Generate the authorization key into `.env.local` without printing it | Register the public key and create the key quorum in the Privy dashboard |
| Check env keys, Privy config, sponsorship status | Set Allowed origins, enable Google, enable embedded wallets |
| Run `npm run doctor`, typecheck, build | Provide the paymaster project key for sponsored templates (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; the bundler defaults to the hosted one) |
| Explain a failed transaction or error | Click through the browser flow and approve Privy prompts |

## A first prompt

```text
Create a PEPU app that has Google login and a wallet. Use the pepu MCP tools and the
pepu-build-dapp skill. Scaffold it in ./my-app with the consumer-app template, tell me
exactly which Privy dashboard settings I must change, then run npm run doctor and
pepu_check_privy_config with origin http://localhost:3000 and report what is left.
```

For no-popup, no-gas, ask for the `sponsored-session-app` template and say you will supply a paymaster project token (the bundler URL defaults to the hosted one).

## What to expect

The agent lists the template choice with one line of reasoning, scaffolds, reports missing env keys by name, and finishes with a doctor report. Fields Privy does not expose come back `unknown`, not failed.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Tools not listed | MCP not registered or the client not restarted | [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md) |
| Doctor: `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` missing | You have not provided it | Add it to `.env.local`, restart dev |
| Agent claims sponsorship is live | Skipped the live check | Run `pepu_sponsorship_status` |

## Related

- [MCP Server Overview](../mcp/index.md)
- [MCP and Skills overview](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md)
- [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](quickstart-app.md)
- [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md)

# Network Reference

Copy-pasteable network parameters for Pepe Unchained V2. If you landed here from a search engine or an AI assistant and haven't confirmed you're looking at V2 (not the dead V1 chain, ID `3409`), read [V1 vs V2](v1-vs-v2.md) first.

## Mainnet

Build here. Every guide in this docs set targets mainnet by default — see "Testnet: out of scope today" below for why.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Chain ID | `97741` (`0x17dcd`) |
| Network name | Pepe Unchained V2 |
| RPC URL | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Currency symbol | PEPU (18 decimals) |
| Block explorer | `https://pepuscan.com` (Blockscout, fully indexed) |
| Contract verification | `https://pepuscan.com/api` (Blockscout verifier — see [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md)) |

### Authenticated RPC

The RPC URL above is public and rate-limited, and gates `debug_*`/`trace_*` methods (`-32401`). Conduit also issues an **authenticated RPC URL** in the form `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz/<API_KEY>` for anyone with a Conduit API key. The authenticated endpoint exposes `debug_traceCall` and `eth_simulateV1` in addition to standard JSON-RPC — useful for local simulation, safer contract-verification tooling, and anything that needs to trace a call before submitting it. There is no public self-serve signup for a key documented here; if you need one, ask whoever operates your Conduit relationship.

## Testnet: out of scope today

Testnet (chain `97740`) is a real, live chain, but there is nothing to build against on it today:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Chain ID | `97740` (`0x17dcc`) |
| Network name | Pepe Unchained V2 Testnet |
| RPC URL | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-testnet-vn4qxxp9og.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Currency symbol | PEPU (18 decimals) |
| Block explorer | **None indexed.** `explorer-pepu-v2-testnet-vn4qxxp9og.t.conduit.xyz` is Conduit's default, non-Blockscout UI, which self-reports no indexer — it can show a single block or transaction by hash and nothing else. No `pepuscan.com`-equivalent Blockscout instance is registered for chain `97740` (confirmed against Blockscout's own public chain registry). |
| Faucet | **None exists.** There is no documented, self-serve way to obtain testnet PEPU. |
| Contracts | **None of the infrastructure on this page is deployed on testnet** — no Multicall3, no Permit2, no ERC-4337 EntryPoint, no Kernel smart-account factory. Everything below this section is mainnet-only unless stated otherwise. |

**Route everyone to mainnet.** With no faucet, no indexed explorer, and no deployed infrastructure, testnet cannot support a real development workflow today — and it doesn't need to: a transaction on PEPU mainnet costs a fraction of a cent. Every quickstart, recipe, and template in this docs set defaults to mainnet for exactly this reason. If testnet gains a faucet and an indexed explorer later, this page will say so plainly — until then, don't spend time trying to make testnet work.

## Sponsorship endpoints

Gas sponsorship needs a bundler and a paymaster. PEPU hosts both, and the SDK uses them by default.

| Service | Variable (override) | Local development default | Hosted (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bundler (ERC-4337, EntryPoint v0.7) | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `http://localhost:4337` | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` |
| Paymaster (ERC-7677) | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `http://localhost:8788/paymaster/<your-app-key>` | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; ERC-7677 URL `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` (always embeds a token) |

See [Endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md) and [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## Add to your wallet

Paste this into a `wallet_addEthereumChain` call, or enter the fields manually under your wallet's "Add Network" screen.

```json
{
  "chainId": "0x17dcd",
  "chainName": "Pepe Unchained V2",
  "nativeCurrency": { "name": "Pepe Unchained", "symbol": "PEPU", "decimals": 18 },
  "rpcUrls": ["https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz"],
  "blockExplorerUrls": ["https://pepuscan.com"]
}
```

There is no reason to add testnet to a wallet today — see "Testnet: out of scope today" above.

## Which standard contracts are deployed

**Multicall3 and the ERC-4337/smart-account stack are live on mainnet**, but at addresses and with caveats that still trip up tooling built for a "default" EVM chain. Read this table before you hardcode anything.

The full table, with deployment notes, verification links, and the reasoning behind each gap, lives on [Deployed Contracts Reference](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md). Summary:

| Contract | Canonical address (other chains) | On Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet |
|---|---|---|
| CREATE2 deterministic deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | **Deployed**, at the canonical address. This is what makes everything else on this table possible. |
| Multicall3 | `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` | **Deployed — but NOT at the canonical address.** See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md) before you wire this up; the canonical address is permanently unreachable on this chain and PEPU's deployment lives somewhere else. |
| Permit2 | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` | **Deployed**, at the canonical address. |
| ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | **Deployed**, at the canonical address. |
| ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | **Deployed**, at the canonical address. |
| Kernel v3 account factory + MetaFactory + ECDSA validator | (ZeroDev, versioned) | **Deployed.** See [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md) and the full reference table for addresses. |
| Sponsored paymaster v2 | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (project-specific, not canonical) | **Deployed.** Sponsorship is available through the hosted endpoints. The v1 paymaster `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` is retired and cannot sponsor. |

**A deployed EntryPoint is not gas sponsorship, and gas sponsorship needs a bundler and a paymaster service on top.** A zero-balance smart account can transact with the paymaster above paying, through PEPU's hosted bundler and ERC-7677 policy service. An app uses those by default and overrides them with `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; see [Endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md). See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md), [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md) and [Social Login & Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) for what that does and doesn't unlock today.

A practical consequence of the gaps that remain: some ecosystem dApps on Pepe Unchained (for example, the native DEX) use their **own non-canonical** Multicall/Permit2 addresses, sized for their own needs — these are not general-purpose substitutes. Don't assume any Multicall or Permit2 address you find referenced by an app on this chain is the canonical one, or compatible with the standard ABI; check it against the [Deployed Contracts Reference](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md), or read it directly from that app's own deployment config.

## A note on gas

The native gas token is PEPU, priced far below ETH, so gwei-denominated gas prices here are not comparable to Ethereum mainnet or most L2s. Expect a base fee around **12,500 gwei-equivalent** — this is a low-value-token artifact, not a sign the chain is expensive or congested, and not a misconfigured RPC. A simple transfer still costs a fraction of a cent in practice. Don't set gas price limits in your tooling based on habits formed on ETH-denominated chains, and don't "fix" the number by hardcoding a lower gas price — your transactions will just get stuck. See [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) if this is the reason you landed here.

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/get-started/network-properties

# Network Properties

This page states plainly what kind of chain Pepe Unchained V2 is, including the parts that are trade-offs rather than selling points. Serious builders check third-party risk assessments before shipping to a chain regardless of what any docs page says — better they read it here first than find it independently and wonder why it wasn't mentioned.

## Stack

Pepe Unchained V2 runs on **Arbitrum Orbit**, using the **Nitro** execution stack, on **ArbOS 51**, operated by Conduit. It settles to Ethereum L1. This is a standard, largely unmodified Orbit deployment — see [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md) for confirmation that ordinary Hardhat/Foundry tooling works against it without special handling.

## Data availability: AnyTrust, 1-of-1 committee

The chain runs in **AnyTrust** mode (sometimes referred to as Optimium), not full Rollup mode. The distinction matters:

- A full Rollup posts all transaction data to Ethereum L1, so anyone can reconstruct chain state from L1 data alone.
- An AnyTrust chain instead relies on a **Data Availability Committee (DAC)**: a set of parties who attest that they're holding the data off-chain. As long as enough committee members are honest and available, the data stays retrievable; if they aren't, data availability isn't guaranteed by L1 alone.

Pepe Unchained's DAC currently has **one member (1-of-1)**. There is no redundancy: data availability depends on that single party. This is a meaningfully weaker trust assumption than either a full Rollup or an AnyTrust chain with a larger, more distributed committee.

## Newer EVM features live on this chain

- **EIP-7702 is live.** EOAs can delegate execution to contract code without a full smart-account migration.
- **The P256 precompile is live at `0x100`.** This makes secp256r1 signature verification (as used by passkeys) cheap to do on-chain — a building block for passkey-based authentication, though it is only one piece of that puzzle. See [Social Login & Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) for how login and wallets are wired up.
- **An ERC-4337 EntryPoint (v0.6 and v0.7), a ZeroDev Kernel v3 smart-account factory, and a funded, staked paymaster are deployed on mainnet.** Smart accounts and gas sponsorship are available through PEPU's hosted bundler and paymaster; an app needs a funded project. See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md) and [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md).

## L2BEAT assessment

[L2BEAT's "Pepe Unchained" page](https://l2beat.com/scaling/projects/pepeunchained) exists, but it is not an assessment of this chain. It covers the **archived V1 chain — chain ID `3409`, an Optimium on the OP Stack** — and carries L2BEAT's own banner stating the project is archived and no longer maintained, having migrated from OP Stack to Orbit. Its stage rating and critical-severity findings (including things like an unenforced upgrade delay and non-permissionless fraud proofs) describe that dead chain, not V2. If you land on that page while researching Pepe Unchained, read it as V1 history — see [V1 vs V2](v1-vs-v2.md) — not as current risk information.

**V2 (chain ID `97741`) has no independent L2BEAT assessment or equivalent third-party risk rating at this time.** No separate L2BEAT page tracks the Orbit chain. That absence is stated here as a fact, not a reassurance — it means the centralization properties described above (the 1-of-1 data availability committee in particular) haven't been independently rated by L2BEAT or a comparable third party, in either direction. Judge V2 on its own documented properties, not on V1's findings and not on the assumption that "no rating" implies a good one.

## What this means practically

None of the above prevents you from deploying and using standard EVM contracts today — the execution environment works as documented in [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md). It does mean you should factor the chain's current centralization and maturity profile into any decision that assumes L1-grade trust guarantees (for example, holding significant value in a bridge or contract that assumes fully trustless exit paths).

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets

# Social Login and Embedded Wallets (Privy)

Pillar 1 of the dev kit: a user signs in with Google (or email) and gets a self-custodial Privy embedded wallet on Pepe Unchained V2, with no seed phrase and no browser extension. This page covers the experience, the architecture and trust model, the SDK code, the dashboard settings it needs, the tools that automate it and the failures you may hit. The SDK's dashboard check treats every field Privy's public config returns as optional and reports `unknown` for a missing one, not a failure. It is the base for sessions and sponsorship, so read it before them.

## Prerequisites

- A Privy app with its App ID and App Secret. Create one at [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io).
- The settings on [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md): Allowed origins with the exact port, Google enabled, embedded wallets on for Ethereum.
- `@pepu-chain/sdk`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@privy-io/node`. Add `@privy-io/wagmi`, `wagmi` and `@tanstack/react-query` if you use wagmi hooks.
- No bundler, no paymaster and no gas: login and wallet creation cost nothing.

## The user experience

1. The user clicks sign in and chooses Google (or email).
2. Privy handles the OAuth flow. The user lands back in your app authenticated.
3. `WalletGate` shows "Setting up your wallet..." for a moment while your server creates the embedded wallet.
4. The app renders with an address. The user never saw a seed phrase.

The wallet is an EOA. On its own it is the only address the user has. With sponsorship or Kernel sessions there is a second, smart-account address; see [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md).

## Architecture and trust model

```
browser                         your Next.js server                 Privy
-------                         -------------------                 -----
PepuPrivyProvider
usePrivy().login()  ───────────────────────────────────────────────► Google OAuth, user created
WalletGate / useEnsureWallet
POST /api/wallet/ensure  ─────►  createEnsureWalletRoute()
  Authorization: Bearer <token>   verifies the token (app secret)  ──► verifyAccessToken
                                  finds an existing wallet         ──► users()._get
                                  else creates one, owner = user   ──► wallets().create
   ◄──── { address, created }
refreshUser()  (client picks up the wallet)
```

What this guarantees, and what it does not:

- **The user id comes only from the verified access token.** The route never reads it from the body or query string.
- **Your server gets no signing authority.** The wallet is created with `owner: { user_id }`. Your backend can create it, and cannot sign for it. Do not add a session signer in this route. Authority is only granted later, with the user's consent, by a session grant (see [Session Keys](session-keys.md)).
- **The route is idempotent.** It looks for an existing Ethereum embedded wallet first, and re-checks after a failed create, so a double submit never makes a second wallet.
- **Custody is Privy's, not yours.** Privy runs two execution modes. `legacy-embedded-wallets-only` reassembles keys on the user's device. `user-controlled-server-wallets-only`, which Privy calls TEE execution, reassembles them inside a secure enclave that only Privy's infrastructure can invoke, gated by the user's session. Both are self-custodial by Privy's description; the live tests ran with TEE. You are trusting Privy's infrastructure either way. See [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md).

### Why the server creates the wallet

Privy's own client-side creation depends on the dashboard's "automatically create embedded wallets on login" setting. With it off, a Google login creates a user, but nothing creates the wallet, and Privy's "Creating your wallet..." screen hangs forever. This was reproduced live. Calling `useCreateWallet()` explicitly did not help, because it still runs through the same client-side machinery. The SDK avoids all of it: `createPepuPrivyConfig` sets `createOnLogin: "off"`, and `WalletGate` calls your ensure route right after login. The `createOnLogin` value you pass is largely symbolic, because Privy resolves it from the dashboard. Leave the dashboard setting on as well; having both is fine.

## Configure the dashboard

Short list, in `.env.local` and the Privy dashboard. The field-by-field table is on [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

| Where | Setting | Value |
|---|---|---|
| env | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | the App ID (public) |
| env | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | the App Secret (server only) |
| dashboard | Allowed origins | `http://localhost:3000` exactly, plus your production origin |
| dashboard | Login methods | Google, plus any method you list in `loginMethods` |
| dashboard | Embedded wallets | on for Ethereum |
| dashboard | Smart Wallets | leave off unless you use the Privy Smart Wallets transport |

## SDK code

Each snippet uses exports that exist today. Add `"use client"` in files that use the React entries.

### 1. Provider

With wagmi (what the templates use), `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` mounts Privy, react-query and wagmi in the order Privy requires, and pins the embedded wallet as wagmi's active account:

```tsx
// app/providers.tsx
"use client";
import { PepuPrivyWagmiProvider } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi";

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <PepuPrivyWagmiProvider
      appId={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID}
      config={{ loginMethods: ["google", "email"] }}
    >
      {children}
    </PepuPrivyWagmiProvider>
  );
}
```

Without wagmi, use `PepuPrivyProvider` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react` with the same props. When `appId` is missing it renders a notice naming the env variable instead of crashing inside Privy. Both providers build their config with `createPepuPrivyConfig`: mainnet only, `createOnLogin: "off"`, and Coinbase Wallet pinned to `eoaOnly` because Coinbase Smart Wallet does not support chain 97741.

### 2. Ensure-wallet route (server)

```ts
// app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts
import { createEnsureWalletRoute } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server";

export const { POST } = createEnsureWalletRoute();
```

It reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` through the SDK's single env reader and returns `{ address, created }`. It answers with typed JSON errors: 401 for a bad token, 500 for missing config, 502 if Privy cannot be reached.

### 3. Wallet gate (browser)

```tsx
import { WalletGate, useEmbeddedWallet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react";

function Home() {
  return (
    <WalletGate>
      <Account />
    </WalletGate>
  );
}

function Account() {
  const { address } = useEmbeddedWallet();
  return <p>{address}</p>;
}
```

`WalletGate` takes render props `loading`, `error(e, retry)` and `stalled(address, reload)` for your own markup. `useEmbeddedWallet` separates the embedded wallet from any external wallet (MetaMask, Phantom) that Privy is also tracking. Gate on the embedded wallet, never on "any connected wallet". The lower-level hook is `useEnsureWallet`, which returns `{ status, address, error, retry }` with status `idle`, `checking`, `creating`, `ready`, `stalled` or `error`.

### 4. Protect an API route

```ts
// app/api/me/route.ts
import { requireUser } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server";

export async function GET(request: Request) {
  const auth = await requireUser(request);
  if (!auth.ok) return auth.response;
  return Response.json({ userId: auth.user.userId, address: auth.user.address });
}
```

And the browser side, which attaches the Privy access token for you:

```tsx
import { usePepuAuthFetch } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react";

const authFetch = usePepuAuthFetch();
const me = await authFetch("/api/me").then((r) => r.json());
```

`requireUser` never throws. It returns either `{ ok: true, user }` or a ready `Response`. Lower-level pieces are `verifyRequestUser`, `createPrivyServer`, `findEmbeddedEthereumWallet` and `readPrivyServerEnv`.

### 5. Wagmi active account

Left alone, an installed extension can silently become wagmi's active account, and balances and sends then act on the wrong wallet. `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` mounts `useActiveWalletPin` to keep the embedded wallet active. Pass `pinEmbeddedWallet={false}` only for an app that is deliberately external-wallet-first.

## MCP tools and skills that automate it

| Need | Tool or skill |
|---|---|
| Canonical code for the provider and the route | `pepu_sdk_snippet` with `privy-provider` or `wagmi-privy`, and `ensure-wallet-route` |
| Check the env keys (presence and length, never values) | `pepu_check_env` |
| Check dashboard settings and get the requirement table | `pepu_check_privy_config` |
| Add login to an existing app | Slash command `/pepu-add-login` |
| The agent's playbook | Skill `pepu-onboarding-privy` |
| Scaffold the whole app | `pepu_scaffold_app` with template `consumer-app` |

See [MCP Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md), [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md) and [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md).

## The template that demonstrates it

`consumer-app`: sign in, see your address and PEPU balance, send a real transaction. It states plainly that gas is not sponsored. See [Consumer App](../templates/consumer-app.md).

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template consumer-app
```

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login fails, iframe blocked, OAuth init 403 | The page origin is not in Allowed origins. Next.js moved to port 3001 because 3000 was taken | Free port 3000, or add the exact new origin to Allowed origins |
| "Creating your wallet..." never ends | A custom `PrivyProvider` is in use and the dashboard creation setting is off | Use `PepuPrivyProvider`, which turns client creation off, and `WalletGate` |
| `POST /api/wallet/ensure` returns 500 | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is unset on the server, or the dev server was not restarted after editing `.env.local` | Set it and restart; Next.js reads `.env.local` once |
| `POST /api/wallet/ensure` returns 401 for a logged-in user | The access token does not verify: wrong secret for this app, or a stale `next dev` still holds the port | Check the secret belongs to the same app as the App ID; kill the leftover process |
| `WalletGate` shows "stalled" | The server confirmed the wallet but this session has not seen it yet | Reload. It is a client sync delay, not a lost wallet |
| Balances or sends use the wrong address | An extension became the active account | Use `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`, or call `useActiveWalletPin()` once near the root |
| Console: "configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741" | The Coinbase connector is not `eoaOnly` | Use the SDK provider, which pins it |
| Console: "Unable to fetch token price" | Privy has no fiat price for PEPU | Harmless |
| A transfer is refused in Privy's modal though the wallet can afford it | Privy's pre-flight gas check is conservative at PEPU's roughly 12,500 gwei base fee | Cannot be fixed in your code; see [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) |

Testing without a faucet: login and wallet creation need no gas. An on-chain action needs a little PEPU, because there is no testnet faucet and the kit targets mainnet, where a transaction costs a fraction of a cent.

# The Two-Address Model

With gas sponsorship, one user has **two addresses**. This is the most common source of confusion when people first run the `sponsored-demo` template, so it is worth understanding before you build anything on smart accounts.

![The two-address model: the embedded wallet EOA signs and owns, the Kernel v3.1 smart account sends and holds assets with 0 PEPU while the paymaster pays gas](../.gitbook/assets/two-address-model.png)

*The signer and the sender are different addresses.*

| | Embedded wallet (EOA) | Kernel smart account |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | A plain key-controlled account that Privy creates at login | A separate contract account, controlled by the EOA |
| Role | The **signer** (owner). It authorizes actions. | The **sender**. It transacts and holds assets. |
| Address | Its own | A different one, derived from the owner and a salt |
| Holds PEPU? | Only if you send it some | Can stay at zero: a paymaster can pay the gas |
| On pepuscan | Not the sender of the sponsored transaction | The sender of the transaction |

They are different addresses. The smart account's address will not match the embedded wallet's, and that is correct.

## What this means in practice

- **Show the smart account address** to users in any sponsored flow. That is the address that transacts, owns the tokens and receives transfers. The `sponsored-demo` template displays the Kernel address, not the EOA.
- **Never tell a user to send funds to one expecting them at the other.** PEPU sent to the EOA does not appear in the smart account, and the reverse. A sponsored smart account can legitimately hold zero PEPU; the demo shows exactly that, then proves sponsorship by watching the paymaster's own EntryPoint deposit drop.
- **Look the transaction up by the smart account address** on [pepuscan.com](https://pepuscan.com). The transaction is submitted by a bundler through the EntryPoint; the smart account is the sender, the account that acted.
- **Without sponsorship, there is only one address.** Plain embedded-wallet apps (the `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint` and `game-app` templates) use the EOA directly. Session signers also act on the plain EOA. The two-address model only applies when you use a smart account, which today means the sponsorship path.
- **The smart account is created counterfactually.** Its address can be computed before it is deployed, and the first sponsored transaction deploys it as part of the same operation.

## Where each address comes from

The embedded wallet is created by Privy at login (or server-side by the template's `POST /api/wallet/ensure` fallback). The Kernel account is built on top of that wallet in one of two ways (the two [smart account paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)). With Privy Smart Wallets enabled for chain 97741 (provider Kernel), Privy's client produces the Kernel address as `account.address`. Otherwise the SDK builds it itself (`toPepuKernelAccount`, or `getKernelAddress` for a read before deployment), which is what `useDirectSponsoredSend` (`/aa/react-direct`) and the Kernel session flow (`useSponsoredSession`, `smartAccount`) do. In both, the address depends only on the owner, not on any session. `usePepuSmartAccount` (Privy Smart Wallets) and `useDirectSmartAccount` (`/aa/react-direct`) return `{ owner, smartAccount }`.

The factory, implementation and validator involved are on [Deployed Contracts](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md#erc-4337--smart-accounts-mainnet-only). If you need to compute a Kernel address for an owner yourself, `getKernelAccountAddress` in [`@pepu-chain/sdk`](../sdk/aa.md) and the `pepu_smart_account_info` tool in the [MCP server](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md) both read it from the factory's own on-chain `getAddress`.

If a user has both a Privy smart wallet and an SDK-built Kernel account, they have two smart accounts and three addresses in total; see [Mixing paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md#mixing-paths).

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: plain wallet, ZeroDev-native or Privy Smart Wallets](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md)
- [Smart Accounts](smart-accounts.md)
- [Privy Setup](privy-setup.md)
