# Architecture: Who Calls What

One page showing the browser, your Next.js route handlers, Privy, the RPC, the bundler, the paymaster and the EntryPoint, and which credential each hop uses. Use it to find which package owns a hop and where a failure comes from.

![Architecture diagram: your app (browser and server) uses @pepu-chain/sdk, which talks to Privy, the hosted bundler and the paymaster service; the bundler submits to EntryPoint v0.7, the v2 paymaster contract pays from its deposit, on PEPU mainnet 97741](../.gitbook/assets/architecture.png)

*Who calls what, from the app down to the chain.*

## Components

```
                       ┌────────────────────────── your app ───────────────────────────┐
 browser ──────────────► Next.js route handlers (SDK server entries) ──► PEPU RPC (Conduit)
 PepuPrivyProvider            │        │                │
 hooks (SDK react)            │        │                └──► bundler (ERC-4337 v0.7) ─► EntryPoint ─► Kernel account
        │                     │        └──► paymaster (ERC-7677 policy service) ─► signs, pays from deposit
        └──► Privy (login, wallets, signing, policies)
```

| Component | Role | Credential used |
|---|---|---|
| Browser | Login, owner signatures, UI | Privy access token (bearer) to your server |
| Route handlers | Verify the token, provision wallets, hold session keys, call services | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, session private key, paymaster URL |
| Privy | Users, embedded wallets, policy engine, signing | App ID (public), app secret, authorization key |
| PEPU RPC | Chain reads and raw transaction broadcast | None (public), or an authenticated URL via `PEPU_RPC_URL` |
| Bundler | Accepts UserOperations, submits through EntryPoint | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (private network or credential) |
| Paymaster | Approves sponsorship, pays gas | App key embedded in `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; Privy access token for the free tier (v2) |
| EntryPoint v0.7 `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | Validates and executes UserOperations | None |

## Sequences

### Plain transaction (embedded wallet, user pays gas)

1. Browser: `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`, wagmi `useSendTransaction` on the pinned embedded wallet.
2. Privy's confirmation modal; the wallet signs; the transaction is broadcast to the PEPU RPC.
3. Bundler, paymaster and your server are not involved.

### Privy session action (user pays gas)

1. Browser: `useSessionAct` posts to your action route with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (`usePepuAuthFetch`).
2. Server: `createSessionActionRoute` verifies the token, finds the delegated wallet, re-checks the call against the scope.
3. Server to Privy: `eth_signTransaction` with `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`. Privy's policy engine evaluates the policy.
4. Server to RPC: `signAndBroadcast` sends the raw transaction (Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` rejects chain 97741).

### Sponsored UserOperation (Privy Smart Wallets or direct)

1. Browser: `useSponsoredSend` (Privy Smart Wallets) or `useDirectSponsoredSend` (own bundler and paymaster) sends from the Kernel account (owner: embedded wallet).
2. Client to paymaster: `pm_getPaymasterStubData`, then bundler gas estimation, then `pm_getPaymasterData` (the second call is the authorization; stub data is unauthenticated by spec).
3. Owner signs the UserOperation; client sends `eth_sendUserOperation` to the bundler.
4. Bundler submits `handleOps` to the EntryPoint; the EntryPoint validates the account and the paymaster signature, executes, and charges the paymaster's deposit.

### Sponsored session action (the combination)

1. Browser: `useSponsoredSession.act()` posts to `/api/session/act`.
2. Server: `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` checks the live session, `assertCallsInScope`, takes the per-user lock.
3. Server: `loadKernelSessionAccount` rebuilds the account from the approval and the session key; `createPepuSponsoredClient` and `sendSponsored` send one UserOperation through the bundler with the paymaster.
4. EntryPoint: the Kernel account's validation runs the call policy and timestamp policy on-chain. Out of scope fails here.

## Package and subpath owning each hop

| Hop | Owner |
|---|---|
| Provider, wallet gate, hooks for auth | `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react`, `/privy/wagmi` |
| Token verification, ensure wallet, `requireUser` | `/privy/server` |
| Session policy, grant, act, revoke (Privy) | `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react` |
| Kernel policies, owner approval, session account | `/session/kernel` |
| Kernel account, sponsored client, probes | `/aa`, `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react`, `/aa/react-direct` |
| Five session routes and browser flow | `/combo`, `/combo/react` |
| v2 project helpers, REST client | `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server` |
| Endpoint resolution | root (`resolvePepuEndpoints`, `PEPU_HOSTED` in `src/endpoints.ts`) |
| Readiness checks | `/doctor` |

## Local development versus hosted

| | Local development | Hosted |
|---|---|---|
| Bundler | `http://localhost:4337` (`services/bundler`) | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) |
| Paymaster | `http://localhost:8788/v2/paymaster/<token>` (`services/paymaster/policy-service`) | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` in `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; the token is always part of the URL, so there is no tokenless default (the SDK default is the base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) |
| App | `http://localhost:3000` (must match Privy Allowed origins) | Your production origin, also in Allowed origins |

The hosted URLs live in one place, `PEPU_HOSTED` in `packages/sdk/src/endpoints.ts` (`bundlerUrl`, `paymasterBaseUrl`, and `paymasterUrl: null`), and the SDK, MCP server and docs read it. See [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Hop | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 401 from your route | Browser to server | Secret belongs to another app, or no token; see [Privy Env Vars](../privy/env-and-checks.md) |
| `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE` | Server to bundler | Fix `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` |
| `PAYMASTER_*` | Server to paymaster | [Error Reference](../reference/errors.md) |
| UserOperation reverts at validation | Kernel account | Call outside session scope, or expired |

- [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md)

# Smart Account Paths: Plain Wallet, ZeroDev-Native or Privy Smart Wallets

PEPU gives you three ways to send transactions for a user, and two of them involve a smart account. This page explains what a smart account is, what each of ZeroDev, Privy and the PEPU paymaster does, and how the two smart-account paths differ: **Path 1, ZeroDev-native** (the SDK builds the Kernel account) and **Path 2, Privy Smart Wallets** (Privy builds it from dashboard settings). Path 0, the plain embedded wallet, is the baseline for contrast. Read it before you pick a template; it answers "which one do I start from?" in one table.

![Comparison of Path 0 plain embedded wallet, Path 1 ZeroDev-native SDK and Path 2 Privy Smart Wallets: who pays gas, sessions, free tier and project budgets](../.gitbook/assets/smart-account-paths.png)

*The three paths side by side.*

## The short answer

| If you want | Use | Start from |
|---|---|---|
| Login and a wallet, users pay their own gas | Path 0: plain embedded wallet | `consumer-app` |
| A game or app with many actions, no popup and no user gas, limits enforced on-chain | Path 1 with the combination | `sponsored-session-app` |
| One gasless button in a client-only app, on your own project budget | Path 2: Privy Smart Wallets | `sponsored-demo` |
| A bot or backend that sends sponsored transactions | Path 1 with a server key as owner | a script (below) |

If you are unsure, take Path 1. It does everything Path 2 does, adds sessions and the free tier, and needs no Privy dashboard setting beyond the usual login ones. Path 2 is the shortcut for a client-only gasless button.

## What a smart account is, and why it needs an owner key

A normal wallet (an EOA) is one key. Whoever holds the key can send a transaction, and the sender pays gas in PEPU. A **smart account** is a contract that acts as the sender. Because it is code, it can do things a key cannot: let someone else pay the gas, accept a limited session key, or batch several calls into one operation. It sends [UserOperations](../reference/glossary.md) (ERC-4337) instead of ordinary transactions.

A contract cannot sign. Every smart account therefore has an **owner key**: an ordinary signer whose signature the contract accepts as proof that the owner approved an action. Without an owner key nothing could authorize the account. The owner can be a Privy embedded wallet, an EOA, or a server key. The smart account's address is derived from the owner (and an index), so it is a different address from the owner's; see [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md).

Three parties do three different jobs:

| Party | Job | What it is in PEPU |
|---|---|---|
| **ZeroDev Kernel v3.1** | The smart account contract logic. It validates UserOperations, runs the calls and enforces on-chain session policies (call policy, timestamp policy). | The factory, implementation and validators are deployed on chain 97741; see [Entrypoints and Kernel](../contracts/entrypoints-and-kernel.md). The SDK pins `KERNEL_VERSION` to v3.1 and [EntryPoint](../reference/glossary.md) v0.7. |
| **Privy** | Login, key custody and user identity. The embedded wallet is the owner key. Privy also verifies who the user is (an access token the paymaster can check). | `PepuPrivyProvider`, `WalletGate`, `useEmbeddedWallet`. |
| **Our paymaster** | Pays the gas. A [bundler](../reference/glossary.md) submits the UserOperation and the [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md) covers the cost from a project's balance or the free tier. | Hosted: bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, paymaster `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; contract `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (v2 paymaster). |

The two smart-account paths differ in exactly one thing: **who builds and drives the Kernel account**. Privy does it in Path 2, the PEPU SDK does it in Path 1. The contract is the same Kernel v3.1 either way.

## Path 0 (for contrast): plain embedded wallet, no smart account

The user's Privy embedded wallet is the account. It signs and sends directly, and it pays gas in PEPU (a fraction of a cent per transaction). There is one address, no bundler, no paymaster, no ZeroDev.

| | |
|---|---|
| Templates | `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint` (user approves each send), `game-app` (popup-free play) |
| Popup-free play | `game-app` uses **Privy session signers**: you register an authorization key and a key quorum, the user grants a session once, and your server asks Privy to sign each action (`eth_signTransaction`) and then broadcasts it. The limits are Privy policies, enforced by Privy's backend (off-chain). The user still pays gas. See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md). |
| SDK | `/privy/*`, and for game sessions `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react` |
| Needs | A Privy app. For game sessions also an authorization key and a key quorum |
| Does not need | A bundler, a paymaster, a project, ZeroDev packages |

Choose it when users pay their own gas and you want the smallest setup. Everything below is about removing that gas cost.

## Path 1: ZeroDev-native, built by the SDK

The SDK creates the Kernel account directly with `toPepuKernelAccount` (`@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel`). The owner is whatever signer you pass: a Privy embedded wallet, an EOA, or a server key (`KernelOwner` is a viem local account, a Privy or ZeroDev signer, or a wallet client). Privy is only login and key custody; the account itself is not a Privy object.

| | |
|---|---|
| Used by | `sponsored-session-app`, and the SDK entries `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react-direct`, `/session/kernel`, `/combo`, `/combo/react` |
| Sponsored sends | `createPepuSponsoredClient` and `sendSponsored` send through our bundler with gas paid by our paymaster. Fees come from the chain with 20% headroom because Alto does not implement ZeroDev's gas price method. In React: `useDirectSponsoredSend`, `useDirectSmartAccount` |
| On-chain session keys | `buildKernelSessionPolicies` (call policy v0.0.4 plus timestamp policy), `approveKernelSession` (one owner signature in the browser), `loadKernelSessionAccount` (server, with the session key). The scope is enforced by the account during validation, so a compromised server can only do what the permission allows until it expires. `/combo` wraps this into five route handlers and one hook |
| Free tier and budgets | The paymaster context carries the user's Privy access token (`useDirectSponsoredSend` and the combo routes forward it by default). That unlocks the [free tier](../reference/glossary.md) **for PEPU's own Privy app only**. Your app pays from your [project](../reference/glossary.md) budget; the project is tried first and the free tier is the fallback. See [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md) |
| Control | You choose the owner, the `index`, the validators, the session scope and expiry, and where the session key lives |
| Privy dashboard | **Smart Wallets not required.** Only the usual settings: Allowed origins, login methods, embedded wallets. Leaving Smart Wallets on is harmless |
| Paymaster credential | From a server (combo routes, scripts, bots): the project **server key** (`ppk_`) in `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` or as `paymasterToken`. A secret. From a browser: a project **client token** (`ppt_`) with allowed origins, never the server key |
| Extra packages | `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`, plus `@zerodev/permissions` for sessions. Not `permissionless` |

### Browser, owner signs each send

```tsx
// Path 1 (ZeroDev-native), browser: the SDK builds the Kernel account for the Privy embedded wallet.
// No Privy Smart Wallets setting is needed. The owner signs each send (no session here).
// NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are visible to every visitor: use a project CLIENT token (ppt_) with allowed origins, never a server key (ppk_).
// See docs/concepts/smart-account-paths.md
import { useDirectSmartAccount, useDirectSponsoredSend } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

export function NativeTap() {
  const { owner, smartAccount } = useDirectSmartAccount(); // two addresses: the EOA signs, the Kernel account sends
  // Next.js only inlines literal process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_X reads, so pass the URLs explicitly.
  const { send, status, result, error } = useDirectSponsoredSend({
    ...(process.env["NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL"] ? { bundlerUrl: process.env["NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL"] } : {}),
    ...(process.env["NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL"] ? { paymasterUrl: process.env["NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL"] } : {}),
  });

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Owner (signs): {owner}</p>
      <p>Smart account (sends): {smartAccount}</p>
      <button
        disabled={status === "signing" || status === "submitting"}
        onClick={() => void send([{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }])}
      >
        Tap, no gas
      </button>
      {status === "confirmed" && result ? <a href={result.explorerUrl}>Paid by {result.paymaster}</a> : null}
      {error ? <p>{error.code}: {error.hint}</p> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Browser plus server, one signature then no popups: the combination

Google login, one scoped on-chain session, then every action is a sponsored UserOperation signed by a server-held session key. This is `sponsored-session-app`; the server routes and the hook are in [/combo](../sdk/combo.md) and the full walkthrough is [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md).

### Server or bot: the owner is a server key

```ts
// Path 1 (ZeroDev-native), server or bot: the owner is a plain server key, the paymaster credential is the project SERVER key.
// SERVER ONLY: both secrets stay in the environment and are never printed or sent to a browser.
// See docs/concepts/smart-account-paths.md
import { getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { createPepuSponsoredClient, sendSponsored, toPepuKernelAccount } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel";
import type { Hex } from "viem";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

export async function botTap() {
  const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);
  // The Kernel account is owned by this key. Its address is a pure function of the owner (and index).
  const owner = privateKeyToAccount(process.env["BOT_OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY"] as Hex);
  const account = await toPepuKernelAccount({ publicClient, owner });
  // paymasterToken is your project's server key (ppk_); the SDK builds https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>.
  const client = createPepuSponsoredClient({ account, paymasterToken: process.env["PEPU_PAYMASTER_SERVER_KEY"] as string });
  return sendSponsored({ client, calls: [{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }] });
}
```

## Path 2: Privy Smart Wallets

Privy builds and manages the Kernel account. You describe it once in the Privy dashboard (provider Kernel v3.1, chain 97741, bundler URL, a static paymaster URL), and Privy's smart-wallet client sends the UserOperations from the browser. The SDK wraps that client: `useSponsoredSend({ transport: "privy-smart-wallets" })` and `usePepuSmartAccount` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react`, with the app wrapped in Privy's `SmartWalletsProvider` (`composeProviders` from `/privy/react` builds the nesting).

| | |
|---|---|
| Used by | `sponsored-demo`, and the SDK entry `/aa/react` |
| Where it runs | Client side, through `useSmartWallets`. No server code is needed for sending (only the ensure-wallet route for login) |
| Quick to enable | One dashboard form and one hook. The bundler and paymaster URLs live in the dashboard, not your env |
| Privy dashboard | **Smart Wallets required**: provider Kernel (ZeroDev) v3.1, custom chain `97741` with RPC `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz`, bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, paymaster `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project client token>`. Field detail: [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md) |
| Paymaster credential | The project **client token** (`ppt_`) inside the dashboard URL. Never the server key |
| Extra packages | `permissionless` (required by Privy's smart-wallets module). Never needs `@zerodev/*` |

```tsx
// Pillar 3, client: send with gas sponsored from a component.
// See docs/sdk/aa.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-send.md
import { usePepuSmartAccount, usePepuSponsorship, useSponsoredSend } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

export function SponsoredTap() {
  const { smartAccount } = usePepuSmartAccount();
  // "privy-smart-wallets" uses the bundler and paymaster URLs from the Privy dashboard.
  // For your own bundler and paymaster, use useDirectSponsoredSend from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct".
  const { send, status, result, error } = useSponsoredSend({ transport: "privy-smart-wallets" });
  const sponsorship = usePepuSponsorship({ pollMs: 0 });

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Smart account: {smartAccount}</p>
      <button
        disabled={status === "signing" || status === "submitting"}
        onClick={() => void send([{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }])}
      >
        Tap, no gas
      </button>
      {status === "confirmed" && result ? <a href={result.explorerUrl}>Paid by {result.paymaster}</a> : null}
      {error ? (
        <p>
          {error.code}: {error.hint}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {!sponsorship.loading && !sponsorship.available ? <p>{sponsorship.reason}</p> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Limits of Path 2

- **The free tier cannot be reached.** The dashboard URL is static, so it carries no per-user Privy access token, and the free tier needs one.
- **It needs a funded project of your own** (claim, deposit, register) and a **client token with allowed origins**, because Privy calls the URL from the browser. Without allowed origins the paymaster answers `project_origin_not_allowed`. The paymaster URL is stored in Privy's dashboard, so it is a credential that lives there.
- **No on-chain session keys through our SDK.** Privy's smart-wallet client cannot install a scoped session validator, so `/session/kernel` and `/combo` build their own Kernel account instead.
- **Less control over account config.** Owner, index, validators and fee handling are Privy's. The result also has `userOpHash: null`, because only the bundle transaction is exposed.
- **A page that spins on "Setting up your smart wallet..."** means Smart Wallets is not configured for chain 97741. That is a dashboard fix, not a code fix.

## Decision table

| | Path 0: plain EOA | Path 0: Privy session signers | Path 1: ZeroDev-native | Path 2: Privy Smart Wallets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Login | Privy | Privy | Privy (or any signer) | Privy |
| Account that sends | The embedded wallet | The embedded wallet | A Kernel v3.1 account built by the SDK | A Kernel v3.1 account built by Privy |
| Who pays gas | The user | The user | Your project, or the free tier for PEPU's own app | Your project |
| Sessions, no popup per action | None: user approves each send | Privy off-chain policies, enforced by Privy's backend | On-chain call and timestamp policies, enforced by the account | None through our SDK |
| Free tier | No | No | Yes, PEPU's own Privy app only (user's Privy token forwarded) | No (static URL carries no token) |
| Project budgets | No | No | Yes (server key, or client token from a browser) | Yes (client token in the dashboard) |
| Server needed | No (only the ensure-wallet route) | Yes (authorization key, session routes) | Yes for sessions and bots; no for a browser-only owner-signed send | No |
| Privy dashboard settings | Origins, login methods, embedded wallets | Those plus authorization key and key quorum | Origins, login methods, embedded wallets. **Not** Smart Wallets | Those plus **Smart Wallets**: Kernel, 97741, bundler and paymaster URLs |
| Start from | `consumer-app` (also `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint`) | `game-app` | `sponsored-session-app` | `sponsored-demo` |
| SDK entries | `/privy/*` | `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react` | `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react-direct`, `/session/kernel`, `/combo` | `/aa/react` |

## Pick this if

- **A game with many actions, or any app where a popup per action would kill the experience.** Path 1 with the combination (`sponsored-session-app`). One signature, then taps with no popup and no user gas, with limits enforced on-chain. Size per-user caps above the worst-case reservation (about 20.5 PEPU for a session's first operation, 6.9 PEPU after).
- **A simple gasless button in a client-only app with its own budget.** Path 2 (`sponsored-demo`). One dashboard form, one hook, no server. Accept that every send needs the user's confirmation and that you cannot use the free tier.
- **A standard dapp where users pay gas.** Path 0 with the plain embedded wallet (`consumer-app`). Do not add a smart account for nothing. If you want popup-free play and the user paying a fraction of a cent is fine, use the Privy session signers in `game-app`.
- **A bot or backend.** Path 1 with a server key as the owner (`botTap` above): the account is owned by a key you hold, and the project server key pays. Nothing in a browser.
- **You are not sure.** Path 1. It can do everything Path 2 can, and it is the only one with sessions and the free tier.

## Mixing paths

Yes, one user can have both. The two accounts are separate contracts and usually separate addresses:

- The Privy smart wallet address comes from Privy (`usePepuSmartAccount`, `useSmartWallets().client.account.address`). The SDK Kernel address comes from `getKernelAddress` or `useDirectSmartAccount`. Both are Kernel v3.1 accounts owned by the same embedded wallet, but the address depends on the owner, the `index` and the account configuration. **Do not assume the two addresses are equal**; they match only if Privy's index and configuration match the SDK's, and you should read each address from the API that created it. Show the user the address that actually sends.
- Assets live at one address. PEPU or tokens held by the Privy smart wallet are not at the SDK Kernel account and the reverse. Pick one account per app and keep to it, unless you have a reason to run both.
- The paymaster accepts both as owned by the user. For the identity check, the sender must be either a Privy smart wallet the user owns, or the Kernel v3.1 account (index 0) derived from one of the user's own Privy embedded wallets. An SDK account built with a non-default `index` is not recognized by that identity check.
- Leaving Smart Wallets switched on while using Path 1 is harmless: users then also get a Privy smart wallet linked to their account, which you simply do not use.

## Migrating between paths

The owner key never changes, so users keep their login and their embedded wallet. The smart account can change, and with it the address that holds assets. Move any balances out of the old account before you cut over.

| Move | What changes in the code |
|---|---|
| Path 0 to Path 1 | Install `@zerodev/sdk` and `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`. Replace `sendTransaction` with `useDirectSponsoredSend` (browser) or `createPepuSponsoredClient` plus `sendSponsored` (server). Show `useDirectSmartAccount().smartAccount` instead of the EOA. Add a paymaster credential. Allowlist your contract. Existing assets at the EOA stay there |
| Path 0 to Path 2 | Enable Smart Wallets in the dashboard, wrap the app in `SmartWalletsProvider`, install `permissionless`, replace sends with `useSponsoredSend`. Show `usePepuSmartAccount().smartAccount` |
| Path 2 to Path 1 | Replace `useSponsoredSend` with `useDirectSponsoredSend` and `usePepuSmartAccount` with `useDirectSmartAccount`. Remove `SmartWalletsProvider`; the dashboard Smart Wallets form can be turned off. Install the `@zerodev/*` peers. Move the bundler URL and the paymaster credential into your env (or into the combo routes). Remove `permissionless` if nothing else uses it. For sessions, add `/combo` and `/combo/react`. The address may change, so move assets from the old Privy smart wallet first |
| Path 1 to Path 2 | The reverse, and you lose sessions and the free tier. Put the client token URL in the Privy dashboard. Rarely a good idea |
| Path 0 session signers to Path 1 sessions | Drop the authorization key and quorum. `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` replaces the session routes. Scope moves from a Privy policy to `KernelSessionCall`s enforced on-chain. The user now signs one EIP-712 message to grant, and no longer pays gas |

The core of a Path 2 to Path 1 browser change is two imports:

```diff
-import { usePepuSmartAccount, useSponsoredSend } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react";
+import { useDirectSmartAccount, useDirectSponsoredSend } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct";
-const { smartAccount } = usePepuSmartAccount();
-const { send } = useSponsoredSend({ transport: "privy-smart-wallets" });
+const { smartAccount } = useDirectSmartAccount();
+const { send } = useDirectSponsoredSend({ bundlerUrl, paymasterUrl });
```

`send(calls)` and its `SponsoredResult` have the same shape on both paths.

## What to expect

- A new Path 1 or Path 2 user holds 0 PEPU at their smart account and still sends. Confirm sponsorship by the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit dropping, not by the transaction hash (the result's `paymaster` field also names who paid).
- The first operation deploys the account, so it reserves more gas than later ones.
- Run `npm run doctor` in the app (or the `pepu_check_privy_config` and `pepu_sponsorship_status` MCP tools) to see which dashboard rows and credentials are missing for your path.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Setting up your smart wallet..." never ends | Path 2 with Smart Wallets not configured for chain 97741 | Fill the dashboard form, or switch to Path 1 |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | A client token (`ppt_`) with no allowed origins, or used from a server | Set the project's allowed origins, or use the server key from a backend |
| Balance "missing" after switching paths | Assets are at the other path's smart account | Look up the old address and send from it |
| Free tier denied on a third-party app | The free tier is only for PEPU's own Privy app | Use a project of your own |
| `Cannot find module '@zerodev/sdk'` | Path 1 peers not installed | `npm i @zerodev/sdk @zerodev/ecdsa-validator` (and `@zerodev/permissions` for sessions) |
| Sponsorship denied right after the first action | Per-user caps below the first-operation reservation | Raise the caps; see [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md) |

- [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/concepts/trust-and-security

# Trust and Security Model

States precisely what each mechanism protects against and who is trusted, so builders do not overclaim. Covers off-chain versus on-chain enforcement, secret handling and the session store. Read it before telling users what a session or sponsorship guarantees.

Deposits to the v2 paymaster are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs. The v1 paymaster is retired.

## Privy session signers (off-chain)

- Scope (one contract, listed functions, zero value, expiry) is enforced by Privy's backend policy engine on each signing request. You trust Privy and your policy configuration.
- It cannot bound gas; the user pays it.
- The authorization key lets your server request signatures for any wallet that granted its quorum, within each policy. A policy must always be attached; the SDK refuses to build an unscoped one.
- Revocation: `removeSigners` from the browser is the real revoke.
- Show `SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE["privy-offchain"]` on the consent screen.

## Kernel session keys (on-chain)

- Scope is enforced by the call policy v0.0.4 and timestamp policy contracts during UserOperation validation. It holds even if your backend is compromised.
- A leaked session key can act within the permission until expiry: the listed targets, selectors, value limit, validity window.
- The owner key never leaves Privy and the browser. The approval holds no secret.
- Revocation deletes the server key at once; the on-chain grant lapses at expiry (uninstalling is an owner-signed call a destination-allowlisted paymaster should not sponsor). Keep sessions short.
- Show `SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE["kernel-onchain"]`.

## Paymaster

- **Signer:** the paymaster contract trusts any signature from its authorized signer, so the signer key is a hot wallet for the deposit. Keep the deposit small and monitored.
- **Policy service:** signs only if the destination allowlist, per-user, per-app and global caps pass. The allowlist limits what sponsorship money can pay for; it does not protect the user's account.
- **Project deposits (v2):** deposits only, no withdrawals by anyone. `projectId = keccak256(bytes(appId))`. Ownership is Privy-verified: verify the app secret, get an EIP-712 attestation, call `claimProject`. The claim sets the owner only; the owner then calls `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit`. Re-claims, and the first claim of a project that already holds funds, are timelocked 48 hours and can be cancelled (the owner once per new owner). A project must have a per-wallet limit. Pausing is the exit. Free tier: 100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per hour (enforced by the service), verified Privy users from PEPU's own Privy app only, no chain-wide ceiling.
- **A paymaster URL is a credential.** It embeds a token. A project client token (`ppt_`) is publishable but works only from the project's allowed origins (`project_origin_not_allowed` otherwise); a project server key (`ppk_`) is secret and belongs in a backend. A third-party app's own Privy token does not unlock the free tier.

## Secrets: where each may live

| Secret | May live | Never |
|---|---|---|
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Server env | `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, client code, git, logs |
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Server env | Same; a production signing key |
| Session private key | Server session store, encrypted at rest in production | Browser, logs |
| `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | Server env | Browser unless you accept exposing the credential |
| Policy service signer, bundler executor keys | Operator's secret store | Repo |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, quorum id | Public by design | n/a |

The SDK's server entries (`/privy/server`, `/session/server`, `/combo`, `/paymaster/server`) call `assertServerOnly` and refuse to load in a browser bundle. Server-only code never reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_` secrets. Doctor and MCP check tools report presence and length, never values. `requestClaimAttestation` sends your Privy app secret to the PEPU service for one request: use a dedicated app and rotate afterwards.

## Session store options

| Store | Durability | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `createMemoryStore()` | Lost on restart, not shared across instances, key in plaintext memory | Development and tests only |
| Your `SessionStore` on a database or KV | Durable | Production, with `sessionPrivateKey` encrypted at rest (KMS or envelope key) and an atomic or distributed `tryLock` |

## Threat table

| Threat | Privy mode | Kernel mode |
|---|---|---|
| Compromised app server | Can sign within each policy via the authorization key | Can act within the on-chain permission until expiry |
| Compromised Privy | Total over wallets | Cannot exceed the owner-signed permission, but controls the owner key |
| Leaked authorization key | Within policies, for all granting users | n/a |
| Leaked session key | n/a | Within scope until expiry |
| Out-of-scope call | Denied by Privy's engine | Fails EntryPoint validation |
| Gas drain of user | Possible: user pays | Sponsored; bounded by paymaster caps |
| Paymaster budget drain | n/a | Bounded by allowlist and caps |

Everything the SDK server boundary enforces: user id only from a verified token, owner address from Privy's records, calls re-checked against scope before signing, per-user lock and rate limit, approval bound to this account and permission id. For Kernel mode these are fail-fast checks; the chain is the real enforcement.

# Privy Configuration Overview

Everything about configuring Privy for a PEPU app: which feature needs which setting, how the SDK and tools verify settings, and where each detail page lives. Start here when login, wallets, sessions or Smart Wallets misbehave.

Menu labels in the dashboard can change; the SDK table `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` is the checklist of record.

## Prerequisites

- A Privy app. Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`.

## Feature to setting matrix

| Feature | Settings it needs | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Google or email login | App ID, secret, Allowed origins (with port), Login methods, Google | [Dashboard Settings](dashboard-settings.md) |
| Embedded wallet | Embedded wallets on for Ethereum; server route with the secret; Coinbase `eoaOnly` (code) | [Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) |
| Privy session signers | Authorization key, key quorum, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` | [Authorization Keys](authorization-keys.md) |
| Smart Wallets (Privy sponsorship transport) | Smart Wallets: chain 97741, Kernel, bundler URL, paymaster URL | [Dashboard Settings](dashboard-settings.md) |
| Kernel session plus sponsorship (the combination) | Login settings only. No Smart Wallets, no authorization key | [End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md) |

## How settings are verified

- `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` is one data table: id, where (`dashboard`, `env` or `code`), label, required, pillars, fix and docs URL. It feeds the docs, the MCP tool, the doctor and in-app notices.
- `checkPrivyDashboardConfig` reads the public app-config endpoint and reports pass, fail or unknown for the dashboard rows.
- `pepu_check_privy_config` is that function as an MCP tool.
- `npm run doctor` checks env presence and shape.

Details: [Privy Env Vars and Verification](env-and-checks.md).

## Pages in this section

- [Privy Setup Walkthrough](../onboarding/privy-setup.md): the short first-time procedure.
- [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](dashboard-settings.md)
- [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](authorization-keys.md)
- [Privy Env Vars and Verification](env-and-checks.md)

## Common failures

| Symptom | Go to |
|---|---|
| Login fails or the iframe is blocked | Allowed origins in [Dashboard Settings](dashboard-settings.md) |
| "Creating your wallet..." hangs | [Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) |
| 401 "No valid authorization keys" | [Authorization Keys](authorization-keys.md) |
| "Setting up your smart wallet..." hangs | Smart Wallets in [Dashboard Settings](dashboard-settings.md) |

# Privy Setup

This page is the short first-time walkthrough for [Privy](https://privy.io). The complete table of every dashboard field, with exact values and failure symptoms, is [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md); authorization keys are in [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md); verification is in [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md). This page is the setup guide for using [Privy](https://privy.io) with Pepe Unchained V2: the Dashboard settings that decide whether login works, the code configuration, and the failures you are most likely to hit. Most of it was learned the hard way during live testing on mainnet, so it is more specific than Privy's own docs.

If you used `create-pepu-app`, the code configuration is already done. The Dashboard settings below are not: they live in your Privy app, not in your repository.

## 1. Create the app and set the environment

1. Go to [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io), sign up and create an app.
2. Copy the **App ID** and the **App Secret** from the app's settings.
3. Put them in `.env.local`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID=your-app-id-here
PRIVY_APP_SECRET=your-app-secret-here
```

The App ID is public by design (it is bundled into client JavaScript). The App Secret is server-only: never give it a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix and never commit it. The templates use it in `POST /api/wallet/ensure` to verify the caller's access token and create their embedded wallet after login.

## 2. Dashboard settings that matter

### Allowed origins must include the exact port

Privy matches the full origin: scheme, host **and port**. For local development that means:

```
http://localhost:3000
```

`http://localhost` with no port is a different origin (an unspecified `http` port means 80), so it will not match.

The trap: if port 3000 is already in use, Next.js does not stop. It silently starts on 3001 instead, and login then fails with errors that do not mention the port (the login iframe is blocked by a CSP `frame-ancestors` rule, and OAuth init returns a 403). Free port 3000 rather than working around it with `-p 3001`. If you deliberately use another port, add that exact origin to **Allowed origins** first. Add your production origin the same way before you deploy.

### Automatically create embedded wallets on login

Turn on **Automatically create embedded wallets on login** in the Dashboard. The `createOnLogin` value you pass to `<PrivyProvider>` does not override the Dashboard: the Dashboard wins.

The templates also provision the wallet server-side right after login, through their own `POST /api/wallet/ensure` route (Privy's documented "pregenerate wallets" pattern, using `@privy-io/node` and your App Secret). That is a fallback for apps where the Dashboard setting is off or Privy's client-side creation screen stalls: without it, the user would sit on "Creating your wallet..." indefinitely. It creates a wallet owned by the signed-in user only if they do not already have one, and it gives your backend no authority to sign for that wallet.

You want both: the Dashboard setting on, and the server-side fallback left in place.

### Wallet execution mode: TEE

Use Privy's **TEE execution** mode (`user-controlled-server-wallets-only` in Privy's SDK types). Wallets are reassembled inside a secure enclave that only Privy can invoke, gated by the user's authenticated session. Neither Privy nor your server sees the full private key. The older `legacy-embedded-wallets-only` mode reassembles keys on the user's device. Both are self-custodial; the difference is the mechanism. Use TEE mode unless you have a reason not to, and know which one your app is in, because it changes how wallet creation behaves.

### Smart Wallets (required only for `sponsored-demo`)

Smart Wallets is a separate Dashboard section. It is **required** for `sponsored-demo` (Privy Smart Wallets). It is **not** required for `sponsored-session-app` or the other templates: the SDK builds the ZeroDev Kernel account itself, and leaving it enabled is harmless (users then also get a Privy smart wallet linked, which the paymaster also accepts as owned). For `sponsored-demo` it needs:

- provider **Kernel** (ZeroDev) v3.1,
- custom chain **PEPU**, chain id **97741**, RPC `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz`,
- bundler URL `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`,
- paymaster URL `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project client token ppt_...>`.

You need a claimed and funded project first (see [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md)). Use the **client token** with your app's origins allowed, because Privy calls the URL from the browser; never use the server key (`ppk_`) there. A static URL carries no per-user token, so the free tier is not reachable here and a funded project is required. Old dashboards may still hold temporary development bundler or paymaster URLs (such as tunnels); replace them with the hosted ones. Details are on [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md). If Smart Wallets is off for `sponsored-demo`, the page spins forever on "Setting up your smart wallet...".

Per-template requirements, including the game template's authorization key and quorum and the paymaster credentials of each sponsored template, are in [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md#per-template-requirements).

### Coinbase smart wallet: set `eoaOnly`

Coinbase's smart wallet does not support chain 97741. If you offer external-wallet login, restrict the Coinbase connector:

```tsx
externalWallets: {
  coinbaseWallet: { config: { preference: { options: "eoaOnly" } } },
},
```

Without it, the browser console fills with "The configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741". `eoaOnly` keeps the Coinbase extension and mobile paths working and drops the one that cannot work here.

## 3. Code configuration

Privy does not ship PEPU as a built-in chain, so give it a chain object. With the SDK:

```tsx
import { PrivyProvider } from "@privy-io/react-auth";
import { pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

<PrivyProvider
  appId={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID!}
  config={{
    loginMethods: ["email", "google"],
    defaultChain: pepuMainnet,
    supportedChains: [pepuMainnet],
    externalWallets: {
      coinbaseWallet: { config: { preference: { options: "eoaOnly" } } },
    },
  }}
>
  {/* your app */}
</PrivyProvider>;
```

`loginMethods` is a starting point, not the source of truth: the methods users actually see are the intersection of this list and what is enabled in the Dashboard. Enable them in both places or Privy hides them silently. Without `@pepu-chain/sdk` (`npm i @pepu-chain/sdk`; see [Quickstart](../get-started/quickstart-app.md)), define the chain yourself with viem's `defineChain` using the values on [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md).

Privy's SDK options change between versions. If something here does not match your installed version, check [docs.privy.io](https://docs.privy.io); the chain object is the stable part.

## Troubleshooting

**Login fails, the iframe is blocked, or OAuth returns 403.** Almost always the origin. Check which port your dev server actually started on, then check **Allowed origins** for that exact `scheme://host:port`.

**"Creating your wallet..." never finishes.** Check that **Automatically create embedded wallets on login** is on, that `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is set in `.env.local`, and that the dev server was restarted afterwards: Next.js reads `.env.local` once at startup, and a stale process keeps failing no matter how correct the file is. If `POST /api/wallet/ensure` returns 401 for a logged-in user, look for a leftover `next dev` still bound to the port.

**Wallet created but `useWallets()` is empty at first.** The client picks up the server-created wallet after a user refresh. The templates call `refreshUser()` and wait a bounded time for it to appear. If you build your own flow, do the same.

**"Setting up your smart wallet..." never clears.** Smart Wallets is not enabled for chain 97741 in the Dashboard, or the bundler and paymaster URLs are missing. See [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md).

**Console error: "The configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741".** Set the Coinbase connector to `eoaOnly` as above.

**Console error: "Unable to fetch token price".** Harmless. Privy cannot fetch a fiat price for PEPU, and the message does not affect login, wallets or transactions.

**A transfer is refused in Privy's confirmation modal even though the wallet can afford it.** Privy's own pre-flight gas estimate is conservative, and PEPU's base fee is around 12,500 gwei, so the estimate can exceed the real cost by enough to block a transfer the wallet could pay for. The check happens inside Privy's modal, so you cannot fix it in your own code. This is why the `consumer-app` template has no "Max" button. If your app sends transactions itself rather than through Privy's modal, `maxSendableAmount` in [`@pepu-chain/sdk`](../sdk/core.md#gas-and-fees) sizes a transfer correctly. See also [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md).

**Server-side `eth_sendTransaction` fails with "Unsupported chain with id 97741".** Expected. See [Sign with Privy, Broadcast Yourself](../recipes/sign-with-privy-broadcast-yourself.md).

**The embedded wallet's address is not the address I see on pepuscan.** If you are using sponsorship, the account that transacts is a Kernel smart account at a different address. See [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md).

## Next

- [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](session-keys.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md)
- [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/privy/dashboard-settings

# Dashboard Settings, Field by Field

Every Privy dashboard setting a PEPU app depends on, with the exact value, why it matters and the symptom when it is wrong. The rows come from `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` in `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy` and from the live testing recorded in the template READMEs. If you only read one Privy page, read this one.

Menu labels are marked where they may change: Privy renames dashboard sections, and the SDK's table is the checklist of record. Fields Privy's public config does not expose cannot be checked automatically and show as `unknown`, not as a failure.

## Prerequisites

- A Privy app from [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io).
- Which pillars you use. The last column of the table says which settings each pillar needs.

## The settings

"Menu label" is where the SDK's table says to look. Privy may rename menu labels.

| Setting | Menu label (may drift) | Exact value | Why | Failure symptom | Login | Session (Privy) | Sponsor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| App ID | Settings, Basics | Copy to `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Public identifier, bundled into client JS | Setup screen "Missing NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID"; `privy.app-id` doctor failure | yes | yes | yes |
| App secret | Settings, Basics | Create one; copy to `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`. Server only | The ensure route, `requireUser` and every session route verify access tokens with it | `/api/wallet/ensure` returns 500; or 401 for a valid session when the secret belongs to another app | yes | yes | yes |
| Allowed origins | Configuration, App settings | The exact origin: `http://localhost:3000`, plus each production origin | Privy matches scheme, host and port. `http://localhost` is a different origin | Login iframe blocked by CSP `frame-ancestors`, OAuth init returns 403, console error naming no port | yes | yes | yes |
| Login methods | User management, Authentication | Enable every method you list in `loginMethods` | Methods not enabled here are hidden even if listed in code | Login button shows fewer methods than the code lists | yes | | |
| Google | User management, Authentication, Socials | On | The code-side `"google"` only shows if this is on | No "Continue with Google" button | yes | | |
| Embedded wallets, Ethereum | Wallets | On for Ethereum | The embedded wallet is created here | `WalletGate` errors; ensure route 502 `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED` | yes | yes | yes |
| Automatically create embedded wallets on login | Wallets | Either value works. On is fine | The dashboard wins over `createOnLogin` in code. The SDK provisions server-side regardless | With it off and a custom provider, "Creating your wallet..." hangs forever | recommended | | |
| Execution mode | Wallets | The live tests used TEE (`user-controlled-server-wallets-only`) | Selects where keys are reassembled | Behavior of wallet creation changes between modes | note | | |
| Coinbase Wallet eoaOnly | Not a dashboard field: set in code | Use `PepuPrivyProvider` or `createPepuPrivyConfig`, which pin it | Coinbase Smart Wallet does not support chain 97741 | Console: "configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741" | yes | | |
| Authorization key | Controls (Wallet infrastructure), Authorization keys, New key | Paste the public key from `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` | Privy checks your server's signature on each signing request | `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH` | | yes | |
| Key quorum | Same area; create a quorum that contains the key | Copy its id to `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` | The grant names this quorum as the signer | 401 "No valid authorization keys or user signing keys available" | | yes | |
| Smart Wallets | Wallets, Smart wallets (the demo README says Settings, Wallet infrastructure, Smart wallets) | Enabled; chain `97741`; provider Kernel; bundler URL `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`; paymaster URL `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | Only the `privy-smart-wallets` transport reads it | Page spins on "Setting up your smart wallet..." | | | Privy transport only |

The combination (`sponsored-session-app`) needs only the Login column. It does not use Smart Wallets, authorization keys or quorums.

## Field notes

### App ID and secret

The App ID is public by design. The secret is server only: never give it a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix, never commit it. Rotate it in the dashboard if it leaks; update `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` and restart. Note the v2 paymaster claim flow sends this secret to the PEPU policy service for one request, so use a dedicated app for sponsorship if you can and rotate afterwards ([Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md)).

### Allowed origins

Include the exact origin of every environment: local, preview, production. Next.js silently moves to port 3001 when 3000 is taken, and login then fails with errors that never mention the port. Free port 3000 rather than passing `-p 3001`. If you deliberately use another port, add that exact origin first. Every template defaults to 3000, and a Privy app id is typically allow-listed for one set of origins, so do not run two templates at once. Preview deployments get their own URLs, so each preview origin needs an entry, or use one stable staging origin. The SDK check accepts a `*` entry as matching, but a wildcard is a security choice you make, not something this kit recommends.

### Google

For the default Privy-managed Google login, enabling the Socials toggle is all the setup. If you use a custom Google OAuth client (your own client id, redirect URL and consent screen), register the redirect URI the dashboard shows and publish the consent screen before real users arrive.

### Embedded wallets and the creation setting

Turn embedded wallets on for Ethereum. `createPepuPrivyConfig` sets `createOnLogin: "off"` and `WalletGate` calls `createEnsureWalletRoute()` right after login; with the dashboard creation setting off, Privy's own client-side creation hangs, which was reproduced live. Having the dashboard setting on and the server route in place is fine.

### TEE execution mode

TEE (`user-controlled-server-wallets-only`) reassembles wallets inside a secure enclave that only Privy can invoke, gated by the user's session. The legacy mode reassembles on the device. The live tests ran with TEE. Whether TEE is a requirement for anything here is **unverified**; only that setting has been proven.

### Smart Wallets (Privy transport only)

Smart Wallets is Path 2 in [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md). If you are unsure whether you need it, read that page first: most apps (anything with sessions, the free tier or a server) use Path 1 and leave this off.

**Required** for `sponsored-demo`, which uses Privy Smart Wallets. **Not required** for `sponsored-session-app` or any other template: the SDK builds the ZeroDev Kernel account itself. Leaving Smart wallets enabled is harmless there; users then also get a Privy smart wallet linked to their account, which the paymaster also accepts as owned by the user.

For `sponsored-demo` configure, under Wallets, Smart wallets (or Settings, Wallet infrastructure, Smart wallets in older layouts):

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Provider | Kernel (ZeroDev) v3.1 |
| Custom chain | PEPU, chain id `97741`, RPC `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Bundler URL | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` |
| Paymaster URL | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project CLIENT token ppt_...>` |

Use the project **client token** (`ppt_`) and add your app's origins to the project's allowed origins, because Privy calls the URL from the browser. Never put the server key (`ppk_`) in the dashboard. The free tier cannot be used on this path: the dashboard URL is static and carries no per-user Privy token, so you need a funded project of your own (claim, set targets and limits, deposit, register). Without both URLs the page cannot sponsor anything. Old dashboards may still hold temporary development bundler or paymaster URLs (for example tunnels); replace them with the hosted ones above. See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md).

### Paymaster credentials by template

| Template | Credential | Where | Secret? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sponsored-demo` | Project client token `ppt_` | Inside the paymaster URL in the Privy dashboard | No, but only works from the allowed origins |
| `sponsored-session-app` | Project server key `ppk_` in `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `.env.local`, server only | Yes |
| Others | None | | |

Sponsorship is project first, then the free tier as a fallback when the project cannot cover an operation. The free tier (100 PEPU/day and 50 PEPU/hour per user, TapScore only for now) needs the user's Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app; the SDK combination routes forward the signed-in user's token automatically, and it is ignored for project billing unless the service can verify it.

### Per-template requirements

| Template | Env vars | Login methods in code | Smart wallets | Extra |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `consumer-app` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (public), `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` (secret) | email, google, wallet | Off | Coinbase `eoaOnly` pinned in code |
| `token-gated-app` | same | email, google, wallet | Off | `eoaOnly` pinned |
| `nft-mint` | same | email, google, wallet | Off | `eoaOnly` pinned |
| `game-app` | same, plus `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` (secret), `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (public id) | email, google, wallet | Off | Authorization key and key quorum |
| `sponsored-demo` | same as `consumer-app` | google, email | Required (above) | Client token in the dashboard URL |
| `sponsored-session-app` | same as `consumer-app`, plus `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (secret), `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | google, email | Not required | Server key in env |

Every template also needs Allowed origins (exact origin with port, plus production) and embedded wallets for Ethereum with creation on login. Each template's `.env.example` carries the same checklist as comments. Find the App ID and App Secret under Settings, Basics. The authorization key pair comes from `npm run generate-authorization-key` in `game-app`; the quorum id is shown after you register the public key.

### Authorization keys, key quorums, policies and TTL

See [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](authorization-keys.md). Policies are not dashboard fields: the SDK creates them per grant through the API. Policy and rule names must be at most 49 characters (`PRIVY_POLICY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`); Privy's live validator says fewer than 50 although its OpenAPI spec says 50. The session TTL is `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` (default 15, clamped to 1 to 1440), baked into the policy's expiry condition.

### Access tokens

Nothing to configure for JWT verification. `verifyRequestUser` verifies the bearer token against Privy with your App ID and App Secret. A verification failure caused by a secret from a different app looks exactly like an expired session, so check the secret first.

## Verify

```ts
import { checkPrivyDashboardConfig } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";
const r = await checkPrivyDashboardConfig({ appId, origin: "http://localhost:3000" });
```

Or the `pepu_check_privy_config` MCP tool. See [Privy Env Vars and Verification](env-and-checks.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login fails, iframe blocked, OAuth 403 | Origin or port missing | Allowed origins |
| No Google button | Google off in the dashboard | Socials, Google |
| "Creating your wallet..." forever | Custom provider with creation off | `PepuPrivyProvider`, `WalletGate` |
| 401 "No valid authorization keys..." | Quorum id and private key from different keys | Realign; users re-grant |
| "Setting up your smart wallet..." forever | Smart Wallets not set for 97741 | Add chain, Kernel, both URLs |
| Everything `unknown` in the check | Privy's public config did not report fields, or the app id is wrong | Not a failure; verify by hand |

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: which one needs Smart Wallets](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Privy Configuration Overview](index.md)
- [Privy Setup Walkthrough](../onboarding/privy-setup.md)
- [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](authorization-keys.md)
- [Privy Env Vars and Verification](env-and-checks.md)

# Authorization Keys and Key Quorums

The authorization key is the credential your server uses to ask Privy to sign for a user's wallet under a session grant. This page covers what it authorizes, how to generate it without printing the private half, how to register it, where it is read and how to rotate it. It applies to Privy session signers only; Kernel sessions use no authorization key.

## Prerequisites

- Pillar 1 working. See [Social Login and Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md).
- Access to the Privy dashboard for the app.

## What it authorizes

Privy requires that a signing request for a delegated wallet be authorized by the key quorum the user granted as a signer. Your server signs each `eth_signTransaction` request with the private half (`PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`); Privy checks it, then evaluates the policy attached to the grant. So the key is a production signing credential: anyone holding it can request transactions for any wallet that granted a signer to its quorum, bounded only by the attached policy (one contract, listed functions, zero value, expiry). Gas is not bounded. It is a server secret: never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, never committed, never logged.

## Generate

Three ways, all producing a P-256 pair in Privy's format (base64 SPKI public, base64 PKCS8 private, no PEM headers):

| Way | How |
|---|---|
| Template script | `npm run generate-authorization-key` in `game-app` |
| SDK | `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey()` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor`. Returns `{ publicKey, privateKey }`; it writes and logs nothing |
| MCP | `pepu_generate_authorization_key` with an absolute `.env.local` path and `confirm_write: true`. It writes the private half to the env file and returns only the public key and a fingerprint; it refuses to replace an existing key unless `overwrite: true` |

```ts
import { generatePrivyAuthorizationKey } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor";
const { publicKey, privateKey } = await generatePrivyAuthorizationKey();
// Show publicKey. Write privateKey straight to .env.local. Never print it.
```

## Register the public key and create the quorum

Menu labels may drift.

1. Privy dashboard, Controls (Wallet infrastructure), Authorization keys, **New key**. Paste the public key.
2. Create a **key quorum** containing that key.
3. Copy the key quorum id into `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`. It is an identifier, not a secret: Privy's own client-side `addSigners` examples pass it from browser code.

## Env vars and where they are read

| Variable | Scope | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Server, secret | `privySessionSigner` and `createSessionActionRoute` (`/session/server`), through `privyEnvVar`. Never given to the Privy client; Privy takes it per request |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (alias `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`) | Public | `createSessionRoutes` (grant returns it as `signerId`) |

The SDK's server entries refuse to load in a browser bundle. Check presence with `pepu_check_env` or `npm run doctor`; both report presence and length only.

## Rotation and revocation

- Rotate if the private key leaks: generate a new pair, register it, create a new quorum, update both env vars, redeploy. Sessions granted under the old quorum stop working, so users must grant again.
- To end one user's session, the browser calls `removeSigners` (`useSessionRevoke`). After it resolves your backend can no longer sign for that wallet.
- Delete a retired key and its quorum in the dashboard.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 401 "No valid authorization keys or user signing keys available" (`PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH`) | The private key is not the half of a key in the quorum named by `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`, or the user granted a different quorum | Realign the pair; grant again |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` naming `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Unset on the server, or the dev server was not restarted | Set it and restart |
| Grant works but signing is denied | The policy rejected the call, or it expired | See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md) |

## Related

- [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](dashboard-settings.md)
- [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md)
- [/doctor](../sdk/doctor.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/privy/env-and-checks

# Privy Env Vars and Verification

The Privy environment variables, and the three ways to verify a Privy setup: `checkPrivyDashboardConfig`, the `pepu_check_privy_config` MCP tool and `npm run doctor`. Use it when login, wallets or sessions fail with a config error.

The dashboard check calls Privy's public app-config endpoint. Every field is treated as optional and reports `unknown` when absent, never a false failure.

## Prerequisites

- `.env.local` in the project, and the Privy App ID (public).

## Env vars

| Variable | Scope | Read by | Needed for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (alias `PRIVY_APP_ID`) | Public | Provider, `createPrivyServer`, doctor | Everything |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Server, secret | `/privy/server`, `/session/server`, `/combo` | Everything with a server route |
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Server, secret | `/session/server` | Privy sessions |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (alias `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`) | Public | `createSessionRoutes` | Privy sessions |

The canonical names are `PRIVY_ENV`; aliases are read only when the canonical name is empty. The full cross-component list is [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md).

## Run the checks

### `npm run doctor`

Every template has a `doctor` script that runs the SDK's `checkPepuEnv` against `.env.local` for that template's requirements. It prints `ok` or `FAIL` per key with a fix, never a value, and exits non-zero on failure. It checks env only, not the dashboard.

```
FAIL PRIVY_APP_SECRET - Set PRIVY_APP_SECRET in .env.local to the app secret from the Privy dashboard (server only).
```

Statuses per key: `ok`, `missing`, `placeholder` (for example `your-app-id`) and `malformed` (the Privy id must look like `c` plus 20 to 29 lowercase alphanumerics; addresses must be 20-byte hex; URLs must be http or https; `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` must be positive).

### The full doctor

`runDoctor` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor` adds the Privy app id format, the RPC chain id (97741), bundler and paymaster reachability, and, when you inject the checker, the dashboard rows:

```ts
import { runDoctor } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor";
import { privyDashboardChecker } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";

const report = await runDoctor({
  env: process.env,
  template: "sponsored-session-app",
  checkPrivyDashboard: privyDashboardChecker,
});
for (const c of report.checks.filter((c) => c.status !== "pass")) console.log(c.id, c.status, c.fix);
```

Check ids: `env.<NAME>`, `privy.app-id`, `chain.rpc`, `sponsorship.bundler`, `sponsorship.paymaster`, `privy.<requirement key>`. Statuses are `pass`, `fail`, `warn` and `skip`. A bundler or paymaster URL that is unset is a skip; set but unreachable is a fail. `runDoctor` does not pass an origin, so `privy.allowed-origins` comes back a warning. Use the next two for the origin.

### `checkPrivyDashboardConfig`

```ts
import { checkPrivyDashboardConfig } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";
const r = await checkPrivyDashboardConfig({ appId, origin: "http://localhost:3000" });
// r.ok is false only if a REQUIRED row definitely failed
for (const i of r.items) console.log(i.id, i.ok, i.detail, i.fix);
```

It never throws and needs no secret. Each item is `true`, `false` or `"unknown"`. Rows: `allowed-origins`, `login-methods`, `login-methods.google`, `embedded-wallets`, `smart-wallets`. Env and code rows (`app-id`, `app-secret`, `coinbase-eoa-only`, `authorization-key-quorum`) are in `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` but cannot be checked remotely.

### `pepu_check_privy_config`

The MCP tool wraps the same function: inputs `appId`, optional `origin` (with port) and optional `pillars` (`login`, `session`, `sponsor`). It returns `dashboard` rows with `pass`, `fail` or `unknown` and a fix, plus `notRemotelyCheckable` rows. Needs network access to `auth.privy.io`. Pair it with `pepu_check_env`, and use `/pepu-doctor` to run both.

## Reading the output

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| pass | Verified from Privy's public config |
| fail | Definitely wrong; apply the `fix` |
| unknown or warn | Privy did not report it, or the origin was not given. Not a failure; verify by hand |
| skip | Not applicable (env or code rows, or no URL configured) |

## Common failures mapped to dashboard fields

| Check failing | Dashboard field | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `allowed-origins` | Allowed origins | Add the exact origin with port |
| `login-methods` | Login methods | Enable the methods in `loginMethods` |
| `login-methods.google` | Socials, Google | Turn Google on |
| `embedded-wallets` | Embedded wallets | Turn on for Ethereum |
| `smart-wallets` | Smart Wallets | Chain 97741, Kernel, both URLs (Privy transport only) |
| `env.PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, quorum | Authorization keys | [Authorization Keys](authorization-keys.md) |
| `privy.app-id` format | Settings, Basics | Use the App ID, not the secret or client id |

## Related

- [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](dashboard-settings.md)
- [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md)
- [/doctor](../sdk/doctor.md), [/privy](../sdk/privy.md)
- [MCP Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/reference

# `@pepu-chain/sdk` Reference

`@pepu-chain/sdk` supplies what viem does not know about Pepe Unchained V2 (chain 97741) and the infrastructure that makes the three pillars work: Google to wallet, session keys and sponsored transactions, plus their combination. It extends viem and never wraps or re-exports viem's own API. This page is the index: install, the subpath map, which subpath serves which pillar, peer dependencies and the server and client boundary. Each subpath has its own page.

Version 0.2.4. The hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster service (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) are the SDK defaults; sponsorship needs a project token in the ERC-7677 URL (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` or `paymasterToken`). The v1 paymaster is retired.

## Install

```sh
npm install @pepu-chain/sdk viem
```

`viem` (`^2.0.0`) is the only required peer dependency. Every other peer is optional and needed only by the subpaths that use it. The core entry never touches React, Privy or ZeroDev and runs in a plain Node script.

```ts
import { pepuMainnet, getPublicClient } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const client = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);
console.log(await client.getBlockNumber());
```

## Pillar-to-subpath decision table

| You want | Use | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Chain, contract registry, ABIs, gas, explorer links, Multicall3, Permit2, errors | `@pepu-chain/sdk` | [Core](core.md) |
| Google sign-in config, requirements table, dashboard check | `/privy` | [/privy](privy.md) |
| Provider, embedded-wallet hook, wallet gate (React, no wagmi) | `/privy/react` | [/privy/react](privy-react.md) |
| The same with wagmi | `/privy/wagmi` | [/privy/wagmi](privy-wagmi.md) |
| Ensure-wallet route, verify the Privy token | `/privy/server` | [/privy/server](privy-server.md) |
| Session keys, Privy mode (off-chain scope, user pays gas): routes, signer, hooks | `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react` | [/session](session.md) |
| Session keys, on-chain scope (Kernel permissions) | `/session/kernel` | [/session/kernel](session-kernel.md) |
| Sponsored transactions: bundler and paymaster clients, Kernel account, hooks | `/aa`, `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react`, `/aa/react-direct` | [/aa](aa.md) |
| Paymaster REST client, v2 project helpers, denial mapping | `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server` | [/paymaster](paymaster.md) |
| Google login plus on-chain session plus sponsored gas, ready-made routes and hook | `/combo`, `/combo/react` | [/combo](combo.md) |
| Project readiness checks, authorization key generator | `/doctor` | [/doctor](doctor.md) |
| Basic React hooks (balance, chain) | `/react` | [Core](core.md) |

The three pillars map to subpaths like this:

| Pillar | Client | Server |
|---|---|---|
| Google to wallet | `/privy/react` or `/privy/wagmi` | `/privy/server` |
| Session keys | `/session/react`, or `/session/kernel` with `/combo/react` | `/session/server`, or `/combo` |
| Sponsored transactions | `/aa/react`, `/aa/kernel` | `/aa`, `/paymaster` |
| All three | `/combo/react` | `/combo` |

Every export of every path is listed in the [Generated API Reference](api-reference.md). Error codes are in the [SDK Error Catalog](errors.md).

## Subpath map and peer dependencies

| Import path | Runs in | Required peers beyond `viem` |
|---|---|---|
| `@pepu-chain/sdk` | client or server | none |
| `/react` | client | `react` |
| `/privy` | client or server | none |
| `/privy/react` | client | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth` |
| `/privy/wagmi` | client (ESM only) | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@privy-io/wagmi`, `wagmi`, `@tanstack/react-query` |
| `/privy/server` | server only | `@privy-io/node` |
| `/session` | client or server | none |
| `/session/server` | server only | `@privy-io/node` |
| `/session/react` | client | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth` |
| `/session/kernel` | mixed | `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |
| `/aa` | client or server | none |
| `/aa/kernel` | client or server | `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |
| `/aa/react` | client | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `permissionless` (no `@zerodev/*`) |
| `/aa/react-direct` | client | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |
| `/paymaster` | client or server | none |
| `/paymaster/server` | server only | none |
| `/combo` | server only | `@privy-io/node` and the three `@zerodev/*` packages |
| `/combo/react` | client | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth` and the three `@zerodev/*` packages |
| `/server` | server only | none |
| `/doctor` | server or script | none |

Peer ranges: `viem ^2.0.0`, `react ^18 || ^19`, `@privy-io/react-auth ^3.44.0`, `@privy-io/node ^0.34.0`, `@privy-io/wagmi ^4.0.0`, `wagmi ^3.0.0`, `@tanstack/react-query ^5.0.0`, `@zerodev/sdk ^5.5.0`, `@zerodev/permissions ^5.6.0`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator ^5.4.0`. A test (`boundaries.test.ts`) enforces that each peer is imported only from its own subpaths, so a subpath you do not import never pulls its peers into your bundle.

## Install: peers per subpath

Every subpath also needs `viem`. The entries below need extra peers, and **the recommended path is the CLI: `create-pepu-app` scaffolds an app with every peer already in its `package.json`**, so you never run these by hand. If you install by hand and a peer is missing, importing the subpath throws `PEPU_MISSING_PEER` naming the subpath and the exact command (under Node; bundlers report their own "module not found"). Subpaths not listed here (`.`, `/privy`, `/session`, `/aa`, `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server`, `/server`, `/doctor`) need only `viem`.

| Subpath | Required peers | Install |
|---|---|---|
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/react` | `react`, `react-dom` | `npm i react react-dom` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react` | `react`, `react-dom`, `@privy-io/react-auth` | `npm i react react-dom @privy-io/react-auth` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi` | `react`, `react-dom`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@privy-io/wagmi`, `wagmi`, `@tanstack/react-query` | `npm i react react-dom @privy-io/react-auth @privy-io/wagmi wagmi @tanstack/react-query` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server` | `@privy-io/node` | `npm i @privy-io/node` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/server` | `@privy-io/node` | `npm i @privy-io/node` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/react` | `react`, `react-dom`, `@privy-io/react-auth` | `npm i react react-dom @privy-io/react-auth` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel` | `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` | `npm i @zerodev/sdk @zerodev/permissions @zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel` | `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` | `npm i @zerodev/sdk @zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react` | `react`, `react-dom`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `permissionless` | `npm i react react-dom @privy-io/react-auth permissionless` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct` | `react`, `react-dom`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` | `npm i react react-dom @privy-io/react-auth @zerodev/sdk @zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/combo` | `@privy-io/node`, `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` | `npm i @privy-io/node @zerodev/sdk @zerodev/permissions @zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/combo/react` | `react`, `react-dom`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` | `npm i react react-dom @privy-io/react-auth @zerodev/sdk @zerodev/permissions @zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |

**Bundle** for the common pillars (Google login + session keys + sponsored gas), client and server together:

```sh
npm i viem react react-dom @privy-io/react-auth @privy-io/node @zerodev/sdk @zerodev/permissions @zerodev/ecdsa-validator permissionless
```

**If npm stops with `ERESOLVE`.** `@privy-io/react-auth` pins an exact `viem` peer, and a newer `viem` (2.57.x with `ox` 0.14.x) can conflict with it. Tell npm to use your one `viem` everywhere by adding this to your `package.json` (the `create-pepu-app` templates already do), then re-run the install:

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "viem": "^2.57.7" },
  "overrides": { "viem": "$viem" }
}
```

Or from a shell: `npm pkg set 'overrides.viem=$viem'`. Do not use `--force` or `--legacy-peer-deps`. Verified in a clean directory: `npm i @pepu-chain/sdk viem`, the override above, then `npm i react react-dom @privy-io/react-auth` gives no warnings, and `import("@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react")` resolves.

## Server and client boundary

Five entries are **server only**: `/privy/server`, `/session/server`, `/paymaster/server`, `/combo` and `/server`. Each calls `assertServerOnly()` at import and throws `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` if `window` exists, so a mistake in a client bundle fails loudly instead of shipping a module that sits next to secrets.

Rules that follow:

- The Privy app secret (`PRIVY_APP_SECRET`), the authorization key (`PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`) and the paymaster claim attestation call exist only on the server and are never read from a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` are public by nature.
- `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` can embed a credential. Keep it server-side unless it holds a publishable client token (`ppt_`). A server key (`ppk_`) in a browser is refused with `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY`.
- The Kernel session private key is created on the server (`generateSessionKey`) and never sent to the browser. The browser signs one owner message with `approveKernelSession` and sends back an approval that carries no secret.
- Never embed a private key in a browser bundle. Scripts read keys from the environment.

## Conventions

- Named exports only. There is no default export.
- Anything the SDK throws is a `PepuError` subclass with `code`, `hint`, `docsUrl`, `retryable` and `status`. See [Core](core.md#error-model).
- Mainnet only. `pepuTestnet` (97740) is a definition with no deployed contracts and is out of scope. Chain `3409` is the dead V1 chain.
- Hosted endpoint URLs live in one place, `src/endpoints.ts`. The hosted bundler and paymaster base are set there; the environment variables override them.

## Known gaps

- **Deposits to the v2 paymaster are one-way;** deposit only what your project needs.
- **`v3Migrator` and `v3Staker` have verified addresses but no ABI** in the package.
- **The token list has two tokens**, WPEPU and USDT.
- **The deprecated `getSponsorshipStatus`** always reports unavailable. See [Migration Notes](migration.md).

## Related

- [Generated API Reference](api-reference.md)
- [SDK Error Catalog](errors.md)
- [Migration Notes](migration.md)
- [The Three Pillars and How They Combine](../get-started/pillars.md)
- [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md)
