Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/core

# Core: @pepu-chain/sdk

The core entry of `@pepu-chain/sdk`: chain definitions, the contract and DEX registries, ABIs, gas helpers, explorer links, Multicall3 and Permit2 helpers, the error model, endpoint resolution, ERC-7677 request builders and the live sponsorship check. It extends viem and never wraps it. Read this page first, then the subpath page for the pillar you are building.

Every registry address is checked against mainnet with `eth_getCode` (`live-check`). The sponsorship pieces (`checkSponsorship`, the ERC-7677 builders) target the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and the hosted paymaster service (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) by default.

## Install and peer dependencies

```sh
npm install @pepu-chain/sdk viem
```

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Import | `@pepu-chain/sdk` |
| Runs in | Browser, Node, edge. No `react`, no Privy, no ZeroDev |
| Peer dependencies | `viem` `^2.0.0` only |
| Server or client | Client-safe |
| Chain | PEPU mainnet, chain ID `97741`. `pepuTestnet` (`97740`) exists as a definition only and is out of scope |

## Chains and clients

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `pepuMainnet` | viem `Chain` | Chain `97741`, RPC, PepuScan explorer, and `contracts.multicall3` set to PEPU's own address, so viem and wagmi batch correctly |
| `pepuTestnet`, `pepuChains` | viem `Chain`, array | Testnet definition, no explorer, no deployed contracts |
| `isPepuChain` | `(chainId: number) => chainId is 97741 \| 97740` | Narrowing guard |
| `PepuChain`, `PepuChainId` | types | Chain object and ID union |
| `getPublicClient` | `(chain: PepuChain, options?: { transport?: Transport }) => PublicClient<Transport, PepuChain>` | `createPublicClient` with the chain's own RPC |
| `toAddEthereumChainParameter` | `(chain: PepuChain) => AddEthereumChainParameter` | The `wallet_addEthereumChain` payload with correct hex chain ID |
| `switchOrAddPepuChain` | `(provider: EIP1193Provider, chain: PepuChain) => Promise<void>` | Switch, then add on error `4902` (viem's `switchChain` does not add) |

## Contract and DEX registries

| Export | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pepuContracts` | registry keyed by chain ID | Names: `create2Factory`, `multicall3`, `permit2`, `entryPoint06`, `entryPoint07`, `kernelFactory`, `kernelMetaFactory`, `ecdsaValidator`, `paymaster`, `kernelImplementation`, `kernelEcdsaSignerModule`, `kernelCallPolicyV004`, `kernelTimestampPolicy`, `tapScore`, `paymasterV1`, `paymasterV2` |
| `getContract` | `(chainId: number, name: PepuContractName) => ContractEntry \| undefined` | Pending entries have no `address` field |
| `listContracts` | `(chainId: number) => readonly ContractEntry[]` | Registry order |
| `isDeployed` | `(entry: ContractEntry \| undefined) => entry is DeployedContract` | Narrow before reading `.address` |
| `getPepuAddresses` | `(chainId?: number) => readonly PepuAddressRow[]` | Flat table for docs and UIs. Returns an **array of rows** (each has a `key`), not an object: use `.find((r) => r.key === "paymaster")`, or `getPepuAddressMap()` |
| `getPepuAddressMap` | `(chainId?: number) => Partial<Record<PepuContractName, PepuAddressRow>>` | The same rows keyed by contract name |
| `pepuSwapContracts`, `getPepuSwapContract`, `listPepuSwapContracts` | PepuSwap registry | `multicallNonCanonical` and `permit2NonCanonical` are PepuSwap's own deployments, not the chain's |
| `pepuTokenList` | Uniswap token-list schema | Four verified tokens: WPEPU (18 decimals), USDT (6), USDC (6) and WETH (18) |
| `createPepuscanClient` | `(chain) => PepuscanClient` | `getVerifiedAbi(address)` and `getTokenMetadata(address)`, both `null` when unknown |

`paymasterV2` and its alias `paymaster` are the v2 paymaster `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`, deployed. Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs. `paymasterV1` (`0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0`) is retired: its EntryPoint deposit was withdrawn, it cannot sponsor anything, and its registry entry carries `retired: true` (so do `getPepuAddresses()` rows). Never deposit to it. A `deployed` registry entry answers "does this contract exist", never "can my app get sponsored gas". Use `checkSponsorship` for that.

Full addresses are in [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md).

## ABIs

Hand-verified subsets, only functions confirmed live: `wpepuAbi`, `pepuSwapV3FactoryAbi`, `pepuSwapV3PoolAbi`, `pepuSwapRouterAbi`, `pepuSwapQuoterAbi`, `pepuSwapPositionManagerAbi`, `pepuSwapTickLensAbi`, `pepuSwapUniversalRouterAbi`, `pepuSwapPermit2Abi`, `pepuSwapMulticallAbi`, `multicall3Abi`, `permit2Abi`, `arbGasInfoAbi` (with `ARB_GAS_INFO_ADDRESS`), `entryPointV07Abi`, `kernelFactoryAbi` (with `KERNEL_V3_1_IMPLEMENTATION_ADDRESS`), `kernelEcdsaValidatorAbi` (with `ERC7579_MODULE_TYPE`), and viem's `erc20Abi` and `erc721Abi` re-exported so apps import every ABI from one place.

## Gas and fees

PEPU is an Arbitrum Nitro chain. The L2 base fee is about 12,500 gwei and PEPU is a low-value token, so Ethereum-style formatting misleads in both directions.

| Export | Signature |
|---|---|
| `getNitroFeeBreakdown` | `(client) => Promise<NitroFeeBreakdown>` live from the `ArbGasInfo` precompile |
| `explainDualFeeModel` | `() => DualFeeModelExplanation` |
| `estimateTransactionCost` | `(client, request) => Promise<TransactionCostEstimate>` with `gas`, `gasPriceWei`, `costWei`, `costFormatted` |
| `formatPepu` | `(wei: bigint, options?: FormatPepuOptions) => string` (`0.00000001 PEPU`, never `0 PEPU`) |
| `formatPepuGasPrice` | `(weiPerGas: bigint) => string` |
| `formatUnitsCompact` | `(value: bigint, decimals: number, maxFractionDigits = 4) => string` for any token |
| `maxSendableAmount` | `(options: MaxSendableAmountOptions) => Promise<MaxSendableAmountResult>` discriminated on `status`: `ok`, `zero-balance`, `insufficient-for-gas` |
| `DEFAULT_MAX_SEND_MARGIN_BPS` | `2000` (20 percent) |

`maxSendableAmount` is right for a UI that submits transactions itself. Privy's own transaction modal runs a separate, over-conservative balance check and can still refuse an amount this function sized correctly.

## Explorer links

| Export | Signature |
|---|---|
| `explorerUrl` | `(chain, type: "tx" \| "address" \| "token" \| "block", value: string \| number) => string` |
| `txUrl`, `addressUrl`, `tokenUrl`, `blockUrl` | shorthands |
| `explorerLinks` | `(o: { tx?, address?, sender?, token?, block? }, chain = pepuMainnet) => { tx?, address?, sender?, token?, block? }` |

`explorerUrl` throws for a chain with no explorer (`pepuTestnet`). pepuscan has no UserOperation pages, so a sponsored operation is linked by its bundle `tx` and its `sender`. Recipe: [Explorer Links](../recipes/explorer-links.md).

## Multicall3 and Permit2

| Export | Signature | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `getMulticall3` | `(chainId = 97741) => DeployedContract` | `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` if the registry ever held the canonical address, `UNKNOWN` if not deployed on that chain |
| `assertNotCanonicalMulticall3` | `(address) => void` | `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` |
| `pepuMulticall` | `(client, calls, { allowFailure?, blockNumber? }) => Promise<MulticallReturnType>` | as `getMulticall3` |
| `encodeAggregate3`, `decodeAggregate3Result` | encode and decode `aggregate3` | none |
| `CANONICAL_MULTICALL3_ADDRESS` | `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` | It has no code on PEPU. PEPU's is `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` |
| `getPermit2`, `permit2Domain` | canonical Permit2 entry and its EIP-712 domain (`name: "Permit2"`, no version) | `UNKNOWN` if not deployed |
| `buildPermitSingleTypedData`, `buildPermitTransferFromTypedData` | typed data for viem `signTypedData` | none |
| `readPermit2Allowance` | `(client, { owner, token, spender }) => Promise<{ amount, expiration, nonce }>` | none |

See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md) and [Permit2](../contracts/permit2.md). Recipes: [Batch Reads with Multicall3](../recipes/batch-reads-with-multicall3.md), [Sign a Permit2 Permit](../recipes/permit2-permit.md).

## Error model

Everything the SDK throws is a `PepuError` with a stable `code`, a one-sentence `hint`, a `docsUrl`, a `retryable` flag and an HTTP `status` for route handlers. Messages name environment variables, never their values.

| Export | Signature |
|---|---|
| `PepuError` and subclasses `PepuConfigError`, `PepuAuthError`, `PepuPolicyError`, `PepuSessionError`, `PepuBundlerError`, `PepuPaymasterError`, `PepuChainError` | `new PepuError(code, message?, { hint?, docsUrl?, retryable?, status?, details?, cause? })` |
| `explainError` | `(e: unknown) => ErrorExplanation` pure, never throws; also decodes raw revert data (`0x...`) |
| `toPepuError` | `(e: unknown, ctx?: { op: string }) => PepuError` |
| `toErrorBody`, `toErrorResponse` | `{ error: { code, message, hint } }` and a JSON `Response` with the catalog status |
| `getErrorEntry`, `errorDocsUrl`, `PEPU_ERROR_CATALOG`, `PEPU_ERRORS_DOCS_URL` | The catalog the MCP tool `pepu_explain_error` also reads |

The constructor is positional: the code first, then an optional message, then an options object (`throw new PepuError("CONFIG_MISSING_ENV", "PEPU_BUNDLER_URL is not set.", { hint: "Set it in .env.local." })`). There is no `{ code, message }` object form.

The full code list is in [SDK Error Catalog](errors.md). Snippet: `docs/snippets/errors.ts`.

```ts
// The SDK error model. See docs/sdk/core.md and docs/sdk/errors.md
import { PepuError, explainError, toErrorResponse, toPepuError } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

export async function handler(run: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<Response> {
  try {
    return Response.json(await run());
  } catch (e) {
    // { error: { code, message, hint } } with the status from the catalog.
    return toErrorResponse(e);
  }
}

export function describe(e: unknown): string {
  if (e instanceof PepuError) return `${e.code}: ${e.hint}`;
  const explained = explainError(e);
  return `${explained.code}: ${explained.fix}`;
}

export function retryable(e: unknown): boolean {
  return toPepuError(e, { op: "send" }).retryable;
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/errors.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Endpoints

```ts
resolvePepuEndpoints(options?: { bundlerUrl?, paymasterUrl?, rpcUrl?, env? }): PepuEndpoints
// { rpcUrl: string; bundlerUrl: string | null; paymasterBaseUrl: string | null; paymasterUrl: string | null; source: "explicit" | "env" | "hosted-default" }
```

Precedence per value: explicit option, then env (the server name, then the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` name), then `PEPU_HOSTED`. Names are in `PEPU_ENV` (`PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, `PEPU_RPC_URL`) and `PEPU_PUBLIC_ENV` (the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variants). `PEPU_HOSTED` is the single swap point: `{ bundlerUrl: "https://bundler.pepeunchained.com", paymasterBaseUrl: "https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com", paymasterUrl: null }`. `isHostedSponsorshipLive()` is `true`. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a project token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`), so there is no tokenless default and `paymasterUrl` stays `null` until you set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` or pass an option. `paymasterBaseUrl` is the paymaster service base (REST API, probes, `/v2/free-tier`): the hosted base, unless `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` is set, in which case it is that URL with the `/v2/paymaster/<token>` tail stripped. For your own services (for example local development) point the variables at `http://localhost:4337` (bundler) and `http://localhost:8788` (paymaster). A malformed value throws `CONFIG_BAD_URL` naming the variable, never the value.

Helpers: `paymasterBaseOf(url)` strips a trailing `/v2/paymaster/<token>` (or `/paymaster/<token>`) and slashes, leaving the service base. `hostedErc7677Url(token)` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`) returns `<hosted base>/v2/paymaster/<token>`; pass a project client token (`ppt_`). `hostedFreeTierUrl()` returns the public `GET` free-tier state route, `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/free-tier`. `buildErc7677Url({ baseUrl, token, version })` builds the URL against any base. `requirePaymasterUrl(explicit?, token?)` (from `/aa`) resolves the complete ERC-7677 URL in the order explicit URL, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, then `token` built against the paymaster base, and otherwise throws `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV`.

A paymaster URL can embed a credential. Treat `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` as a secret and never expose it with a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` name unless it holds a publishable client token (`ppt_`).

## Sponsorship status and ERC-7677 builders

| Export | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `checkSponsorship` | `(options?: CheckSponsorshipOptions) => Promise<SponsorshipReport>` | Probes the bundler and paymaster live. Never throws for an unreachable service. Fields: `available`, `transport`, `bundler`, `paymaster`, `reason`, `fixes` |
| `getSponsorshipStatus` | `(options?) => SponsorshipStatus` | Deprecated. Always `{ available: false }`. See [Migration Notes](migration.md) |
| `getPepuKernelStack` | `(chainId: number) => PepuKernelStack \| undefined` | The five Kernel contracts, `undefined` unless all are deployed |
| `getKernelAccountAddress` | `(client, factory, { data, salt }) => Promise<Address>` | Pass-through to the factory's `getAddress`. Build `data` with `@zerodev/sdk` or use `toPepuKernelAccount` |
| `buildPaymasterContext` | `(entries?) => PaymasterContext` | For example `{ privyAccessToken }` |
| `buildPaymasterStubDataRequest`, `buildPaymasterDataRequest` | `(options: BuildPaymasterRequestOptions) => request` | ERC-7677 JSON-RPC bodies for chain 97741 and EntryPoint v0.7 |

`checkSponsorship` is also exported from `/aa`. The page [/aa](aa.md) has the sponsored-send flow. Snippet: `docs/snippets/check-sponsorship.ts`.

```ts
// Live sponsorship status and the endpoint resolver. See docs/sdk/core.md and docs/sdk/aa.md
import { PEPU_ENV, checkSponsorship, getPublicClient, pepuMainnet, resolvePepuEndpoints } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

export async function report(): Promise<void> {
  const { bundlerUrl, paymasterBaseUrl, paymasterUrl, source } = resolvePepuEndpoints();
  // The hosted bundler and paymaster service are the defaults. paymasterUrl (the complete ERC-7677 URL)
  // stays null until you set PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL, because that URL embeds a project token
  // (names only below: values can embed credentials).
  console.log(PEPU_ENV.bundlerUrl, bundlerUrl !== null, paymasterBaseUrl !== null, PEPU_ENV.paymasterUrl, paymasterUrl !== null, source);

  const s = await checkSponsorship({ publicClient: getPublicClient(pepuMainnet) });
  console.log(s.available, s.reason);
  for (const fix of s.fixes) console.log(`- ${fix}`);
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/check-sponsorship.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `explorerUrl: no block explorer is configured` | You passed `pepuTestnet` | Use `pepuMainnet`. Testnet has no explorer |
| `TS2339: Property 'address' does not exist on type 'ContractEntry'` | You skipped `isDeployed` | Narrow with `isDeployed(entry)` first |
| Multicall returns empty data | A hand-written chain definition uses the canonical Multicall3 | Use `pepuMainnet` or `pepuMulticall` |
| `CONFIG_BAD_URL` | A set `PEPU_*_URL` is not an `http(s)` URL | Fix the variable the message names |
| `checkSponsorship` says no URL is configured | A variable was cleared, or the paymaster has no token | The hosted bundler and paymaster service are the defaults. Set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` (or pass a token), or point both variables at your own services |

## Related

- [SDK Overview and Reference](reference.md)
- [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md)
- [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md)

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/privy

# /privy

`@pepu-chain/sdk/privy` is the client-safe Privy layer: the typed `<PrivyProvider>` config for PEPU, the Privy requirements table, and the dashboard checker. It has no dependency on any Privy package, so it runs in the browser, in Node scripts and in the doctor.

The dashboard checker reads Privy's public app-config endpoint, which is undocumented, so anything it cannot read is reported as `unknown`, never as a failure.

## Import, peers and boundary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Import | `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy` |
| Server or client | Client-safe. No secrets, no Node APIs |
| Peer dependencies | None (the config is structurally assignable to `PrivyClientConfig`) |
| Pillar | Google to wallet |

## Exports

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `createPepuPrivyConfig` | `(options?: CreatePepuPrivyConfigOptions) => PepuPrivyClientConfig` | The `config` prop for `<PrivyProvider>`: `defaultChain` and `supportedChains` are PEPU mainnet only, `embeddedWallets.ethereum.createOnLogin` defaults to `"off"`, Coinbase Wallet is pinned to `eoaOnly` |
| `CreatePepuPrivyConfigOptions` | `{ loginMethods?, appearance?, createOnLogin?, chain? }` | `createOnLogin` is `"off" \| "users-without-wallets" \| "all-users"` |
| `PrivyLoginMethod` | `"email" \| "google" \| "wallet" \| "sms" \| "apple" \| "twitter" \| "discord" \| "github"` | |
| `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` | `readonly PrivyRequirement[]` | Everything a PEPU app needs from Privy as one data table. It feeds these docs, the MCP tool `pepu_check_privy_config`, the CLI doctor and in-app notices |
| `PRIVY_ENV`, `PRIVY_ENV_ALIASES` | name maps | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`. Aliases `PRIVY_APP_ID` and `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` are read only when the canonical name is empty |
| `checkPrivyDashboardConfig` | `(o: { appId: string; origin?: string; fetch? }) => Promise<{ ok: boolean; items: PrivyDashboardCheckItem[] }>` | Reads the public app config and checks dashboard rows. Never throws; anything unverifiable is `"unknown"` |
| `privyDashboardChecker` | `(input: { appId; requirementKeys: string[]; appSecret?; fetch; origin? }) => Promise<PrivyDoctorCheck[]>` | Adapter that plugs the dashboard check into [/doctor](doctor.md). `appSecret` is accepted and never used or logged |
| Types | `PepuPrivyClientConfig`, `PrivyRequirement`, `PrivyRequirementResult`, `PrivyPublicAppConfig`, `PrivyDashboardCheckItem`, `PrivyDoctorCheck`, `EmbeddedWalletCreateOnLogin` | |

### The requirements table

Each row has `id`, `where` (`dashboard`, `env` or `code`), `label`, `required`, `pillars` (`login`, `session`, `sponsor`), an optional `check` and a `fix`. The rows today:

| id | where | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|
| `app-id` | env | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` is set |
| `app-secret` | env | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is set (server only) |
| `allowed-origins` | dashboard | The page origin, including the port, is in Allowed origins |
| `login-methods` | dashboard | At least one login method is enabled |
| `login-methods.google` | dashboard | Google login is enabled |
| `embedded-wallets` | dashboard | Embedded wallets are enabled for Ethereum |
| `coinbase-eoa-only` | code | Coinbase Wallet is pinned to `eoaOnly` |
| `authorization-key-quorum` | env | `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` is set and `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` is its quorum id |
| `smart-wallets` | dashboard | Smart wallets are enabled with the bundler and paymaster URLs (Privy transport only) |

The dashboard settings themselves are explained field by field in [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

## Example

```tsx
import { createPepuPrivyConfig, checkPrivyDashboardConfig } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";

export const privyConfig = createPepuPrivyConfig({ loginMethods: ["email", "google", "wallet"] });

const r = await checkPrivyDashboardConfig({ appId, origin: "http://localhost:3001" });
for (const item of r.items.filter((i) => i.ok === false)) console.log(item.id, item.fix);
```

Most apps never call `createPepuPrivyConfig` directly: [/privy/react](privy-react.md)'s `PepuPrivyProvider` and [/privy/wagmi](privy-wagmi.md)'s `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` call it for you.

## Errors

This entry throws nothing for the Privy dashboard. Its codes appear when you map failures:

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD` | A dashboard setting is wrong (surfaced by the doctor and MCP check) |
| `CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN` | The dashboard's wallet-creation setting conflicts with the code value |
| `CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH` | The page origin is not an allowed origin |
| `WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN` | Coinbase Smart Wallet is not pinned to `eoaOnly` |

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The login modal hangs on "Creating your wallet" | The dashboard creates wallets on login and the code value is ignored, because **the dashboard setting wins** | Turn automatic creation off in the dashboard and provision server-side with `createEnsureWalletRoute` |
| Console floods with "configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet" | Coinbase is not `eoaOnly` | Use `createPepuPrivyConfig`, which pins it |
| Origin errors on a new port | The origin with its port is not in Allowed origins | Add `http://localhost:<port>` |

## Related

- [/privy/react](privy-react.md), [/privy/wagmi](privy-wagmi.md), [/privy/server](privy-server.md)
- [Privy Configuration Overview](../privy/index.md)
- [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md)

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/privy-react

# /privy/react

`@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react` is the React layer for Google to wallet: a PEPU-configured Privy provider, the embedded-wallet hook, the server-provisioning gate, the active-wallet pin and an authenticated `fetch`. Use it when you do not need wagmi. With wagmi use [/privy/wagmi](privy-wagmi.md), which builds on this entry.

## Import, peers and boundary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Import | `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react` |
| Server or client | Client only (React) |
| Peer dependencies | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth` `^3.44.0` |
| Pillar | Google to wallet |

## Exports

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `PepuPrivyProvider` | `(props: PepuPrivyProviderProps) => ReactElement` | `<PrivyProvider>` with PEPU mainnet only, Coinbase `eoaOnly`, wallet creation off. Renders `fallback` instead of crashing when `appId` is empty. Props: `appId`, `config?`, `fallback?`, `wrapper?`, `children` |
| `useEmbeddedWallet` | `() => { ready: boolean; wallet: ConnectedWallet \| null; address?: Address; external: ConnectedWallet[] }` | The user's embedded wallet, separated from an installed extension Privy tracks. Uses Privy's own `getEmbeddedConnectedWallet` |
| `useEnsureWallet` | `(o?: { endpoint?; requestTimeoutMs?; appearTimeoutMs? }) => { status: EnsureWalletStatus; address?; error?: PepuError; retry() }` | Provisions the wallet through your ensure route, not Privy's client-side creation, which hangs when the dashboard creation setting is off. `status`: `idle`, `checking`, `creating`, `ready`, `stalled`, `error` |
| `WalletGate` | `(p: { endpoint?; loading?: ReactNode; error?: (e, retry) => ReactNode; stalled?: (address, reload) => ReactNode; children }) => ReactElement` | Renders children once the embedded wallet exists, with a render prop for each of the three non-ready states |
| `requestEnsureWallet` | `(o: { getAccessToken; endpoint?; timeoutMs?; fetch?; signal? }) => Promise<{ address: Address; created: boolean }>` | The bare POST used by the hook. Bounded by a timeout, never leaks the token |
| `usePepuAuthFetch` | `() => (input, init?) => Promise<Response>` | A `fetch` that adds `Authorization: Bearer <Privy access token>` |
| `usePinEmbeddedWallet` | `(o: { enabled; activeAddress; setActiveWallet }) => void` | Generic half of the active-wallet pin |
| `shouldPinEmbeddedWallet` | `(o: { enabled; ready; embeddedAddress; activeAddress }) => boolean` | The pure decision, so the pin cannot loop |
| `composeProviders` | `(layers, leaves?) => ComponentType` | Building block used by `/privy/wagmi` |
| Types | `PepuPrivyProviderProps`, `EnsureWalletStatus` | |

## Errors

| Code | Where |
|---|---|
| `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` | `usePepuAuthFetch` and `requestEnsureWallet` when there is no access token (signed out or expired) |
| `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED` | The ensure route answered but returned no wallet |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` | Surfaced from the ensure route when `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is unset |

## Example

```tsx
// Pillar 1, client: Google sign-in and an embedded wallet.
// See docs/sdk/privy-react.md and docs/onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { PepuPrivyWagmiProvider } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi";
import { WalletGate, useEmbeddedWallet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react";

export function Providers({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <PepuPrivyWagmiProvider
      // Read literally so the framework inlines it into the browser bundle.
      appId={process.env["NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID"]?.trim()}
      config={{ loginMethods: ["email", "google", "wallet"] }}
      fallback={<p>Set NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID</p>}
    >
      {children}
    </PepuPrivyWagmiProvider>
  );
}

function Address() {
  const { address } = useEmbeddedWallet();
  return <code>{address}</code>;
}

// Renders children once the embedded wallet exists, provisioning it through
// the ensure-wallet route (see ensure-wallet-route.ts) if needed.
export function Gated() {
  return (
    <WalletGate
      loading={<p>Setting up your wallet</p>}
      error={(e, retry) => (
        <button onClick={retry}>
          {e.message} Retry
        </button>
      )}
      stalled={(address, reload) => <button onClick={reload}>Wallet {address} is ready, reload</button>}
    >
      <Address />
    </WalletGate>
  );
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/login-providers.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

The matching server route is in [/privy/server](privy-server.md). The pin and the gate together are in [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](../recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A notice instead of the app | `appId` is empty, so the provider rendered `fallback` | Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` and read it as a literal `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` so the framework inlines it |
| `WalletGate` stays on `stalled` | The server created the wallet but this session has not synced it | Call `reload`; the gate offers it through the `stalled` render prop |
| Gate skips provisioning for a user with only an extension | Gating on `wallets.length > 0` | Gate on the embedded wallet, which is what `useEnsureWallet` does |
| `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` from the ensure route | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` does not match the app, which looks identical to an expired session | Check the secret first |

## Related

- [/privy](privy.md), [/privy/wagmi](privy-wagmi.md), [/privy/server](privy-server.md)
- [Social Login and Embedded Wallets (Privy)](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md)
- [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/privy-wagmi

# /privy/wagmi

`@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi` is the wagmi layer: a wagmi config for PEPU built with `@privy-io/wagmi`, one provider that mounts Privy, react-query and wagmi in the order Privy requires, and the active-wallet pin. Use it when your app reads and writes with wagmi hooks.

This entry is ESM-only because `@privy-io/wagmi` ships no CommonJS build.

## Import, peers and boundary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Import | `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi` |
| Server or client | Client only (React) |
| Peer dependencies | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@privy-io/wagmi` `^4.0.0`, `wagmi` `^3.0.0`, `@tanstack/react-query` `^5.0.0` |
| Module format | ESM only. There is no `require` condition |
| Pillar | Google to wallet |

## Exports

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` | `(p: PepuPrivyWagmiProviderProps) => ReactElement` | `PepuPrivyProvider` plus react-query plus `@privy-io/wagmi`'s `WagmiProvider`, with the pin mounted. Props: everything on `PepuPrivyProvider` except `wrapper`, plus `wagmiConfig?`, `queryClient?`, `pinEmbeddedWallet?` |
| `pepuWagmiConfig` | `(o?: { chain?: PepuChain; rpcUrl?: string }) => Config` | A wagmi config for PEPU built with `@privy-io/wagmi`'s `createConfig`. Plain wagmi's `createConfig` is a footgun with Privy: the embedded wallet would not appear as a connector |
| `useActiveWalletPin` | `(o?: { enabled?: boolean }) => void` | Keeps wagmi's active account pinned to the embedded wallet, so an extension such as Phantom cannot silently become the account |
| `EMBEDDED_WALLET_IS_ACTIVE_BY_DEFAULT` | `true` | Default policy for the pin |

`pepuMainnet` carries `contracts.multicall3` at PEPU's own address, so `useReadContracts` batches with no extra configuration.

## Errors

None thrown. A missing `appId` renders the provider's `fallback` instead of throwing.

## Example

```tsx
import { PepuPrivyWagmiProvider } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi";

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <PepuPrivyWagmiProvider
      appId={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID?.trim()}
      config={{ loginMethods: ["email", "google", "wallet"] }}
    >
      {children}
    </PepuPrivyWagmiProvider>
  );
}
```

The same provider is compiled in `docs/snippets/login-providers.tsx` (see [/privy/react](privy-react.md)), and a wagmi read is in `docs/snippets/multicall-in-react.tsx` (see [Batch Reads with Multicall3 in React](../recipes/multicall-in-react.md)).

To opt out of the pin for an external-wallet-first app, pass `pinEmbeddedWallet={false}` to the provider or `{ enabled: false }` to the hook.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The embedded wallet is not a connector | Plain `wagmi` `createConfig` or `WagmiProvider` was used | Use `pepuWagmiConfig` and this provider |
| Balance reads show another address | An extension became the active account | Keep the pin on, and compare `useAccount().address` with `useEmbeddedWallet().address` before labeling it "your wallet" |
| `Cannot find module` for `require("@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi")` | The entry is ESM only | `import` it, or use dynamic `import()` from CommonJS |

## Related

- [/privy/react](privy-react.md), [/privy](privy.md)
- [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](../recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md)
- [Batch Reads with Multicall3 in React](../recipes/multicall-in-react.md)

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/privy-server

# /privy/server

`@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server` is the server half of Google to wallet: the Privy server client, access-token verification, the authenticated-route helper and the ensure-wallet route factory. It is **server-only** and refuses to load in a browser bundle.

## Import, peers and boundary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Import | `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server` |
| Server or client | Server only. It calls `assertServerOnly()` at import and throws `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` when `window` exists |
| Peer dependencies | `@privy-io/node` `^0.34.0` |
| Secrets read | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (the canonical names in `PRIVY_ENV`), optionally `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` for sessions |
| Pillar | Google to wallet |

## Exports

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `privyEnvVar` | `(name: "appId" \| "appSecret" \| "authorizationKey" \| "keyQuorumId") => string \| undefined` | The single reader of the Privy variables and their aliases, trimmed |
| `readPrivyServerEnv` | `(o?) => PrivyServerEnv` | Reads the variables, explicit options winning. Throws one `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` listing every missing variable by name only |
| `createPrivyServer` | `(o?) => PrivyClient` | A cached `@privy-io/node` client per credential set. The authorization key is not given to the client; Privy takes it per request |
| `verifyRequestUser` | `(request: Request, o?: { privy? }) => Promise<{ userId: string; claims: unknown }>` | Verifies the `Authorization: Bearer` token. Throws `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` (HTTP 401) when missing or invalid; Privy's reason is in `details.reason` with the token redacted |
| `requireUser` | `(request, o?) => Promise<{ ok: true; user: PepuUser } \| { ok: false; response: Response }>` | Route-handler helper. Never throws: failure is a ready JSON `Response` (401 bad token, 500 missing config, 502 Privy unreachable). `PepuUser` is `{ userId, address: Address \| null, privyUser }` |
| `findEmbeddedEthereumWallet` | `(user: PrivyUser) => LinkedWallet \| null` | The user's Ethereum embedded wallet, delegated or not |
| `findDelegatedEthereumWallet` | `(user: PrivyUser) => LinkedWallet \| null` | The wallet that has a session signer attached |
| `createEnsureWalletRoute` | `(o?: { privy?; onCreated? }) => { POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> }` | Creates the signed-in user's embedded wallet server-side if they have none. Idempotent, user id only from the verified token, wallet owned by the user |
| Types | `PrivyUser`, `PepuUser`, `PrivyServerEnv`, `LinkedWallet` | |

### Custody

`createEnsureWalletRoute` creates the wallet with `owner: { user_id }`. Your backend holds no signing authority over it. Do not add a session signer in this route: grants are explicit and scoped, see [/session](session.md).

## Errors

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` | The entry was imported in a browser bundle |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` or the app id is unset (names only in the message) |
| `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` | Missing header or a token that does not verify. A mismatched `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` looks identical to an expired session, so check it first |
| `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED` | The wallet could not be read or created |
| `UNKNOWN` | Privy could not be reached |

## Example

```ts
// Pillar 1, server: provision the embedded wallet and authenticate requests.
// SERVER ONLY (reads PRIVY_APP_SECRET). See docs/sdk/privy-server.md
import { createEnsureWalletRoute, requireUser } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server";

// app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts
export const { POST } = createEnsureWalletRoute();

// Any other authenticated route handler. The user id comes only from the
// verified Privy access token, never from the request body.
export async function whoAmI(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const auth = await requireUser(request);
  if (!auth.ok) return auth.response; // ready-made JSON error with the right status
  return Response.json({ userId: auth.user.userId, address: auth.user.address });
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/ensure-wallet-route.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` at build or load | A client component imports this entry | Move the import to a route handler, server action or script |
| 401 on a valid-looking session | Wrong `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` for the app id | Use the secret from the same Privy app |
| Two wallets for one user | A hand-rolled route without the re-check | Use `createEnsureWalletRoute`, which re-checks after a failed create |

## Related

- [/privy/react](privy-react.md), [/session](session.md)
- [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md)

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/session

# /session

`@pepu-chain/sdk/session` is the session-key layer in **Privy mode**: the user grants your app a scoped, time-bound Privy session signer once, and your server then signs for them with no popup per action. This page covers three entries that belong together: `/session` (pure, shared), `/session/server` (routes and signer) and `/session/react` (hooks). The on-chain alternative is [/session/kernel](session-kernel.md).

The scope is enforced by Privy's backend policy engine, **not on-chain**, and the user still pays gas. For an on-chain limit and no user gas, use [/combo](combo.md).

## Import, peers and boundary

| Entry | Server or client | Peer dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/session` | Client-safe, pure | `viem` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/server` | **Server only** (`CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` in a browser) | `@privy-io/node` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/react` | Client only | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/server` | **Server only**. Stable alias that re-exports the pure policy helpers from `/session` | `viem` |

Secrets read by `/session/server`: `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`. The authorization key never reaches the browser and is never logged or put in an error.

## How the pieces fit

1. The browser calls `grant` (`useSessionGrant`). The server builds a fresh scoped policy with `buildSessionPolicy` and returns its id.
2. The browser asks the user to approve with Privy's `addSigners`. One consent, no gas.
3. Each action calls your action route (`useSessionAct`). The server re-checks the call against the scope, signs with `eth_signTransaction` and **broadcasts the raw transaction itself**, because Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` rejects chain 97741.
4. `revoke` removes the signer (`removeSigners` in the browser is the real revoke) and the server deletes the policy.

## Pure exports (`/session`)

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `buildSessionPolicy` | `(p: { contractAddress: Address; functions: readonly AbiFunction[]; expiresAtUnixSeconds: number; name?: string }) => SessionPolicy` | One `ALLOW` rule per function pinning contract, function, zero value and expiry, on `eth_signTransaction`. Throws `POLICY_UNSCOPED` instead of building an unscoped policy |
| `describeSessionScope` | `(p: { contractAddress; functions; expiresAtUnixSeconds }) => SessionScope` | Consent-screen data: contract, each function's name, signature and selector, value `"0"`, expiry |
| `signAndBroadcast` | `(params: SignAndBroadcastParams) => Promise<Hash>` | Resolves pending nonce, gas (+20 percent) and gas price against PEPU's RPC, builds the legacy transaction, hands it to your `sign` callback, broadcasts, returns the hash |
| `broadcastSignedTransaction` | `(client: BroadcastClient, signed: SignedTransactionLike) => Promise<Hash>` | Broadcast a raw signed transaction (hex or `{ signed_transaction }`) |
| `withGasLimitBuffer` | `(estimatedGas: bigint) => bigint` | Estimate plus 20 percent |
| `resolveSessionMinutes` | `(raw: string \| number \| null \| undefined) => number` | Session length rule: default 15, clamped to 1..1440 (`DEFAULT_SESSION_MINUTES`, `MAX_SESSION_MINUTES`) |
| `sessionExpiry` | `(nowSeconds: number, minutes: number) => number` | Unix-seconds expiry |
| `assertWithinPolicyNameLimit`, `PRIVY_POLICY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` | `(value, field) => string`, `49` | Privy rejects names of 50 or more characters; the real limit is 49 |
| `SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE` | `Record<"privy-offchain" \| "kernel-onchain", string>` | The mandatory honest statement of who enforces the limits. Show the one for your mode on the consent screen |
| `describeKernelSessionScope`, `isCallInScope`, `parseApproval`, `checkApproval` | pure Kernel helpers | Re-exported so you can avoid the `@zerodev/*` peers. See [/session/kernel](session-kernel.md) |

## Server exports (`/session/server`)

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `createSessionRoutes` | `(o: { scope: LazySessionScopeInput; contractAddressEnv?; minutes?; keyQuorumId?; privy?; verifyUser? }) => { grant: { POST }, status: { GET }, revoke: { POST } }` | The three route handlers. `grant` answers `{ alreadyGranted, policyId, expiresAt, signerId, durationMinutes }`. When a signer is already attached it answers `{ alreadyGranted: true }` and the client must not call `addSigners` again (Privy fails with "Duplicate signer"). `status` answers `{ delegated, active, address }` |
| `createSessionActionRoute` | `<I>(o: { scope; contractAddressEnv?; parse(body): I; buildCall(i, ctx): SessionCall; rateLimit?: { perMinute }; authorizationKey?; client?; ... }) => { POST }` | The action route. 409 `SESSION_NONE` is the only "no session" signal. It answers `{ hash, address, explorerUrl }` |
| `privySessionSigner` | `(o: { privy; walletId; address; authorizationKey?; client? }) => { signTransaction(tx), signAndBroadcast(p) }` | A signer for a session wallet that signs with `eth_signTransaction` and broadcasts itself |
| `signAndBroadcast`, `broadcastSignedTransaction`, `withGasLimitBuffer` | as above | Re-exported |
| Types | `SessionScopeInput`, `LazySessionScopeInput`, `VerifyUser`, `SessionPrivyClient`, `CreateSessionRoutesOptions`, `PrivySessionSignerOptions`, `SessionCall`, `CreateSessionActionRouteOptions` | |

An empty or `undefined` `scope.contractAddress` (an unset env variable) does not throw at module load: every route answers `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` as JSON at request time, naming `contractAddressEnv`. A non-empty malformed address still throws at creation. Auth defaults to `verifyRequestUser` from [/privy/server](privy-server.md); pass `verifyUser` for your own.

```ts
// Pillar 2 (Privy mode), server: grant, status, revoke and one scoped action.
// SERVER ONLY (reads PRIVY_APP_SECRET and PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY).
// See docs/sdk/session.md and docs/recipes/grant-a-session.md
import { createSessionActionRoute, createSessionRoutes } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/server";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapFunction } from "./tapscore";

const scope = { contractAddress: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, functions: [tapFunction] } as const;

const routes = createSessionRoutes({ scope });

// app/api/session/grant/route.ts
export const grant = routes.grant;
// app/api/session/status/route.ts
export const status = routes.status;
// app/api/session/revoke/route.ts
export const revoke = routes.revoke;

// app/api/game/tap/route.ts: signs with Privy eth_signTransaction and broadcasts itself,
// because Privy's server-side eth_sendTransaction rejects chain 97741.
export const tap = createSessionActionRoute({
  scope,
  parse: () => ({}),
  buildCall: () => ({ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: [tapFunction], functionName: "tap" }),
  rateLimit: { perMinute: 60 },
});
```

Source: `docs/snippets/session-privy-server.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## React exports (`/session/react`)

| Export | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `useSessionGrant` | `(o?: BaseOptions & { grantEndpoint? }) => { grant(), status: SessionGrantStatus, error?: PepuError }` | POST the grant route, then ask for consent with `addSigners`. Skips `addSigners` when `alreadyGranted`. `status`: `idle`, `creating-policy`, `awaiting-consent`, `granted`, `error` |
| `useSessionStatus` | `(o?: BaseOptions & { statusEndpoint?, pollMs? }) => { state, loading, expiresAt?, secondsLeft?, refetch() }` | `state` is `none`, `active` or `expired`. `loading` is true until the first response, so the consent screen does not flash on reload |
| `useSessionRevoke` | `(o?: BaseOptions & { revokeEndpoint? }) => { revoke(), status, error? }` | `removeSigners` is the real revoke |
| `useSessionAct` | `<I, O>(o: BaseOptions & { endpoint }) => { act(input): Promise<O>, status, error? }` | A 409 is `error.code === "SESSION_NONE"`. Any other failure is a failed transaction, not a lost session |
| `deriveSessionState` | `(p: { delegated; expiresAt?; nowSeconds }) => { state, secondsLeft? }` | Pure |
| `errorFromResponse` | `(res: Response) => Promise<PepuError>` | Reads the `{ error: { code, message, hint } }` body |

`BaseOptions` is `{ authFetch?, address? }`; auth defaults to `usePepuAuthFetch()` from [/privy/react](privy-react.md). Privy does not expose a policy's expiry, so the client tracks `expiresAt` from the grant.

```tsx
// Pillar 2 (Privy mode), client: grant once, then act with no popup.
// See docs/sdk/session.md and docs/recipes/grant-a-session.md
import { useSessionAct, useSessionGrant, useSessionRevoke, useSessionStatus } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/react";

export function Session() {
  const { state, secondsLeft, loading } = useSessionStatus({ pollMs: 30_000 });
  const { grant, status: grantStatus, error: grantError } = useSessionGrant();
  const { revoke } = useSessionRevoke();
  const { act, status: actStatus, error: actError } = useSessionAct<Record<string, never>, { hash: string }>({
    endpoint: "/api/game/tap",
  });

  // Avoid flashing the consent screen on reload.
  if (loading) return <p>Checking session</p>;

  if (state !== "active") {
    return (
      <button onClick={() => void grant()} disabled={grantStatus === "creating-policy" || grantStatus === "awaiting-consent"}>
        {state === "expired" ? "Session expired, start a new one" : "Start session"}
        {grantError ? ` (${grantError.code})` : ""}
      </button>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <p>{secondsLeft}s left</p>
      <button onClick={() => void act({}).then((r) => console.log(r.hash))} disabled={actStatus === "pending"}>
        Tap
      </button>
      <button onClick={() => void revoke()}>End session</button>
      {actError ? <p>{actError.code === "SESSION_NONE" ? "No active session" : actError.message}</p> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/session-privy-react.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Errors

| Code | Where |
|---|---|
| `POLICY_UNSCOPED` | `buildSessionPolicy`, `describeSessionScope`, and the action route when a call is outside the scope (invalid address, no functions, non-function ABI item, bad expiry) |
| `POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG` | A policy or rule name over 49 characters |
| `SESSION_NONE` | The action route (HTTP 409) with no signer attached; the hooks surface it |
| `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` | The route cannot authenticate the request |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` | Unset contract address or Privy variable, at request time |
| `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` | `/session/server` or `/server` imported in a browser bundle |
| `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH` | Privy 401 "No valid authorization keys": the server key is not the signer the user granted |
| `PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741` | Someone used Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction`. Sign and broadcast instead |
| `TX_NONCE_RACE`, `TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT`, `TX_REVERTED` | Broadcast failures. A failed transaction, not proof the session is gone |

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every action is denied | The policy rule targets `eth_sendTransaction` | Rules must use `eth_signTransaction`; `buildSessionPolicy` does |
| "Duplicate signer" | `addSigners` called when `alreadyGranted` was true | Use `useSessionGrant`, which skips it |
| Policy create returns 400 on name length | Name of 50 or more characters | Keep names at 49 or fewer |
| 401 "No valid authorization keys" | Key quorum mismatch | `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` must be the private half of the key whose quorum id is `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` |
| Two quick taps race | Nonce collision on the same wallet | Use `rateLimit`, serialize per wallet |

## Related

- [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md)
- [Grant a Session](../recipes/grant-a-session.md)
- [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md)
- [/session/kernel](session-kernel.md), [/combo](combo.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/session-kernel

# /session/kernel

`@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel` is the **on-chain** session key: a ZeroDev Kernel permission whose scope is enforced by policy contracts during UserOperation validation. A UserOperation outside the scope is rejected by the EntryPoint itself, whoever relays it and whatever your backend does. Most apps use [/combo](combo.md), which wires these primitives to routes and hooks. Use this page when you build a custom flow.

Pinned to call policy v0.0.4 because v0.0.5 is not deployed on PEPU.

## Import, peers and boundary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Import | `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel` |
| Server or client | Mixed by function. `approveKernelSession` runs in the browser. `generateSessionKey` and `loadKernelSessionAccount` are **server only** by contract: the session private key must never reach a browser. The module itself has no server-only guard |
| Peer dependencies | `@zerodev/sdk` `^5.5.0`, `@zerodev/permissions` `^5.6.0`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` `^5.4.0`, `viem` |
| Avoid the peers | Import the pure helpers from [/session](session.md) instead |

## Exports

| Export | Signature | Server or client | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `buildKernelSessionPolicies` | `(p: { calls: readonly KernelSessionCall[]; validUntil: number; validAfter?: number }) => Policy[]` | Both | Call policy v0.0.4 plus the timestamp policy. Pure and deterministic |
| `generateSessionKey` | `() => { privateKey: Hex; address: Address }` | Server | A fresh random key. Send only the address to the owner |
| `expectedPermissionId` | `(p: { publicClient; sessionKeyAddress; policies }) => Promise<string>` | Server | The permission id the chain derives, to compare with the browser's approval |
| `approveKernelSession` | `(p: { publicClient; owner: KernelOwner; sessionKeyAddress; policies }) => Promise<{ approval: string; kernelAddress: Address }>` | Browser | The owner signs ONE EIP-712 message. The `approval` holds no secret |
| `loadKernelSessionAccount` | `(p: { publicClient; approval: string; sessionPrivateKey: Hex }) => Promise<KernelSmartAccount>` | Server | Rebuilds the session's Kernel account. Pass it to `createPepuSponsoredClient` |
| `describeKernelSessionScope` | `(p: { calls; validUntil; validAfter? }) => KernelSessionScope` | Both | Consent-screen data: target, function, signature, selector, max value |
| `isCallInScope` | `(scope, call: { to; data; value? }) => boolean` | Both | Fail-fast check before sponsoring. The chain enforces the real limit |
| `parseApproval`, `checkApproval` | `(approval) => ParsedApproval \| null`, `(approval, { kernelAddress, permissionId }) => ApprovalCheck` | Server | Reject an approval that carries a private key, is for another account, or whose permission id differs from the one issued |
| `createMemoryStore`, `isLive` | `() => SessionStore`, `(record, nowSeconds) => boolean` | Server | Dev-grade store and the liveness test |
| `SessionStore`, `SessionRecord` | interfaces | Server | `get`, `set`, `delete`, `tryLock`, `unlock`. Implement on a database with the session key encrypted at rest |
| `KernelSessionCall` | `{ target: Address; abi: Abi; functionName: string; valueLimit?: bigint }` | Both | One function a session may call. Default value limit `0n` |
| `CALL_POLICY_V0_0_4_ADDRESS`, `TIMESTAMP_POLICY_ADDRESS` | addresses | Both | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` and `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` |
| `SESSION_GAS_RESERVATION_PEPU` | `{ firstOperation: 20.5, laterOperation: 6.9 }` | Both | Worst-case gas the paymaster reserves per operation. Size spend caps above these |
| `KERNEL_VERSION`, `getKernelAddress`, `KernelOwner`, `KernelSmartAccount` | re-exported from `/aa/kernel` | | |

## Errors

| Code | Where |
|---|---|
| `POLICY_UNSCOPED` | A scope with no calls or a call outside it |
| `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH` | Raised by the `/combo` routes when `checkApproval` fails |
| `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `SESSION_NONE` | Raised by the `/combo` routes for an expired offer or no live session |

`checkApproval` returns `{ ok: false, reason }` and does not throw.

## Example

```ts
// Pillar 2 (Kernel mode), the low-level primitives behind /combo.
// Most apps use createSponsoredSessionRoutes instead (see combo-server.ts).
// See docs/sdk/session-kernel.md
import { getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import {
  approveKernelSession,
  buildKernelSessionPolicies,
  checkApproval,
  describeKernelSessionScope,
  expectedPermissionId,
  generateSessionKey,
  isCallInScope,
  loadKernelSessionAccount,
} from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel";
import type { KernelOwner, KernelSessionCall } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel";
import { encodeFunctionData } from "viem";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

const calls: KernelSessionCall[] = [{ target: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }];
const validUntil = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 15 * 60;

// --- SERVER: create the session key. The private key never leaves the server. ---
export const sessionKey = generateSessionKey();
export const policies = buildKernelSessionPolicies({ calls, validUntil });

// Consent-screen data, plain JSON.
export const scope = describeKernelSessionScope({ calls, validUntil });

// --- BROWSER: the owner signs ONE EIP-712 message. No gas, no private key leaves the wallet. ---
export function grant(owner: KernelOwner) {
  return approveKernelSession({ publicClient, owner, sessionKeyAddress: sessionKey.address, policies });
}

// --- SERVER: verify the approval before storing it, then act with the session key. ---
export async function activate(approval: string, kernelAddress: `0x${string}`) {
  const permissionId = await expectedPermissionId({ publicClient, sessionKeyAddress: sessionKey.address, policies });
  const check = checkApproval(approval, { kernelAddress, permissionId });
  if (!check.ok) throw new Error(check.reason);
  return loadKernelSessionAccount({ publicClient, approval, sessionPrivateKey: sessionKey.privateKey });
}

// Pure, fails fast before sponsoring. The chain enforces the real limit.
export const tapIsAllowed = isCallInScope(scope, {
  to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS,
  data: encodeFunctionData({ abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }),
  value: 0n,
});
```

Source: `docs/snippets/session-kernel.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## What the chain enforces

- **Call policy v0.0.4:** only the listed targets and function selectors, with native value at most `valueLimit`.
- **Timestamp policy:** the permission is invalid outside `validAfter` to `validUntil`.
- Revoking server-side deletes the session key and approval at once. The on-chain grant stays valid until its expiry, but only the deleted key could use it and only within the scope.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Sponsorship denied with a spend-cap message right after the first action | Caps below the reserved worst case | Size caps above `SESSION_GAS_RESERVATION_PEPU` |
| `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH` | The browser built different policies than the server issued | Share one `scope` object between server and browser |
| A production store loses sessions | `createMemoryStore` is lost on restart and not shared across instances | Implement `SessionStore` on a database and encrypt `sessionPrivateKey` |

## Related

- [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md)
- [/combo](combo.md), [/aa](aa.md)
- [EntryPoints and Kernel](../contracts/entrypoints-and-kernel.md)

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/aa

# /aa

`@pepu-chain/sdk/aa` is the sponsored-transactions layer: ERC-4337 bundler and ERC-7677 paymaster clients for PEPU, endpoint probes, UserOperation failure mapping, and receipt decoding. This page covers four entries that belong together: `/aa` (viem account abstraction only), `/aa/kernel` (ZeroDev Kernel account and sponsored client), `/aa/react` (hooks for Privy Smart Wallets) and `/aa/react-direct` (hooks for your own bundler and paymaster).

A zero-balance Kernel smart account can transact with gas paid by a paymaster. The hosted bundler is the SDK default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`. The ERC-7677 paymaster URL always embeds a project token, so there is no tokenless default: set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` or pass `paymasterToken`. Local development defaults (`http://localhost:4337`, `http://localhost:8788`) are for people running their own services. The v1 paymaster is retired (see [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md)).

Which entry to use depends on who builds the Kernel account: `/aa/react` is Path 2 (Privy Smart Wallets), `/aa/kernel` and `/aa/react-direct` are Path 1 (ZeroDev-native). See [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md).

## Import, peers and boundary

| Entry | Server or client | Peer dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa` | Client-safe, isomorphic | `viem` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel` | Client-safe, but the owner key must stay where the owner is | `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`, `viem` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react` | Client only | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `permissionless` (required by Privy's smart-wallets module). Never needs `@zerodev/*` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct` | Client only | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`, `viem` |

EntryPoint v0.7 (`0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032`, `ENTRY_POINT_V07`) is the only version PEPU's bundler and paymaster speak. A bundler URL embeds nothing secret; a paymaster URL can embed a credential, so keep it server-side unless it holds a publishable client token.

## Exports: `/aa`

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `ENTRY_POINT_V07` | `{ address, version: "0.7" }` | |
| `createPepuBundlerClient` | `(o: { bundlerUrl?; account: SmartAccount; paymaster?; paymasterContext?; publicClient? }) => BundlerClient` | A viem bundler client with the Alto-compatible fee estimator pre-wired |
| `createPepuPaymasterClient` | `(o?: { paymasterUrl?; paymasterToken?; context?: PaymasterContext }) => PaymasterClient` | A viem ERC-7677 paymaster client. With `paymasterToken` (a project token) the URL is built against the paymaster base (the hosted service by default); an explicit `paymasterUrl` or `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` wins. The context (for example the user's Privy access token) goes into every `pm_getPaymasterStubData` and `pm_getPaymasterData` call |
| `estimatePepuUserOpFees` | `(publicClient) => Promise<{ maxFeePerGas; maxPriorityFeePerGas }>` | The chain's `estimateFeesPerGas` with `maxFeePerGas` times 1.2. Alto does not implement ZeroDev's `zd_getUserOperationGasPrice`, so ZeroDev's default estimator fails |
| `probeBundler` | `(url?: string | null, o?: { fetch?; timeoutMs? }) => Promise<BundlerProbeResult>` | Defaults to the hosted bundler. Chain ID, supported entry points, which JSON-RPC methods exist, latency |
| `probePaymaster` | `(url?: string | null, o?) => Promise<PaymasterProbeResult>` | Defaults to the hosted service base. Checks `/health`, `/v2/free-tier` and the v2 ERC-7677 route `/v2/paymaster/<token>` (a placeholder token when you pass only the base). A structured JSON-RPC error such as invalid params or an unknown credential counts as responding (`erc7677: "needs-credential"`); only network errors, non-JSON answers and 5xx are `"not-responding"`. Read-only |
| `getPaymasterDeposit` | `(client, paymasterAddress?) => Promise<bigint>` | The paymaster's EntryPoint deposit; defaults to PEPU's deployed paymaster |
| `checkSponsorship` | `(options?) => Promise<SponsorshipReport>` | Live status: `available`, `transport` (`direct` or `none`), `reason`, `fixes`. Never throws for an unreachable service |
| `describeUserOpFailure` | `(e: unknown) => PepuBundlerError \| PepuPaymasterError` | Walks the `cause` chain, maps `AA10` to `AA9x` to a fix, maps paymaster reason codes through the catalog, redacts tokens and URL credentials |
| `redactSecrets` | `(text: string) => string` | Strips `/paymaster/<token>` paths, bearer tokens, API keys, JWTs and URL credentials |
| `encodeKernelExecute` | `(calls: readonly Call[]) => Hex` | ERC-7579 `execute` callData: single mode for one call, batch mode for several. Pure |
| `normalizeCalls` | `(calls: readonly Call[]) => EncodedCall[]` | Encodes `abi`/`functionName`/`args` into `data` |
| `userOpEventsFromReceipt`, `userOpEventFromReceipt` | `(receipt) => UserOpEvent[]`, `(receipt, sender) => {...} \| null` | Who paid and how much, from the `UserOperationEvent` in a bundle receipt |
| `getPepuKernelStack`, `getKernelAccountAddress`, `getSponsorshipStatus` | see [Core](core.md) | `getSponsorshipStatus` is deprecated |
| Types | `Call`, `SponsoredResult`, `EncodedCall`, `UserOpEvent`, `SponsorshipReport`, `CheckSponsorshipOptions`, `BundlerProbeResult`, `PaymasterProbeResult`, `ProbeOptions`, `FetchLike` | |

Probing the hosted services, with the strict-mode types: `docs/snippets/probe-health.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

`Call` is `{ to; value?; data?; abi?; functionName?; args? }`: give raw `data`, or `abi` plus `functionName`. `SponsoredResult` is `{ userOpHash: Hex | null; transactionHash; success; paymaster: Address | null; actualGasCostWei; explorerUrl }`. `userOpHash` is `null` through Privy Smart Wallets, which expose only the bundle transaction.

## Exports: `/aa/kernel`

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `toPepuKernelAccount` | `(p: { publicClient; owner: KernelOwner; index?: bigint; plugins?: { regular?: object } }) => Promise<KernelSmartAccount>` | A Kernel v3.1 account owned by `owner` (ECDSA root validator). The address depends only on owner and `index`. `plugins.regular` adds a permission validator, which is how [/session/kernel](session-kernel.md) builds on it |
| `getKernelAddress` | `(publicClient, owner: Address) => Promise<Address>` | The counterfactual address with no signature |
| `createPepuSponsoredClient` | `(p: { account; bundlerUrl?; paymasterUrl?; paymasterToken?; paymasterContext?; publicClient? }) => KernelAccountClient` | A Kernel client that sends through the bundler (hosted by default) with gas paid by your paymaster. `paymasterToken` builds the hosted ERC-7677 URL for a project token |
| `sendSponsored` | `(p: { client; calls: Call[]; timeoutMs? }) => Promise<SendSponsoredResult>` | Encode, send one UserOperation, wait for the receipt, report who paid. Failures go through `describeUserOpFailure`. Result: `userOpHash`, `transactionHash`, `success`, `paymaster`, `actualGasCostWei`, `explorerUrl` |
| `KERNEL_VERSION`, `encodeKernelExecute`, `KernelOwner`, `KernelSmartAccount`, `KernelAccountClient`, `Call` | | `KernelOwner` is a viem local account, a Privy signer or a wallet client |

```ts
// Pillar 3: a sponsored transaction from a script (direct transport).
// Needs a bundler and a paymaster: set PEPU_BUNDLER_URL and PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL
// (the bundler defaults to https://bundler.pepeunchained.com; the ERC-7677 URL is https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>).
// Local dev defaults are http://localhost:4337 and http://localhost:8788 for your own services.
// See docs/sdk/aa.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-send.md
import { buildPaymasterContext, checkSponsorship, explorerLinks, getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { createPepuSponsoredClient, sendSponsored, toPepuKernelAccount } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel";
import type { Hex } from "viem";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

// SCRIPT ONLY: the owner key stays in your environment.
const owner = privateKeyToAccount(process.env["OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY"] as Hex);

export async function sponsoredTap(privyAccessToken?: string) {
  // 1. Is sponsorship reachable? Never throws for an unreachable service.
  const status = await checkSponsorship({ publicClient });
  if (!status.available) throw new Error(`${status.reason} ${status.fixes.join(" ")}`);

  // 2. The Kernel smart account that sends and holds assets. The owner EOA only signs.
  const account = await toPepuKernelAccount({ publicClient, owner });

  // 3. A client that sends through your bundler and has gas paid by your paymaster.
  const client = createPepuSponsoredClient({
    account,
    // The v2 free tier wants the user's Privy access token (from PEPU's own Privy app).
    ...(privyAccessToken ? { paymasterContext: buildPaymasterContext({ privyAccessToken }) } : {}),
  });

  // 4. One UserOperation: encode, send, wait for the receipt, report who paid.
  const result = await sendSponsored({
    client,
    calls: [{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }],
  });

  return { ...result, links: explorerLinks({ tx: result.transactionHash, sender: account.address }) };
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/sponsored-send.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Exports: `/aa/react`

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `usePepuSmartAccount` | `() => { owner?: Address; smartAccount?: Address; ready: boolean }` | The two-address model made explicit: `owner` is the embedded wallet that signs, `smartAccount` is the Kernel account that sends and holds assets |
| `useSponsoredSend` | `(o?: { transport?: "privy-smart-wallets" }) => { send(calls: Call[]): Promise<SponsoredResult>; status; result?; error?: PepuError }` | Send with sponsored gas through Privy's smart-wallet client, using the bundler and paymaster URLs from the Privy dashboard. One send at a time. `status`: `idle`, `signing`, `submitting`, `confirmed`, `error`. For your own bundler and paymaster, use `useDirectSponsoredSend` from `/aa/react-direct` |
| `usePepuSponsorship` | `(o?: { pollMs?; bundlerUrl?; paymasterUrl? }) => SponsorshipReport & { loading: boolean }` | Polled `checkSponsorship`. The live replacement for `useSponsorshipStatus` |

```tsx
// Pillar 3, client: send with gas sponsored from a component.
// See docs/sdk/aa.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-send.md
import { usePepuSmartAccount, usePepuSponsorship, useSponsoredSend } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

export function SponsoredTap() {
  const { smartAccount } = usePepuSmartAccount();
  // "privy-smart-wallets" uses the bundler and paymaster URLs from the Privy dashboard.
  // For your own bundler and paymaster, use useDirectSponsoredSend from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct".
  const { send, status, result, error } = useSponsoredSend({ transport: "privy-smart-wallets" });
  const sponsorship = usePepuSponsorship({ pollMs: 0 });

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Smart account: {smartAccount}</p>
      <button
        disabled={status === "signing" || status === "submitting"}
        onClick={() => void send([{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }])}
      >
        Tap, no gas
      </button>
      {status === "confirmed" && result ? <a href={result.explorerUrl}>Paid by {result.paymaster}</a> : null}
      {error ? (
        <p>
          {error.code}: {error.hint}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {!sponsorship.loading && !sponsorship.available ? <p>{sponsorship.reason}</p> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/sponsored-send-react.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Errors

| Code | Where |
|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` | No bundler or paymaster URL is configured (`createPepuBundlerClient`, `createPepuPaymasterClient`, probes). The message names the variable |
| `CONFIG_BAD_URL` | A configured URL is not `http(s)` |
| `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE` | The bundler probe or send could not reach the bundler |
| `PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE` | The paymaster probe or API call could not reach the paymaster service (network error, DNS, timeout) |
| `PAYMASTER_API_ERROR` | The paymaster host answered but its `/v2/paymaster/<token>` route did not speak ERC-7677 JSON-RPC (probe), or a REST route failed |
| `BUNDLER_AA_FAILED` | An `AAxx` failure from the EntryPoint, mapped by `describeUserOpFailure` |
| `PAYMASTER_DENIED`, `PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE`, `PAYMASTER_CAP`, and the other `PAYMASTER_*` codes | The paymaster refused. See [SDK Error Catalog](errors.md) |
| `POLICY_UNSCOPED` | `normalizeCalls` or `encodeKernelExecute` got an empty list or an ambiguous call |
| `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED` | `useSponsoredSend` ran before the embedded wallet existed |

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `checkSponsorship` says no URL is configured | The paymaster has no tokenless URL, or an env var was cleared | Set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` (or pass `paymasterToken`); the bundler defaults to the hosted one |
| `zd_getUserOperationGasPrice` not found | ZeroDev's default fee estimator against Alto | Use `createPepuSponsoredClient` or `estimatePepuUserOpFees` |
| `PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE` | The paymaster's EntryPoint deposit is empty | Deposit PEPU to it; `checkSponsorship({ publicClient })` reports `depositWei` |
| Smart account address differs from the wallet address | They are two addresses by design | See [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md) |

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: which one to use](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)
- [Send a Sponsored Transaction](../recipes/sponsored-send.md)
- [/paymaster](paymaster.md), [/combo](combo.md)
- [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md)
