Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/paymaster

# /paymaster

`@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster` is the typed client for the PEPU paymaster policy service (v1 and v2 REST), the on-chain helpers for v2 projects (claim, configure, deposit, read), and the mapping from denial reasons to `PepuError` codes. `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server` adds the one call that carries a Privy app secret.

The v2 tiered paymaster `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` is at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (registry keys `paymasterV2` and `paymaster`). The hosted policy service at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` serves it through `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>`. The v1 paymaster is retired (EntryPoint deposit withdrawn); the v1 REST routes remain in the client for reference only. Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs.

## Import, peers and boundary

| Entry | Server or client | Peer dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster` | Isomorphic (plain `fetch` plus viem). Never put a server key (`ppk_`) in a browser | `viem` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server` | **Server or CLI only**. `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` in a browser | `viem` |

Credentials: a **client token** (`ppt_`, publishable, bound to allowed origins) and a **server key** (`ppk_`, secret, any wallet). `credentialKind` tells them apart by prefix only.

## v2 facts the helpers encode

- `projectId = keccak256(bytes(appId))`, case-sensitive. A typo deposits into a project nobody can claim.
- **Deposits only.** There are no withdrawals, for owners or anyone. Pausing is the exit. Anyone may `depositFor` any project.
- Ownership is Privy-verified: prove the app secret, get an EIP-712 attestation, call `claimProject`. **The claim sets the owner only.** Then the owner must call `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit`. Nothing is sponsored until all three have run (a project with no per-wallet limit is rejected on chain). An empty project is claimed at once; a project that already holds deposits is **pending** for the admin delay (at least 48 hours) and finished with `encodeExecuteReclaim`.
- A re-claim of an owned project is timelocked 48 hours and the owner can cancel it once per new owner. Ownership transfer is two-step (propose, accept).
- Free tier: 100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per user per hour (enforced by the service), for Privy users only, no chain-wide ceiling. The free-tier targets are TapScore only for now (`0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`); the manager can add more. Beyond the free tier a dApp deposits into its own project. The free tier needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app, sent as `context.privyAccessToken` in the ERC-7677 request (REST: `Authorization: Bearer`). A third-party app's own Privy token is ignored for billing, so third-party apps use a project.

## Tokens and origins

- **Client token** (`ppt_`): publishable, works only from the project's allowed origins. With no origins set, or from another origin, it is refused with `project_origin_not_allowed`.
- **Server key** (`ppk_`): secret. Backend callers put it in the ERC-7677 URL: `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`.
- Developer flow: SIWE login (`/v2/auth/nonce`, `/v2/auth/login`), `POST /v2/projects/verify` with the Privy app id and secret (used for one request, never stored), `claimProject` (immediate if the project is empty; pending 48 hours if already funded), `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`, `depositFor` (one-way, nobody can withdraw), register the project to get the `ppt_` client token and `ppk_` server key, then set allowed origins for the client token.
- Build the URL with `hostedErc7677Url(token)` (from `/paymaster`) or `buildErc7677Url({ baseUrl, token, version })`. `createPepuPaymasterClient` and `createPepuSponsoredClient` accept `paymasterToken` and build the URL for you; `requirePaymasterUrl(explicit?, token?)` is the resolver they share.

## REST client

```ts
createPaymasterApi(options?: { baseUrl?; fetch?; env?; timeoutMs?; sessionToken? }): PaymasterApi
// PaymasterApi: { baseUrl: string; v1: PaymasterApiV1; v2: PaymasterApiV2 }
```

`baseUrl` defaults to `resolvePepuEndpoints().paymasterBaseUrl`: `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (or the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` name) with any `/v2/paymaster/<token>` tail stripped, then the hosted base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. It throws `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` only if the hosted base was cleared. Default timeout 15000 ms.

| Method | Calls | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `v1.sponsor(userOp, auth)` | `POST /sponsor` | Needs `auth.privyAccessToken` (`PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED` if missing) |
| `v1.health()` | `GET /health` | |
| `v1.erc7677Url(token)`, `v2.erc7677Url(token)` | URL builder | `<base>/paymaster/<token>` and `<base>/v2/paymaster/<token>` |
| `v2.sponsor(userOp, auth)` | `POST /v2/sponsor` | Returns approvals and denials; use `assertApproved` to throw |
| `v2.config()`, `v2.contract()`, `v2.freeTier()` | `GET /v2/config`, `/v2/contract`, `/v2/free-tier` | `contract()` gives the deployed address and ABI |
| `v2.auth.nonce()`, `login(message, signature)`, `logout()`, `v2.me()` | SIWE session | |
| `v2.loginWithWallet(sign, { address, domain, uri?, chainId?, statement?, lifetimeSeconds? })` | nonce, EIP-4361 message, login | One-hour session stored on the client. `domain` must be one of the service's `SIWE_DOMAINS` |
| `v2.projects.prepare(request)` | `POST /v2/projects/prepare` | Calldata for the owner's wallet. Sends nothing |
| `v2.projects.register`, `list`, `get`, `updateSettings`, `usage`, `events`, `allowlist` | `/v2/projects/*` | `register` returns the client token, the ERC-7677 URL and the secret server key, each shown once |
| `v2.projects.rotateClientToken`, `rotateServerKey` | | |
| `v2.request(method, path, options?)` | any `/v2` path | Escape hatch with the same error mapping |

`SponsorAuth` is `{ apiKey; privyAccessToken?; origin? }` and `apiKey` is sent as `X-Api-Key`. Full endpoint behavior is in [REST API v1](../infra/paymaster/rest-api-v1.md), [REST API v2](../infra/paymaster/rest-api-v2.md) and [Credential Matrix](../infra/paymaster/auth.md).

Helpers: `buildErc7677Url({ baseUrl, token, version? = 2 })` refuses a `ppk_` key in a browser (`CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY`); `assertApproved(result)` returns the approval or throws the mapped error; `serializeAttestation(a)` converts to the wire format.

## On-chain helpers (v2)

Every helper takes an optional `paymaster` address and defaults to the registry's `paymasterV2` entry (the deployed paymaster). Pass one explicitly to target another deployment; with no registry entry and no address it throws `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV`. No transaction is sent without the caller's wallet client.

| Export | Signature | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `resolvePaymasterV2Address` | `(explicit?: Address) => Address` | Explicit, then registry, else `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` |
| `computeProjectId`, `getProjectId` | `(appId: string) => Hex` | `keccak256(bytes(appId))`, 1 to 128 characters |
| `readProject` | `(client, projectId, { paymaster?, checkTargets?, now? }) => Promise<ProjectState>` | owner, `claimed`, `paused`, `balance`, limits, `spentToday`, `limitsConfigured`, `pendingReclaim` (a re-claim, or the first claim of a funded project while `claimed` is false), `pendingOwner`, optional per-target allowance |
| `encodeDeposit` | `(projectId, amountWei, options?) => PaymasterCall` | One-way `depositFor` |
| `encodeClaimProject`, `encodeReclaimProject`, `encodeClaimFromVerification` | `(attestation or verified, options?) => PaymasterCall` | `encodeClaimFromVerification` picks claim or reclaim from the verify result's `action` |
| `encodeExecuteReclaim`, `encodeCancelReclaim` | `(projectId, options?)` | Finish or cancel a pending claim or re-claim. `cancelReclaim` is the owner's (once per new owner); for a pending first claim of an unowned project the contract owner or manager cancels |
| `encodeSetTargets` | `(projectId, targets, allowed, options?)` | At most 50 per call. Owner only |
| `encodeSetDailyLimit`, `encodeSetSenderDailyLimit` | `(projectId, limitWei, options?)` | Owner only |
| `encodeSetPaused` | `(projectId, paused, options?)` | Pausing is the exit |
| `encodeProposeProjectOwner`, `encodeAcceptProjectOwnership` | | Two-step transfer |
| `configureProject` | `(params: { appId? \| projectId?; targets; dailyLimitWei; senderDailyLimitWei; paymaster? }) => { projectId; calls: PaymasterCall[] }` | The three post-claim calls, in order |
| `sendPaymasterCalls` | `(walletClient, calls, { publicClient? }) => Promise<Hash[]>` | Sends one after another; with `publicClient` waits for each receipt and throws `TX_REVERTED` on failure |
| `depositFor` | `(params: { walletClient; appId? \| projectId?; amountWei; requireClaimed? = true; publicClient?; paymaster? }) => Promise<Hash>` | Refuses an unclaimed project by default (`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED`) |
| `pepuSponsoredPaymasterV2Abi` | ABI | |

`PaymasterCall` is `{ to; data; value; function }`: a transaction a wallet or smart-account batch can send.

## Server: claim attestation

```ts
requestClaimAttestation(api: PaymasterApi, params: { appId: string; newOwner: Address; privyAppSecret: string }): Promise<ClaimAttestationResult>
```

`POST /v2/projects/verify`. The `api` client must already be signed in as `newOwner`. **This sends your Privy app secret to the PEPU policy service**, which documents it as never stored, logged or echoed. This SDK never logs, returns or puts the secret in an error. Use a dedicated Privy app for sponsorship if you can and rotate the secret afterwards. The result has `projectId`, `action` (`claimProject` for an unclaimed project, `reclaimProject` for an owned one), `attestation` and `expiresAt` (at most one hour).

## Denial reasons

| Export | Signature |
|---|---|
| `mapPaymasterReason` | `(reason: string \| undefined) => PepuErrorCode` |
| `paymasterReasonToError` | `(reason, message?, details?) => PepuPaymasterError` |
| `decodePaymasterRevert` | `(data: Hex) => { errorName; args } \| null` |
| `PAYMASTER_DENIAL_REASONS`, `PAYMASTER_REASON_CODES` | The full reason list and its exhaustive mapping to codes |

## Errors

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` | No `baseUrl`, no v2 paymaster address, no wallet account |
| `CONFIG_BAD_URL`, `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` | Bad `baseUrl`; a server key in a browser |
| `PAYMASTER_DENIED` | Generic refusal; bad argument to an encoder |
| `PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE`, `PAYMASTER_CAP` | Balance exhausted; a project, user, sender or free-tier limit reached |
| `PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | Origin or target not on the project's allowlist |
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED`, `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED`, `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED` | Project state |
| `PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`, `PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`, `PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED`, `PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED`, `PAYMASTER_API_ERROR` | Credential, tier, rate and session problems |
| `PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE` | The service did not answer; the message omits the credential |
| `TX_REVERTED` | A prepared call reverted in `sendPaymasterCalls` |

## Example

```ts
// Register, claim, configure and fund a v2 paymaster project.
// Deposits are one-way; deposit only what your project needs.
// SERVER OR CLI ONLY: requestClaimAttestation sends your Privy app secret to the policy service.
// See docs/sdk/paymaster.md and docs/recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md
import { getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import {
  buildErc7677Url,
  computeProjectId,
  configureProject,
  createPaymasterApi,
  depositFor,
  encodeClaimFromVerification,
  readProject,
  sendPaymasterCalls,
} from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";
import { requestClaimAttestation } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server";
import { createWalletClient, getAddress, http, parseEther } from "viem";
import type { Hex } from "viem";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS } from "./tapscore";

const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);
const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env["PROJECT_OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY"] as Hex);
const walletClient = createWalletClient({ account, chain: pepuMainnet, transport: http() });

// The registry's paymasterV2 entry is the deployed paymaster; the helpers default to it. It is passed explicitly here
// (GET /v2/contract on the service returns it too). Override with PEPU_PAYMASTER_V2_ADDRESS.
const paymaster = getAddress(process.env["PEPU_PAYMASTER_V2_ADDRESS"] ?? "0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D");
const appId = process.env["PRIVY_APP_ID"] as string;
const projectId = computeProjectId(appId); // keccak256(bytes(appId)), case-sensitive

export async function registerClaimConfigureFund() {
  // The paymaster service defaults to https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com (override with PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL).
  const api = createPaymasterApi();

  // 1. Sign in with the wallet that should own the project (SIWE, 1 hour session).
  await api.v2.loginWithWallet((message) => account.signMessage({ message }), {
    address: account.address,
    domain: process.env["PEPU_SIWE_DOMAIN"] as string,
  });

  // 2. Prove control of the Privy app, then submit the claim on-chain. The claim sets the owner ONLY.
  const verified = await requestClaimAttestation(api, {
    appId,
    newOwner: account.address,
    privyAppSecret: process.env["PRIVY_APP_SECRET"] as string,
  });
  const claim = encodeClaimFromVerification(verified, { paymaster });
  await sendPaymasterCalls(walletClient, [claim], { publicClient });

  // 3. Nothing is sponsored until the owner sets targets and both daily limits.
  const { calls } = configureProject({
    appId,
    paymaster,
    targets: [TAPSCORE_ADDRESS],
    dailyLimitWei: parseEther("100"), // project budget per day
    senderDailyLimitWei: parseEther("25"), // per wallet; must exceed one first-operation reservation (about 21 PEPU)
  });
  await sendPaymasterCalls(walletClient, calls, { publicClient });

  // 4. Deposits are ONE-WAY. depositFor refuses an unclaimed project by default (catches a mistyped app id).
  await depositFor({ walletClient, publicClient, appId, amountWei: parseEther("25"), paymaster });

  // 5. Index the project to get credentials (client token is browser-safe, the server key is not).
  const registered = await api.v2.projects.register({ appId, allowedOrigins: ["https://app.example.com"] });

  const state = await readProject(publicClient, projectId, { paymaster, checkTargets: [TAPSCORE_ADDRESS] });
  return {
    claimed: state.claimed,
    limitsConfigured: state.limitsConfigured,
    balance: state.balance,
    // Paste into the Privy "Paymaster URL" field, or pass to a viem paymaster client.
    erc7677Url: buildErc7677Url({ baseUrl: api.baseUrl, token: registered.token }),
  };
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/v2-deposit-and-claim.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` on every v2 helper | The registry has no `paymasterV2` address on the chain you passed (for example testnet) | Pass `paymaster` explicitly; on mainnet the registry holds the deployed v2 paymaster |
| Project claimed but nothing sponsored | `setTargets` and both limits not set | Run `configureProject` |
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED` on deposit | Mistyped app id, or not yet claimed | Check the case-sensitive id; claim first |
| `PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` from a browser | The page origin is not in the project's allowed origins | Add the exact scheme, host and port |

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/combo

# /combo

`@pepu-chain/sdk/combo` is the combination of all three pillars: Google sign-in, one scoped on-chain session, then actions with no popup and no user gas. The server entry (`/combo`) gives you five route handlers; the browser entry (`/combo/react`) gives you one hook. This is the shortest path to the product experience PEPU is built for.

An on-chain Kernel session key plus sponsorship, end to end (the `sponsored-session-app` template). The bundler defaults to the hosted `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`. The paymaster needs a project token: set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project server key>` (a secret, server only) or pass `endpoints.paymasterToken`. You bring a project: claim, deposit, token.

`/combo` is Path 1 (ZeroDev-native): the SDK builds the Kernel account, so Privy Smart Wallets is not needed. [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md) compares it with the other setups.

## Import, peers and boundary

| Entry | Server or client | Peer dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/combo` | **Server only** (`CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` in a browser) | `@privy-io/node`, `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`, `viem` |
| `@pepu-chain/sdk/combo/react` | Client only | `react`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, the `@zerodev/*` peers |

Secrets read on the server: `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, and the bundler and paymaster URLs (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` can embed an app key, so treat it as a secret). The session private key is generated and held on the server and never reaches the browser. The browser's only signing job is the one owner signature that grants the session.

## The flow

1. `prepare`: the server creates a session key, decides the expiry, and returns only the key's address, the expiry and the scope.
2. The browser asks the owner (the Privy embedded wallet) for ONE EIP-712 signature. No gas.
3. `activate`: the server checks the approval is for this user's smart account and exactly the key, scope and expiry it issued, then stores it.
4. `act`: the server signs one sponsored UserOperation with the session key. The scope is enforced on-chain by the call and timestamp policies; the paymaster pays the gas.
5. `revoke`: deletes the key and approval from the server immediately. The on-chain grant lapses at its expiry, and only the deleted key could use it.

## Exports: `/combo`

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` | `<I>(o: SponsoredSessionRoutesOptions<I>) => SponsoredSessionRoutes` | The five handlers: `prepare.POST`, `activate.POST`, `status.GET`, `act.POST`, `revoke.POST` |
| `assertCallsInScope` | `(scope: Pick<KernelSessionScope, "calls">, calls: readonly Call[]) => void` | Throws `POLICY_UNSCOPED` (403) unless every call hits an allowed target, selector and value. Pure; used by `act` and exported for custom routes |
| `createMemoryStore`, `isLive`, `SessionStore`, `SessionRecord` | | Dev-grade store. See [/session/kernel](session-kernel.md) |
| `resolveSessionMinutes` | `(raw) => number` | Default 15, clamped 1..1440 |
| Types | `SponsoredSessionRoutesOptions`, `SponsoredSessionRoutes`, `ComboUser`, `ComboAuthenticate`, `SponsoredActResult`, `KernelSessionCall`, `KernelSessionScope` | |

`SponsoredSessionRoutesOptions<I>`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `scope` | `{ calls: readonly KernelSessionCall[]; targetEnv? }`. Enforced on-chain. An empty target (unset env variable) answers `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` at request time, naming `targetEnv` |
| `store` | Where session records, including the private key, live. `createMemoryStore()` for development only |
| `act` | `{ parse(body): I; buildCalls(input, { kernelAddress, ownerAddress }): Call[] }`. Every call is re-checked against `scope` before sponsoring |
| `endpoints?` | `{ bundlerUrl?, paymasterUrl?, paymasterToken? }`. The bundler defaults to env, then the hosted bundler. The paymaster needs a complete ERC-7677 URL (`paymasterUrl` or `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`) or a project `paymasterToken`, built against the hosted paymaster base |
| `forwardPrivyToken?` | Default `true`: forwards the request's `Authorization: Bearer` Privy token to the paymaster as ERC-7677 `context.privyAccessToken`. The v2 free tier needs it; a project paying from its own deposit ignores it. Set `false` if your paymaster URL is not a PEPU policy service you trust with the token |
| `minutes?` | Session length, default `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` then 15 |
| `privy?`, `authenticate?` | Privy client and custom auth. Default: `requireUser` from [/privy/server](privy-server.md) |
| `publicClient?` | Chain reads. Default viem on the PEPU RPC (`PEPU_RPC_URL` aware) |

Route behavior: `activate` answers 409 `SESSION_NONE` with nothing pending, 410 `SESSION_EXPIRED` for an expired offer, 400 `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH` for a wrong approval. `act` answers 409 `SESSION_NONE` without a live session and 429 while another action is running. `status` never returns the key or the approval. Calling `prepare` again replaces any pending or active session. A brand-new user's embedded wallet exists in the browser a moment before Privy's server lists it, so with the default authentication the routes look the user up again (`provisioningWait`, default 3 retries, 400 ms times the attempt number); if the wallet is still not visible, `status` answers a normal `{ active: false, provisioning: true }` and the other routes a retryable 409 `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED`.

```ts
// The combination, server: Google login + on-chain session key + sponsored gas.
// SERVER ONLY. See docs/sdk/combo.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-session.md
// Needs PRIVY_APP_SECRET and PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL (https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project server key>).
// PEPU_BUNDLER_URL defaults to https://bundler.pepeunchained.com.
import { createMemoryStore, createSponsoredSessionRoutes } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo";
import type { SessionStore } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

// DEV ONLY. The store holds session private keys: production needs a persistent
// SessionStore with sessionPrivateKey encrypted at rest.
const store: SessionStore = createMemoryStore();

export const routes = createSponsoredSessionRoutes({
  scope: { calls: [{ target: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }] },
  store,
  act: {
    parse: () => ({}),
    buildCalls: () => [{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }],
  },
});

// app/api/session/prepare/route.ts   export const { POST } = routes.prepare;
// app/api/session/activate/route.ts  export const { POST } = routes.activate;
// app/api/session/status/route.ts    export const { GET } = routes.status;
// app/api/session/act/route.ts       export const { POST } = routes.act;
// app/api/session/revoke/route.ts    export const { POST } = routes.revoke;
export const { prepare, activate, status, act, revoke } = routes;
```

Source: `docs/snippets/combo-server.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Exports: `/combo/react`

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `useSponsoredSession` | `<I = undefined, O = unknown>(o: { scope; endpoints?; authFetch?; publicClient?; pollMs?; provisioningRetryDelaysMs? }) => { phase; statusLoading; owner?; smartAccount?; scope?; expiresAt?; actions?; grant(); act(input?); revoke(); refetch(); error? }` | The whole session flow for a component |
| `grantKernelSession` | `(p: { authFetch; publicClient; owner; scope; endpoints? }) => Promise<PreparedSession>` | The grant outside React: prepare, owner signs, activate |
| `deriveSessionPhase` | `(p: { authenticated; hasWallet; validUntil?; nowSeconds; granting?; hasError? }) => SponsoredSessionPhase` | Pure phase logic |
| `DEFAULT_SESSION_ENDPOINTS` | `{ prepare, activate, status, act, revoke }` | Defaults match `app/api/session/<name>/route.ts` |
| Types | `SponsoredSessionPhase`, `PreparedSession`, `SponsoredSessionStatus`, `SponsoredSessionEndpoints`, `UseSponsoredSessionOptions`, `SponsoredActResult` | |

`phase` is `signed-out`, `provisioning`, `ready`, `granting`, `active`, `expired` or `error`. While `statusLoading` is true, `phase` is `ready` only because nothing is known yet: render a spinner, not the "start a session" card. `statusLoading` also stays true while the server cannot see a just-created wallet yet: the hook re-checks with backoff (0.5 s to 5 s, about 30 s) and shows no error for that state, and `grant()` retries `prepare` for about 6.5 s before surfacing `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED`. `useSponsoredSession` rebuilds the policies from the same `scope` the server uses, and the server rejects any difference with `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH`.

```tsx
// The combination, client: one owner signature, then actions with no popup and no gas.
// See docs/sdk/combo.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-session.md
import { describeKernelSessionScope } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel";
import type { KernelSessionCall } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel";
import { useSponsoredSession } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo/react";
import type { SponsoredActResult } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo/react";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

// The browser rebuilds the policies from the same scope the server uses.
const calls: KernelSessionCall[] = [{ target: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }];
const scope = { calls };

export function SponsoredSession() {
  const { phase, statusLoading, owner, smartAccount, expiresAt, grant, act, revoke, error } = useSponsoredSession<
    undefined,
    SponsoredActResult
  >({ scope });

  if (statusLoading) return <p>Checking session</p>;
  const preview = describeKernelSessionScope({ calls, validUntil: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 15 * 60 });

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Owner (signs once): {owner}</p>
      <p>Smart account (sends, holds assets): {smartAccount}</p>

      {phase === "ready" || phase === "expired" ? (
        <div>
          <p>This session may call: {preview.calls.map((c) => c.signature).join(", ")}</p>
          <button onClick={() => void grant()}>Start session</button>
        </div>
      ) : null}

      {phase === "active" ? (
        <div>
          <p>Active until {expiresAt}</p>
          <button onClick={() => void act().then((r) => console.log(r.explorerUrl))}>Tap, no popup, no gas</button>
          <button onClick={() => void revoke()}>End session</button>
        </div>
      ) : null}

      {error ? (
        <p>
          {error.code}: {error.hint}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/combo-react.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Gas reserved per action

The paymaster policy service reserves worst-case cost per operation: about 20.5 PEPU for a session's first operation (it deploys the account and enables the permission) and about 6.9 PEPU after (`SESSION_GAS_RESERVATION_PEPU`). The real first-session cost measured was about 12.8 PEPU for two operations. Size per-user hourly and daily caps above the reservation or users hit a cap error after their first action.

## Errors

| Code | HTTP | When |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` | 401 | Bad or missing Privy token |
| `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED` | 409 | The user has no embedded wallet yet, or Privy's server does not list it yet (retryable; the hook retries it for you) |
| `SESSION_NONE` | 409 | `activate` with nothing pending, `act` without a live session |
| `SESSION_EXPIRED` | 410 | An expired offer or session |
| `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH` | 400 | The approval is not for the issued key, scope and expiry |
| `POLICY_UNSCOPED` | 403 | A call outside the scope |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` | 500 | Unset call target or Privy variable (request time) |
| `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` | | `/combo` imported in a browser bundle |
| `BUNDLER_*`, `PAYMASTER_*` | varies | Sponsorship failures, mapped by `describeUserOpFailure`. See [SDK Error Catalog](errors.md) |

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Sessions vanish after a deploy | `createMemoryStore` is lost on restart | Implement `SessionStore` on a database with the key encrypted at rest |
| 429 on `act` | Another action is in flight for the user | Wait; the store's `tryLock` serializes per user. A multi-instance deployment needs a distributed lock |
| `PAYMASTER_CAP` after the first action | Spend caps below the reservation | Raise caps above 20.5 PEPU |
| `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | The contract is not on the paymaster allowlist | Add it to the project's targets |

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: which one to use](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Sponsored Session: No Popup, No Gas](../onboarding/sponsored-session.md)
- [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md)
- [Sponsored Session in One Flow](../recipes/sponsored-session.md)
- [Sponsored Session App template](../templates/sponsored-session-app.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/doctor

# /doctor

`@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor` runs project readiness checks: environment variables, Privy app id format, chain RPC, bundler and paymaster reachability, and the Privy dashboard settings. It never returns or logs a value from your environment: presence and length only.

It backs the CLI doctor, the MCP tools `pepu_check_env` and `pepu_check_privy_config`, and the `/pepu-doctor` command.

## Import, peers and boundary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Import | `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor` |
| Server or client | Node or any runtime with `fetch`. Use it in scripts and server code; it reads an env map you pass in |
| Peer dependencies | None (the key generator uses WebCrypto) |

## Exports

| Export | Signature | What it abstracts |
|---|---|---|
| `runDoctor` | `(o: RunDoctorOptions) => Promise<DoctorReport>` | Every check in one call. `RunDoctorOptions`: `env`, `template?`, `pillars?`, `fetch?`, `offline?`, `checkPrivyDashboard?` |
| `checkPepuEnv` | `(o: { env; template?; pillars? }) => EnvCheckResult` | Per-variable verdict: `ok`, `missing`, `placeholder` or `malformed`, with `secret`, `length`, `required` and a `fix`. Never the value |
| `checkChainRpc` | `(o?: { rpcUrl?; fetch? }) => Promise<DoctorCheck>` | The RPC answers and reports chain 97741 |
| `checkPrivyAppIdFormat` | `(appId: string \| undefined) => DoctorCheck` | `PRIVY_APP_ID_PATTERN`: a leading `c` then 20 to 29 lowercase alphanumerics |
| `checkSponsorshipEndpoints` | `(o?: { env?; fetch? }) => Promise<DoctorCheck[]>` | The hosted bundler and paymaster service are the defaults and are probed (the paymaster at `<base>/health`); a URL that resolves to nothing is a skip, and one that is set but unreachable is a failure. URLs never appear in messages |
| `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS` | `Record<string, TemplateRequirement>` | Per-template env and Privy dashboard needs: `requiredEnv`, `optionalEnv`, `requiredAnyOf?`, `pillars`, `privyDashboard` |
| `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` | `() => Promise<PrivyAuthorizationKeyPair>` | A P-256 key pair in the format Privy expects (`publicKey` base64 SPKI, `privateKey` base64 PKCS8). Writes and logs nothing. Register the public half in the dashboard, keep the private half in server env only |
| Types | `DoctorCheck`, `DoctorReport`, `EnvCheckResult`, `EnvItem`, `EnvItemStatus`, `CheckStatus`, `Pillar`, `PrivyDashboardChecker`, `PrivyDashboardRequirementKey`, `TemplateRequirement`, `RunDoctorOptions`, `PrivyAuthorizationKeyPair` | |

`Pillar` is `login`, `wallet`, `session`, `sponsorship`, `gate` or `mint`. `CheckStatus` is `pass`, `fail`, `warn` or `skip`. `DoctorReport` is `{ ok, checks, env }` and `ok` is true when no check failed.

Plug in the Privy dashboard check with `privyDashboardChecker` from [/privy](privy.md). Without it the report carries a `privy.dashboard` skip.

## Example

```ts
// Readiness checks for a project. See docs/sdk/doctor.md
import { runDoctor } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor";
import { privyDashboardChecker } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";

export async function check(): Promise<boolean> {
  const report = await runDoctor({
    env: process.env,
    template: "sponsored-session-app",
    // Adds the Privy dashboard checks (login methods, allowed origins, wallet creation setting).
    checkPrivyDashboard: privyDashboardChecker,
  });
  // Env values never appear in the report: presence and length only.
  for (const c of report.checks) {
    if (c.status === "fail" || c.status === "warn") console.log(c.status, c.id, c.fix ?? c.message);
  }
  return report.ok;
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/doctor.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Errors

`runDoctor` reports problems as `DoctorCheck`s and does not throw for a failing project. An unknown `template` becomes a failing `template` check. `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` can reject if WebCrypto is unavailable.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `env.PEPU_BUNDLER_URL is missing` for a sponsorship template | The variable was cleared, or the template needs an explicit value | Set it to `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (the hosted bundler) or your own bundler (local default `http://localhost:4337`) |
| `privy.dashboard` is skipped | No checker injected, unknown template, or no app id | Pass `checkPrivyDashboard: privyDashboardChecker` |
| A check says `placeholder` | The value is still `your-...` or `<...>` from `.env.example` | Replace it with the real value |

## Related

- [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md)
- [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md)
- [/privy](privy.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/sdk/api-reference

# Generated API Reference

A complete index of every export of `@pepu-chain/sdk` version 0.2.4, one table per import path, derived from the compiled type declarations. Use it to confirm a symbol exists before you import it. Signatures, behavior, errors and examples are on the per-subpath pages linked from each section.

The lists below were extracted from the built package with the TypeScript compiler API, so they match the shipped exports and not the source comments.

## How this page is produced

This index comes from a one-off extraction, not a typedoc build. typedoc would add a dev dependency and a config outside `docs/`, and its per-symbol pages would duplicate the signatures that the subpath pages already carry next to their examples and error codes. Two sources keep it honest:

- The SDK test `packages/sdk/test/exports.test.ts` fails when the set of import paths changes.
- The MCP tool `pepu_sdk_exports` returns the export list live from the installed package.

When an export changes, update this page and the subpath page in the same change.

## How it relates to the subpath pages

| You want | Go to |
|---|---|
| Which import path holds a symbol | This page |
| Signature, what it abstracts, server or client, peers, errors, an example | The subpath page, linked under each heading |
| Which subpath for which pillar | [SDK Overview and Reference](reference.md#pillar-to-subpath-decision-table) |
| Error codes | [SDK Error Catalog](errors.md) |

# SDK Error Catalog


Everything `@pepu-chain/sdk` throws is a `PepuError` subclass with a stable `code`, a one-sentence `hint` and a `docsUrl`. This page is the catalog as a table, with the helpers that read it: `explainError`, `toPepuError`, `toErrorBody` and `toErrorResponse`. The long-form entries, with anchors, are on [Error Reference](../reference/errors.md).

## Prerequisites

- `@pepu-chain/sdk` installed. The error helpers are exported from the package root.

## Using the catalog

```ts
import { PepuError, explainError, toErrorResponse } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

// Explain anything: an Error, an error message, or raw revert data (0x...). Pure; never throws.
export function describe(e: unknown): string {
  const x = explainError(e);
  return `${x.code}: ${x.fix} (${x.docsUrl})`;
}

// Route handlers: return the typed error as JSON with the catalog's HTTP status.
export async function POST(): Promise<Response> {
  try {
    // Positional constructor: new PepuError(code, message?, { hint?, docsUrl?, retryable?, status?, details?, cause? })
    throw new PepuError("CONFIG_MISSING_ENV", "PEPU_BUNDLER_URL is not set.", { hint: "Set it in .env.local." });
  } catch (e) {
    return toErrorResponse(e); // { error: { code, message, hint } }
  }
}
```

| Helper | Does |
|---|---|
| `explainError(e)` | Returns `{ code, title, cause, fix, docsUrl, matched }` for an error, a message or revert data. First matching catalog entry wins. |
| `toPepuError(e, ctx?)` | Wraps anything thrown into the right `PepuError` subclass. `PepuError`s pass through. |
| `toErrorBody(e)` | The `{ error: { code, message, hint } }` JSON body. |
| `toErrorResponse(e)` | A `Response` with that body and the status from the table below. |
| `errorDocsUrl(code)` | `https://docs.pepeunchained.com/reference/errors#<CODE>` |
| `mapPaymasterReason(reason)` | Paymaster denial reason to catalog code. See [Error Reference](../reference/errors.md#paymaster-denial-reasons). |

## Catalog

| Code | HTTP | Retryable | Title | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="CONFIG_BAD_URL"></a>[`CONFIG_BAD_URL`](../reference/errors.md#CONFIG_BAD_URL) | 500 | no | Invalid endpoint URL | A configured bundler, paymaster or RPC URL is not a valid http(s) URL. | Use a full URL such as https://bundler.example.com. |
| <a id="CONFIG_MISSING_ENV"></a>[`CONFIG_MISSING_ENV`](../reference/errors.md#CONFIG_MISSING_ENV) | 500 | no | Missing environment variable | A required environment variable is not set. | Set the listed variables (see .env.example) and restart the process. |
| <a id="CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH"></a>[`CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH`](../reference/errors.md#CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH) | 500 | no | Origin is not allowed by Privy | The page origin (scheme, host and port) is not in the Privy app's allowed origins. A different dev port is the usual cause. | Add the exact origin, including the port, to Privy dashboard Allowed origins. |
| <a id="CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN"></a>[`CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN`](../reference/errors.md#CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN) | 500 | no | Embedded wallet never appears after login | The dashboard's automatic embedded wallet creation is off, so createOnLogin never resolves. | Create the wallet server-side with the ensure-wallet route (createEnsureWalletRoute), or enable creation in the Privy dashboard. |
| <a id="CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD"></a>[`CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD`](../reference/errors.md#CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD) | 500 | no | Privy dashboard misconfiguration | A required Privy dashboard setting is missing. | Run checkPrivyDashboardConfig() and follow its fix list. |
| <a id="CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY"></a>[`CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY`](../reference/errors.md#CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY) | 500 | no | Server-only module imported in the browser | A server entry point was bundled into client code. | Import server entries only from route handlers, server actions and scripts. |
| <a id="AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN"></a>[`AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`](../reference/errors.md#AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN) | 401 | no | Invalid or missing Privy access token | The request carried no bearer token, or Privy could not verify it. | Send Authorization: Bearer <getAccessToken()> and verify the token server-side. |
| <a id="WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN"></a>[`WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN`](../reference/errors.md#WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN) | 400 | no | Coinbase Smart Wallet does not support PEPU | Coinbase Smart Wallet is a smart-contract wallet on chains it knows; PEPU (97741) is not one of them, and it floods the console with unsupported-chain errors. | Pin Coinbase to eoaOnly via createPepuPrivyConfig() from @pepu-chain/sdk/privy. |
| <a id="WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE"></a>[`WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE`](../reference/errors.md#WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE) | 400 | no | An injected browser wallet is the active account | wagmi's active account is a browser extension rather than the Privy embedded wallet. | Pin the embedded wallet with useActiveWalletPin() from @pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi. |
| <a id="WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED"></a>[`WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED`](../reference/errors.md#WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED) | 409 | yes | User has no embedded wallet yet | The user is signed in but no embedded Ethereum wallet exists. | Call the ensure-wallet route (useEnsureWallet or WalletGate) before acting. |
| <a id="PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741"></a>[`PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741`](../reference/errors.md#PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741) | 502 | no | Privy rejects server-side eth_sendTransaction on PEPU | Privy's server-side send path does not know chain 97741 and rejects it. Signing works; sending does not. | Sign with eth_signTransaction on the server and broadcast the raw transaction yourself (signAndBroadcast from @pepu-chain/sdk/session). |
| <a id="PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH"></a>[`PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH`](../reference/errors.md#PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH) | 500 | no | Privy authorization key does not match the wallet owner | Privy returned 401 'No valid authorization keys or user signing keys available': the server's PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY is not a signer on the wallet, or the key quorum id differs from the one the user granted. | Make sure PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY is the private half of the key whose quorum id is NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID, and that the user granted that quorum as a signer. |
| <a id="POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG"></a>[`POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG`](../reference/errors.md#POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG) | 400 | no | Privy policy or rule name is too long | Privy rejects policy and rule names of 50 or more characters (the real limit is 49). | Shorten the policy or rule name to 49 characters or fewer. |
| <a id="POLICY_UNSCOPED"></a>[`POLICY_UNSCOPED`](../reference/errors.md#POLICY_UNSCOPED) | 400 | no | Session policy is not scoped | A session policy needs a target contract, at least one function and an expiry. | Pass contractAddress, functions and expiresAtUnixSeconds to buildSessionPolicy(). |
| <a id="SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH"></a>[`SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH`](../reference/errors.md#SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH) | 409 | no | Session approval does not match | The approval was made for another account, permission id or mode. | Re-run prepare, have the owner sign again, then activate. |
| <a id="SESSION_EXPIRED"></a>[`SESSION_EXPIRED`](../reference/errors.md#SESSION_EXPIRED) | 410 | no | Session expired | The session's expiry has passed. | Grant a new session. |
| <a id="SESSION_NONE"></a>[`SESSION_NONE`](../reference/errors.md#SESSION_NONE) | 409 | no | No active session | The user has not granted a session, or it was revoked. | Ask the user to grant a session first. |
| <a id="BUNDLER_AA_FAILED"></a>[`BUNDLER_AA_FAILED`](../reference/errors.md#BUNDLER_AA_FAILED) | 502 | no | EntryPoint rejected the UserOperation | The EntryPoint reported FailedOp with an AAxx code during validation or execution. | Read the AAxx code: AA21 prefund missing, AA23 signature or validation reverted, AA25 invalid nonce, AA31/AA33/AA34 paymaster problems. |
| <a id="BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE"></a>[`BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE`](../reference/errors.md#BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE) | 502 | yes | Bundler or paymaster is unreachable | The request to the bundler or paymaster URL failed before any response. | Check PEPU_BUNDLER_URL and PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL. Use checkSponsorship() to see which one failed. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_API_ERROR"></a>[`PAYMASTER_API_ERROR`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_API_ERROR) | 502 | no | Paymaster API request failed | The paymaster API returned an error that has no more specific PEPU code. | Read error.details (HTTP status and the service's error code) and the OpenAPI spec for that route. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_CAP"></a>[`PAYMASTER_CAP`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_CAP) | 429 | yes | Sponsorship cap reached | A daily, per-sender or per-operation sponsorship cap was hit. | Wait for the cap window to reset, or raise the project's daily and sender limits. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_DENIED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_DENIED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_DENIED) | 403 | no | Paymaster denied the sponsorship | The paymaster rejected the credential or the sender (for example unknown_or_invalid_app_credential or sender_not_owned_by_token_user). | Check the app credential or token, and that the smart account belongs to the user whose access token you sent. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED) | 403 | no | Paymaster refused the call destination | The UserOperation targets a contract that is not on the project's target allowlist. | Add the contract to the project's targets, or sponsor only calls to allowed targets. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE"></a>[`PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE) | 429 | yes | Free tier cannot sponsor this operation | The free tier is disabled, its pool is empty, or the operation is larger than the per-op cap. | Deposit into your own project and use its credentials, or retry later. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED) | 401 | no | A verified Privy account is required | The free tier (and any project with requireIdentity on) only sponsors users with a verified Privy access token. | Send the user's Privy access token as Authorization: Bearer (or context.privyAccessToken for ERC-7677). |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE"></a>[`PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE) | 429 | yes | Sponsorship project has no balance | The project's paymaster deposit cannot cover this operation. | Deposit more PEPU to the project, then retry. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED) | 403 | no | Paymaster refused the request origin | The request Origin is not on the project's allowlist. | Add the exact origin (scheme, host and port) to the project's allowed origins. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED) | 409 | no | Sponsorship project is not claimed on-chain | Deposits can sit in an unclaimed project, but nothing is sponsored until its owner has claimed it on-chain (the contract reports ProjectNotClaimed, the service project_not_claimed_onchain). | Prove the Privy app (requestClaimAttestation from @pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server), call claimProject, then configureProject (setTargets, setDailyLimit, setSenderDailyLimit). |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED) | 403 | no | Project owner changed since the credentials were issued | The on-chain owner of the project is no longer the address the off-chain credentials were issued to (an ownership transfer or re-claim completed). | As the new owner, sign in with SIWE, register the project again and rotate the client token and server key. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED) | 403 | no | Sponsorship project is paused | The project owner paused sponsorship on-chain. | The owner can resume it with setPaused(projectId, false). |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED) | 429 | yes | Paymaster API rate limit | Too many requests to the paymaster API from this IP or account. | Back off for the Retry-After interval (error.details.retryAfterSeconds when present). |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED"></a>[`PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED) | 401 | no | Paymaster owner session missing or expired | Owner endpoints need a SIWE session token (1 h lifetime) for the project's current on-chain owner. | Call loginWithWallet() on the paymaster API client, then retry. |
| <a id="PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE"></a>[`PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE`](../reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE) | 502 | yes | Paymaster service is unreachable | The request to the paymaster service failed before any response (network error, DNS failure or timeout). | Check PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL and your network. The hosted service is https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com; run checkSponsorship() or probePaymaster() for detail. |
| <a id="MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS"></a>[`MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS`](../reference/errors.md#MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS) | 500 | no | Canonical Multicall3 address used on PEPU | PEPU's Multicall3 is not at the canonical 0xcA11...CA11 address. | Use getMulticall3() or pepuMulticall() from @pepu-chain/sdk, or the pepuMainnet chain object, which carries the right address. |
| <a id="TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT"></a>[`TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT`](../reference/errors.md#TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT) | 502 | yes | Gas limit too low | Nitro gas estimation undershoots on PEPU: the L1 data component is not covered by the plain estimate. | Add headroom to the estimate, 20% via withGasLimitBuffer() from @pepu-chain/sdk/session. |
| <a id="TX_NONCE_RACE"></a>[`TX_NONCE_RACE`](../reference/errors.md#TX_NONCE_RACE) | 409 | yes | Nonce conflict | Two transactions raced for one nonce, or a replacement was underpriced. | Serialize sends per account (a lock), re-read the pending nonce, and retry. |
| <a id="TX_REVERTED"></a>[`TX_REVERTED`](../reference/errors.md#TX_REVERTED) | 502 | no | Transaction reverted | The contract call reverted. | Decode the revert reason with explainError(<revert data>) and check arguments, allowances and balances. |
| <a id="UNKNOWN"></a>[`UNKNOWN`](../reference/errors.md#UNKNOWN) | 500 | no | Unknown error | The error did not match any known PEPU failure. | Read the original message. Run pepu_known_gotchas in the MCP server, or search the docs. |

## What to expect

- Messages name environment variables, never their values. Nothing in this catalog is a secret.
- Order in the catalog matters for `explainError`: specific entries match before general ones.

## Common failures

- `explainError` returns `UNKNOWN` for an error you expected to match: the SDK is older than the error text. Upgrade, or open the [Error Reference](../reference/errors.md) and search the symptom.

# Migration Notes

Upgrade notes for `@pepu-chain/sdk`. The only upgrade today is 0.1 to 0.2. It adds subpaths and keeps every 0.1 export, so no code has to change to upgrade, but one helper is deprecated and several hand-rolled patterns now have SDK replacements.

Every 0.1 export is still present in 0.2.4. The full list of changes is in the [Changelog](../reference/changelog.md).

## 0.1 to 0.2

### Breaking changes

None. Additive only.

### Deprecated

| 0.1 | Status in 0.2 | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| `getSponsorshipStatus(options?)` | Deprecated. Still exported from `@pepu-chain/sdk` and `/aa`. Always returns `{ available: false, reason }` and ignores `bundlerUrl` | `checkSponsorship(options?)`, a live probe of the bundler and paymaster |
| `useSponsorshipStatus(options?)` from `/react` | Deprecated for the same reason | `usePepuSponsorship({ pollMs? })` from `/aa/react` |

```ts
// 0.1
import { getSponsorshipStatus } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
const { available } = getSponsorshipStatus(); // always false

// 0.2
import { checkSponsorship, getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
const s = await checkSponsorship({ publicClient: getPublicClient(pepuMainnet) });
if (!s.available) console.log(s.reason, s.fixes);
```

`checkSponsorship` resolves the bundler and paymaster URLs from options, then env (`PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`), then the hosted defaults: the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and the hosted paymaster service base (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`). The complete ERC-7677 paymaster URL has no default because it embeds a project token. It probes both and reports `available`, `transport`, `reason` and `fixes`. It never throws for an unreachable service.

### New subpaths

| Subpath | Replaces this hand-rolled code |
|---|---|
| `/privy`, `/privy/react`, `/privy/wagmi`, `/privy/server` | Your own `PrivyProvider` config, wallet gate, wagmi config, active-wallet pin and ensure-wallet route. See [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](../recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md) |
| `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react` | Your own session policy builder, grant, status and revoke routes and sign-then-broadcast code. See [Grant a Session](../recipes/grant-a-session.md) |
| `/session/kernel` | Hand-built ZeroDev permission validators and approval handling |
| `/aa`, `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react` | Your own bundler and paymaster clients, the Alto fee estimator, UserOperation error decoding and receipt parsing. See [Send a Sponsored Transaction](../recipes/sponsored-send.md) |
| `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server` | Direct calls to the policy service and hand-encoded v2 contract calls |
| `/combo`, `/combo/react` | The five session routes and the browser flow in the `sponsored-session-app` template |
| `/doctor` | Ad hoc env checks |
| `/server` | Kept as a stable path that re-exports the pure session policy helpers. New server code lives in `/privy/server`, `/session/server` and `/paymaster/server` |

### New exports on existing paths

On `@pepu-chain/sdk`: the error model (`PepuError` and subclasses, `explainError`, `toPepuError`, `toErrorBody`, `toErrorResponse`, `PEPU_ERROR_CATALOG`), `resolvePepuEndpoints` and `PEPU_ENV`, `pepuMulticall` and `getMulticall3`, `getPermit2` and the Permit2 typed-data builders, `explorerLinks`, `getPepuAddresses`, `formatUnitsCompact`, `erc20Abi` and `erc721Abi`, `multicall3Abi`, `permit2Abi`, `checkSponsorship`. The registry gained `kernelImplementation`, `kernelEcdsaSignerModule`, `kernelCallPolicyV004`, `kernelTimestampPolicy`, `tapScore`, `paymasterV1` and `paymasterV2` (pending).

### Behavior changes to know about

- `pepuContracts.multicall3` was always PEPU's own address. Code that hard-coded the canonical address `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` was always wrong on PEPU. Use `pepuMulticall` or `getMulticall3`, which throws `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` rather than use it.
- Everything the SDK throws now carries a stable `code`. Replace string matching on messages with `error.code` or `explainError(e)`.
- Route factories (`createSessionRoutes`, `createSessionActionRoute`, `createSponsoredSessionRoutes`) answer `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` as JSON at request time when the contract address is empty, instead of throwing at module load.

### Checklist

1. Upgrade: `npm install @pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.4 viem`.
2. Replace `getSponsorshipStatus` and `useSponsorshipStatus` with `checkSponsorship` and `usePepuSponsorship`.
3. Install the optional peers for the subpaths you adopt (see the [peer table](reference.md#subpath-map-and-peer-dependencies)).
4. Swap hand-rolled infrastructure for the SDK function. Keep your code where the SDK has no equivalent.
5. Run the doctor: `runDoctor({ env: process.env })` from [/doctor](doctor.md).

## Related

- [Changelog](../reference/changelog.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](reference.md)
- [SDK Error Catalog](errors.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/mcp/index

# MCP Server Overview

`@pepu-chain/mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server that gives a coding agent a way to check PEPU-specific facts and run PEPU-specific checks instead of guessing. It has 33 tools, 6 prompts and 5 resources. This page explains what it is for, what it will and will not do, and where the details live.

The sponsorship probes target the hosted bundler and paymaster service by default. The v2 paymaster tools default to the registry's deployed paymaster.

## What and why

Coding agents are strong at generic EVM patterns and weak at chain-specific facts. A wrong chain ID, an invented contract address, or the canonical Multicall3 address (which has no code on PEPU) are all failures an agent can produce with confidence. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md).

The server answers those questions from the source of truth:

- Addresses, chain facts and endpoints come from `@pepu-chain/sdk` (`getPepuAddresses`, `pepuMainnet`, `resolvePepuEndpoints`).
- Failures are explained from the SDK's shared error catalog (`explainError`).
- Env and Privy checks use the SDK's doctor (`checkPepuEnv`, `checkPrivyDashboardConfig`).
- Generated code comes from export-checked SDK snippets, so an agent wires the SDK instead of hand-rolling infrastructure.

It is not a generic Blockscout wrapper. pepuscan is a Blockscout instance, and the official Blockscout MCP server covers generic chain-data lookups well. This server adds only what is PEPU-specific or what composes several RPC and Blockscout calls into one answer. PEPU is a chain, not "an AI chain": this is tooling that helps builders, human or agent-assisted, get PEPU facts right.

## What it contains

| Part | Count | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Tools | 33 | [Tool Reference](tools.md) |
| Prompts | 6 | [Resources and Prompts](resources-and-prompts.md) |
| Resources | 5 (`pepu://chain-facts`, `pepu://addresses`, `pepu://docs/{slug}`, `pepu://skills/{name}`, `pepu://sdk/exports`) | [Resources and Prompts](resources-and-prompts.md) |

## Security model

- **No tool returns a secret.** `pepu_check_env` reports presence and length only. A secret-leak test in the package checks tool outputs for leaks. URLs that may carry a credential, such as the paymaster URL, are reduced to their host.
- **No private key, ever.** The server holds no key and has no tool that signs or sends a transaction. `pepu_prepare_project_tx` and `pepu_encode_calls` return unsigned data. There is no `pepu_send_transaction` tool, by design.
- **Local execution.** The server runs on your machine over stdio, started by your client. It talks to the public PEPU RPC, pepuscan's public API and, if you configure them, your bundler and paymaster. Docs, skills, template metadata and the SDK export list are bundled into the package, so those lookups make no network call.
- **File access is narrow.** Only two tools touch your filesystem, and both take absolute paths only, refuse `..`, filesystem roots and system folders, and refuse to overwrite. `pepu_generate_authorization_key` writes only `.env*` files and never returns the private key.
- **Annotations on every tool.** All four MCP hints (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`) are set, so a client can auto-approve reads and ask before writes.
- **Mainnet only.** Chain `97741`. Some tools accept `network: "testnet"` only to explain that it is out of scope.

## Read versus write tools

| Class | Tools |
|---|---|
| Read-only, no network | `pepu_known_gotchas`, `pepu_decode_error`, `pepu_explain_error`, `pepu_verify_contract_guide`, `pepu_list_templates`, `pepu_check_env` (reads local env files), `pepu_session_policy`, `pepu_encode_calls`, `pepu_prepare_project_tx`, `pepu_get_docs`, `pepu_sdk_snippet`, `pepu_sdk_exports` |
| Read-only, remote | `pepu_chain_info`, `pepu_health_check`, `pepu_gas_price`, `pepu_estimate_gas_cost`, `pepu_read_contract`, `pepu_check_contract_deployed`, `pepu_get_token_info`, `pepu_get_address_overview`, `pepu_get_transaction`, `pepu_search`, `pepu_smart_account_info`, `pepu_verify_contract_status`, `pepu_bundler_health`, `pepu_paymaster_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_project_balance`, `pepu_explain_tx`, `pepu_decode_tx_logs`, `pepu_check_privy_config` |
| Write (local files only) | `pepu_scaffold_app` (creates a new project folder), `pepu_generate_authorization_key` (writes one env key) |

Neither write tool is destructive. Neither can overwrite an existing project or an existing authorization key without an explicit flag.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| An agent still uses the canonical Multicall3 address | The server is not connected or the agent did not call it | Check the connection ([Install per Client](install.md)) and have the agent call `pepu_check_contract_deployed` or `pepu_chain_info`. |
| An agent says sponsorship works or does not work from memory | It skipped the live check | Call `pepu_sponsorship_status` and report what it says. |

- [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md)

# Install the MCP Server per Client

Exact configuration for each supported client, the environment variables the server reads, and how to confirm the connection. Use this page when you want the `pepu` tools in your editor or agent.

`@pepu-chain/mcp` runs over stdio from npm with no clone and no build. It needs no API key.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer. The server runs as `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`.
- A client that supports MCP over stdio.
- Optional: the three environment variables below. The server works without any of them.

## Environment variables the server reads

| Variable | Used by | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PEPU_RPC_URL` | every RPC-backed tool (through the SDK's `resolvePepuEndpoints`) | public Conduit RPC for chain `97741` | Use an authenticated endpoint here. A malformed value falls back to the public default. Mainnet only: the testnet RPC is fixed. |
| `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `pepu_bundler_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_health_check`, `pepu_explain_tx` (UserOperation hashes) | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` | The hosted bundler. Local default for your own service is `http://localhost:4337`. |
| `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `pepu_paymaster_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_health_check` | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (service base) | The probes target the hosted paymaster service base. Set this to a full ERC-7677 URL (`.../v2/paymaster/<token>`) to probe a project URL; local default for your own service is `http://localhost:8788`. May embed a credential, so it is only ever reported as a host. |

One more variable exists for development of the server itself, not for normal use: `PEPU_CREATE_APP_BIN` points `pepu_scaffold_app` at a local build of the create-pepu-app CLI. See [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md) for the full list across the kit.

## Claude Code

Plugin (recommended). The plugin wires the MCP server for you and adds the skills, the six slash commands and the builder subagent:

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

Claude Code asks you to trust the plugin before it loads. The plugin passes `PEPU_RPC_URL`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` from your shell environment to the server (empty when unset). See [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md).

Fallback, MCP server only:

```bash
claude mcp add pepu -- npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp
```

To pass environment variables with the fallback:

```bash
claude mcp add pepu -e PEPU_RPC_URL=https://<your-rpc> -- npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp
```

Scaffolded apps from [create-pepu-app](../cli/create-pepu-app.md) also offer the plugin on first open through `.claude/settings.json`. See [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md).

## Cursor

Create `.cursor/mcp.json` in the project (or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for all projects):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pepu": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Reload Cursor, then enable `pepu` under Settings, MCP.

## VS Code

Create `.vscode/mcp.json` in the workspace. VS Code uses a top-level key named `servers`, not `mcpServers`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "pepu": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Open the file in VS Code and use the Start action above the server entry, then use the tools in Copilot agent mode.

## Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Cline and other clients

Any client that launches a stdio MCP server accepts the same command. The usual shape is a JSON file with an `mcpServers` map:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pepu": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

| Client | Where the config lives |
|---|---|
| Windsurf | `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` |
| Claude Desktop | `claude_desktop_config.json` (Settings, Developer, Edit Config) |
| Cline | The MCP servers panel, "Configure MCP Servers" (`cline_mcp_settings.json`) |
| Anything else | Generic stdio: command `npx`, arguments `-y @pepu-chain/mcp`, no environment variables required |

Config file locations and menu names belong to the clients and can change. If one does not match, the command and arguments above are the part that matters.

To pass environment variables, add an `env` object next to `args`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pepu": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"],
      "env": { "PEPU_RPC_URL": "https://<your-rpc>" }
    }
  }
}
```

For a global install or local development, replace the command:

```bash
npm install -g @pepu-chain/mcp          # then command: pepu-mcp
```

```json
{ "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/packages/mcp/dist/index.js"] }
```

## Verifying the connection

1. Ask your agent: "List the tools from the pepu MCP server." You should see 33 tools whose names start with `pepu_`.
2. Ask it to call `pepu_health_check`. A healthy answer reports the mainnet RPC reachable at chain id `97741` and pepuscan reachable.
3. Ask it to call `pepu_chain_info`. It returns the network facts and contract table.
4. In Claude Code, `/mcp` lists the server and its connection state.

From a checkout of the repository you can also list every tool, resource and prompt over stdio with `pnpm smoke` in `packages/mcp` (run `pnpm build` first). It makes real network calls.

## What to expect

- The first launch downloads the package through `npx`, which takes a few seconds. Later launches use the cache.
- Pin a version if you need reproducibility: `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp@0.2.8`. The plugin pins `@pepu-chain/mcp@^0.2`.
- No tool needs a private key. The server never holds one.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The client shows the server as failed or never connects | Node.js older than 18, or `npx` not on the client's PATH | Install Node 18+, and on Windows try the `npx.cmd` command or an absolute path to `node`. |
| Tools are missing in VS Code | The config uses `mcpServers` instead of `servers`, or lacks `"type": "stdio"` | Use the VS Code shape shown above. |
| `pepu_bundler_health` says "not configured" | The default was cleared or `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` is empty in the server's environment | Set it in the client's `env` block, or in your shell before launching the client. |
| Env vars set in your shell are ignored | The client does not pass its environment to child processes | Put the variables in the client's `env` block. |
| Stale facts or docs | An old cached package version | Run `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp@latest`, or clear the npx cache. |

## Related

- [MCP Server Overview](index.md)
- [Tool Reference](tools.md)
- [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md)
- [Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes](../get-started/ai-assisted.md)
