Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/mcp/tools

# MCP Tool Reference

All 33 tools of `@pepu-chain/mcp`, derived from the tool registry in `packages/mcp/src/tools`: what each does, its inputs (from the zod schemas), what it returns, the SDK function it uses, its safety properties and an example call. Read this when you are wiring an agent to the server or when you need to know exactly what a tool will and will not do.

Every tool runs against live mainnet RPC and pepuscan. Tools that probe the bundler or paymaster target the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and the paymaster service base (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) by default; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` override them. Tools that touch the v2 paymaster default to the registry's deployed paymaster `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`; an explicit `paymaster` address overrides it.

## Prerequisites

- The server is installed in your client. See [Install per Client](install.md).
- For the sponsorship probes: `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` in the server's environment. Local development defaults are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`. See [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md).
- Mainnet only (chain `97741`). Several tools accept `network: "testnet"` only so they can explain that the testnet is out of scope instead of failing schema validation.

## How to read this page

Every tool declares four MCP annotation hints. A client uses them to decide what to auto-approve.

| Class | `readOnlyHint` | `openWorldHint` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Static read | true | false | Pure data or computation. No network, no files. |
| Remote read | true | true | Reads PEPU RPC, pepuscan or a configured bundler or paymaster. Changes nothing. |
| Write | false | true | Writes a file on your machine. Never destructive, never idempotent. Only two tools are in this class. |

Conventions shared by all tools:

- `response_format` is `"concise"` (default) or `"detailed"` wherever output can be large.
- Results are JSON text. Big integers are returned as decimal strings.
- Errors are actionable: what happened, why, and the fix.
- No tool returns a secret. URLs that may carry a credential are reduced to their host. See [MCP Server Overview](index.md#security-model).

## Tool index

| Tool | Group | Class | SDK function or source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pepu_chain_info` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | `getPepuAddresses` |
| `pepu_known_gotchas` | Chain and lookups | Static read | `PEPU_ERROR_CATALOG` |
| `pepu_health_check` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | `resolvePepuEndpoints`, `probeBundler`, `probePaymaster` |
| `pepu_gas_price` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | RPC (viem) |
| `pepu_estimate_gas_cost` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | RPC (viem) |
| `pepu_read_contract` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | RPC (viem) |
| `pepu_check_contract_deployed` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | RPC (`eth_getCode`) and the SDK registry |
| `pepu_get_token_info` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan plus RPC cross-check |
| `pepu_get_address_overview` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan |
| `pepu_get_transaction` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan |
| `pepu_search` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan |
| `pepu_smart_account_info` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | Kernel factory `getAddress` over RPC |
| `pepu_decode_error` | Chain and lookups | Static read | `explainError` |
| `pepu_verify_contract_guide` | Chain and lookups | Static read | static reference |
| `pepu_verify_contract_status` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan |
| `pepu_bundler_health` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `probeBundler` (`/aa`) |
| `pepu_paymaster_health` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `probePaymaster` (`/aa`) |
| `pepu_sponsorship_status` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `checkSponsorship` |
| `pepu_project_balance` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `readProject`, `computeProjectId` (`/paymaster`) |
| `pepu_explain_error` | Probe, status, explain | Static read | `explainError`, `mapPaymasterReason` |
| `pepu_explain_tx` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `explorerLinks`, `formatPepu`, `userOpEventFromReceipt` |
| `pepu_decode_tx_logs` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `explorerLinks` and viem `decodeEventLog` |
| `pepu_list_templates` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS` (`/doctor`) |
| `pepu_scaffold_app` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Write | create-pepu-app CLI, `checkPepuEnv` |
| `pepu_check_env` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | `checkPepuEnv` (`/doctor`) |
| `pepu_check_privy_config` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Remote read | `checkPrivyDashboardConfig` (`/privy`) |
| `pepu_generate_authorization_key` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Write | `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` (`/doctor`) |
| `pepu_session_policy` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | `buildSessionPolicy`, `buildKernelSessionPolicies` and the `describe*` helpers |
| `pepu_encode_calls` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | `encodeAggregate3`, `getMulticall3` |
| `pepu_prepare_project_tx` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | the `encode*` helpers and `configureProject` (`/paymaster`) |
| `pepu_get_docs` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | bundled docs snapshot |
| `pepu_sdk_snippet` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | bundled, export-checked snippets |
| `pepu_sdk_exports` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | bundled SDK export list |

The groups follow the registry: the original lookups first, then the SDK-backed probes and explainers, then generate, scaffold and docs.

---

## Chain facts and lookups

### `pepu_chain_info`

Network facts: chain ids, RPC and explorer URLs, native currency, ArbOS version, and which infrastructure contracts are deployed (Multicall3, Permit2, EntryPoint, Kernel factory, the verifying paymaster), including the sponsorship status. Call it first, before writing any PEPU chain config.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet`, `both` | `both` | |
| `verify_live` | boolean | `false` | Adds a live `eth_chainId` and `eth_gasPrice` call to confirm the cached facts. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds canonical-contract notes and the gotchas list. |

Returns network facts and the registry rows from `getPepuAddresses`. Safety: remote read. It lists the v2 paymaster as deployed and the v1 paymaster as retired.

```json
{ "network": "mainnet", "verify_live": true }
```

### `pepu_known_gotchas`

The curated list of PEPU footguns as one flat list, with no network calls: the Multicall3 address, sponsorship status, the two-address model, Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` limit on chain 97741, Privy setup traps, scope decisions and more.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the full canonical-contract table and the SDK error catalog (`PEPU_ERROR_CATALOG`). |

Safety: static read. Call `pepu_check_contract_deployed` for a live check of one address and `pepu_explain_error` for a specific failure.

```json
{ "response_format": "detailed" }
```

### `pepu_health_check`

Is the RPC (mainnet and or testnet) and pepuscan's Blockscout API (mainnet only) reachable right now, with chain id and latest block. When a bundler or paymaster URL is configured it adds those rows. It separates "pepuscan is behind", "wrong network" and "testnet has no explorer".

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet`, `both` | `both` | Blockscout is only ever checked for mainnet. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds latency and full error text. |

Safety: remote read. Use it to rule out chain-side unavailability before assuming a bug in your code.

```json
{ "network": "mainnet" }
```

### `pepu_gas_price`

The current live gas price and what it costs in PEPU for a transfer, an ERC-20 transfer, a swap and a rough contract deploy. No other inputs needed.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | RPC-direct, so testnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the raw wei value and block number. |

Safety: remote read. The base fee is about 12,500 gwei. That is high in gwei terms and not an error. The tool never returns a USD figure.

```json
{ "response_format": "detailed" }
```

### `pepu_estimate_gas_cost`

Estimates the PEPU cost of a call (live simulation), of a contract deployment (pass init bytecode as `data` and omit `to`), or of a `gas_limit` you already know.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | |
| `to` | string | none | Recipient or contract. Omit for a deployment estimate. |
| `from` | string | none | Sender to simulate from. |
| `data` | string | `0x` | Calldata, or init bytecode for a deployment. |
| `value` | string | `0` | Wei, as a decimal string. |
| `gas_limit` | string or number | none | Skip simulation and price this gas amount. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | |

Safety: remote read. No USD figure: there is no on-chain price oracle for PEPU, so bring your own price feed.

```json
{ "to": "0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078", "data": "0x" }
```

### `pepu_read_contract`

Calls a view or pure function over RPC, given the address, a minimal ABI fragment and the arguments. Works on testnet too.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | 0x address of the contract. |
| `abi` | array of objects | required | At least one ABI item. Only the function you call is needed. |
| `functionName` | string | required | Must match a function in `abi`. |
| `args` | array | `[]` | Positional. uint and int values may be strings or numbers. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | |

Safety: remote read. Sends no transaction and needs no key. Use `pepu_verify_contract_status` first if you do not know the ABI.

```json
{
  "address": "0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8",
  "abi": [{ "type": "function", "name": "decimals", "stateMutability": "view", "inputs": [], "outputs": [{ "type": "uint8" }] }],
  "functionName": "decimals"
}
```

### `pepu_check_contract_deployed`

A live `eth_getCode` check by well-known name ("Multicall3", "Permit2", "EntryPoint v0.7", "Kernel Factory", "WPEPU", "TapScore") or by address. When you ask about a canonical address that has no code on PEPU, it surfaces the PEPU-specific replacement. It is the guardrail against assuming Multicall3 sits at its usual address. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string, min 1 char | required | Address or partial, case-insensitive name. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Works on both. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed lists every matching known contract. |

Safety: remote read.

```json
{ "query": "multicall" }
```

### `pepu_get_token_info`

An ERC-20's name, symbol, decimals, supply and holder count from pepuscan, cross-checked against the contract over RPC, and flagged when it is WPEPU. Never returns a USD value.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | ERC-20 contract address. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works; testnet returns an explanation. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the raw RPC cross-check and reputation metadata. |

Safety: remote read. Use `pepu_search` first if you only have a symbol.

```json
{ "address": "0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8" }
```

### `pepu_get_address_overview`

One call for an address: native balance, contract or EOA, verification status, transaction count and token holdings.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | 40 hex characters. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Concise shows the top 5 holdings; detailed up to 25 plus proxy information. |

Safety: remote read, mainnet only. Internal Blockscout ids are stripped from the output.

```json
{ "address": "0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd" }
```

### `pepu_get_transaction`

A transaction with its decoded call when pepuscan has the ABI, and PEPU-denominated value and fee. Detailed adds the gas breakdown, nonce and Arbitrum L1 batch status. The server deliberately has no bulk transaction-history tool.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hash` | string | required | 64 hex characters. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | |

Safety: remote read, mainnet only. For an EOA versus UserOperation breakdown use `pepu_explain_tx`.

```json
{ "hash": "0x<64-hex-transaction-hash>", "response_format": "detailed" }
```

### `pepu_search`

Resolves an ambiguous string (address, transaction hash, block number, token or contract name) to an entity and points to the next tool to call.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string, min 1 char | required | Anything you would type into an explorer search box. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Top 5 versus top 20 matches. |

Safety: remote read, mainnet only.

```json
{ "query": "WPEPU" }
```

### `pepu_smart_account_info`

The counterfactual address of a ZeroDev Kernel v3 account (single EOA owner) for an owner and salt, taken from the factory's own on-chain `getAddress(bytes,bytes32)` and checked with `eth_getCode` for deployment. This is the smart account address, which is not the owner address. See [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | required | The EOA that controls the account. |
| `salt` | string | `"0"` | Integer string or a full 0x 32-byte value. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | The factory exists on mainnet only. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the encoded init data and assumptions. |

Safety: remote read. Never deploys, never holds a key. It does not imply sponsorship works.

```json
{ "owner": "0x<owner-address>", "salt": "0" }
```

### `pepu_decode_error`

Decodes revert data into an error name and arguments: your own custom errors (pass `abi`), Solidity `Error` and `Panic`, ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7 errors with AA-code phase explanations, and a small ArbOS precompile table. The public RPC does not expose `debug_traceCall`, so this is often the only way to read a failure.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | string | required | Revert payload, 0x hex. Bare selector or selector plus args. |
| `abi` | array of objects | none | Your contract's error fragments. Checked first. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds which table matched. |

Safety: static read. For the PEPU-specific cause and fix of any failure prefer `pepu_explain_error`; keep this tool for decoding custom errors from your own ABI.

```json
{ "data": "0x08c379a0..." }
```

### `pepu_verify_contract_guide`

The exact command to verify a contract on pepuscan: Foundry (`--verifier blockscout` with the `--verifier-url` ending in `/api`) and or the Hardhat `customChains` and `verify.blockscout` configuration.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tool` | `foundry`, `hardhat`, `both` | `both` | |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet is verifiable. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the Hardhat config, failure modes and proxy handling. |

Safety: static read. Call it right after deploying, then `pepu_verify_contract_status` to check the result. See [Deploy and Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md).

```json
{ "tool": "foundry" }
```

### `pepu_verify_contract_status`

Is this address a verified contract on pepuscan, and if so its ABI, compiler and Sourcify link. It tells an unverified contract apart from an address that is not a contract at all.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the full ABI, license and proxy information. |

Safety: remote read, mainnet only.

```json
{ "address": "0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078" }
```

---

## Probes, status and explainers

### `pepu_bundler_health`

Probes an ERC-4337 bundler with `probeBundler` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`: chain id (must be `97741`), supported EntryPoints (must include v0.7), which UserOperation methods exist, latency, and a verdict with a fix. Defaults to `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | URL string | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | Never echoed back, only its host. |

Safety: remote read. Sends nothing on-chain. The default is the hosted bundler; an explicitly cleared or unreachable value is reported with next steps.

```json
{}
```

### `pepu_paymaster_health`

Probes a PEPU paymaster service with `probePaymaster`: `GET /health`, `GET /v2/free-tier` and the v2 ERC-7677 route (`POST /v2/paymaster/<token>`). With only the service base, the probe uses a placeholder token and empty params, so a structured JSON-RPC error (invalid params, unknown credential, denial) is the expected answer and reported as `erc7677: "needs-credential"`, which counts as healthy. Only network errors, non-JSON answers and 5xx are `not-responding`. Nothing is sent on chain. Defaults to the hosted service base (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) when `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` is unset.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | URL string | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, then the hosted service base | The service base (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) or an ERC-7677 endpoint `https://host/v2/paymaster/<token>`. Returns only the host. |

Safety: remote read. The URL can embed a credential and is never returned.

```json
{}
```

### `pepu_sponsorship_status`

Answers "can my app send a gas-sponsored transaction right now?" with `checkSponsorship`: resolves the URLs with `resolvePepuEndpoints`, probes both, optionally reads the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit, and returns `available`, a reason and fixes. Always run this before making any claim about sponsorship.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bundlerUrl` | URL string | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | |
| `paymasterUrl` | URL string | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | Never echoed back. |
| `include_deposit` | boolean | `true` | Reads the paymaster's EntryPoint v0.7 deposit (the v2 paymaster from the registry). An empty deposit makes sponsorship unavailable. |

Returns `available`, `transport`, `reason`, `fixes`, a bundler section, a paymaster section (host, health, ERC-7677 stub result, free tier, deposit) and notes. Safety: remote read. The notes state that the hosted bundler and paymaster service are the defaults and that the paymaster URL needs a project token. Without a token URL the paymaster service is probed at its base.

```json
{ "include_deposit": true }
```

### `pepu_project_balance`

Reads a v2 sponsorship project on-chain with `readProject`: owner, claimed, balance, spendable limits, spent today, paused and pending re-claim. The project id is `computeProjectId`, which is `keccak256(bytes(appId))` and case-sensitive.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | string | none | Privy app id. Give `appId` or `projectId`. |
| `projectId` | string | none | 32-byte id, 0x plus 64 hex. |
| `paymaster` | string | none | Address of the v2 paymaster. Defaults to the registry's deployed paymaster. |

Safety: remote read. With no `paymaster` argument the tool reads the registry's deployed v2 paymaster (`0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`); an explicit `paymaster` overrides it, and only if neither exists does it return the computed project id and say so. Deposits are one-way and cannot be withdrawn. See [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md).

```json
{ "appId": "<your-privy-app-id>" }
```

### `pepu_explain_error`

Explains any PEPU failure from the SDK's shared error catalog (`explainError`): an error message or stack text, a paymaster denial reason code (mapped with `mapPaymasterReason`, for example `project_not_claimed_onchain`), or raw revert data. Returns the catalog code, cause, fix, whether a retry can help, the HTTP status the SDK route factories use and a docs link.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string, 1 to 20,000 chars | required | Pass the text exactly as given. It is never echoed back. |

Safety: static read, pure and offline. It is the first call for any failure and a superset of `pepu_decode_error`. See [SDK Error Catalog](../sdk/errors.md).

```json
{ "error": "AA21 didn't pay prefund" }
```

### `pepu_explain_tx`

Explains a transaction or ERC-4337 bundle from the RPC alone: EOA transaction or UserOperation bundle, sender, who paid gas (the EOA, a paymaster, or the smart account's own deposit), success or revert, fee in PEPU and pepuscan links. Each `UserOperationEvent` is decoded with `userOpEventFromReceipt`. A UserOperation hash also works when `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` is set.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hash` | string | required | Transaction hash, or a UserOperation hash when a bundler URL is configured. |

Safety: remote read. Use `pepu_get_transaction` for pepuscan's decoded input and L1 batch status. For decoded event args use `pepu_decode_tx_logs`.

```json
{ "hash": "0x<64-hex-transaction-hash>" }
```

### `pepu_decode_tx_logs`

Decodes any transaction on PEPU mainnet from its hash alone: the event logs into named arguments and the top-level input into a named call. Each log is decoded by the first of these that succeeds, and the result records it as `source`:

1. `abi`: the ABI or fragments you pass.
2. `verified`: the verified ABI of the emitting contract on pepuscan. For a proxy, the implementation ABIs are merged in. Each distinct address is fetched once per call.
3. `pepuscan`: pepuscan's own decoded signature for the log. Only its signature text is used; the arguments are decoded locally from the raw topics and data.
4. `builtin`: an offline set of standards: ERC-20 and ERC-721 `Transfer` and `Approval` (a 4-topic Transfer is read as an ERC-721 with an indexed `tokenId`), WPEPU `Deposit` and `Withdrawal`, the ERC-4337 EntryPoint events and the Uniswap V2 and V3 pool events (PepuSwap is a Uniswap V3 fork).
5. `signature-db`: the event signature from the public 4byte.directory database, with the indexed parameters inferred by trying each layout. If more than one layout decodes, the first is returned with `ambiguous: true`. Arguments are keyed by position because the database has no parameter names.

Logs that still do not decode are listed with their `topic0`, topic count, data length, a hint and, when the database knows the event, `candidateSignatures`. The top-level input follows the same ladder: your function fragments, the verified ABI of `tx.to`, pepuscan's decoded call, built-in functions (`handleOps`, Universal Router `execute`, ERC-20 calls, WPEPU `deposit` and `withdraw`), then 4byte function signatures. For an EntryPoint `handleOps` bundle the result also points to the decoded `UserOperationEvent` logs; inner account calldata is not decoded. A lookup that fails or times out is skipped and never turns into an error. A UserOperation hash also works when `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` is set.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hash` | string | required | Transaction hash, or a UserOperation hash when a bundler URL is configured. |
| `abi` | JSON ABI array, array of fragments, or one string | none | Usually not needed: verified contracts decode without it. Human-readable fragments such as `"event Swap(address indexed sender, uint256 amount0In, uint256 amount1In, uint256 amount0Out, uint256 amount1Out, address indexed to)"` or `"function swapExactTokensForTokens(uint256,uint256,address[],address,uint256)"`. A bad fragment fails with the fragment named and how to fix it. |
| `address` | address string | none | Only decode logs emitted by this contract (case-insensitive). |
| `includeUndecoded` | boolean | `true` | List logs no event matched. |
| `offline` | boolean | `false` | Skip every network lookup (steps 2, 3 and 5 and their input equivalents). Use when pepuscan is unreachable. |

The result has `txHash`, `status`, `from`, `to`, `block`, `logCount`, `decodedCount`, `undecodedCount`, `truncated`, `lookups`, `logs`, an optional `input` and `notes`, and pepuscan `links`. Each decoded log carries `logIndex`, `address`, `eventName`, `signature`, `source` and `args`: a plain object keyed by parameter name (position for unnamed parameters) with big integers as decimal strings. `lookups` is `{ verifiedAbis, pepuscanLogs, signatureDb }`: how many addresses returned a verified ABI, whether pepuscan's log decoding was `ok`, `failed` or `skipped`, and how many signature-database lookups ran. Output is capped at 200 logs (`truncated: true`).

Safety: remote read, mainnet only. It never signs or sends anything. Use `pepu_explain_tx` first for the transaction kind, payer and fee.

```json
{
  "hash": "0x<64-hex-transaction-hash>",
  "abi": ["event Swap(address indexed sender, uint256 amount0In, uint256 amount1In, uint256 amount0Out, uint256 amount1Out, address indexed to)"],
  "address": "0x<pool-address>"
}
```

---

## Generate, scaffold and docs

### `pepu_list_templates`

Lists the create-pepu-app templates with their doctor pillars (login, wallet, session, sponsorship, gate, mint) and, separately, `features` (the CLI display tags login, session, sponsor), required and optional env vars, Privy dashboard settings (`TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS`), when to pick each, and the exact scaffold and run commands. Metadata comes from the bundled `templates.json`. Takes no inputs. Safety: static read. Call it before `pepu_scaffold_app`. See [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md).

```json
{}
```

### `pepu_scaffold_app`

Creates a PEPU Next.js app by running the create-pepu-app CLI with `--yes --json`. It never reimplements the CLI. Optionally writes the Privy app id and the bundler and paymaster URLs into the new `.env.local`, then reports which env vars are still missing with `checkPepuEnv`. See [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | required | A name from `pepu_list_templates`. |
| `directory` | string | required | ABSOLUTE path. Must not exist or must be empty; the parent must exist. Relative paths and `..` are refused. |
| `packageManager` | `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun` | auto-detected | Used in the printed commands (CLI `--pm`). |
| `privyAppId` | string | none | Written as `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`. Public value. Format-checked. |
| `bundlerUrl` | URL string | none | Written as `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`. Never echoed. |
| `paymasterUrl` | URL string | none | Written as `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`. Can embed a credential. Never echoed. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | `false` | Validates and shows the command without creating anything. |

Safety: write class (not read-only, not destructive, not idempotent). It refuses a non-empty directory, so nothing is overwritten. It runs `npx -y create-pepu-app@latest` unless a local build is found, and falls back to the human-readable CLI output if an older CLI lacks `--json`. Returns the created path, top-level entries, env keys written, env still missing (key names and fixes only) and next steps.

```json
{ "template": "sponsored-session-app", "directory": "C:/projects/my-pepu-app", "dry_run": true }
```

### `pepu_check_env`

Checks a project's environment with `checkPepuEnv` and `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor`. Reads `.env` and `.env.local` (the latter wins) or pasted text, and reports each key as ok, missing, placeholder or malformed, with whether it is a secret, its value length and the fix.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projectDir` | string | none | ABSOLUTE path. Give `projectDir`, `envText` or both (`envText` wins). |
| `envText` | string, max 100,000 chars | none | Pasted dotenv text. Values are never echoed. |
| `template` | string | none | Selects required and optional keys. Omit for the base Privy keys. |
| `pillars` | array of `login`, `wallet`, `session`, `sponsorship`, `gate`, `mint` | none | Extra pillars to require, for example `["sponsorship"]` adds `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`. |

Safety: static read that reads local files. It never returns or logs a value, only presence and length. The result includes `valuesReturned: false`.

```json
{ "projectDir": "C:/projects/my-pepu-app", "template": "game-app" }
```

### `pepu_check_privy_config`

Checks the Privy dashboard settings an app needs with `checkPrivyDashboardConfig` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy`, using Privy's public app-config endpoint (no secret): allowed origin with the exact port, create-on-login, Google login, Smart Wallets with bundler and paymaster URLs, and session signers. Each requirement comes back `pass`, `fail` or `unknown` with a fix. `unknown` means Privy did not report it, not that it failed. The result also carries the full `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` table, including env and code requirements that cannot be checked remotely.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | string, min 1 char | required | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, a public value. |
| `origin` | URL string | none | The origin including the port, such as `http://localhost:3000`. A different dev port is the usual cause of login failure. |
| `pillars` | array of `login`, `session`, `sponsor` | all | Only report requirements that matter for these pillars. |

Safety: remote read. It needs network access to `auth.privy.io`. See [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

```json
{ "appId": "<your-privy-app-id>", "origin": "http://localhost:3000", "pillars": ["login", "session"] }
```

### `pepu_generate_authorization_key`

Generates the P-256 Privy authorization key for session signers with `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey`. The private half is written straight to the env file as `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` and is never returned. Only the public key and a short fingerprint come back, with the next dashboard step: register the public key as a key quorum, then set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`. See [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `envFile` | string | required | ABSOLUTE path, normally `<project>/.env.local`. Created if missing; the folder must exist. Must be named `.env` or `.env.<something>`. |
| `confirm_write` | boolean | `false` | Must be `true` to generate and write. When false the tool only reports what it would do. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | `false` | Required to replace an existing non-empty key. Replacing invalidates sessions granted under the old quorum. |

Safety: write class. Refuses an existing key without `overwrite: true`, refuses to write anything but an `.env*` file, and returns `privateKeyReturned: false`.

```json
{ "envFile": "C:/projects/my-pepu-app/.env.local", "confirm_write": true }
```

### `pepu_session_policy`

Builds a scoped session policy for one contract and a list of functions. Mode `privy` uses `buildSessionPolicy` and `describeSessionScope` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session`: an off-chain Privy policy, the user pays gas, value is always zero. Mode `kernel` uses `buildKernelSessionPolicies` and `describeKernelSessionScope` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel`: on-chain call and timestamp policies on a Kernel account, which compose with sponsorship.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `privy`, `kernel` | required | |
| `contract` | string | required | The one contract the session may call. |
| `functions` | array of strings or ABI fragments, min 1 | required | Solidity signatures such as `tap()` or `transfer(address to, uint256 amount)`, or JSON ABI function fragments. |
| `minutes` | positive number | 15 | Clamped to 1 to 1440. |
| `valueLimitWei` | decimal string | `0` | Kernel mode only. Privy mode always requires zero value. |

Returns the policy, a consent summary, selectors, the trust notice (`SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE`) and a paste-ready snippet. Safety: static read, pure; nothing is signed or sent. In kernel mode the `@zerodev/*` optional peers must be installed to build the policy objects; without them the tool still describes the scope and says so. See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md) and [Sponsored Session](../onboarding/sponsored-session.md).

```json
{ "mode": "kernel", "contract": "0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078", "functions": ["tap()"], "minutes": 15 }
```

### `pepu_encode_calls`

ABI-encodes contract calls with viem's `encodeFunctionData` from a signature or an ABI and optionally wraps them. `multicall3` builds one `aggregate3` call to PEPU's own Multicall3 with `encodeAggregate3` and `getMulticall3`, never the canonical `0xcA11...` address. `kernel-execute` and `userop-callData` build the Kernel v3 ERC-7579 execute calldata for a UserOperation (single or batch mode).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calls` | array of 1 to 50 call objects | required | See below. |
| `as` | `calldata`, `multicall3`, `kernel-execute`, `userop-callData` | `calldata` | `kernel-execute` and `userop-callData` produce the same bytes; the second name is what goes in a UserOperation. |

Each call object:

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | string | required | Target contract. |
| `signature` | string | none | Solidity signature. Give `signature`, or `abi` plus `functionName`. |
| `abi` | array of objects | none | Full or single-function ABI. |
| `functionName` | string | none | Function to call in `abi`. |
| `args` | array | `[]` | In order. |
| `value` | decimal string | `0` | Wei. |
| `allowFailure` | boolean | `false` | `multicall3` only. |

Returns hex, a decoded echo and a gas hint. Safety: static read, pure; nothing is signed or sent.

```json
{
  "as": "multicall3",
  "calls": [
    { "to": "0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8", "signature": "balanceOf(address account)", "args": ["0x<holder-address>"] }
  ]
}
```

### `pepu_prepare_project_tx`

Encodes unsigned transactions for a v2 sponsorship project with the helpers in `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`: `encodeDeposit` (`depositFor`), `encodeClaimProject` and `encodeReclaimProject` (from a claim attestation), `encodeExecuteReclaim`, `encodeCancelReclaim`, `configureProject` (`setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`) and `encodeSetPaused`. Returns `{ to, data, value }` and a plain-English warning.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `deposit`, `claim`, `reclaim`, `executeReclaim`, `cancelReclaim`, `configure`, `setPaused` | required | `claim` and `reclaim` need the attestation from `requestClaimAttestation` (server). |
| `paymaster` | string | none | The v2 paymaster address. Defaults to the registry's deployed paymaster. |
| `appId` | string | none | Case-sensitive. Give `appId` or `projectId`. |
| `projectId` | string | none | bytes32. |
| `amountPepu` | string | none | `deposit`: decimal PEPU such as `"2.5"`. |
| `amountWei` | decimal string | none | `deposit`: wei. Give `amountPepu` or `amountWei`. |
| `attestation` | object | none | `claim` and `reclaim`: `{ appId, newOwner, nonce, deadline, signature }`, the EIP-712 `ProjectClaim` attestation. |
| `targets` | array of up to 50 strings | none | `configure`: destination contracts to sponsor. |
| `dailyLimitPepu` | string | none | `configure`: total daily budget. |
| `senderDailyLimitPepu` | string | none | `configure`: per-wallet daily budget. |
| `paused` | boolean | none | `setPaused`. |

Safety: static read. It never signs or sends. With no `paymaster` argument it uses the registry's deployed v2 paymaster; an explicit address overrides it. Deposits are one-way, the app id is case-sensitive, and a claim sets the owner only: the owner must then call `configure` (a claim of a project that already holds funds is pending for the 48-hour admin delay and needs `executeReclaim`). See [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md).

```json
{ "action": "deposit", "paymaster": "0x<verified-v2-paymaster>", "appId": "<your-privy-app-id>", "amountPepu": "2.5" }
```

### `pepu_get_docs`

Reads the PEPU developer docs from a snapshot of this repository's `docs/` folder, bundled at build time (no network). `query` returns the best-matching sections with their `docs.pepeunchained.com` URL, `slug` returns a whole page, and no arguments lists every page.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string, min 2 chars | none | A few words, for example `privy allowed origins port`. |
| `slug` | string | none | A page slug such as `onboarding/session-keys`. Long pages are truncated; then ask for a section with `query`. |

Safety: static read. The snapshot is only as new as the installed server version. Docs describe the SDK; for exact exports use `pepu_sdk_exports` and for working code `pepu_sdk_snippet`.

```json
{ "query": "sponsored session" }
```

### `pepu_sdk_snippet`

Canonical code that uses `@pepu-chain/sdk` for one task. Each snippet names its file, peer packages, env vars and caveats, and every import is checked against the SDK export list in the package's tests. Omit `task` to list them all.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | enum, optional | list all | One of the ids below. |

Snippet ids: `privy-provider`, `ensure-wallet-route`, `wagmi-privy`, `grant-session`, `session-routes`, `session-action-route`, `kernel-session-policy`, `sponsored-send`, `sponsored-send-server`, `check-sponsorship`, `sponsored-session`, `sponsored-session-client`, `multicall-read`, `permit2-permit`, `v2-deposit`.

Safety: static read. The `v2-deposit` snippet targets the v2 paymaster. Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs.

```json
{ "task": "sponsored-session" }
```

### `pepu_sdk_exports`

Lists the exports of `@pepu-chain/sdk` per import path with one-line summaries, from an export list generated from the SDK build and bundled with the server. Use it to find the right function before writing code. Omit `subpath` to list the paths with export counts.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subpath` | string | none | `@pepu-chain/sdk/session` or just `session`. |
| `search` | string | none | Name or summary contains this text, case-insensitive. |
| `kind` | `function`, `value`, `type`, `class`, `enum` | none | Only this kind of export. |

Safety: static read. The same data is available as the `pepu://sdk/exports` resource.

```json
{ "subpath": "session/kernel", "kind": "function" }
```

---

## What to expect

- Every tool returns one JSON text block, or an actionable error with what, why and fix.
- Tools that depend on a service you have not configured say so. They do not guess and they do not invent a hosted URL.
- The two write tools (`pepu_scaffold_app`, `pepu_generate_authorization_key`) are the only ones that touch your filesystem, and both accept absolute paths only.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A Blockscout-backed tool says testnet is not supported | pepuscan does not index testnet `97740` | Use mainnet, or an RPC-direct tool (`pepu_read_contract`, `pepu_gas_price`, `pepu_estimate_gas_cost`, `pepu_check_contract_deployed`). |
| `pepu_bundler_health` or `pepu_paymaster_health` reports "not configured" | A default was cleared, or the URL you passed is empty | The hosted bundler and paymaster service are the defaults. Set `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` / `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` in the server env, or pass `url`. |
| `pepu_scaffold_app` refuses the directory | Not absolute, contains `..`, or exists and is not empty | Pass an absolute path to a folder that does not exist yet. |
| `pepu_generate_authorization_key` refuses | An existing key is set, or `confirm_write` is false | Pass `confirm_write: true`; add `overwrite: true` only if you mean to rotate (that invalidates existing sessions). |
| `pepu_project_balance` or `pepu_prepare_project_tx` asks for a paymaster address | The registry has no `paymasterV2` address for the chain in use | On mainnet the registry holds the deployed v2 paymaster and both tools default to it. Pass an address to override. |
| `pepu_session_policy` kernel mode warns about missing packages | The optional `@zerodev/*` peers are not installed next to the server | Install `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions` and `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`, or accept the scope description only. |
| `pepu_check_privy_config` shows `unknown` rows | Privy's public config did not report that setting | Check the dashboard by hand; `unknown` is not a failure. |

# MCP Resources and Prompts

The five `pepu://` resources the server exposes and its six prompts: what each is for, its arguments, and how an agent should chain them with the tools. Read this if you attach context by hand in a client UI, or if you want to know what the prompt starters tell the agent to do.

Resources and prompts are static text and bundled data; nothing here sends a transaction or needs a key.

## Prerequisites

- The server is installed in your client. See [Install per Client](install.md).
- A client that supports MCP resources and prompts. Not every client does: Claude Code lists prompts as slash commands and resources as `@` mentions, other clients vary. Tools work everywhere.

## Resources

Resources are read-only context that you or the agent can attach without a tool call.

| URI | Content | MIME type |
|---|---|---|
| `pepu://chain-facts` | Mainnet network facts (chain `97741`), a note that the testnet `97740` is out of scope, and the known gotchas list | `application/json` |
| `pepu://addresses` | Every tracked mainnet contract from the SDK registry (`getPepuAddresses`): deployed addresses with notes (including the v2 paymaster and the retired v1 paymaster, flagged `retired`), and contracts not yet deployed, with the reason | `application/json` |
| `pepu://docs/{slug}` | A page of these docs, from a snapshot bundled at build time. `{slug}` is a page path such as `onboarding/session-keys` | `text/markdown` |
| `pepu://skills/{name}` | A skill's `SKILL.md`, bundled at build time. `{name}` is a skill name such as `pepu-session-keys` | `text/markdown` |
| `pepu://sdk/exports` | Every `@pepu-chain/sdk` import path with its exports and one-line summaries, generated from the SDK build | `application/json` |

Notes:

- `pepu://docs/{slug}` and `pepu://skills/{name}` are resource templates. A client lists the available slugs and names, and the server completes partial values.
- The docs and skills snapshots are bundled when the package is built. They are as current as the installed server version. For a newer answer, update the server (`npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp` fetches the latest unless a version is pinned) or read the docs directly.
- An unknown slug or skill name returns an error that lists what is available.
- `pepu://addresses` shows `paymasterV2` (and its alias `paymaster`) at the deployed paymaster `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`, and `paymasterV1` as retired. Do not deposit to the retired v1 paymaster. See [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md).

The tools that mirror resources: `pepu_chain_info` and `pepu_known_gotchas` (chain facts), `pepu_get_docs` (docs), `pepu_sdk_exports` (SDK exports). Use the resource when you want to attach the whole thing; use the tool when the agent should decide.

## Prompts

A prompt returns one user message that tells the agent which tools and SDK functions to use, in order. Each ends with a short reminder: sponsorship uses the hosted bundler and paymaster service with a project token, Privy session mode is off-chain and the user pays gas, Kernel session mode is on-chain, deposits to the v2 paymaster are one-way, and a transaction is never called gasless unless a paymaster paid it.

| Prompt | Arguments (all optional) | What it tells the agent to do |
|---|---|---|
| `new-pepu-app` | `idea`, `directory` (absolute path) | Read `pepu://chain-facts`, call `pepu_list_templates` and choose a template, call `pepu_scaffold_app`, run `pepu_check_env`, then `pepu_check_privy_config` with the dev origin and port, and use `pepu_sdk_snippet` and `pepu_sdk_exports` for extra wiring. |
| `add-google-login` | `projectDir` | Apply the `privy-provider` and `ensure-wallet-route` snippets, run `pepu_check_env` (template `consumer-app`) then `pepu_check_privy_config`, and pin Coinbase to `eoaOnly` and the embedded wallet when wagmi is used. |
| `add-session` | `mode` (`privy` or `kernel`), `contract`, `functions` (comma-separated signatures) | Explain the two trust models and confirm one, call `pepu_session_policy`, apply the session snippets (Privy mode also runs `pepu_generate_authorization_key` and asks you to register the public key), and show the consent text and trust notice. |
| `add-sponsorship` | `projectDir` | Run `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_bundler_health` and `pepu_paymaster_health`; apply `sponsored-send` (and `sponsored-send-server` for scripts); use `pepu_explain_error` on failures; do not tell you to deposit into v2. |
| `add-sponsored-session` | `contract`, `functions` | Build the Kernel scope with `pepu_session_policy`, apply `sponsored-session` and `sponsored-session-client` (the scope on server and client must match), confirm with `pepu_sponsorship_status`, size spend caps above the gas reservation (about 20.5 PEPU for a session's first operation, 6.9 later), and warn that `createMemoryStore` is dev only. |
| `debug-tx` | `hash`, `error` | With a hash: `pepu_explain_tx`. With an error: `pepu_explain_error` using the text exactly as given. Then `pepu_sponsorship_status` if sponsorship is involved, `pepu_decode_error` for custom errors, and `pepu_known_gotchas`. |

The three pillar prompts map one to one onto the three pillars: `add-google-login` (Google to wallet), `add-session` (session keys), `add-sponsorship` (sponsored transactions), and `add-sponsored-session` is the combination. See [The Three Pillars and How They Combine](../get-started/pillars.md).

## How agents should chain them

1. Start from a prompt when one fits. It encodes the right order. In Claude Code the [plugin commands](../agent-tooling/plugin.md) wrap the same flows (`/pepu-new-app`, `/pepu-add-login`, `/pepu-add-session`, `/pepu-add-sponsorship`, `/pepu-add-sponsored-session`, `/pepu-doctor`).
2. Ground the facts first: `pepu_chain_info` or the `pepu://chain-facts` resource. Never answer chain questions from memory.
3. Pick code from `pepu_sdk_snippet` and confirm names with `pepu_sdk_exports` before writing anything by hand.
4. Verify with `pepu_check_env` and `pepu_check_privy_config`, then the project's own typecheck and build.
5. When something fails, `pepu_explain_error` with the exact text, then `pepu_known_gotchas`.

## What to expect

- Invoking a prompt produces a message, not a result. The agent then makes the tool calls itself, and you approve them according to your client's permission rules.
- The read-only tools run without prompting in most clients. The two write tools (`pepu_scaffold_app`, `pepu_generate_authorization_key`) ask first in clients that honour the annotation hints.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The client shows no prompts or resources | The client only supports MCP tools | Use the tools directly, or the plugin commands in Claude Code. |
| `pepu://docs/...` returns "No docs page" | The slug is not in the bundled snapshot | Read the slug list the error prints, or call `pepu_get_docs` with no arguments. |
| Resource content looks stale | The snapshot is bundled at build time | Update the server to the latest version, or pin a newer one. |

## Related

- [MCP Server Overview](index.md)
- [Tool Reference](tools.md)
- [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md)
- [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md)

# Agent Tooling: MCP Server and Skills

This is the hub for the PEPU agent tooling: infrastructure that helps coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and similar) build on Pepe Unchained and get PEPU's specific facts right. It is not a claim that PEPU is "an AI chain". It is not one. AI is a feature builders add to their own products. This tooling exists so an agent, or a person using one, does not guess a chain ID, invent an address or use the canonical Multicall3 address that has no code here (see [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md)).

![Dev kit map: the SDK at the base; the MCP server with 33 tools, 12 skills, the Claude Code plugin, the create-pepu-app CLI and 6 templates all build on it](../.gitbook/assets/devkit-map.png)

*Everything builds on the SDK.*

The hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster service (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) are the defaults. Sponsorship needs a project token in the paymaster URL (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`).

## The pieces

| Piece | What it is | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `pepu` MCP server | `@pepu-chain/mcp`: 33 tools, 6 prompts and 5 resources for chain facts, probes, explainers, scaffolding, env and Privy checks, session policies and SDK snippets | [MCP Server Overview](../mcp/index.md), [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md), [Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md) |
| Skills | 12 `SKILL.md` playbooks, each built on `@pepu-chain/sdk` and the MCP tools | [Skills Catalog](skills.md) |
| Claude Code plugin | `pepu-devkit`: the MCP server, the 12 skills, 6 slash commands and the `pepu-builder` subagent in one install | [Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md) |
| Template agent kit | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and editor configs shipped in every scaffolded app | [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](agents-md.md) |

## Quick start

In Claude Code, install the plugin (recommended):

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

Or add only the MCP server with `claude mcp add pepu -- npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`. Cursor, VS Code and other clients are covered in [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md).

## How they fit together

- The SDK (`@pepu-chain/sdk`) holds the functions. Skills and tools tell the agent to wire them, not to hand-roll infrastructure.
- The MCP server answers live questions: what is deployed, is sponsorship available, what does this error mean, which env var is missing.
- Skills carry the method: the order of steps, the dashboard settings, the safety rules and the pitfalls.
- Each skill tells the agent to call `pepu_chain_info` or the relevant probe first, so a fact that changed since the skill was written is caught by a live check.

The same line applies to everything here: it makes building on PEPU easier, or it does not belong.

## Related

- [Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes](../get-started/ai-assisted.md)
- [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/agent-tooling/skills

# Skills Catalog

The 12 PEPU skills: what each one does, when it triggers, the chain facts they all share, how they use the SDK and the MCP tools instead of hand-rolled code, and the rules for writing a new one. Read it to know which skill an agent will load, or before adding one.

The skills ship in the `pepu-devkit` plugin and are also served by the MCP server as `pepu://skills/{name}`.

## Prerequisites

- The skills are installed through the [Claude Code plugin](plugin.md), or read one on demand through the `pepu://skills/{name}` MCP resource.
- For method, not just text: the [MCP server](../mcp/index.md) connected, because every skill tells the agent to call its tools.

## The 12 skills

| Skill | What it does | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `pepu-build-dapp` | The entry point from zero to a running app. Scaffolds with `create-pepu-app` or the MCP tools `pepu_list_templates` and `pepu_scaffold_app`, picks the template by pillar, fills and checks env and Privy config, runs the app and hands off to the pillar skills. | Building, starting, scaffolding or extending a PEPU app. |
| `pepu-sdk` | A cheat sheet for `@pepu-chain/sdk`: the subpath map, "if you want X, import Y", which entries are server-only, client-only or ESM-only, and the rule against reimplementing what it ships. | Before writing any PEPU infrastructure code by hand, or to pick the right import. |
| `pepu-chain-setup` | Configures viem, wagmi, Hardhat and Foundry for chain `97741` with the SDK instead of a hand-written chain object. Carries the traps: PEPU-specific Multicall3, the huge-looking gas price, the 2,000-block `eth_getLogs` cap, no WebSocket RPC. | Adding PEPU to any project, setting up a client, batching reads. |
| `pepu-onboarding-privy` | Google (and email) login with a server-provisioned Privy embedded wallet, built from the SDK provider, `WalletGate`, `createEnsureWalletRoute` and `requireUser`. Gives the Privy dashboard fields and the troubleshooting for login hangs and a missing wallet. Pillar: Google to wallet. | Sign-in, wallets, protecting an API route by user. |
| `pepu-session-keys` | Privy session signers on a plain embedded wallet, so an app acts for the user with no popup per action. The scope is enforced off-chain by Privy and the user pays gas. Includes the three safety rules. Pillar: session keys. | "No wallet popup" actions with the user paying gas. |
| `pepu-sponsored-transactions` | Gasless transactions with a Kernel v3.1 smart account, an EntryPoint v0.7 bundler and an ERC-7677 paymaster. Covers both transports (Privy Smart Wallets or direct URLs). Check sponsorship availability with `pepu_sponsorship_status`; do not assume it. Pillar: sponsored transactions. | Gasless, paymaster, bundler or UserOperation work. |
| `pepu-sponsored-session` | The combination: Google login, one owner signature that grants an on-chain Kernel session key, then actions with no popup and no user gas. The scope is enforced on-chain. Includes the five routes and the production `SessionStore` warning. | The full flow, matching the `sponsored-session-app` template. |
| `pepu-smart-accounts` | Account mechanics: the two-address model (embedded EOA owner plus Kernel smart account), counterfactual addresses and when a smart account is the right choice. Deliberately slim. | Computing or inspecting a smart account, explaining owner versus smart account. |
| `pepu-paymaster-projects` | The v2 tiered model: claim a project keyed by Privy app id, deposit PEPU one-way, set targets and daily limits. Advise depositing only what the project needs. | Preparing, reviewing or scripting the v2 workflow, and answering tier questions. |
| `pepu-deploy-contract` | Deploys and verifies a Solidity contract on mainnet with Foundry (primary) or Hardhat. Detects the `foundry-zksync` binary shadowing `forge` before it produces a wrong deployment. | Deploying or verifying a contract on PEPU. |
| `pepu-token-and-nft` | Deploys and uses an ERC-20 or ERC-721 on PEPU, and explains what "getting listed" actually means: the PepuSwap list and the kit's own token list are separate and neither is automatic. | Creating a token or NFT collection, or interacting with one. |
| `pepu-debug-transaction` | Diagnoses a failed, stuck, denied or expensive transaction, UserOperation or Privy, paymaster or session error. Starts with `pepu_explain_tx`, `pepu_decode_tx_logs`, `pepu_explain_error` and `pepu_known_gotchas`. | Reverts, transactions that never land, denied sponsored sends, session 409s. |

The three pillar skills (`pepu-onboarding-privy`, `pepu-session-keys`, `pepu-sponsored-transactions`) and their combination (`pepu-sponsored-session`) match the pillars in [The Three Pillars and How They Combine](../get-started/pillars.md).

## Shared chain facts

Every skill carries two shared files in its own `reference/` folder, so a skill is self-contained when installed alone:

- `reference/chain-facts.md` is generated from the built SDK (chains, endpoints, the contract registry). It states chain `97741`, mainnet only, the default RPC and explorer, the PEPU-specific Multicall3, the full registry table with deployment status, the gas explanation, the endpoint-resolution order and a "where to look things up" table.
- `reference/rules.md` is hand-written: "use the SDK, call the MCP tools, never hand-roll". It holds the order of work, a table of what never to write by hand and the SDK function to use instead, the hard rules and the MCP tool contract.

The hard rules every skill repeats:

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Mainnet only | Chain `97741`. Do not add the testnet to a chain list. |
| Never print secrets | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, paymaster URLs and session private keys. Report key names and presence only. |
| Sponsorship wording follows the live answer | Call `pepu_sponsorship_status` or `checkSponsorship()`. The hosted bundler and paymaster service are live and are the defaults, but the ERC-7677 URL needs a project token, so the app brings a project. |
| Say which session mode | Privy session mode is enforced off-chain and the user pays gas. Kernel session mode is enforced on-chain. |
| Deposits are one-way | Deposits to the v2 paymaster are one-way; advise depositing only what the project needs. The v1 paymaster is retired: never deposit to it. |
| Never call a transaction free or gasless | Unless a paymaster actually paid it. |
| Always a scoped session policy | Never an empty `policyIds`. |
| No server-side `eth_sendTransaction` on 97741 | Privy rejects it. Sign with `eth_signTransaction` and broadcast; the SDK does this. |

## How skills use the SDK and MCP

A skill follows one pattern: ask the tools, wire the SDK, verify.

1. Ground the facts with `pepu_chain_info` or the matching probe (`pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_check_contract_deployed`).
2. Take canonical code from `pepu_sdk_snippet` and confirm names with `pepu_sdk_exports`. Import from the documented subpaths only.
3. Check `pepu_check_env` and `pepu_check_privy_config` before debugging application code.
4. Verify with the project's typecheck and build, then confirm the pillar works (sign in, grant, act, send).
5. On failure, `pepu_explain_error` with the exact text, then `pepu_known_gotchas`.

Each `SKILL.md` has the same sections: When to use, Chain facts, SDK functions to use, MCP tools to call first, Steps, Verify, Pitfalls and Never hand-roll (the pillar skills add their safety rules).

If the SDK lacks something, the skill says so, writes the smallest local code and marks it `// TODO(sdk): ...`.

## Authoring rules for a new skill

1. Create `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with frontmatter `name` equal to the directory name and a non-empty `description` that says when to use it.
2. Use the uniform sections above, in that order.
3. Name only SDK functions that exist, and only MCP tools that are registered. Import paths must exist in the SDK exports map.
4. Do not copy chain facts into the skill. Link to `reference/chain-facts.md`, which is generated.
5. State facts plainly and keep wording consistent with the docs style guide.
6. Run the sync and the check:

```bash
pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk build        # the scripts read the built SDK
node scripts/sync-skill-shared.mjs         # regenerate chain-facts.md and copy shared files into every skill
node scripts/check-plugin.mjs              # validate skills, commands, agents, tool names, SDK imports and counts
```

`check-plugin.mjs` fails if a skill's name does not match its directory, a named `pepu_*` tool is not registered, an imported SDK symbol is not exported, a count in the manifest descriptions is wrong, or the shared files are stale. `node scripts/sync-skill-shared.mjs --check` is the CI form of the sync.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The agent does not load a skill | The plugin is not installed or enabled | Install it ([Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md)), or ask the agent to read `pepu://skills/<name>`. |
| `check-plugin.mjs` reports stale shared files | The SDK registry changed | Rebuild the SDK and run `node scripts/sync-skill-shared.mjs`. |
| `check-plugin.mjs` reports an unknown tool or export | A skill names something that does not exist | Fix the name against `pepu_sdk_exports` or the tool registry. |

## Related

- [Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md)
- [MCP Server Overview](../mcp/index.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)
- [Agent Tooling hub](mcp-and-skills.md)

# Claude Code Plugin

The `pepu-devkit` plugin bundles everything the kit gives a coding agent into one Claude Code install: the `pepu` MCP server, the 12 skills, 6 slash commands and the `pepu-builder` subagent. This page covers installing it, what each command does, what loads, and the trust prompt you will see.

Commands that touch sponsorship use the hosted bundler and paymaster service by default and need a project token for the paymaster URL (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`). `scripts/check-plugin.mjs` checks the manifests, commands and subagent against the real MCP tools and SDK exports.

## Prerequisites

- Claude Code with plugin support.
- Node.js 18 or newer, because the plugin starts the MCP server with `npx`.
- Optional: `PEPU_RPC_URL`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` exported in your shell. The plugin forwards them to the server and uses an empty value when they are unset.

## Install

Plugin (recommended):

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

The first command registers the marketplace named `pepu` from the GitHub repository `pepu-org/pepu-devkit`. The second installs the plugin `pepu-devkit` from it.

If you only want the MCP server, use the fallback instead: `claude mcp add pepu -- npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`. See [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md).

Apps scaffolded with [create-pepu-app](../cli/create-pepu-app.md) carry a `.claude/settings.json` that declares the `pepu` marketplace and enables `pepu-devkit@pepu`, so Claude Code offers the plugin the first time you open the project. See [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](agents-md.md).

## What loads

| Part | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| MCP server `pepu` | 1 server, 33 tools, 6 prompts, 5 resources | Started with `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp@^0.2`. Environment: `PEPU_RPC_URL`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`. See [Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md). |
| Skills | 12 | Listed in the [Skills Catalog](skills.md). |
| Commands | 6 | Below. |
| Subagent | 1 | `pepu-builder`, below. |

Inside Claude Code, the plugin's MCP tools are named `mcp__plugin_pepu-devkit_pepu__<tool>`, for example `mcp__plugin_pepu-devkit_pepu__pepu_chain_info`. Each command and the subagent list exactly the tools they may call.

## The trust prompt

A plugin runs code and can start a server on your machine, so Claude Code asks before it enables one. Expect:

1. A prompt to trust the marketplace or the folder when you add it, and to confirm the plugin install.
2. An approval for the plugin's MCP server the first time it starts. It runs `npx` with the package above.
3. Permission prompts for tool calls according to your normal rules. Read-only tools are annotated as such. The two write tools, `pepu_scaffold_app` and `pepu_generate_authorization_key`, are the ones that ask first.

Read the manifest before you trust it: it is `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` in the repository. Exact prompt wording belongs to Claude Code and can change.

## Commands

All six commands call the SDK through the MCP snippets. None hand-writes chain, Privy, session or sponsorship code.

| Command | Argument | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/pepu-new-app` | `[app name or idea]` | Lists templates, picks one by pillar and says why (default `consumer-app`), scaffolds to an absolute directory with `pepu_scaffold_app` (or the CLI with `--yes --no-install --no-git --json`), installs, runs `pepu_check_env` and `pepu_check_privy_config`, reports sponsorship status for sponsorship templates, then typechecks and builds. Follows the `pepu-build-dapp` skill. |
| `/pepu-add-login` | `[login methods, default google and email]` | Adds Google login and a Privy embedded wallet to the current Next.js app: `PepuPrivyProvider` or `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` with `WalletGate`, and `createEnsureWalletRoute()`. Adds env placeholders, checks the dashboard (allowed origin with port, Google on, embedded wallets on). Follows `pepu-onboarding-privy`. |
| `/pepu-add-session` | `<contract address> <function signatures, e.g. tap()>` | Adds Privy session keys: builds the policy with `pepu_session_policy` (Privy mode), generates the authorization key with `pepu_generate_authorization_key` and asks you to register the public key and paste the quorum id, then applies the session routes and hooks. The consent screen says the user pays gas. Follows `pepu-session-keys`. |
| `/pepu-add-sponsorship` | `[transport: privy-smart-wallets or direct]` | Runs `pepu_sponsorship_status` first and reports the answer exactly, then wires `useSponsoredSend` or `useDirectSponsoredSend` (browser) or `sendSponsored` (server). Prefers the Privy Smart Wallets transport for browser code because a paymaster URL embeds a credential. Only says a send was sponsored when `result.paymaster` is set. Follows `pepu-sponsored-transactions`. |
| `/pepu-add-sponsored-session` | `<contract address> <function signatures>` | Adds the combination: Kernel scope from `pepu_session_policy`, `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` with its five route files and a `useSponsoredSession` component. Warns that `createMemoryStore()` is dev only and sizes spend caps above the gas reservation. For a new project prefer `/pepu-new-app` with `sponsored-session-app`. Follows `pepu-sponsored-session`. |
| `/pepu-doctor` | `[template name, optional]` | Readiness check: `pepu_check_env`, `npm run doctor` if defined, `pepu_check_privy_config`, `pepu_sponsorship_status` for sponsorship templates and `pepu_health_check`. Ends with a table of check, status and fix, applies the fixes it can, and lists exactly what only you can do. Never reads secret values. |

## The pepu-builder subagent

`pepu-builder` builds and extends PEPU apps end to end and asks you only for what only you have. Claude Code delegates to it for any task that creates or changes a PEPU app, a contract deployment or a PEPU chain integration.

How it works:

1. Scaffold first, never from a blank folder.
2. Ask the tools, not memory: `pepu_chain_info`, `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_check_env`, `pepu_check_privy_config`, `pepu_sdk_snippet`, `pepu_sdk_exports`.
3. Load the matching skill and obey its never-hand-roll list.
4. Verify before saying done: env check, Privy check, typecheck, build, then confirm the pillar works.
5. On failure, `pepu_explain_error` with the exact text, then `pepu_known_gotchas`.

What only you can do, and it will name each precisely: paste the Privy App ID and App Secret, register the authorization public key in the Privy dashboard, add the allowed origin, supply bundler and paymaster URLs, and fund wallets.

It never prints, logs or commits secrets, never calls a transaction free unless a paymaster paid it, and says which session mode it built. It finishes with a report of what it built, which SDK functions it uses, what was checked and what you still have to do. Its tools are Claude Code's file and shell tools (Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash) plus an explicit allow-list of all 33 PEPU MCP tools that includes both write tools. The list is in `agents/pepu-builder.md`.

## Versions and checks

The plugin version, the marketplace version and the MCP server's declared range move together. From a checkout:

```bash
node scripts/check-versions.mjs   # plugin.json, marketplace.json and packages/mcp/server.json in lock-step; prints SDK, MCP, CLI and plugin versions
node scripts/check-plugin.mjs     # validates skills, commands, agents, tool names, SDK imports and manifest counts
```

`check-plugin.mjs --write` regenerates the counts in the manifest descriptions.

## What to expect

- After install, `/mcp` shows the plugin's `pepu` server, and the six commands appear when you type `/pepu`.
- Without a project token for the paymaster URL, the sponsorship commands still set up the code and leave `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` as a marked placeholder (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`; the bundler defaults to the hosted one). They do not claim sponsorship works.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `/plugin marketplace add` fails | No network, or the repository is not reachable | Check access to `github.com/pepu-org/pepu-devkit`, or use the `claude mcp add` fallback. |
| The MCP server does not start | Node older than 18 or `npx` not on PATH | Install Node 18+. |
| Sponsorship tools say "not configured" | The environment cleared a default, or the paymaster URL has no project token | Export `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`) and, for your own bundler, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` before launching Claude Code. |
| A command asks for something and stops | It needs a value only you have | Provide the Privy App ID or secret, or complete the named dashboard step, then continue. |

## Related

- [Skills Catalog](skills.md)
- [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](agents-md.md)
- [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md)
- [Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes](../get-started/ai-assisted.md)

# AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates

Every app scaffolded from a PEPU template carries an agent kit: instructions and editor configs that point a coding agent at the SDK and the MCP server. This page lists what is in the kit, which part of `AGENTS.md` is hand-written and which is generated, and how the kit is kept in sync. Read it if you work with an agent inside a scaffolded app, or if you maintain a template.

The plugin route for Claude Code is recommended. Templates do not ship a `.mcp.json`. `templates/scripts/check-agent-kit.mjs` fails when any template drifts from the shared kit.

## Prerequisites

- An app from [create-pepu-app](../cli/create-pepu-app.md). Pass `--skip-agent-files` to leave the kit out.
- An agent client that reads `AGENTS.md` (Cursor, VS Code Copilot and others) or `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code).

## What is in the kit

| File | Who reads it | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Most agents | The template's instructions: how to build and run, which SDK functions the template uses, design rules, plus the generated "PEPU dev kit: agent wiring" block. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code | One line, `@AGENTS.md`, which imports `AGENTS.md` so both agents read the same text. |
| `.cursor/mcp.json` | Cursor | Declares the `pepu` MCP server under the `mcpServers` key, with `"type": "stdio"`. |
| `.vscode/mcp.json` | VS Code | Declares the `pepu` MCP server under the top-level key `servers`, with `"type": "stdio"`. |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Claude Code | Declares the `pepu` marketplace from `pepu-org/pepu-devkit` and enables `pepu-devkit@pepu`, so Claude Code offers the plugin when you open the project. |

The editor configs all run the same command, `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`. See [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md) for the exact shapes and the environment variables.

`.claude/settings.json` carries exactly this:

```json
{
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "pepu": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "pepu-org/pepu-devkit" } }
  },
  "enabledPlugins": { "pepu-devkit@pepu": true }
}
```

What the plugin then gives you is described in [Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md). You still see Claude Code's trust prompt.

## Per-template section versus generated block

`AGENTS.md` has two parts.

1. **Per-template section (hand-written, above the markers).** Build and run commands, the table of SDK functions the template uses and where, the template's own rules (for example, game-app keeps `tap()` non-payable and never grants an unscoped signer; sponsored-demo never labels a send gasless unless a paymaster paid it), the design notes and what the template deliberately does not do. Edit this freely.
2. **Generated block (between the markers).** Everything between `` and `` is generated. Do not edit it by hand: the next sync overwrites it and the check fails.

The generated block says:

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Header | Template name, title and features (login, session, sponsor). "Use the kit; do not hand-roll what it already provides." |
| Chain facts | Chain `97741`, mainnet only, no testnet switch. RPC, pepuscan, native token PEPU with 18 decimals. Multicall3 at the PEPU-specific `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`, never the canonical address. Get everything from the SDK (`pepuMainnet`, `explorerLinks`, `getPepuAddresses`). |
| Use the SDK | The SDK subpaths this template should import from, chosen by its features, then a table of every subpath and what it is for. |
| Use the MCP tools | The `pepu` server, the 33 tools grouped by purpose, the 6 prompts and the resources. `pepu_chain_info` is called first. |
| Skills and the plugin | The plugin install commands (`/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit`, `/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu`). |
| Environment | The template's required and optional env vars, its Privy dashboard settings and extra steps, and `npm run doctor`. |
| Never print secrets | Do not print, log, echo, commit or paste `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, any private key or credential-bearing URL. Do not read `.env*` into the conversation: use `npm run doctor`, which prints no values. Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are safe to show. |

The per-template values come from `packages/create-pepu-app/src/templates.json` (name, title, features, env, Privy dashboard ids, extra steps).

## Sync and check scripts

The shared source is `templates/_agent`: the editor configs, `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.base.md` (the generated block's template).

```bash
# After editing anything in templates/_agent or templates.json:
node templates/scripts/sync-agent-kit.mjs     # copies the verbatim files, renders the block into every template's AGENTS.md
node templates/scripts/check-agent-kit.mjs    # fails (exit 1) on any drift
```

`check-agent-kit.mjs` fails when a kit file is missing or does not parse, a kit file differs from `templates/_agent`, the generated block in a template's `AGENTS.md` is missing or stale, or a template lacks the `doctor` npm script or `scripts/doctor.mjs`.

The design system has the same pattern (`sync-design.mjs` and `check-design.mjs`). See `templates/BRAND.md`.

## What to expect

- The agent knows to call `pepu_chain_info` first, to use SDK functions, and to run `npm run doctor` instead of reading `.env.local`.
- With `--skip-agent-files`, none of these files are in the app and the agent has only what you give it.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `check-agent-kit.mjs` reports a stale block | Someone edited the generated block, or `templates.json` or `_agent` changed | Run `node templates/scripts/sync-agent-kit.mjs`, and make hand edits above the markers only. |
| VS Code ignores the MCP config | The file uses `mcpServers` instead of `servers` | Use the shape in `.vscode/mcp.json` shown in [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md). |
| Claude Code does not offer the plugin | The folder is not trusted, or `.claude/settings.json` was removed | Trust the folder, or install by hand with the two `/plugin` commands. |
| The agent reads `.env.local` | It ignored the rules | Point it at the "Never print secrets" section and run `npm run doctor` yourself. |

## Related

- [Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md)
- [Skills Catalog](skills.md)
- [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md)
- [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md)
- [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md)
