# Template Gallery

Six starter templates, each a complete Next.js app on Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet (chain `97741`) built on `@pepu-chain/sdk`. This page shows which pillars each one demonstrates, what each needs, and how to pick. It is derived from `packages/create-pepu-app/src/templates.json` and the SDK's `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS`.

![The six starter templates with the pillars each includes: consumer-app, token-gated-app, nft-mint, game-app, sponsored-demo and sponsored-session-app](../.gitbook/assets/templates.png)

*Six templates, from a first login to the full stack.*

Each template README lists its setup. The sponsorship templates use the hosted bundler and paymaster but need a funded project of yours (claim, deposit, token).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer.
- A Privy app (App ID and App Secret) from [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io). Every template needs one. See [Privy Setup Walkthrough](../onboarding/privy-setup.md).
- A little PEPU in the wallet for templates where the user pays gas.

## Gallery

| Template | What it shows | Difficulty | Pillars |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`consumer-app`](consumer-app.md) | Sign in, get an embedded wallet, send native PEPU | starter | Google to wallet |
| [`token-gated-app`](token-gated-app.md) | Unlock content by holding an ERC-20 or NFT, balances batched through Multicall3 | starter | Google to wallet |
| [`nft-mint`](nft-mint.md) | An ERC-721 mint page plus the Foundry and Hardhat contract | intermediate | Google to wallet |
| [`game-app`](game-app.md) | Grant a session once, then play with no wallet popup per move | advanced | Google to wallet, session keys |
| [`sponsored-demo`](sponsored-demo.md) | A zero-balance smart account taps on-chain, the paymaster pays | advanced | Google to wallet, sponsored transactions |
| [`sponsored-session-app`](sponsored-session-app.md) | Google or email sign-in, one on-chain session, then actions with no popup and no user gas | advanced | All three, combined |

## Pillar matrix

The three core pillars and their combination. "Login" means Privy login with a server-provisioned embedded wallet; Google is one of the login methods and is required by `sponsored-session-app`.

| Template | Google to wallet | Session keys | Sponsored transactions | Combination |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `consumer-app` | Yes | No | No | No |
| `token-gated-app` | Yes | No | No | No |
| `nft-mint` | Yes | No | No | No |
| `game-app` | Yes | Yes, Privy session signer (off-chain scope, user pays gas) | No | No |
| `sponsored-demo` | Yes | No | Yes, Privy Smart Wallets transport | No |
| `sponsored-session-app` | Yes | Yes, on-chain Kernel session key | Yes, direct bundler and paymaster | Yes |

See [The Three Pillars and How They Combine](../get-started/pillars.md).

## Env needs at a glance

| Template | Required | Optional | Extra setup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `consumer-app` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | none | none |
| `token-gated-app` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, and at least one of `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC20_ADDRESS` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC721_ADDRESS` | the two gate addresses | none |
| `nft-mint` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | none | Deploy the contract in `contracts/` first |
| `game-app` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES`, `PEPU_RPC_URL` | Generate and register the authorization key, deploy `TapScore` |
| `sponsored-demo` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMASTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | Enable Smart Wallets in the Privy dashboard with `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project token>` |
| `sponsored-session-app` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (hosted URL with your project server key) | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (defaults to the hosted bundler), `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES`, `PEPU_RPC_URL` | A claimed and funded paymaster project of your own |

## Privy dashboard settings at a glance

| Setting | consumer | token-gated | nft-mint | game | sponsored-demo | sponsored-session |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A login method enabled | Required | Required | Required | Required | Required | Required |
| Google login enabled | | | | | | Required |
| Allowed origin with exact port (`http://localhost:3000`) | Required | Required | Required | Required | Required | Required |
| Embedded wallets enabled | Required | Required | Required | Required | Required | Required |
| Authorization key and key quorum | | | | Required | | |
| Smart Wallets (chain `97741`, Kernel, bundler and paymaster URLs) | | | | | Required | Not needed: it builds its own Kernel account |

Field-by-field instructions: [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

## Choosing a template

| If you want | Use |
|---|---|
| Your first app: login, wallet, send | `consumer-app` |
| Holder-only content, communities, perks | `token-gated-app` |
| A mint page for your own collection | `nft-mint` |
| Many fast actions with no popup, and your users pay gas | `game-app` |
| To see sponsorship work, or build gasless sends on Privy Smart Wallets | `sponsored-demo` |
| The full stack: Google or email sign-in, session key, no popup, no user gas | `sponsored-session-app` |

Rules of thumb:

- Start with `consumer-app` unless you need a specific pillar. The other starters share its login and wallet code.
- If your users must never pay gas you need a funded paymaster project; the bundler and paymaster are hosted by PEPU. The free tier is only for PEPU's own Privy app.
- `game-app` and `sponsored-session-app` solve the same popup problem with different trust models. `game-app`: Privy enforces the scope off-chain and the user pays gas. `sponsored-session-app`: the chain enforces the scope and a paymaster pays. See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md) and [Sponsored Session](../onboarding/sponsored-session.md).

## Scaffold one

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template <name>
```

Add `--yes` to skip prompts. Every flag, the `--json` output and the vendored-SDK note are in [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md).

Then, in every template:

```bash
cd my-app
npm install            # or pnpm install, yarn, bun install
npm run doctor         # checks .env.local against the template's requirements; prints no values
npm run dev            # http://localhost:3000
```

Run on port 3000. Privy's allowed origins match the exact origin including the port, and Next.js silently falls back to 3001 when 3000 is taken, which breaks login.

## What every template shares

- The SDK is the source for chain, addresses, providers, wallet provisioning and explorer links. Nothing redefines a chain, RPC URL or address.
- Mainnet only. No network switch.
- In the wagmi-based templates (consumer, token-gated, nft-mint, game), the embedded wallet is pinned as the active account (`useActiveWalletPin`), so a browser extension cannot silently become the sender.
- A setup screen that lists what is missing in most templates, so the app runs before you configure it.
- A gas notice. No template calls a transaction free or gasless unless a paymaster paid it.
- The shared PEPU design system and the agent kit (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, editor configs). See [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login fails with a CSP or 403 error | The app is on port 3001, or the origin is not allowed | Free port 3000, or add the exact origin to Allowed origins in Privy. |
| The app shows a setup screen | Required env vars are blank | Run `npm run doctor` and set the keys it lists. |
| A sponsorship template spins on "Setting up your smart wallet" or denies a send | No paymaster token configured, or the project is unfunded or unclaimed | Set the paymaster URL with your project token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`) and run `pepu_sponsorship_status`. |

## Related

- [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md)
- [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](../get-started/quickstart-app.md)
- [Privy Configuration Overview](../privy/index.md)
- [Template: Consumer App](consumer-app.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/templates/consumer-app

# Template: Consumer App

The `consumer-app` template shows that onchain onboarding can feel like a normal app: sign in with email or Google, get an embedded wallet, see a live PEPU balance and send native PEPU, with no seed phrase and no browser extension. It is the best first template and the base the other starters build on.

No sponsorship: the user pays gas in PEPU.

## What it demonstrates

| Pillar | Covered |
|---|---|
| Google to wallet | Yes: login (email, Google, or an existing wallet), server-side wallet provisioning, embedded wallet as the active account |
| Session keys | No |
| Sponsored transactions | No. A permanent notice says sponsorship is not usable by this app, and there is no "gasless" badge |

- Signed out: a landing page with one sign-in button.
- Signed in: provisions the wallet if the user has none, shows its address (copy button and a pepuscan link), its live PEPU balance and a form to send native PEPU with a pending state and a transaction link.
- Gas notice: every send costs the user real PEPU, a fraction of a cent.

## Scaffold

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template consumer-app
```

See [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md) for every flag.

## SDK functions it uses

| Job | SDK function (subpath) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Privy, react-query and wagmi providers, mainnet-only Privy config, active-wallet pin | `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` (`/privy/wagmi`), which uses `createPepuPrivyConfig`, `pepuWagmiConfig` and `useActiveWalletPin` | `app/providers.tsx` |
| Wallet provisioning (request, timeouts, `refreshUser`, retry) | `useEnsureWallet` (`/privy/react`) | `WalletGate` in `components/signed-in-view.tsx` |
| Server-side wallet creation | `createEnsureWalletRoute` (`/privy/server`) | `app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts` |
| Embedded versus external wallet | `useEmbeddedWallet` (`/privy/react`) | `components/wallet-card.tsx` |
| Chain facts, explorer links, amount formatting | `pepuMainnet`, `explorerLinks`, `formatPepu` (core) | wallet card, send form, network badge |
| Env check | `checkPepuEnv` (`/doctor`) | `scripts/doctor.mjs` |

## Environment and Privy settings

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Yes | Public by design. |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Yes | Server only. Used by `app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts`. |

No optional variables.

Privy dashboard checklist (the same list sits in the template's `.env.example`). Doctor requirements `login-methods`, `allowed-origins`, `embedded-wallets`:

- Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (public) and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` (secret, server only), both under Settings, Basics.
- Allowed origins: the exact origin with the port, `http://localhost:3000`, plus your production domain.
- Login methods: email, Google and external wallet, matching `loginMethods` in `app/providers.tsx` (enable what you list).
- Embedded wallets: enable for Ethereum, create on login. `WalletGate` calls `/api/wallet/ensure` after login and creates the wallet server-side with the app secret if the dashboard setting is off, so both together is fine. TEE (user-controlled) mode is what the live tests used.
- Smart Wallets: leave off. Not used here; enabling it is harmless.
- Coinbase Wallet is pinned to `eoaOnly` in code because it does not support chain `97741`.

Field by field: [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

## Run and check

```bash
cd my-app
npm install
npm run doctor      # ok or FAIL per key, no values printed
npm run dev         # http://localhost:3000, the port must be free
```

Fund the wallet with a small amount of PEPU to send something. Mainnet gas costs a fraction of a cent.

## Project structure

```text
app/            layout, providers (PepuPrivyWagmiProvider), page, api/wallet/ensure
components/     signed-out-view, signed-in-view, wallet-card, send-pepu-form, gas-notice, missing-config-notice
lib/format.ts   address truncation
scripts/doctor.mjs
contracts/      foundry and hardhat projects with a trivial example contract
```

## Limitations

- Sending PEPU is a standard wagmi send. Privy's pre-flight gas check is conservative at PEPU's base fee of about 12,500 gwei.
- No sponsorship: the user pays gas in PEPU.

Privy runs two wallet architectures, and which one your Privy app uses changes what happens on login. The template README spells it out.

## Customizing it

- Add your own panels to `components/signed-in-view.tsx`; keep `WalletGate` so a signed-in user always has a wallet.
- To let an external wallet be the active account, pass `pinEmbeddedWallet={false}` to `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`. The default is deliberate: the template's story depends on the embedded wallet being the sender.
- Do not add a "Max" button: Privy's pre-flight balance check is over-conservative at PEPU's base fee. If you build one, size it with `maxSendableAmount()` from the SDK.
- Do not add a gasless badge unless you wire real sponsorship ([Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login hangs or returns 403 | The app is on port 3001, or the origin is not in Allowed origins | Free port 3000, or add the exact origin to Privy. |
| Wallet never appears | Automatic creation is off and the fallback route lacks the secret | Set `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` and check the `app/api/wallet/ensure` route. |
| A different address sends the transaction | A browser extension became the active wagmi account | Keep `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` (it pins the embedded wallet). |
| Privy refuses a transfer the wallet can afford | Its pre-flight gas check is conservative at the PEPU base fee | Send a slightly smaller amount. |
| "Unable to fetch token price" in the console | Harmless Privy noise | Ignore it. |

- [Template Gallery](index.md)
- [Social Login and Embedded Wallets (Privy)](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md)
- [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](../recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md)
- [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md)

# Template: Token-Gated App

The `token-gated-app` template signs a user in, then unlocks content when their wallet holds a positive balance of an ERC-20 or an NFT. The balance checks are batched into one RPC round trip through PEPU's own Multicall3. Use it for holder-only content, communities and perks.

The gate check is a free read.

## What it demonstrates

| Pillar | Covered |
|---|---|
| Google to wallet | Yes: login, server-side wallet provisioning, embedded wallet as the active account |
| Session keys | No |
| Sponsored transactions | No. The balance check is a read and costs no gas |

- Signed in: shows the embedded wallet's address and PEPU balance, then one batched read checks the configured token balance or balances. Any positive balance of at least one configured token unlocks the gated panel.
- The rule is deliberately the simplest possible (`balance > 0`): no minimum, allowlist or tiers. The batched-read pattern is the part worth reusing.

## Scaffold

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template token-gated-app
```

## SDK functions it uses

| Job | SDK function (subpath) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Providers, mainnet-only Privy config, active-wallet pin | `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` (`/privy/wagmi`) | `app/providers.tsx` |
| Wallet provisioning | `useEnsureWallet` (`/privy/react`) | `WalletGate` in `components/signed-in-view.tsx` |
| Server-side wallet creation | `createEnsureWalletRoute` (`/privy/server`) | `app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts` |
| Embedded versus external wallet | `useEmbeddedWallet` (`/privy/react`) | `components/wallet-card.tsx` |
| Batched balance reads | `pepuMulticall` (core), viem's `multicall` pinned to PEPU's own Multicall3 | `components/token-gate-panel.tsx` |
| Chain facts, explorer links | `pepuMainnet`, `explorerLinks` (core) | wallet card, gate panel |
| Env check | `checkPepuEnv` (`/doctor`) | `scripts/doctor.mjs` |

The ERC-20 and ERC-721 read ABIs come from viem (`erc20Abi`, `erc721Abi`); the SDK does not ship its own. PEPU's Multicall3 is `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`, not the canonical address. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md).

## Environment and Privy settings

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Yes | Public. |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Yes | Server only. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC20_ADDRESS` | At least one of the two | Defaults in `.env.example` to WPEPU (`0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8`), only so the template runs out of the box. It is not a recommendation to gate on WPEPU: replace it with your token. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC721_ADDRESS` | At least one of the two | Blank by default. Deploy the `nft-mint` template or your own ERC-721 and paste its address. The template will not invent an address. |

The doctor reports an error until at least one gate address is valid.

Privy dashboard checklist (the same list sits in the template's `.env.example`). Doctor requirements `login-methods`, `allowed-origins`, `embedded-wallets`:

- Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (public) and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` (secret, server only), both under Settings, Basics.
- Allowed origins: the exact origin with the port, `http://localhost:3000`, plus your production domain.
- Login methods: email, Google and external wallet, matching `loginMethods` in `app/providers.tsx` (enable what you list).
- Embedded wallets: enable for Ethereum, create on login. `WalletGate` calls `/api/wallet/ensure` after login and creates the wallet server-side with the app secret if the dashboard setting is off, so both together is fine. TEE (user-controlled) mode is what the live tests used.
- Smart Wallets: leave off. Not used here; enabling it is harmless.
- Coinbase Wallet is pinned to `eoaOnly` in code because it does not support chain `97741`.

Field by field: [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

## Run and check

```bash
cd my-app
npm install
npm run doctor
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000
```

## Project structure

```text
app/            layout, providers, page (behind SetupGate), api/wallet/ensure
components/     signed-out-view, signed-in-view, wallet-card, token-gate-panel, gated-content, setup-gate, missing-config-notice
lib/env.ts      parses the gate addresses once
lib/format.ts   address and token-amount formatting for any decimals
scripts/doctor.mjs
```

## Limitations

- The gate check runs in the browser and can be bypassed by editing browser state. Re-check on the server for anything server-enforced.
- No sponsorship: the user pays gas.

## Customizing it

- Replace `components/gated-content.tsx` with what you gate.
- Set your own token addresses. For tiers or minimums, change the rule in `components/token-gate-panel.tsx`.
- If you gate something server-enforced (an API route, a paid download), re-check the balance on the server too.
- If you add a write path, remember the user pays gas. Do not add a gasless badge without real sponsorship.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The app shows a setup screen | Neither gate address is set to a valid address | Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC20_ADDRESS` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC721_ADDRESS`. |
| The batched read fails | Hardcoded canonical Multicall3 address in custom code | Use `pepuMulticall` from the SDK. |
| Login hangs or returns 403 | Wrong port or origin | Use `http://localhost:3000` and add it to Allowed origins. |

- [Batch Reads with Multicall3](../recipes/batch-reads-with-multicall3.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/templates/nft-mint

# Template: NFT Mint

The `nft-mint` template is an ERC-721 mint page: connect, see the collection's live mint price and supply, mint with a real transaction and list the tokens the wallet owns. It ships the `PepuNft` contract twice, for Foundry and for Hardhat. Use it as the base for a mint page for your own collection.

There is no pre-deployed collection: you deploy `PepuNft` yourself before the app runs. Minting is a real transaction and the user pays gas.

## What it demonstrates

| Pillar | Covered |
|---|---|
| Google to wallet | Yes |
| Session keys | No |
| Sponsored transactions | No. Even a zero-price mint costs the caller gas, and there is no gasless badge |

- Collection read in one batched Multicall3 call: name, symbol, mint price, total supply, `MAX_SUPPLY`.
- A Mint button that sends a real transaction.
- The owned token ids, from a second batched read using `ERC721Enumerable`.

## Scaffold

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template nft-mint
```

## Deploy the contract first

Pick one toolchain, each in `contracts/`:

- `contracts/foundry` (Foundry, `forge` and `cast`)
- `contracts/hardhat` (Hardhat with TypeScript)

Both deploy the same `PepuNft`: OpenZeppelin Contracts v5.7.0 `ERC721`, `ERC721Enumerable` and `Ownable`, with `MAX_SUPPLY = 1000`, token ids from 1, and a `payable` `mint()` whose price the deployer sets. Neither project is wired into the Next.js build. If `foundry-zksync` is installed, the `forge` on your PATH may be the wrong fork for an Arbitrum Orbit chain: run `forge --version` and confirm it does not mention `zksync`. Verification and deployment: [Deploy and Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md).

Then set `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` to the deployed address.

## SDK functions it uses

| Job | SDK function (subpath) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Providers, mainnet-only Privy config, active-wallet pin | `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` (`/privy/wagmi`) | `app/providers.tsx` |
| Wallet provisioning | `useEnsureWallet` (`/privy/react`), `createEnsureWalletRoute` (`/privy/server`) | `WalletGate`, `app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts` |
| Embedded versus external wallet | `useEmbeddedWallet` (`/privy/react`) | `components/wallet-card.tsx` |
| Batched collection reads | `pepuMulticall` (core), pinned to PEPU's Multicall3 | `components/mint-panel.tsx` |
| Owned tokens | wagmi `useReadContracts`, routed through the same Multicall3 because `pepuMainnet` carries `contracts.multicall3` | `components/owned-tokens.tsx` |
| Chain facts, explorer links, amount formatting | `pepuMainnet`, `explorerLinks`, `formatPepu` (core) | wallet card, mint panel |
| Env check | `checkPepuEnv` (`/doctor`) | `scripts/doctor.mjs` |

The contract ABI is the template's own (`lib/nft-abi.ts`), covering only the functions the app calls.

## Environment and Privy settings

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Yes | Public. |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Yes | Server only. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | Yes | Blank on purpose. Until set, a setup screen shows the exact steps. |

Privy dashboard checklist (the same list sits in the template's `.env.example`). Doctor requirements `login-methods`, `allowed-origins`, `embedded-wallets`:

- Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (public) and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` (secret, server only), both under Settings, Basics.
- Allowed origins: the exact origin with the port, `http://localhost:3000`, plus your production domain.
- Login methods: email, Google and external wallet, matching `loginMethods` in `app/providers.tsx` (enable what you list).
- Embedded wallets: enable for Ethereum, create on login. `WalletGate` calls `/api/wallet/ensure` after login and creates the wallet server-side with the app secret if the dashboard setting is off, so both together is fine. TEE (user-controlled) mode is what the live tests used.
- Smart Wallets: leave off. Not used here; enabling it is harmless.
- Coinbase Wallet is pinned to `eoaOnly` in code because it does not support chain `97741`.

Field by field: [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

## Run and check

```bash
cd my-app
# deploy the contract first (contracts/foundry or contracts/hardhat)
npm install
npm run doctor
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000
```

Fund the wallet with a little PEPU: a mint needs gas, plus the mint price if it is above zero.

## Project structure

```text
app/            layout, providers, page (behind SetupGate), api/wallet/ensure
components/     signed-out-view, signed-in-view, wallet-card, mint-panel, owned-tokens, gas-notice, setup-gate, missing-config-notice
lib/            env.ts, nft-abi.ts, format.ts
scripts/doctor.mjs
contracts/      foundry/ and hardhat/ (PepuNft)
```

## Limitations

- No pre-deployed collection: deploy `PepuNft` yourself and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`.
- No sponsorship: the user pays gas.

## Customizing it

- Change the supply, price or metadata in `contracts/`, redeploy and update the address and `lib/nft-abi.ts`.
- To list a collection somewhere, note that being listed (for example on PepuSwap) is a third-party decision and is not automatic from deploying.
- For a gasless mint you would need real sponsorship ([Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)), which this template does not include.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Setup screen with deployment steps | `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` is blank | Deploy `PepuNft` and set the address. |
| Deploy goes wrong or produces odd output | `forge` is the `foundry-zksync` fork | Install upstream Foundry and recheck `forge --version`. |
| Mint transaction fails | Not enough PEPU for gas plus the price, or supply is exhausted | Fund the wallet, or check `totalSupply` against `MAX_SUPPLY`. |

## Related

- [Template Gallery](index.md)
- [Deploy an ERC-20](../recipes/deploy-an-erc20.md)
- [Deploy and Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md)
- [Template: Token-Gated App](token-gated-app.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/templates/game-app

# Template: Game App

The `game-app` template shows how a game can write on-chain on every move without a wallet popup per move. The player signs in with Google or email, grants one scoped Privy session signer, and then taps. Each tap is a real transaction submitted by the app's backend on the player's behalf. The player pays gas.

No sponsorship: the user pays gas in PEPU.

## What it demonstrates

| Pillar | Covered |
|---|---|
| Google to wallet | Yes |
| Session keys | Yes: a Privy session signer on a plain embedded wallet. The scope is enforced off-chain by Privy's policy engine |
| Sponsored transactions | No. The player's wallet pays gas, a fraction of a cent per tap |

The flow: sign in, grant a session (one consent screen, one signature), play (the backend submits `tap()` with no further prompts), revoke at any time or let it expire.

The scope, built by `buildSessionPolicy` from the one definition in `lib/scope.ts`:

| Constraint | Value |
|---|---|
| Contract | only the deployed `TapScore` address |
| Function | only `tap()`, matched by selector |
| Value | exactly `0x0` |
| Expiry | denied after `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` |

Trust model, stated in the app and the README: Privy's backend policy engine enforces the scope. There is no on-chain validator to audit. For the on-chain model see [`sponsored-session-app`](sponsored-session-app.md).

## Scaffold

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template game-app
```

## SDK functions it uses

| Job | SDK function (subpath) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Providers and active-wallet pin | `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` (`/privy/wagmi`) | `app/providers.tsx` |
| Wallet provisioning | `createEnsureWalletRoute` (`/privy/server`), `useEnsureWallet`, `useEmbeddedWallet` (`/privy/react`) | `app/api/wallet/ensure`, `components/` |
| Scoped policy and consent data | `buildSessionPolicy`, `describeSessionScope`, `SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE`, `PRIVY_POLICY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` (`/session`) | `lib/scope.ts`, `components/session-consent-screen.tsx` |
| Grant, status and revoke routes | `createSessionRoutes` (`/session/server`) | `app/api/session/*` |
| One gameplay transaction: Privy signs, the SDK broadcasts | `createSessionActionRoute` (`/session/server`) | `app/api/game/tap` |
| Client session flow | `useSessionGrant`, `useSessionStatus`, `useSessionRevoke`, `useSessionAct` (`/session/react`) | `components/` |
| Authorization key generation | `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` (`/doctor`) | `scripts/generate-authorization-key.mjs` |
| Explorer links | `explorerLinks` (core) | components |

Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` does not support chain `97741`. The SDK works around it by asking Privy to sign only (`eth_signTransaction`) and broadcasting the signed transaction to PEPU's RPC itself, with a 20% gas-limit buffer. See [Sign with Privy, Broadcast Yourself](../recipes/sign-with-privy-broadcast-yourself.md).

## Environment and Privy settings

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Yes | Public. |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Yes | Server only. Authenticates the backend that submits taps and provisions wallets. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` | Yes | Id of the key quorum Privy returns after you register the public key. An identifier, not a secret. |
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Yes | The private half, base64 PKCS8. A real secret: anyone holding it can request transactions as any wallet that granted a signer to the quorum, bounded by the policy. Never commit it. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | Yes | Your deployed `TapScore`. The policy names this contract explicitly. |
| `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` | No | Default 15, clamped to 1440. Baked into the policy expiry, so Privy enforces it. |
| `PEPU_RPC_URL` | No | Server only. RPC the backend broadcasts to. Without it the SDK uses the public default. |

Privy dashboard checklist (the same list sits in the template's `.env.example`). Doctor requirements `login-methods`, `allowed-origins`, `embedded-wallets`, `authorization-key-quorum`:

- Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (public) and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` (secret, server only), both under Settings, Basics.
- Allowed origins: the exact origin with the port, `http://localhost:3000`, plus your production domain.
- Login methods: email, Google and external wallet, matching `loginMethods` in `app/providers.tsx` (enable what you list).
- Embedded wallets: enable for Ethereum, create on login. `WalletGate` calls `/api/wallet/ensure` after login and creates the wallet server-side with the app secret if the dashboard setting is off, so both together is fine. TEE (user-controlled) mode is what the live tests used.
- Smart Wallets: not needed. This template uses a session signer on a plain embedded wallet.
- Coinbase Wallet is pinned to `eoaOnly` in code because it does not support chain `97741`.
- Authorization key and key quorum (Wallet infrastructure, Authorization keys): run `npm run generate-authorization-key`, register the public key, put it in a key quorum, and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (public id) and `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` (the private half, secret). They must come from the same pair. Policy and rule names are limited to 49 characters.

See [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md) and [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

## Run and check

```bash
cd my-app
npm install
npm run generate-authorization-key   # register the public half in Privy, then fill .env.local
# deploy contracts/foundry or contracts/hardhat (TapScore) and set NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_CONTRACT_ADDRESS
npm run doctor
npm run dev                          # http://localhost:3000
npm test                             # the scope tests
```

TapScore is also deployed on mainnet at `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` (used by the sponsored templates). Deploy your own for your own game.

## Project structure

```text
app/api/config/          booleans only, never values
app/api/wallet/ensure/   createEnsureWalletRoute()
app/api/session/*        createSessionRoutes(): grant, status, revoke
app/api/game/tap/        createSessionActionRoute(): one gameplay tx
components/              session-consent-screen (the most important UI), session-status-card, game-board
lib/scope.ts             the ONE session scope and the game ABI
lib/env.ts               client-safe NEXT_PUBLIC_* values
contracts/               TapScore for Foundry and Hardhat
```

## Limitations

- Sessions are Privy session signers scoped off-chain. The user pays gas.

## Customizing it

- To add a gameplay function, add its ABI fragment to `lib/scope.ts` and add a condition for it. Widening the policy widens what a compromised key can do.
- Keep gameplay functions non-payable: that is what makes the zero-value condition meaningful.
- Keep sessions short. The 15 minute default is deliberate.
- Never add a code path that grants an unscoped signer. An empty `policyIds` makes a signer effectively unscoped over the whole wallet, and `buildSessionPolicy` refuses to build one.
- Policy and rule names must be at most 49 characters (Privy's live validator); `buildSessionPolicy` enforces it.
- Keep the off-chain notice in the README and the consent screen. Do not soften it.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Grant fails with a name error | A custom policy name is 50 characters or more | Keep names at 49 or fewer. |
| A tap returns 409 or is denied | The session expired, was revoked, or the call is outside the scope | Grant a new session; check `lib/scope.ts` against the call. |
| "Unsupported chain with id 97741" | Something is calling Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` | Use `createSessionActionRoute`, which signs and broadcasts itself. |
| Taps fail to broadcast | Public RPC rate limit | Set `PEPU_RPC_URL` to an authenticated endpoint. |
| Login hangs or returns 403 | Wrong port or origin | Use `http://localhost:3000` and allow it in Privy. |

## Related

- [Template Gallery](index.md)
- [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md)
- [Grant a Session](../recipes/grant-a-session.md)
- [Template: Sponsored Session App](sponsored-session-app.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/templates/sponsored-demo

# Template: Sponsored Demo

The `sponsored-demo` template is a minimal browser demo of gas sponsorship end to end on PEPU. A user signs in with Privy, gets a Kernel smart account holding zero PEPU, clicks one button to send a sponsored `TapScore.tap()` UserOperation, and watches the paymaster's own EntryPoint deposit drop. The drop, not the transaction alone, is the evidence of who paid.

To make this demo sponsor with your own Privy app you must bring a project: claim it, set targets and limits, deposit, and use its token (below). It uses the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`). The free tier is not reachable from this demo: it needs a verified Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app, and the Privy Smart Wallets dashboard URL is static and cannot attach a token.

## What it demonstrates

| Pillar | Covered |
|---|---|
| Google to wallet | Yes: the embedded wallet is the owner (signer) of the smart account |
| Session keys | No |
| Sponsored transactions | Yes, over the Privy Smart Wallets transport |

It is a demo, not a production starter: no wagmi, no external-wallet connect, one screen, no retry or backoff. A failed tap shows a typed error and lets you press again.

## Two addresses

Sign-in produces two addresses and the demo shows the second:

- The embedded wallet is an EOA that only acts as the signer (owner) of the smart account.
- The Kernel smart account is a separate contract account with its own address. It holds `0 PEPU`, sends the UserOperation and appears as the sender on pepuscan.

Do not expect them to match and do not send funds to one expecting them in the other. See [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md).

## Scaffold

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template sponsored-demo
```

## SDK functions it uses

| Job | SDK function (subpath) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Privy provider with Smart Wallets nested inside | `PepuPrivyProvider`, `composeProviders` (`/privy/react`) | `app/providers.tsx` |
| Provision the owner wallet | `createEnsureWalletRoute` (`/privy/server`), `useEnsureWallet` (`/privy/react`) | `app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts`, `WalletGate` |
| The sponsored send | `useSponsoredSend({ transport: "privy-smart-wallets" })` (`/aa/react`), no ZeroDev packages (needs `permissionless`, which Privy's smart-wallets module requires) | `components/sponsored-tap-demo.tsx` |
| The Kernel smart account address | `usePepuSmartAccount` (`/aa/react`) | same |
| The paymaster deposit before and after | `getPaymasterDeposit` (`/aa`) | same |
| Readable failures | `describeUserOpFailure` (`/aa`, applied inside `useSponsoredSend`) | same |
| Is a bundler and paymaster configured | `usePepuSponsorship` (`/aa/react`), wrapping `checkSponsorship` | same |
| Chain facts, explorer links | `getContract`, `isDeployed`, `pepuMainnet`, `explorerLinks` (core) | components |

`lib/tapscore.ts` is the only template-specific code: the hardcoded target (`TapScore` at `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`) and its ABI.

## Environment and Privy settings

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Yes | Public. |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Yes | Server only. Used to provision the owner wallet. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMASTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | No | Public on-chain address. Defaults to the deployed v2 paymaster `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (the v1 paymaster is retired). The demo reads its EntryPoint deposit to show the before and after. |

Sponsorship is configured entirely in the Privy dashboard, not in the app. Settings, Wallet infrastructure, Smart wallets:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Chain | `97741` |
| Provider | Kernel |
| Bundler URL | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (local default for your own: `http://localhost:4337`) |
| Paymaster URL | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project token>` (local default for your own: `http://localhost:8788`; the token is a credential) |

Use your project's client token (`ppt_`) with your app's origins set as the project's allowed origins, because Privy calls the paymaster from the browser. Never use the server key (`ppk_`) in the dashboard.

Also required (doctor requirements `login-methods`, `allowed-origins`, `embedded-wallets`, `smart-wallets`):

- Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (public) and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` (secret, server only), both under Settings, Basics.
- Allowed origins: `http://localhost:3000` (exact port) plus your production domain.
- Login methods: Google and email, matching `loginMethods` in `app/providers.tsx`.
- Embedded wallets: Ethereum, create on login. `WalletGate` and `/api/wallet/ensure` provision the owner wallet server-side as a fallback. TEE (user-controlled) mode is what the live tests used.
- Smart Wallets: **required**, with provider Kernel (ZeroDev) v3.1 and the custom chain PEPU, chain id `97741`, RPC `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz`. If it is off, the page spins forever on "Setting up your smart wallet..." and the app cannot work around it. Old dashboards may still hold temporary development bundler or paymaster URLs (tunnels): replace them with the hosted ones in the table above.
- Paymaster credential: the project **client token** (`ppt_`) inside the dashboard paymaster URL, with your app's origins allowed. Never use the server key (`ppk_`) there. The free tier cannot be used on this path (a static URL carries no per-user Privy token), so a funded project is required.

### What you must configure to sponsor with your own project

The demo does not sponsor out of the box for a third-party app. In order:

1. Sign in with Ethereum to the policy service (`/v2/auth/nonce`, `/v2/auth/login`).
2. Verify your Privy app: `POST /v2/projects/verify` with the Privy app id and secret (used for one request, never stored).
3. Claim the project (`claimProject`): immediate if the project is empty, pending 48 hours if someone already funded it.
4. Set the targets and limits: `setTargets` (include `TapScore`), `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`.
5. Deposit PEPU (`depositFor`). Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs.
6. Register the project to get the client token and the server key, then set allowed origins for the client token.
7. Enter the token in the Privy dashboard paymaster URL above.

The steps are in [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md) and [Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](../recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md).

The paymaster only sponsors allowlisted destinations. `TapScore` must be in the project's targets. See [Paymaster Overview](../infra/paymaster/overview.md) and [Bundler Overview](../infra/bundler/overview.md).

## Run and check

```bash
cd my-app
npm install
npm run doctor
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000 only
```

Run on port 3000 only. Privy's allowed origins match the exact origin including the port, and Next.js silently falls back to 3001 when 3000 is taken.

What you see: sign in, wait for the wallet and then the smart wallet to be set up, see the Kernel address with `0 PEPU`, click Sponsor a tap, then a transaction link and a before, after and drop panel for the paymaster deposit. A nonzero drop from a wallet that paid nothing shows the paymaster paid.

## Project structure

```text
app/            layout, providers (PepuPrivyProvider plus SmartWalletsProvider), page, api/wallet/ensure
components/     signed-in-view (WalletGate), sponsored-tap-demo (the whole sponsored path)
lib/            tapscore.ts (target and ABI), env.ts
scripts/doctor.mjs
```

## Limitations

- Using this demo with your own Privy app needs your own claimed and funded project and its token, plus the dashboard setup above.
- The free tier is not reachable from this demo.
- Each tap spends real paymaster deposit.

Idempotency: one tap is one UserOperation, a retry builds a fresh operation with the next nonce and never replays, and wallet provisioning looks for an existing wallet first.

## Customizing it

- Change the target in `lib/tapscore.ts` and add the new contract to the paymaster's allowlist and your app's allowed destinations.
- For a browser flow with a session key and no popups, use [`sponsored-session-app`](sponsored-session-app.md). This template keeps the Privy Smart Wallets transport: `/aa/react` never resolves `@zerodev/*`, and `permissionless` (required by Privy's smart-wallets module) is the only extra package it needs.
- Treat the paymaster URL as a secret and keep it out of the browser where you can.

## Common failures

| `code` or symptom | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Spinner on "Setting up your smart wallet" | Smart Wallets is off, or the bundler or paymaster URL is missing in the dashboard | Set chain `97741`, provider Kernel, both URLs. |
| `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | The call targets a contract not on the allowlist | Add `TapScore` to the global allowlist and your app's allowed destinations. |
| `PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` | The page origin is not allowed | Allow the exact origin including the port. |
| `PAYMASTER_DENIED` (also `AA32` to `AA34`) | The credential or sender was rejected, or the policy signer does not match the paymaster contract | Check the app key in the paymaster URL and that the smart account belongs to the signed-in user. |
| `PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE` (also `AA31`) | The paymaster's EntryPoint deposit cannot cover the operation | Deposit PEPU to the paymaster contract. |
| `PAYMASTER_CAP` | A daily, per-sender or per-operation cap was hit | Wait for the window to reset, or raise the limits. |
| `BUNDLER_AA_FAILED` (`AA25`) | Invalid nonce: another operation from this account is pending | Wait for it to confirm, then retry. |
| `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE` | The bundler or paymaster URL is unset or wrong | Fix the dashboard values. |
| The failure box says "not configured" but the dashboard is right | With this transport the working URLs live in Privy, not env | Treat that line as a hint. Export the env vars too if you want the probe to agree. |

## Related

- [Template Gallery](index.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)
- [Send a Sponsored Transaction](../recipes/sponsored-send.md)
- [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/templates/sponsored-session-app

# Template: Sponsored Session App

The `sponsored-session-app` template combines all three pillars in one flow: sign in with Google, approve one scoped, time-limited session, then act on Pepe Unchained V2 with no wallet popup and no gas from the user. The session is an on-chain ZeroDev Kernel permission and a paymaster pays the gas, so the user's accounts can stay at 0 PEPU. The demo action is `TapScore.tap()`.

![The live sponsored-session demo sign-in screen on desktop and mobile: Grant once, then act, with no popups and no gas](../.gitbook/assets/demo.png)

*The live demo's sign-in screen. [Try the live demo](https://roadmap-demo.pepeunchained.com).*

Live demo: [roadmap-demo.pepeunchained.com](https://roadmap-demo.pepeunchained.com) (being deployed now).

Sessions live in server memory in this template; use a persistent store in production. `npm run prove-session` runs the mechanism from a script: a throwaway owner signs one grant and a throwaway session key then sends two sponsored UserOperations that deploy the account and call `tap()`. The smart account balance stays 0 and `TapScore.scores(account)` is 2. The browser flow is Google login, one `eth_signTypedData_v4` signature on chain 97741, sponsored taps with no popup, and revoke. It uses the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`); you must bring a project: claim it, set targets and limits, deposit, and use its server key (below).

## What it demonstrates

| Pillar | Covered |
|---|---|
| Google to wallet | Yes: Google is required. The embedded wallet is the owner of the smart account |
| Session keys | Yes: an on-chain Kernel permission made of a call policy and a timestamp policy |
| Sponsored transactions | Yes: direct bundler and paymaster, no Privy Smart Wallets |
| The combination | Yes |

Who signs and where the limit lives:

```text
Google sign-in (Privy)  -> embedded wallet = OWNER
Start session           -> server makes a session key, decides expiry
Owner signs ONE EIP-712 message that enables the permission
Tap                     -> the session key signs a UserOperation; the bundler and paymaster send it
Kernel validates        -> call policy + expiry, on-chain
Revoke                  -> the server forgets the key
```

The first session-signed UserOperation also deploys the smart account and enables the permission, so the first action costs more gas than later ones.

Scope enforcement is on-chain, by the user's smart account, not by Privy and not by the app:

- Call policy v0.0.4 (`0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2`): only `TapScore` (`0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`), only the `tap()` selector (`0xfd221031`), value exactly zero.
- Timestamp policy (`0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F`): the permission is invalid after the expiry.

The paymaster separately sponsors only allowlisted destinations. That is an off-chain boundary on what sponsorship money can be spent on, not what protects the user.

## Scaffold

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template sponsored-session-app
```

## SDK functions it uses

| Job | SDK function (subpath) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The five session routes (prepare, activate, status, act, revoke) | `createSponsoredSessionRoutes`, `createMemoryStore` (`/combo`) | `lib/session-routes.ts`, `app/api/session/*` |
| The client flow | `useSponsoredSession` (`/combo/react`) | `components/session-flow.tsx` |
| The on-chain scope | `buildKernelSessionPolicies`, `approveKernelSession`, `describeKernelSessionScope`, `isCallInScope` (`/session/kernel`) | `lib/scope.ts` |
| Privy provider | `PepuPrivyProvider`, `WalletGate` (`/privy/react`) | `app/providers.tsx` |
| Wallet provisioning | `createEnsureWalletRoute` (`/privy/server`) | `app/api/wallet/ensure` |
| Shared trust text | `SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE`, `resolveSessionMinutes` (`/session`) | consent screen |
| Explorer links, errors | `explorerLinks`, `PepuError` (core) | components |

The state machine lives in the SDK; the route files are one-line mounts. The Kernel account is built with ZeroDev's SDK, not Privy's smart-wallet client, because Privy's client cannot install a scoped session validator. That is why you do not enable Smart Wallets in the Privy dashboard.

## Environment and Privy settings

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Yes | Public. |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Yes | Server only. |
| `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | No | Server only. ERC-4337 v0.7 bundler tuned for PEPU. Defaults to `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`; `.env.example` sets it. Local default for your own: `http://localhost:4337`. |
| `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | Yes | Server only. `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project server key>`. The server key (`ppk_`) is secret, so this URL is a credential. The session routes forward the signed-in user's Privy token as ERC-7677 context (ignored for project billing unless the service can verify it, in which case it must belong to the owner of the sending account; the free tier is the automatic fallback when the project cannot cover an operation). Local default for your own: `http://localhost:8788/paymaster/<your-app-key>`. |
| `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` | No | Default 15, clamped to 24 hours. Baked into the on-chain permission. |
| `PEPU_RPC_URL` | No | Authenticated RPC for server chain reads. Falls back to the public endpoint. |

What you must configure to sponsor with your own project (the free tier is not available here: it needs a verified Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app, and a third-party app's own Privy token is ignored for billing):

1. Sign in with Ethereum to the policy service (`/v2/auth/nonce`, `/v2/auth/login`).
2. Verify your Privy app: `POST /v2/projects/verify` with the Privy app id and secret (used for one request, never stored).
3. Claim the project (`claimProject`): immediate if the project is empty, pending 48 hours if someone already funded it.
4. Set the targets and limits: `setTargets` (include `TapScore`), `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`.
5. Deposit PEPU (`depositFor`). Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs.
6. Register the project to get the server key (`ppk_`, secret) and a client token (`ppt_`, which works only from the allowed origins you set; this template's server does not need it).
7. Put the server key in `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`.

See [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md) and [Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](../recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md).

Privy dashboard checklist (the same list sits in the template's `.env.example`). Doctor requirements `login-methods`, `allowed-origins`, `embedded-wallets`:

- Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (public) and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` (secret, server only), both under Settings, Basics.
- Allowed origins: the exact origin with the port, `http://localhost:3000`, plus your production domain.
- Login methods: Google and email, matching `loginMethods` in `app/providers.tsx` (the doctor checks Google as `login-methods.google`).
- Embedded wallets: enable for Ethereum, create on login. `WalletGate` calls `/api/wallet/ensure` after login and creates the wallet server-side with the app secret if the dashboard setting is off, so both together is fine. TEE (user-controlled) mode is what the live tests used.
- Coinbase `eoaOnly` does not apply: this template offers no external wallets.
- Smart Wallets: not required. The SDK builds the ZeroDev Kernel account itself. Leaving it enabled is harmless: users then also get a Privy smart wallet linked, which the paymaster also accepts as owned. If an old dashboard still has temporary development bundler or paymaster URLs (tunnels), replace them with the hosted ones or turn Smart Wallets off.
- Paymaster credential: `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` holds the project server key (`ppk_`), server only. Sponsorship tries your project first and falls back to the free tier; the free tier needs the user's Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app, which the SDK combination routes forward automatically.

Field by field: [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

Your app must also be registered in the paymaster policy service with `TapScore` in its allowed destinations. See [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](../infra/paymaster/policy-and-caps.md).

Gas budget (measured): the policy service reserves each operation's worst-case cost, about 20.5 PEPU for the first operation of a session (deploy plus enable permission) and about 6.9 PEPU for later ones. The real first-session cost measured about 12.8 PEPU for two taps. With the stock per-user hourly cap of 25 PEPU, a second tap in the same hour was denied. Size `USER_HOURLY_SPEND_CAP_WEI`, `USER_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_WEI` and your app's `dailySpendCapWei` above that. The SDK exports the numbers as `SESSION_GAS_RESERVATION_PEPU`.

## Run and check

```bash
cd my-app
npm install
npm run doctor
npm run dev                  # http://localhost:3000, the port must be 3000
npm test                     # scope, route wiring, formatting
```

Prove it without a browser (this sends real sponsored transactions on mainnet with throwaway keys that need no balance):

```bash
PEPU_BUNDLER_URL=http://localhost:4337 \
PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=http://localhost:8788/paymaster/<your-app-key> \
npm run prove-session
```

It runs the template's own scope through `createSponsoredSessionRoutes`: prepare, one owner signature, activate, two taps, the account balance (0), the score (2), then revoke. The two refusals (a different selector on the allowed contract, an expired grant) are covered by the SDK's own `prove-session` script (`pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk prove-session` in the devkit repository).

## Project structure

```text
lib/scope.ts             the only place the scope is defined (tap() on TapScore, address from the SDK registry)
lib/session-routes.ts    createSponsoredSessionRoutes plus the in-memory store
lib/tapscore.ts          the ABI
app/api/session/{prepare,activate,status,act,revoke}   one-line mounts
app/api/wallet/ensure    createEnsureWalletRoute()
components/              session-flow, consent-screen, address-card, action-panel
scripts/prove-session.ts end-to-end session script for mainnet
```

## Limitations

- The template is a reference implementation. Review the trust model below before production use.
- Sessions are stored in server memory; use a persistent store in production.

## Trust model and limits

- The owner key never leaves Privy and the user's browser. The server never signs as the owner.
- The session key is held by your server. A compromised server or a leaked key can do exactly what the permission allows (`tap()`, zero value) until it expires, and nothing else.
- The approval holds no secret. The owner address always comes from Privy's records for the verified access token, never from the request.
- Sessions are stored in server memory (`createMemoryStore`). A restart ends every session and it does not work across several serverless instances. For production, implement `SessionStore` on a database or KV and encrypt the session private key at rest.
- Revoke deletes the key and approval on the server, so the app stops acting immediately. It does not uninstall the permission on-chain. The grant stays valid until its expiry but only the deleted key can use it, and only for `tap()`. Keep sessions short.
- The smart account address is per owner and does not change between sessions. Funds sent to the signer do not appear in the smart account. See [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md).

## Customizing it

To sponsor your own contract: change the ABI in `lib/tapscore.ts`, then `scope` in `lib/scope.ts` and `act.buildCalls` in `lib/session-routes.ts`; deploy the contract; add it to the paymaster's allowlist and your app's allowed destinations. Each `KernelSessionCall` takes a target, an ABI, a function name and an optional `valueLimit`; add more calls for more functions. Argument rules and ZeroDev's rate-limit policy are not wrapped by the SDK yet. Keep the policy as narrow as the action allows: it is the user's safety, not a formality. See [Sponsored Session in One Flow](../recipes/sponsored-session.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Setup screen lists missing items | Env not set | Run `npm run doctor` and fill `.env.local`. `/api/config` reports booleans only. |
| A second tap is denied with a trailing-hour cap message | Per-user cap below the gas reservation | Raise the caps above about 20.5 PEPU for the first operation and 6.9 after. |
| Denied for the destination | `TapScore` is not in the paymaster's allowed destinations | Add it for your app. |
| Sessions vanish | Server restart with the in-memory store | Expected in development. Use a persistent, encrypted store in production. |
| Login hangs or returns 403 | Wrong port or origin, or Google not enabled | Use `http://localhost:3000`, allow it, enable Google. |
| `sponsored session` calls fail with a config error | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` or `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` unset | Set both, then run `pepu_sponsorship_status`. |

## Related

- [Template Gallery](index.md)
- [Sponsored Session: No Popup, No Gas](../onboarding/sponsored-session.md)
- [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md)
- [Template: Game App](game-app.md)

# create-pepu-app CLI

`create-pepu-app` scaffolds a PEPU starter template into a new folder: it copies the template, vendors the SDK, writes `.env.local`, adds the agent kit, optionally installs dependencies and runs `git init`, then prints what is left for you to do. This page is the reference for its prompts, flags, `--json` output, env prefill and the vendored-SDK behaviour.

Run it with `npx create-pepu-app@latest`. The default is the npm SDK, with a vendored fallback when npm cannot be reached. The templates it ships scaffold `@pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.3`.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer.
- A package manager: npm, pnpm, yarn or bun. The CLI detects the one that launched it.
- A target folder that does not exist or is empty.

## Usage

```bash
npx create-pepu-app                       # interactive
npx create-pepu-app my-app --yes          # defaults, no prompts
npm create pepu-app@latest my-app -- --pm pnpm
npx create-pepu-app my-app --template token-gated-app --yes
npx create-pepu-app --list                # show the templates
npx create-pepu-app my-app --template sponsored-session-app --yes --no-install --no-git --json
```

Agents can do the same through the MCP tool `pepu_scaffold_app`, which runs this CLI with `--yes --json`. See [Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md#pepu_scaffold_app).

## Flags

```text
create-pepu-app [directory] [options]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` (positional) | prompted, or `./pepu-app` with `--yes` | Where to create the project. Only one is accepted. A path such as `./apps/my-app` works; the package name is derived from the last segment. |
| `-t`, `--template <name>` | `consumer-app` | The template to scaffold. Passing it skips the template question. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | off | Skip prompts and accept defaults. Installs and runs `git init` unless you pass `--no-install` or `--no-git`. |
| `--pm <manager>` | auto-detected | `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` or `bun`. Detected from `npm_config_user_agent`, falling back to `npm`. |
| `--install` / `--no-install` | ask, or install | Install dependencies after scaffolding, or skip. |
| `--git` / `--no-git` | ask, or `git init` | Run `git init`, or skip. It is also skipped when the folder is already inside a git repository or git is missing. |
| `--sdk <mode>` | `npm` | How the app depends on `@pepu-chain/sdk`: `vendor` or `npm`. See [Vendored SDK versus npm](#vendored-sdk-versus-npm). |
| `--skip-agent-files` | off | Leave out the agent kit: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json` and `.claude/settings.json`. See [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md). |
| `--json` | off | Print exactly one JSON document on stdout. Implies `--yes`. For agents and scripts. |
| `--list` | off | Print the templates and exit. With `--json`, as JSON. |
| `-h`, `--help` | | Show usage. |
| `-v`, `--version` | | Show the CLI version. |

Parsing rules: an unknown flag, a missing value (`--template` with nothing after it), an invalid `--pm` or `--sdk` value, or a second positional argument is an error.

## Interactive flow

The prompts run only when stdin is a terminal and neither `--yes` nor `--json` is set. Each question is skipped when its flag was given. With no terminal (CI, piped input) the CLI behaves as if `--yes` were passed instead of waiting for an answer.

1. **Which template?** An arrow-key list. Each row shows the template title and its features (sign-in + embedded wallet, session keys, sponsored gas), and the description appears on the highlighted row. Default `consumer-app`.
2. **Project name.** Defaults to the directory's name, or `pepu-app`. The package name is a slug of it.
3. **Package manager.** `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` or `bun`, with the detected one marked.
4. **Install dependencies?** Yes by default.
5. **Initialize a git repository?** Yes by default.

Then the CLI copies the template, rewrites `package.json`, vendors the SDK, writes `.env.local`, adds the agent files, installs and runs `git init` as chosen, and shows numbered next steps.

Cancelling at any prompt exits with code 1 and creates nothing.

## What the scaffold does

1. Copies `templates/<name>` into the target folder and restores dotfiles.
2. Sets the `package.json` `name` to a slug of the project name and rewrites the `@pepu-chain/sdk` dependency (`workspace:*`) to the SDK spec.
3. Vendors the SDK into `vendor/pepu-sdk` when in vendor mode.
4. Generates `.env.local` from `.env.example`.
5. Applies the agent kit (kept, filled in from the shared kit, or dropped with `--skip-agent-files`).
6. Installs dependencies and runs `git init` when chosen.
7. Computes the next steps from the template's requirements and the actual contents of `.env.local`.

## Env prefill and next steps

`.env.local` keeps every comment and line of `.env.example` and is prefixed with a header that states the network: Pepe Unchained V2, mainnet, chain `97741`, currency PEPU, the public RPC and the explorer. The SDK already knows these, so no network variable needs setting by hand.

Secrets are never prefilled. `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` stay blank (any variable whose name matches `SECRET`, `AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `API_KEY`, `PAYMASTER_URL` or `BUNDLER_URL` is treated as a credential). Values that a template's `.env.example` already carries as a public default stay as they are, for example the `WPEPU` address in `token-gated-app` and the paymaster contract address in `sponsored-demo`. If `.env.local` already exists it is not overwritten.

The next steps come from the SDK doctor's `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS` and the Privy requirements table, checked against the real `.env.local`:

1. `cd <dir>`
2. The install command, when you skipped the install or it failed.
3. The env vars still blank, by name. Secrets stay server-side and out of git.
4. "Set at least one of A or B" for any-of groups (token-gated-app needs one gate token address).
5. The Privy dashboard settings the template needs, from `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS`.
6. The template's extra steps, with `{run:<script>}` expanded to your package manager's command (for example generating the authorization key for `game-app`, or deploying the contract for `nft-mint`).
7. The doctor command, if the template defines `doctor`.
8. The dev command.

The app runs and shows a setup screen even before you add a Privy App ID.

### Doctor

Every template has an `npm run doctor` script. It loads `.env.local` and runs `checkPepuEnv` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor` for that template. It prints one line per required key (`ok` or `FAIL` plus the fix), never a value, and exits 1 when any required key is missing or malformed. The same check is available to agents as `pepu_check_env` and, for the dashboard, `pepu_check_privy_config`. See [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md).

## JSON output

`--json` prints one document to stdout and sends everything else (including the package manager's install output) to stderr. Key names only, never values.

Success:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `true` | |
| `path` | string | Absolute path of the new project. |
| `targetDir` | string | Same as `path`. |
| `template` | string | Template name. |
| `title` | string | Template title. |
| `features` | array of `login`, `session`, `sponsor` | What the template demonstrates (display tags). The SDK doctor's `pillars` are separate. |
| `packageManager` | string | The one used for printed commands and the install. |
| `sdk` | object | `{ mode: "vendor" or "npm", spec?: string, fellBackToVendor: boolean }`. |
| `installed` | boolean | Whether the install ran and succeeded. |
| `gitInitialized` | boolean | Whether `git init` ran. |
| `envFile` | string, optional | `.env.local`, when generated. |
| `requiredEnv` | array | `{ key, secret, missing }` for each required variable. `missing` is true when the scaffold left it blank. |
| `missingEnv` | array of strings | The keys still to set. |
| `privyDashboard` | array | `{ id, label, fix }` for each Privy dashboard setting needed. |
| `nextSteps` | array of strings | The same steps the human output prints. |
| `agentFiles` | array of strings | Agent kit files present in the project. |
| `warnings` | array of strings | For example a failed install, a skipped `git init`, an SDK fallback. |

An example for a no-install scaffold (abridged):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "path": "/home/me/my-app",
  "template": "game-app",
  "features": ["login", "session"],
  "packageManager": "pnpm",
  "sdk": { "mode": "npm", "spec": "^0.2.4", "fellBackToVendor": false },
  "installed": false,
  "gitInitialized": false,
  "envFile": ".env.local",
  "requiredEnv": [
    { "key": "NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID", "secret": false, "missing": true },
    { "key": "PRIVY_APP_SECRET", "secret": true, "missing": true }
  ],
  "missingEnv": ["NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID", "PRIVY_APP_SECRET"],
  "nextSteps": ["cd my-app", "pnpm install", "..."],
  "warnings": []
}
```

Failure (also exit code 1):

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": "Unknown template \"foo\".", "templates": ["consumer-app", "..."] }
```

`error` is always present. `templates` is added for an unknown template. Argument errors and an existing non-empty directory also come back this way.

`--list --json` prints `{ "ok": true, "templates": [...] }`, where each entry is the registry record (name, title, description, features, required and optional env, Privy dashboard ids, extra steps, `hasContracts`, difficulty, `recommendedFor`).

## Vendored SDK versus npm

By default the scaffold depends on `@pepu-chain/sdk` from npm. If the registry has no such package (or npm is offline), the CLI bundles a copy of the SDK instead. This is the vendored-SDK note:

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--sdk npm` (default) | Writes `^<version>` from the registry. The CLI checks the registry with `npm view @pepu-chain/sdk version` (15 second timeout). If the SDK is not published, or npm is offline, it falls back to the vendored copy, says so as a warning, and reports `fellBackToVendor: true`. |
| `--sdk vendor` | Copies the bundled SDK into `vendor/pepu-sdk` in your project and rewrites the dependency to `file:./vendor/pepu-sdk`. The vendor folder is part of your project: commit it. |

If the CLI cannot find a bundled SDK, it warns that a dependency install may fail until the SDK is published or vendored.

To move a vendored project to npm later, change the `@pepu-chain/sdk` dependency to a registry range and delete `vendor/pepu-sdk`.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Scaffold completed (even if the install or `git init` produced a warning), or `--help`, `--version`, `--list`. |
| 1 | Bad arguments, unknown template, target directory exists and is not empty, a prompt was cancelled, or an unexpected error. With `--json` the error is printed as `{ ok: false, error }` first. |

A failed install does not fail the scaffold: the project is created, a warning is recorded and the next steps tell you to run the install command yourself.

## What to expect

- The scaffold takes seconds; the install dominates.
- You end up with a folder that runs with `dev` and shows a setup screen listing exactly what is still missing.
- For sponsorship templates the CLI does not invent endpoints. It points you to the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, the default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) and tells you to set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` with your own project token (local defaults for your own services are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `"<dir>" already exists and isn't empty.` | The target has files in it | Choose a new directory or empty it. The CLI never overwrites. |
| `Unknown template "<name>".` | Typo or a removed template | Run `npx create-pepu-app --list` and pass one of those names. |
| `--sdk requires "vendor" or "npm"` | Missing or wrong value | Pass `--sdk vendor` or `--sdk npm`. |
| Warning: `--sdk npm` fell back to the vendored copy | You are offline, or the registry check failed | Nothing to fix. Pass `--sdk vendor` to skip the registry check. |
| Warning: dependency install failed | Network, registry or package manager error | Run the printed install command in the project to see the error. |
| Warning: skipped git init | git is not installed, or the folder is already inside a repository | Nothing to fix, or run `git init` yourself. |
| Login fails after the first run | The Privy allowed origin does not match the port | Use the exact origin including the port (`http://localhost:3000`). See [Privy Setup Walkthrough](../onboarding/privy-setup.md). |

- [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md)

# Infrastructure Map

One page listing every endpoint and address the PEPU dev kit relies on: bundler, paymaster, EntryPoints, Kernel, Multicall3, Permit2 and the CREATE2 deployer. Start here to find the right detail page. For the call flow between these pieces see [Architecture: Who Calls What](../concepts/architecture.md).

The hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster service (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) are the SDK defaults. You can also run your own bundler or policy service.

## Endpoints

| Service | Variable | Hosted URL | Local default | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bundler (Alto, ERC-4337 v0.7) | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default) | `http://localhost:4337` | [Bundler Overview](bundler/overview.md), [API](bundler/api.md), [Operating](bundler/operating.md) |
| Paymaster policy service | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`) | Base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default). The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token: `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, so there is no tokenless default | `http://localhost:8788` | [Paymaster Overview](paymaster/overview.md) |
| RPC | `PEPU_RPC_URL` | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` | | [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md) |

The SDK resolves these in `src/endpoints.ts` (`resolvePepuEndpoints()`): explicit option, then env, then the hosted default (`PEPU_HOSTED`: `bundlerUrl`, `paymasterBaseUrl`, and `paymasterUrl: null` because the ERC-7677 URL needs a token). `isHostedSponsorshipLive()` returns true. Build the token URL with `hostedErc7677Url(token)` (`@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`). The `/v2` routes of the service are public (free-tier, config, SIWE login, project verify); `/v2/admin` is not exposed. Health checks: `probeBundler` and `probePaymaster` (`@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`), or the MCP tools `pepu_bundler_health`, `pepu_paymaster_health` and `pepu_sponsorship_status`. Complete list: [Endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md).

## Addresses (mainnet 97741)

| Name | Address | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | Deployed |
| EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | Deployed |
| Kernel v3 factory | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` | Deployed |
| Kernel MetaFactory | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` | Deployed |
| Kernel v3.1 implementation | `0xbAC849bB641841b44E965fb01A4Bf5F074F84B4d` | Deployed |
| Kernel ECDSA validator | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` | Deployed |
| Kernel ECDSA signer module | `0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF` | Deployed |
| Call policy v0.0.4 | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` | Deployed. v0.0.5 is not deployed |
| Timestamp policy | `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` | Deployed |
| Multicall3 (PEPU-specific) | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | Deployed. Canonical address has no code |
| Permit2 (canonical) | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` | Deployed |
| CREATE2 deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | Deployed |
| Paymaster v2 (`paymaster`, `paymasterV2`) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` | Deployed |
| Paymaster v1 | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` | Retired: deposit withdrawn (0), cannot sponsor. Never deposit |
| TapScore (demo) | `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` | Deployed |

Notes and sources for each are in the [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` for a bundler or paymaster URL | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` unset and the call needs the complete ERC-7677 URL, which always embeds a token (there is no tokenless default) | Set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, or pass `paymasterToken`. The bundler defaults to the hosted URL |
| Batched reads fail | Tooling uses the canonical Multicall3 address | Use the PEPU address |
| Policy-service call works locally, fails for others | You pointed at `http://localhost:8788` | Use `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` |
