# Bundler Overview

The PEPU bundler is an ERC-4337 bundler for Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet (chain ID `97741`), hosted by PEPU at `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and also runnable on your own machine. It runs Pimlico's open-source [Alto](https://github.com/pimlicolabs/alto) (`@pimlico/alto@0.0.21`) and takes UserOperations from Kernel smart accounts, wraps them into `handleOps` transactions and submits them to the chain. Read this page to know what the bundler does, which EntryPoints it supports, how it is configured and what its limits are.

The hosted bundler at `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` is the SDK default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`. You can also run your own (see [Operating the Bundler](operating.md)); point your app at `http://localhost:4337` or your own URL.

## What it does

- Accepts the ERC-4337 JSON-RPC methods an app needs: estimate gas, send, look up by hash, get the receipt. See [Bundler JSON-RPC API](api.md).
- Simulates each UserOperation against the real EntryPoint, then bundles accepted operations and submits them from one **executor** EOA.
- The executor fronts gas for the whole bundle and is reimbursed by each operation's payer out of its EntryPoint deposit: the sender's own deposit, or the [paymaster](../paymaster/overview.md)'s when the operation is sponsored.
- **It is a bundler, not gas sponsorship.** On its own it never pays gas for anyone. Sponsorship comes from the paymaster contract and its policy service.

## What it is not

- It does not gossip to a public mempool. It receives operations directly from your app or from Privy's smart-wallet client.
- It does not hold user funds. The only key it holds is the executor key, which should carry a small float (see [Operating the Bundler](operating.md)).

## EntryPoints and chain type

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | The version Kernel v3.x, the PEPU paymaster and Privy's smart-wallet integration target. |
| EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | Also served. Deployed on mainnet. |
| Chain type | `arbitrum` | PEPU is an Arbitrum Orbit (Nitro) chain. This makes Alto price UserOperations for Nitro's two-part fee: L2 execution gas plus a separate L1 data fee. Do not remove it. |
| `arbitrum-base-fee-multiplier` | `150` (a 1.5x safety margin on the L2 base fee) | Default value; tune it for your load. |
| Chain ID | `97741` (`0x17dcd`) | Mainnet only. |
| Multicall3 | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | PEPU's own deployment, used by Alto for batched reads during simulation. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../../contracts/multicall3.md). |
| CREATE2 deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920ca78fbf26c0b4956c` | Alto uses it to deploy its own simulation contracts the first time it runs against a chain (`deploy-simulations-contract: true`). |

`eth_supportedEntryPoints` returns both EntryPoints and `eth_chainId` returns `0x17dcd` (full responses in [Bundler JSON-RPC API](api.md)).

## Safe mode is off (known Alto 0.0.21 bug)

`safe-mode` is `false` in the committed configuration. With it on, `eth_sendUserOperation` fails for every operation, valid or not, with an HTTP 500 and the error `Encoded error signature "0x99410554" not found on ABI`. The selector is EntryPoint v0.7's own `DelegateAndRevert(bool,bytes)` error. Alto's Node-side decoder for its simulation contract has no error definitions in its ABI, so it throws on the wrapper that every simulation returns. The behavior is present in Alto `0.0.21`, the latest npm release.

What safe mode off means:

- Alto still validates signature, nonce, prefund and gas. What is skipped is the ERC-7562 storage-access and opcode tracer, which protects a **shared public mempool** from operations crafted to behave differently at inclusion time.
- That is acceptable only with the controls around it. This matters because the RPC is public, which is why the hosted deployment sits behind a reverse proxy (see below and [Operating the Bundler](operating.md)).
- The v2 paymaster contract depends on this setting: it gates payment on `tx.origin` being an allowlisted bundler, and `ORIGIN` is banned under ERC-7562, so a conformant public-mempool bundler would reject its operations. See [Paymaster v2 Spec Summary](../../contracts/paymaster-v2-spec.md).
- Re-test and re-enable safe mode when Alto publishes a release past `0.0.21`.

## The paymaster bundler allowlist

The v2 paymaster only pays out to allowlisted bundler executor addresses. A third-party bundler would see operations that pass simulation but fail at inclusion. In practice: sponsored operations must go through the PEPU bundler (or one whose executor has been added to the paymaster's allowlist). v1 does not have this restriction. See [PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract](../paymaster/contracts.md).

## CORS and the proxy policy

Browsers call the bundler directly (Privy's smart-wallet client sends `eth_estimateUserOperationGas` from the user's browser), so CORS has to work.

- `enable-cors` is `true`. In Alto 0.0.21 that is a boolean that **reflects any `Origin`** and answers `OPTIONS` preflights; it cannot be turned into an allowlist.
- CORS is not an access boundary. A script or `curl` can call the endpoint regardless. What actually gates cost is EntryPoint validation (signature, nonce, prefund) and, for sponsored operations, the paymaster's policy.
- For a hosted deployment, put a reverse proxy in front that terminates TLS and rate-limits; the PEPU-hosted endpoint is served through one. Plan for the endpoint URL to be treated as semi-public.

## Rate limits

Alto has no built-in per-client limits. Any limits on the hosted endpoint are applied at the proxy and are not a contract; do not hammer the endpoint.

## Health probe

Use the SDK probe or the MCP tool rather than hand-rolled calls:

```ts
import { probeBundler } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa";

const result = await probeBundler(process.env.PEPU_BUNDLER_URL ?? "http://localhost:4337");
console.log(result.ok, result.chainId, result.entryPoints, result.supportedMethods);
```

`probeBundler` calls `eth_chainId`, `eth_supportedEntryPoints` and a capability check for `eth_sendUserOperation`, `eth_estimateUserOperationGas`, `eth_getUserOperationReceipt`, `eth_getUserOperationByHash`, `pimlico_getUserOperationGasPrice` and `zd_getUserOperationGasPrice`. A method counts as supported if it answers with anything other than "method not found". Nothing is sent on chain. `ok` is true only when the chain ID is `97741` and EntryPoint v0.7 is listed. It never throws for network trouble; it returns `ok: false` with a `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE` error. The MCP equivalent is the `pepu_bundler_health` tool, and `pepu_sponsorship_status` checks bundler and paymaster together.

## Configuration summary

The committed file is `services/bundler/alto.config.json`; secrets live only in `.env`.

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `entrypoints` | v0.7 and v0.6 |
| `chain-type` | `arbitrum` |
| `safe-mode` | `false` (see above) |
| `enable-cors` | `true` (reflect any origin) |
| `enable-debug-endpoints` | `false` (the `debug_bundler_*` methods are not served) |
| `dangerous-skip-user-operation-validation` | `false` |
| `legacy-transactions` | `false` (EIP-1559) |
| `is-gas-free-chain` | `false` |
| `eip-7702-support` | `true` |
| `refilling-wallets` | `false` (no utility wallet) |
| `port` | `4337` |
| `block-time` | `5000` ms |

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `eth_sendUserOperation` returns HTTP 500 mentioning `0x99410554` | `safe-mode` is on | Set `safe-mode` to `false` and restart. Alto reads its config once at startup. |
| Browser shows `Failed to fetch` on the first call, `curl` works | CORS disabled, so the `OPTIONS` preflight got a 404 | Set `enable-cors` to `true` and restart. |
| Estimation works, sending never lands | The executor EOA has no PEPU. Estimation does not need funds, sending does | Top up the executor. See [Operating the Bundler](operating.md). |
| `probeBundler` returns `ok: false` with the wrong chain | The URL points at a different network | Use a mainnet (`97741`) bundler. |
| Config change has no effect | Alto does not hot reload | Restart the process. |

# Bundler JSON-RPC API

Method-by-method reference for the PEPU bundler (Alto, ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7, chain `97741`). Read this when you are calling the bundler without the SDK, debugging a failing UserOperation or writing your own client. Most apps do not call these methods by hand: viem's bundler client, Privy's smart-wallet client and the SDK (`@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`) do it for you.

Write `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` in your config, or rely on the SDK default (the hosted URL `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`). The local development default is `http://localhost:4337`. The examples show the response shape and are abridged.

## Endpoint and transport

| | |
|---|---|
| URL | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (browser-exposed variant `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`). Hosted default `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`. Local default `http://localhost:4337`. |
| Method | `POST`, `Content-Type: application/json`, JSON-RPC 2.0 body |
| Auth | None at the Alto layer. The hosted deployment sits behind a proxy that may add its own |
| CORS | Enabled; any `Origin` is reflected, `OPTIONS` preflights return 204. See [Bundler Overview](overview.md#cors-and-the-proxy-policy) |
| Batching | Not covered by this page; send one request per call |
| Rate limits | Applied at the proxy if at all; Alto itself has none. Do not rely on them |

The SDK resolves the URL for you (explicit option, then the env variables, then the hosted default, `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`). Never hard-code a tunnel URL.

Quantities are `0x`-prefixed hex strings, as in all Ethereum JSON-RPC. A v0.7 UserOperation is sent in its **unpacked** form:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sender` | address | The Kernel smart account |
| `nonce` | hex quantity | EntryPoint nonce (key and sequence packed) |
| `factory`, `factoryData` | address, hex | Only when the account is not yet deployed |
| `callData` | hex | A Kernel `execute(bytes32,bytes)` call |
| `callGasLimit`, `verificationGasLimit`, `preVerificationGas` | hex quantity | |
| `maxFeePerGas`, `maxPriorityFeePerGas` | hex quantity | PEPU's base fee is about 12,500 gwei; this is normal |
| `paymaster`, `paymasterVerificationGasLimit`, `paymasterPostOpGasLimit`, `paymasterData` | | Only for sponsored operations; from the [paymaster](../paymaster/erc7677.md) |
| `signature` | hex | The account's signature (or a dummy of the right length when estimating) |

## Supported methods

| Method | Supported | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `eth_chainId` | Yes | Returns `0x17dcd` (97741) |
| `eth_supportedEntryPoints` | Yes | v0.7 first, then v0.6 |
| `eth_estimateUserOperationGas` | Yes | |
| `eth_sendUserOperation` | Yes | Needs `safe-mode: false` (known Alto 0.0.21 bug) |
| `eth_getUserOperationByHash` | Yes | `null` if unknown |
| `eth_getUserOperationReceipt` | Yes | `null` until included |
| `pimlico_getUserOperationGasPrice` | Implemented in Alto 0.0.21 | `probeBundler` reports whether a given deployment answers it |
| `pimlico_getUserOperationStatus` | Implemented in Alto 0.0.21 | `probeBundler` reports whether a given deployment answers it |
| `zd_getUserOperationGasPrice` | Not an Alto method | `probeBundler` checks for it because ZeroDev's client prefers it; expect "method not found" |
| `debug_bundler_*` | Disabled | `enable-debug-endpoints` is `false` |

## eth_chainId

Request:

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "eth_chainId", "params": [] }
```

Response:

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": "0x17dcd" }
```

`0x17dcd` is 97741. Any other value means you are pointed at the wrong network.

## eth_supportedEntryPoints

Request:

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "eth_supportedEntryPoints", "params": [] }
```

Response:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": [
    "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032",
    "0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789"
  ]
}
```

Use the first entry (EntryPoint v0.7) for Kernel v3.x. The addresses are documented in [EntryPoints and Kernel](../../contracts/entrypoints-and-kernel.md).

## eth_estimateUserOperationGas

Params: `[userOperation, entryPoint]`, optionally a third argument of state overrides. Pass a dummy-but-well-formed `signature` (the right length for your account) so signature validation does not fail the simulation. For a **sponsored** operation, attach the paymaster fields from `pm_getPaymasterStubData` first. Estimating without them makes EntryPoint demand the sender's own prefund and fail with `AA21 didn't pay prefund` for a zero-balance account.

Request (abridged):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "eth_estimateUserOperationGas",
  "params": [
    {
      "sender": "0xA43CDA364c524551640206A5A22906dBD989F373",
      "nonce": "0x0",
      "factory": "0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419",
      "factoryData": "0x…",
      "callData": "0x…",
      "callGasLimit": "0x0",
      "verificationGasLimit": "0x0",
      "preVerificationGas": "0x0",
      "maxFeePerGas": "0x…",
      "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…",
      "signature": "0x…"
    },
    "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032"
  ]
}
```

Response (an account-deploying operation):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "preVerificationGas": "0xc769",
    "verificationGasLimit": "0x51e44",
    "callGasLimit": "0x3fc3"
  }
}
```

When the request carried paymaster fields, the result also includes `paymasterVerificationGasLimit` and `paymasterPostOpGasLimit`.

`preVerificationGas` is large because PEPU is a Nitro chain: it includes the L1 data fee component (`chain-type: arbitrum`).

## eth_sendUserOperation

Params: `[userOperation, entryPoint]`, with real gas limits and a real signature (and paymaster fields for a sponsored operation). Returns the **userOpHash** (not a transaction hash).

Request: same shape as above, with the estimated gas limits filled in.

Response:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": "0xc20a1c642b0b61d4c545de2ec5d333b37440ff8a0b0ec9307b8e64cfe3c6e0f8"
}
```

The operation is queued, bundled on the next bundling pass (about `block-time`, 5 seconds) and submitted by the executor. Poll for the receipt.

If the call fails with HTTP 500 and `Encoded error signature "0x99410554" not found on ABI`, `safe-mode` is on. See [Bundler Overview](overview.md#safe-mode-is-off-known-alto-0021-bug).

## eth_getUserOperationByHash

Params: `[userOpHash]`.

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "eth_getUserOperationByHash", "params": ["0xc20a1c642b0b61d4c545de2ec5d333b37440ff8a0b0ec9307b8e64cfe3c6e0f8"] }
```

Response when the operation is included:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "userOperation": { "sender": "0xA43CDA364c524551640206A5A22906dBD989F373", "…": "…" },
    "entryPoint": "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032",
    "blockNumber": "0xa08cc7",
    "blockHash": "0x…",
    "transactionHash": "0x8232872612eb500033faf8ef605f7c14f4fef556defdbb4d7c67c1731d0b00d3"
  }
}
```

`result` is `null` when the operation is unknown or not yet mined.

## eth_getUserOperationReceipt

Params: `[userOpHash]`. Returns `null` until the operation is included, so poll (every 2 to 5 seconds, with a timeout).

Response (abridged; `actualGasCost` is 7.725575 PEPU, `actualGasUsed` is 309,023):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "userOpHash": "0xc20a1c642b0b61d4c545de2ec5d333b37440ff8a0b0ec9307b8e64cfe3c6e0f8",
    "entryPoint": "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032",
    "sender": "0xA43CDA364c524551640206A5A22906dBD989F373",
    "nonce": "0x0",
    "actualGasCost": "0x6b36c187d8a37000",
    "actualGasUsed": "0x4b71f",
    "success": true,
    "logs": [],
    "receipt": { "transactionHash": "0x8232872612eb500033faf8ef605f7c14f4fef556defdbb4d7c67c1731d0b00d3", "blockNumber": "0xa08cc7", "status": "0x1" }
  }
}
```

`success: false` means the call inside the operation reverted (see `reason`) even though the transaction itself succeeded. For a sponsored operation the response includes `paymaster`. The SDK helpers `userOpEventFromReceipt` and `userOpEventsFromReceipt` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`) decode the `UserOperationEvent` from the transaction receipt.

## pimlico_getUserOperationGasPrice

Alto implements this method; it returns three tiers of fee suggestion. The SDK probe checks for it. Treat it as optional: if a deployment does not answer, read `eth_gasPrice`/fee history from the chain RPC instead.

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "pimlico_getUserOperationGasPrice", "params": [] }
```

Response shape:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "slow":     { "maxFeePerGas": "0x…", "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…" },
    "standard": { "maxFeePerGas": "0x…", "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…" },
    "fast":     { "maxFeePerGas": "0x…", "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…" }
  }
}
```


## Error codes

Errors follow ERC-7769 and use the standard JSON-RPC envelope `{ "error": { "code", "message", "data" } }`. Alto 0.0.21 defines:

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `-32601` | Method not found | You called a method this deployment does not serve (for example a `debug_` method) |
| `-32602` | Invalid fields | A field is missing, mistyped or the wrong width. Check the unpacked v0.7 shape above |
| `-32500` | Rejected in account validation (`validateUserOp`) | The sender or its validator rejected the operation. An `AAxx` code is in the message: `AA21` prefund not paid, `AA23` reverted, `AA25` invalid nonce, `AA33` paymaster reverted |
| `-32501` | Rejected by the paymaster | Sponsorship was refused or the paymaster data is invalid. `AA33`, `AA34` (bad signature) and `AA31` (paymaster deposit too low) all surface here or as `-32508` |
| `-32502` | Opcode validation | Banned opcode or storage access. Only raised with `safe-mode: true` |
| `-32503` | Expires shortly | The paymaster approval (`validUntil`) is about to lapse. Request fresh paymaster data and retry |
| `-32504` | Reputation | A throttled or banned entity |
| `-32505` | Insufficient stake | A staked entity is required |
| `-32506`, `-32507` | Unsupported aggregator, invalid signature | |
| `-32508` | Paymaster deposit too low | Fund the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit |
| `-32521` | Execution reverted | The operation's call failed in simulation |

Failures that are not JSON-RPC errors: an HTTP 500 with a raw message (the safe-mode bug above) and a browser `Failed to fetch` (CORS off, or the endpoint is down). The Privy-side symptom of a bundler error is usually opaque; call the bundler directly with `curl` to see the real message.

## Using the SDK instead

```ts
import { probeBundler } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa";
import { createPepuSponsoredClient, sendSponsored } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel";
```

`createPepuSponsoredClient` and `sendSponsored` build the Kernel account, estimate, request paymaster data and send, so you only deal with raw JSON-RPC when debugging. See [/aa](../../sdk/aa.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `AA21 didn't pay prefund` on estimate | Estimated without paymaster fields on a zero-balance sender | Attach stub paymaster fields first, or fund the sender |
| `AA33 reverted` on send | The paymaster rejected the operation: expired `validUntil`, or the bundler executor is not allowlisted (v2) | Re-request paymaster data; for v2 use the PEPU bundler |
| `AA25 invalid account nonce` | A pending operation from the same sender holds the nonce | Wait for the receipt, or use the next nonce |
| `null` receipt forever | The executor is out of PEPU, or the operation was dropped | Check executor balance and the bundler log. See [Operating the Bundler](operating.md) |
| 500 with `0x99410554` | `safe-mode` is on | Turn it off and restart |

# Operating the Bundler

Runbook for anyone running the PEPU Alto bundler: locally for development, or as a hosted service. The source is `services/bundler` in the repository. Read [Bundler Overview](overview.md) first for what the service is and why it is configured the way it is.

PEPU runs this bundler as the hosted service at `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, behind nginx and pm2 (see the hosting kit in `deploy/`). Treat "Hosting readiness" as the requirements for any hosted deployment, including your own. `docker-compose.yml` is a starting point; adjust it for your environment.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js v24.4.1 or later.
- A PEPU mainnet RPC URL. The Conduit URL embeds an API key, so the whole URL is a secret.
- A **fresh executor key** (an EOA used only by the bundler) with a small PEPU float. Never reuse a deploy key or a key that holds meaningful funds.

## Run it locally

From `services/bundler`:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env: set ALTO_RPC_URL and ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS

npm install
npm start          # alto run --config alto.config.json, listens on :4337
```

Confirm it is alive:

```bash
npm run healthcheck
```

or by hand:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4337 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_chainId","params":[]}'
# {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":"0x17dcd"}
```

Alto reads its config **once at startup**; there is no hot reload. After any change to `alto.config.json` or `.env`, restart the process and confirm the new process started after the file changed.

### Configuration files

| File | Contents | Committed |
|---|---|---|
| `alto.config.json` | EntryPoints, chain type, safe mode, CORS, ports and so on. No secrets | Yes |
| `.env` | `ALTO_RPC_URL`, `ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS` | **No**, never |
| `alto.config.unsafe-diagnostic.json` | Same shape on port 4338, for running a second isolated instance to compare behavior | Yes |

Alto's CLI maps every `ALTO_`-prefixed environment variable onto the matching `--kebab-case` flag. That is how the RPC URL and keys reach it without being written into the committed config or passed as arguments (which would leak into process listings). Never put either in `alto.config.json`.

| Variable | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ALTO_RPC_URL` | PEPU mainnet RPC URL (secret: embeds the API key) |
| `ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS` | Comma-separated executor private key(s) (secret) |
| `ALTO_UTILITY_PRIVATE_KEY` | Refills executors below the minimum balance. Deliberately unset; `refilling-wallets` is `false` |
| `ALTO_LOG_LEVEL` | Optional override of `log-level` (default `info`) |

## Docker

`services/bundler/docker-compose.yml` runs `ghcr.io/pimlicolabs/alto:v1.2.8`, mounts `alto.config.json` read-only, reads secrets from `.env`, publishes `4337:4337` and has a Node-based `eth_chainId` health check. Note the following:

- The `v1.2.8` image corresponds to `@pimlico/alto@0.0.20`, one release behind the `0.0.21` that the npm path pins. Track the Alto repository for a newer image tag before relying on the container.
- Validate the container with `npm run healthcheck` equivalents and a real `scripts/estimate-kernel-userop.mjs --send` before relying on it.

Bind to `127.0.0.1:4337:4337` if the host is internet-facing and you want only the proxy to reach Alto.

## Hosting readiness

What a hosted deployment needs (PEPU publishes `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` as `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`; use this list for your own):

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Containerised service | Docker or compose (or an equivalent platform) with a restart policy, instead of a foreground `npm start`. Validate `docker-compose.yml` first |
| Reverse proxy in front | Fixed hostname, TLS, `Origin` filtering (Alto reflects any origin), rate limiting and request size limits. Alto should not be reachable except through it |
| Fresh executor key, small float | A key created for this service only, funded with a bounded amount and topped up on a schedule. See the next section |
| Secrets management | RPC URL and executor key in a secrets manager or the host's protected environment, never in the repository. Plan key rotation |
| More than one executor | Production should use several executor keys so one in-flight bundle does not block the next. The default configuration uses one |
| Monitoring and alerting | Alert on health-check failure, executor balance, process exit and error rate. Ship the JSON logs somewhere searchable |
| Stable URL | Tunnels change URL on restart and break every Privy Dashboard that has the old URL pasted in |
| Safe-mode decision | Off because of the Alto 0.0.21 bug. Re-test on each Alto release. Do not expose the RPC to untrusted submitters while off without the proxy controls above |

## Executor funding

- The executor EOA signs and submits every `handleOps` transaction and pays gas up front, then is reimbursed per operation from each payer's EntryPoint deposit (the sender's own, or the paymaster's).
- **If it runs dry, `eth_sendUserOperation` is still accepted but bundles never land.** Estimation does not need executor funds, so the bundler keeps looking healthy to clients. This is the most common silent failure.
- Operations on mainnet cost 3 to 8 PEPU in gas each. Keep the float small on purpose (it is a hot key) but large enough for hours of runway.
- Top up with any normal PEPU transfer to the executor address, or `node scripts/fund-address.mjs`.
- A smart account that sends **without** a paymaster must hold enough PEPU to pay its own prefund. That is a per-account concern, not something the bundler can fix.

## Monitoring

`npm run healthcheck` (`scripts/healthcheck.js`) runs four independent checks and exits `0` if all pass, `1` otherwise:

1. **Bundler responding**: `eth_chainId` against the bundler's port, and it must be `0x17dcd`.
2. **Chain RPC reachable**: `eth_blockNumber` straight against `ALTO_RPC_URL`, so an RPC outage can be told apart from a bundler outage.
3. **EntryPoints reachable**: `eth_supportedEntryPoints` must list both v0.6 and v0.7.
4. **Executor funded**: every executor address derived from `ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS` must hold at least `ALTO_HEALTHCHECK_MIN_EXECUTOR_BALANCE_PEPU` (default 500). Only the address is ever printed.

Wire it into the supervisor, a container health check or an uptime checker. Alert on:

- Any health-check failure, especially executor balance.
- Alto process exit.
- A sustained rise in `eth_sendUserOperation` errors, especially the `0x99410554` signature (it means safe mode was switched back on).

Client-side, `probeBundler` (SDK) and `pepu_bundler_health` (MCP) give an external view without needing server access.

When the bundler is down, every UserOperation flow stops: nothing can be estimated or submitted. Receiving funds and reading balances still work, because they go straight to the chain RPC.

## Verify a change

1. Restart the process.
2. `npm run healthcheck`.
3. `node scripts/estimate-kernel-userop.mjs` confirms gas estimation.
4. `node scripts/estimate-kernel-userop.mjs --send` confirms a real operation lands. It costs a few PEPU of real gas and is the only check that sending works: a successful estimate is not enough (the safe-mode bug affects only sending).

## Limitations

- Single executor key, no utility wallet (refilling is off).
- `safe-mode: false` as a tracked workaround for the Alto 0.0.21 bug.
- The `docker-compose.yml` image is one Alto release behind the npm package.
- `arbitrum-base-fee-multiplier` (150) and `block-time` (5000 ms) are default values; tune them for your load.
- No rate limiting or origin allowlist at the Alto layer.
- This service never sponsors gas. Do not describe it as gasless.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Healthcheck: executor below threshold | Float is low | Top up the executor address |
| Healthcheck: wrong chain | `ALTO_RPC_URL` points at another network | Use the mainnet RPC |
| 500 with `0x99410554` | Safe mode on | Set `safe-mode` to `false` and restart |
| Browser `Failed to fetch` | CORS off, or an old process is still serving the port | Enable CORS, restart, verify the new process is the one listening |
| Config edit ignored | Alto does not hot reload | Restart |

## Related

- [Bundler Overview](overview.md)
- [Bundler JSON-RPC API](api.md)
- [Paymaster Overview](../paymaster/overview.md)
- [Infrastructure Map](../overview.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/infra/paymaster/overview

# Paymaster Overview

The PEPU paymaster lets an app pay gas on behalf of its users. It has two parts: an on-chain contract that holds the gas money and pays the EntryPoint, and an off-chain **policy service** that decides whether to approve a request and signs the approval. There are two versions. Version 2, the tiered model, is the live version. Version 1 is retired. Read this page to know which is which, what credentials each uses and where to go next.

![Sponsorship tiers: the project budget is tried first, then the chain free tier of 100 PEPU a day and 50 PEPU an hour per Privy user, otherwise the operation is denied; deposits are one-way](../../.gitbook/assets/sponsorship-tiers.png)

*Who pays: project first, then the free tier, else denied.*

The v2 paymaster is deployed at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` and served through the hosted [bundler](../bundler/overview.md) and policy service. The hosted service base is `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; the ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`), so there is no tokenless default. Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs. The v1 paymaster is retired. Local development default: `http://localhost:8788`.

## v1 versus v2

| | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| Contract | `PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7` at `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` (retired) | `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (registry `paymasterV2`, alias `paymaster`) |
| Availability | Retired: the EntryPoint deposit has been withdrawn (0), so it cannot sponsor anything. Never deposit | Live on mainnet |
| Money | One shared EntryPoint deposit, no on-chain accounting | A ledger per sponsor inside one contract: a free pool plus one balance per project |
| Who sponsors | One operator (PEPU) for registered apps | The chain's free tier (Privy users) and any number of projects |
| Caps | Entirely off-chain in the policy service; the contract enforces none | Service caps plus on-chain destination allowlist, daily limit, per-wallet limit and gas-price cap per sponsor |
| Deposits | Operator tops up the EntryPoint deposit | Anyone deposits into any project; **one-way, nobody can withdraw** |
| Onboarding an app | An operator adds the app to `apps.json` by hand | Self-serve: claim the project on chain with a Privy-verified attestation, then configure it |
| Routes | `/health`, `/sponsor`, `/paymaster/:appToken`, `/admin/circuit-breaker/reset` (v1; not usable for sponsorship now) | The v1 routes plus `/v2/*`. The `/v2` routes are public (free-tier, config, SIWE, projects, verify); `/v2/admin` is not exposed |
| Auth | Privy access token and `X-Api-Key` (or the app key in the URL) | Server key `ppk_`, client token `ppt_` with allowed origins, SIWE session for owners, Privy token for the free tier |
| Pages | [REST API v1](rest-api-v1.md) | [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md), [Register, Deposit and Claim](v2-register-deposit-claim.md), [Spec Summary](../../contracts/paymaster-v2-spec.md) |

v1 is retired. The two versions use different contracts, different SQLite files and different URL prefixes.

## What both versions share

- **ERC-7677 surface.** `pm_getPaymasterStubData` and `pm_getPaymasterData`, which is what Privy's smart-wallet client and viem's paymaster client call. See [ERC-7677 Methods](erc7677.md).
- **Kernel only.** The policy service decodes Kernel v3 `execute(bytes32,bytes)` calls (single or batch) to see which contracts an operation calls. Other account types and `executeUserOp` are denied.
- **EntryPoint v0.7**, chain `97741`, native PEPU as the only funding asset.
- **Operating model.** The service signs only after every check passes, the contract checks the signature and pays from its deposit. A compromised signer key is the one thing the v1 contract cannot stop; the float is kept small for that reason. See [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md).

## Credentials in brief

| Credential | Format | Used for | Safe in a browser |
|---|---|---|---|
| Privy access token | JWT | Proving a Privy user (v1 `/sponsor`; v2 free tier) | Yes, it is the user's own |
| App key (v1) | raw key, hashed in `apps.json` | v1 `X-Api-Key` and the `/paymaster/<appToken>` URL segment | The URL is a secret; treat it as one |
| Server key | `ppk_...` | v2 backend sponsorship for any wallet | **No** |
| Client token | `ppt_...` | v2 ERC-7677 URL in a browser, only from allowed origins | Yes, by design (origin-bound) |
| SIWE session | opaque bearer, 1 hour | v2 project management | Held by the owner's browser |
| Privy app secret | Privy dashboard | One call, `POST /v2/projects/verify`; never stored | **No**, server or CLI only |

Details and the per-endpoint matrix are in [Credential Matrix](auth.md).

## Tiers

v2 splits sponsorship into a **free tier** (the chain pays, live allowance 100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per user per hour, enforced by the service; Privy users only, no chain-wide ceiling) and a **project tier** (a project funds its own budget and can sponsor any wallet). Free-tier targets are TapScore only for now (`0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`); the manager can add more. The free pool was seeded with 300 PEPU. Beyond the free tier a dApp deposits into its own project. The full model, numbers and draw order are on [Sponsorship Tiers](../../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md) and in [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md).

## How tokens behave

- **Client token (`ppt_`)** is publishable and works only from that project's allowed origins. With no origins set, or from another origin, it is refused with `project_origin_not_allowed`.
- **Server key (`ppk_`)** is secret. Backend callers put it in the ERC-7677 URL.
- **Free tier** needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app, sent as `context.privyAccessToken` in the ERC-7677 request (REST: `Authorization: Bearer`). A third-party app's own Privy token is ignored for billing, so third-party apps use a project. The Privy Smart Wallets dashboard URL is static and cannot attach a token, so the free tier is not reachable there.
- **Developer flow:** SIWE login, `POST /v2/projects/verify` with a Privy app id and secret (used for one request, never stored), `claimProject`, `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`, `depositFor`, register the project to get `ppt_` and `ppk_`, then set allowed origins for the client token. See [Register, Deposit and Claim](v2-register-deposit-claim.md).

## Hosting

| Piece | Location |
|---|---|
| v2 contract | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` |
| v2 policy service | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` |
| ERC-7677 URL | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` (always a token; `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` holds the complete URL) |

The SDK defaults to the hosted base for `createPaymasterApi`, probes, `checkSponsorship` and `doctor`; `getSponsorshipStatus()` and the `pepu_sponsorship_status` MCP tool probe the hosted bundler and paymaster base. `resolvePepuEndpoints()` returns `paymasterBaseUrl` and `paymasterUrl` (the complete ERC-7677 URL, or `null` when none is configured). Build a token URL with `hostedErc7677Url(token)` or pass `paymasterToken` to `createPepuPaymasterClient`. You can still run the policy service yourself; v2 is the path for outside teams.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` for the paymaster URL | No complete ERC-7677 URL: the URL always embeds a token, so there is no tokenless default | Set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` or pass `paymasterToken` |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | A `ppt_` client token used with no allowed origins set, or from another origin | Set the project's allowed origins, or use the server key from a backend |
| `resolvePaymasterV2Address` throws | Only on a chain without a deployed v2 entry (testnet) | On mainnet it resolves to `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`; never guess an address elsewhere |
| Sponsorship works locally but a teammate cannot reach it | You pointed at `http://localhost:8788` | Use `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` |
## Related

- [REST API v1](rest-api-v1.md) and [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md)
- [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md)

# ERC-7677 Paymaster Methods

The policy service speaks [ERC-7677](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7677), the paymaster web-service standard. Two JSON-RPC methods, `pm_getPaymasterStubData` and `pm_getPaymasterData`, are what Privy's smart-wallet client and viem's paymaster client call. Read this page to understand how the two differ, what to put in `context`, what the responses look like and how to build the requests with the SDK.

Endpoint `POST /v2/paymaster/<token>`, hosted at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. The URL always embeds a token, so there is no tokenless default; `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` holds the complete URL. The v1 route `POST /paymaster/<appToken>` is retired. Local default: `http://localhost:8788`.

## Endpoints

| Version | Path | Credential in the URL |
|---|---|---|
| v1 | `POST {PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL}/paymaster/<appToken>` (and `OPTIONS` for CORS), retired | The app's raw API key. Treat the whole URL as a secret |
| v2 | `POST https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` (and `OPTIONS`) | A project's client token `ppt_...` (browser-safe, origin-bound) or server key `ppk_...` (secret) |
Privy's dashboard "Paymaster URL" field is a bare URL with no separate header or secret field, which is why the credential travels in the path. See [Credential Matrix](auth.md).

A `ppt_` client token works only from the project's allowed origins; with none set, or from another origin, the service answers `project_origin_not_allowed`. If Privy calls from its own servers, use the `ppk_` server key and keep it secret. The free tier needs `context.privyAccessToken` from PEPU's own Privy app; a third-party app's token is ignored for billing, and the dashboard URL cannot attach one, so the free tier is not reachable from the Smart Wallets dashboard.
Privy's dashboard "Paymaster URL" field is a bare URL with no separate header or secret field, which is why the credential travels in the path. See [Credential Matrix](auth.md).

Both routes accept a single request or a JSON-RPC batch array (v2 handles at most 20 per batch). Only these two methods exist; anything else returns `-32601`. `pm_sponsorUserOperation` is not implemented.

## Request shape

Both methods take positional params `[userOperation, entryPoint, chainId, context?]`:

| Param | Value |
|---|---|
| `userOperation` | Unpacked v0.7 UserOperation |
| `entryPoint` | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` (v0.7 only) |
| `chainId` | `"0x17dcd"` (97741). A decimal number or string is also accepted |
| `context` | Optional object. v1 accepts and ignores it. v2 reads `privyAccessToken` |

## Stub versus data semantics

| | `pm_getPaymasterStubData` | `pm_getPaymasterData` |
|---|---|---|
| When it is called | Before gas estimation | Right before submission to the bundler |
| Purpose | Fields that let `eth_estimateUserOperationGas` simulate without reverting | The real, signed approval |
| Runs the policy engine | **No.** No cap consumed, no audit row, nothing recorded | **Yes.** Every cap, allowlist, budget and the signing step |
| Authenticated | **No, by spec.** The URL credential is not resolved for the stub (v1). Unknown credentials get the same stub | Yes |
| Signature | A real ECDSA signature from a throwaway key over a zero hash: well formed, never authorised | From the policy signer |
| `isFinal` | `false` | not returned |

**Stub data is unauthenticated by design, and that is not a hole.** ERC-7677 defines the stub call purely as a gas-estimation aid and draws the authorisation line at `pm_getPaymasterData`. The stub carries a dummy signature that the contract treats as an unauthorised signer, so using it on chain fails cleanly (`sigFailed`), never pays. The only cost of a bad credential is that you learn about it at the second call instead of the first. In v2 the stub carries the project's sponsor id if the URL token resolves to an active project, otherwise the free pool id, in the real 97-byte layout so `preVerificationGas` estimates match.

### The dummy signature must be well formed

If you estimate without paymaster fields, EntryPoint demands the sender's own prefund and a zero-balance account fails with `AA21 didn't pay prefund`. If you attach a signature-shaped blob that is not a valid ECDSA signature, the contract's recovery reverts instead of failing closed. That is why the service returns a real signature from a disposable key. Use the stub fields exactly as returned.

## pm_getPaymasterStubData

Request:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "pm_getPaymasterStubData",
  "params": [
    {
      "sender": "0x…",
      "nonce": "0x0",
      "callData": "0x…",
      "callGasLimit": "0x0",
      "verificationGasLimit": "0x0",
      "preVerificationGas": "0x0",
      "maxFeePerGas": "0x0",
      "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x0"
    },
    "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032",
    "0x17dcd"
  ]
}
```

Only `sender` is validated for the stub; gas fields may be placeholders.

Response:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "paymaster": "0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D",
    "paymasterData": "0x…",
    "paymasterVerificationGasLimit": "0x…",
    "paymasterPostOpGasLimit": "0x…",
    "isFinal": false
  }
}
```

For v1 (retired) the `paymaster` was the v1 contract and `paymasterData` is `mode(1)=0x00 ‖ validUntil(6) ‖ validAfter(6) ‖ signature(65)`. For v2 the `paymaster` is the v2 contract and `paymasterData` is `mode(1)=0x02 ‖ validUntil(6) ‖ validAfter(6) ‖ sponsorId(32) ‖ signature(65)`. You do not need to build these yourself.

## pm_getPaymasterData

Request: the same shape with the real, estimated gas fields filled in. For v2 add `context` when the free tier may be used:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "pm_getPaymasterData",
  "params": [
    { "sender": "0x…", "nonce": "0x…", "factory": "0x…", "factoryData": "0x…", "callData": "0x…",
      "callGasLimit": "0x…", "verificationGasLimit": "0x…", "preVerificationGas": "0x…",
      "maxFeePerGas": "0x…", "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…" },
    "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032",
    "0x17dcd",
    { "privyAccessToken": "<the user's Privy access token>" }
  ]
}
```

Success:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "paymaster": "0x…",
    "paymasterData": "0x…",
    "paymasterVerificationGasLimit": "0x…",
    "paymasterPostOpGasLimit": "0x…"
  }
}
```

The approval is valid for a short window: 90 seconds on v1 (`VALIDITY_WINDOW_SECONDS`), 60 seconds on v2. A signature that sits unsubmitted past `validUntil` is rejected by EntryPoint. If you hit `-32503` or `AA32`, ask for fresh paymaster data.

### Idempotency: duplicate calls are expected

Privy's smart-wallet client can run its prepare flow twice in parallel, producing two `pm_getPaymasterData` calls for the **same** UserOperation 10 to 300 ms apart. The policy service de-duplicates by **userOpHash**: if a live (unexpired, not voided) approval already exists for that hash, the second call skips the cap checks and the cost booking and returns a fresh signature for the same hash, so the spend is booked once. v2 also treats a re-request for the same (sponsor, sender, nonce) as a replacement of the earlier unexecuted approval, so retries never stack reservations (a smaller re-request keeps the earlier, larger reservation live until its signature expires). Design your own client to be safe to call twice, and do not treat a repeat as a new spend.

## Context fields

| Field | Version | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `privyAccessToken` | v2 | The user's verified Privy access token. **Required for the free tier**; without it the free tier is denied with `free_tier_identity_required`. A project's own budget does not need it (unless the project turned on `requireIdentity`) |
| anything else | both | Accepted and ignored |

`buildPaymasterContext` from the SDK drops `undefined` entries and rejects values that do not survive JSON (bigint, function, symbol).

## Errors

JSON-RPC errors use the standard envelope. Sponsorship denials carry the machine-readable reason in `error.data.reason` (v2 also adds `detail`, the reason per tier tried).

| `error.code` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-32700` | Parse error |
| `-32600` | Invalid request |
| `-32601` | Method not found (only the two methods above exist) |
| `-32602` | Invalid params: bad entry point, wrong chain, malformed UserOperation |
| `-32603` | Internal error |
| `-32000` | Sponsorship denied. `error.data.reason` is one of the [denial reasons](rest-api-v2.md#denial-reason-catalog) |
| `-32001` | New-account deployment (`factory`/`factoryData`) is disabled on this endpoint (`PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOW_ACCOUNT_DEPLOYMENT` is `false`). Default is allowed, because a first transaction needs it |

Example denial:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "error": {
    "code": -32000,
    "message": "Sponsorship denied: …",
    "data": { "reason": "user_hourly_spend_cap_exceeded" }
  }
}
```

The SDK maps reasons to typed errors: `paymasterReasonToError` and `mapPaymasterReason` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`. See [Error Reference](../../reference/errors.md).

## CORS

The route is called straight from browsers, so it answers `OPTIONS` itself. By default it allows any origin (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`); v1 narrows that with `PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. That is a browser speed bump only, not authentication. v2 binds the **project** to allowed origins separately, per client token, inside the engine.

## Using the SDK builders

```ts
import {
  buildPaymasterContext,
  buildPaymasterDataRequest,
  buildPaymasterStubDataRequest,
} from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { buildErc7677Url } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";

const url = buildErc7677Url({
  baseUrl: "https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com", // hosted base; http://localhost:8788 locally
  token: process.env.PEPU_CLIENT_TOKEN!,    // a ppt_ client token, never a ppk_ server key in a browser
  version: 2,                               // v2 serves /v2/paymaster/<token>; use 1 for /paymaster/<token>
});

const context = buildPaymasterContext({ privyAccessToken });
const stubRequest = buildPaymasterStubDataRequest({ userOperation, context });
const dataRequest = buildPaymasterDataRequest({ userOperation, context });
```

Both builders default the EntryPoint to the registry's v0.7 address and the chain to 97741. `buildErc7677Url` refuses a `ppk_` server key in a browser because the URL would embed the secret. In practice, Privy or viem makes these calls once you give them the URL; reach for the builders when debugging or writing a custom client. See [/paymaster](../../sdk/paymaster.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid params: entryPoint ... not supported` | Sent a v0.6 EntryPoint | Use `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` |
| `invalid params: chainId` | Wrong chain, or a typo such as 97721 | `0x17dcd` (97741) |
| `-32000` with `invalid_or_expired_token` | Missing, expired or unverifiable Privy token | Send a fresh token |
| `-32000` with `unknown_or_invalid_app_credential` | The credential in the URL is unknown or revoked | Check the URL; rotate if a key leaked |
| Works in `curl`, fails in the browser | Origin not allowed for this client token, or CORS | Add the origin to the project's `allowedOrigins`; see [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md) |
| `AA33 reverted` at the bundler | Approval expired, or (v2) the bundler executor is not allowlisted | Request fresh data; use the PEPU bundler |
| First sponsored transaction denied on cap | Per-user cap smaller than the one-time account deployment (about 12 PEPU worst case) | Size caps above it. See [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md) |

## Related

- [Paymaster Overview](overview.md)
- [Credential Matrix](auth.md)
- [REST API v1](rest-api-v1.md), [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md)
- [Bundler JSON-RPC API](../bundler/api.md)
- [Send a Sponsored Transaction](../../recipes/sponsored-send.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/infra/paymaster/rest-api-v1

# Paymaster REST API v1

Reference for the v1 policy service: `GET /health`, `POST /sponsor`, `POST /paymaster/:appToken` and the admin circuit-breaker reset. It decides whether to sign a sponsorship for `PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7` and says exactly why when it refuses. Read this if you run or call the v1 service.

The v1 paymaster is retired and this API is documented for reference only. Its EntryPoint deposit has been withdrawn, so it cannot sponsor anything. For new work use [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md) at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. Local default: `http://localhost:8788` (the service's own code default port is `8787`).

## Routes

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | None | Liveness probe. Returns `{"status":"ok"}` |
| `POST /sponsor` | `Authorization: Bearer <Privy access token>` and `X-Api-Key: <app key>` | Evaluate a sponsorship request directly (your own frontend or backend calls this) |
| `POST /paymaster/:appToken` | The app key in the URL | ERC-7677 JSON-RPC. What Privy's smart-wallet client calls. See [ERC-7677 Methods](erc7677.md) |
| `OPTIONS /paymaster/:appToken` | None | CORS preflight, answers 204 |
| `POST /admin/circuit-breaker/reset` | `X-Admin-Token` equal to `ADMIN_TOKEN` | Clear the global circuit breaker. Disabled (not served) when `ADMIN_TOKEN` is unset |

The SDK client for these is `createPaymasterApi().v1` (`sponsor`, `health`, `erc7677Url`) from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`.

## POST /sponsor

Headers:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <Privy access token>`. Verified against Privy's JWKS |
| `X-Api-Key` | The app's raw API key. The service stores only `sha256(key)` and compares in constant time |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

Body: `{ "userOp": { ... } }` with the v0.7 unpacked fields, numeric fields as `0x` hex:

```json
{
  "userOp": {
    "sender": "0x…",
    "nonce": "0x0",
    "factory": "0x…",
    "factoryData": "0x…",
    "callData": "0x…",
    "callGasLimit": "0x…",
    "verificationGasLimit": "0x…",
    "preVerificationGas": "0x…",
    "maxFeePerGas": "0x…",
    "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…"
  }
}
```

`factory` and `factoryData` are present only when the operation deploys the user's smart account.

Approved (HTTP 200):

```json
{
  "status": "approved",
  "chainId": 97741,
  "paymaster": "0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0",
  "paymasterVerificationGasLimit": "0x…",
  "paymasterPostOpGasLimit": "0x…",
  "paymasterData": "0x…",
  "validUntil": 0,
  "validAfter": 0,
  "userOpHash": "0x…"
}
```

Denied (4xx or 5xx):

```json
{ "status": "denied", "reason": "invalid_or_expired_token", "message": "The Privy access token is missing, expired, or does not verify." }
```

A missing bearer token returns `401 invalid_or_expired_token` ("Missing or empty Authorization bearer token."). An invalid bearer token returns the same status after a round trip to Privy's JWKS endpoint.

## POST /paymaster/:appToken

`<appToken>` is the app's raw API key, the same value as `X-Api-Key`, carried in the path because Privy's dashboard field is a bare URL. **Treat the full URL as a secret.** Methods and shapes are on [ERC-7677 Methods](erc7677.md).

The trade-off, stated plainly: Privy calls this URL straight from the end user's browser with no Privy access token. So the `/sponsor` ownership check (the smart wallet must belong to the authenticated Privy user) is **not available** here. The app token is the only per-caller credential. Every other check still runs (allowlist, per-app budget, circuit breaker), but per-"user" caps are keyed on the UserOperation's **sender address**, not a verified identity. That opens a sybil path (fresh Kernel accounts each get fresh per-sender caps), which the per-app caps, the destination allowlist and the global circuit breaker bound. Worst case is denial of sponsorship, never fund theft, because every sponsored call must still clear the allowlist. See [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md).

## Status and reason table

HTTP statuses for a denial come from the reason. Every `*_cap_exceeded` reason is a 429.

| Reason | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_or_expired_token` | 401 | Missing, expired or unverifiable Privy token |
| `unknown_or_invalid_app_credential` | 401 | The API key (header or URL) is not a registered app |
| `sender_not_owned_by_token_user` | 403 | `/sponsor` only: the sender smart wallet is not owned by the token's Privy user, or the check failed (fail closed) |
| `destination_not_globally_allowed` | 403 | A decoded target is not on the global allowlist |
| `destination_not_allowed_for_app` | 403 | A decoded target is not on this app's own list |
| `calldata_decode_failed` | 400 | Not a Kernel v3 `execute` single or batch call (static-call or delegatecall flavours are always denied) |
| `malformed_request` | 400 | Body failed validation |
| `user_hourly_count_cap_exceeded`, `user_daily_count_cap_exceeded`, `user_lifetime_count_cap_exceeded` | 429 | Per-user count caps |
| `user_hourly_spend_cap_exceeded`, `user_daily_spend_cap_exceeded`, `user_lifetime_spend_cap_exceeded` | 429 | Per-user worst-case spend caps |
| `app_daily_spend_cap_exceeded`, `app_lifetime_spend_cap_exceeded` | 429 | Per-app spend caps |
| `global_circuit_breaker_tripped` | 503 | Aggregate daily ceiling reached; clear with the admin reset |

On the ERC-7677 route the same reasons arrive as JSON-RPC `-32000` with `error.data.reason`.

## Caps

All are environment variables of the service with defaults in `src/config.ts`; caps are booked at the **worst-case** cost (all five gas limits times `maxFeePerGas`) when the approval is signed.

| Cap | Code default | Hosted deployment |
|---|---|---|
| Per-user count: hourly, daily, lifetime | 20, 100, 2,000 | same |
| Per-user spend: hourly, daily, lifetime | 25, 100, 1,000 PEPU | same |
| Per-app daily and lifetime spend | per app in `config/apps.json`; `null` lifetime means uncapped | the demo app: 200 PEPU a day |
| Global daily ceiling | 1,000 PEPU | 500 PEPU a day |
| Validity window | 90 seconds | same |

Per-user caps use a trailing window (no resetting by waiting for midnight); per-app and global use calendar-day UTC. Detail is on [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md).

## Rate limiting and proxying

There is no built-in per-IP rate limiting in v1. For a hosted deployment, put a reverse proxy with rate limits in front, set `PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` once frontend origins are known and keep the per-app URL secret.

## What to expect

- A sponsored first transaction costs about 12 PEPU of worst-case reservation (it deploys the account), later ones about 3 PEPU.
- A denial never consumes budget.
- State is a SQLite file (`DB_PATH`); spend accounting assumes a single process.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `401 invalid_or_expired_token` | No or stale Privy token | Fetch a fresh access token and retry |
| `401 unknown_or_invalid_app_credential` | Wrong or revoked key | Check `X-Api-Key` or the URL; ask the operator to register or rotate |
| `403 sender_not_owned_by_token_user` | Smart Wallets not enabled in the Privy Dashboard, or the sender belongs to someone else | Enable Smart Wallets (Kernel, chain 97741); see [Dashboard Settings](../../privy/dashboard-settings.md) |
| `403 destination_not_globally_allowed` | The call goes to a contract not on `config/allowlist.json` | Add the contract (operator action) |
| `429 user_hourly_spend_cap_exceeded` on a first transaction | Cap is below the ~12 PEPU account deployment | Raise the per-user caps above the deployment cost |
| `503 global_circuit_breaker_tripped` | Daily ceiling hit | Wait for UTC rollover, or `POST /admin/circuit-breaker/reset` |

## Related

- [Paymaster Overview](overview.md)
- [ERC-7677 Methods](erc7677.md)
- [Credential Matrix](auth.md)
- [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md)
- [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md)
