Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/infra/paymaster/rest-api-v2

# Paymaster REST API v2

Reference for the tiered sponsorship API (`/v2/*`) of the policy service, derived from `services/paymaster/policy-service/openapi.yaml` and the service source. Read it to log in as a project owner, prove ownership of a Privy app, issue and rotate credentials, change origins, check the free tier, encode transactions with `prepare` and to decode a denial.

Base URL `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. The `/v2` routes are public (free-tier, config, SIWE login, projects, verify; CORS `*`); `/v2/admin` returns 404 on the hosted host. The routes exist only when the service runs with `SPONSORSHIP_V2_ENABLED=true` (the hosted one does). Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs.

**Funds never move through this API, and it is not required to use the contract.** Deposits are one-way: anyone can deposit into any project (claimed or not) or the free pool, and nothing can withdraw. The API is a convenience layer that encodes calldata, indexes a claimed project and issues the credentials the service needs to sign sponsorships.

Conventions: all amounts are decimal **wei strings**. Errors are `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "...", "reason"?: "..." }`. HTTP 429 carries a `Retry-After` header. Base URL is `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default; override with `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` or run your own service).

## Auth tiers

| Tier | Credential | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Public | None | `config`, `contract`, `free-tier`, `auth/nonce`, `auth/login` |
| Session | `Authorization: Bearer <SIWE session token>` | `me`, `auth/logout`, `projects/verify` (any signed-in address) |
| Owner | Session whose address equals the project's **current on-chain owner**, re-checked against the chain on every call | `projects` routes |
| Admin | `X-Admin-Token` equal to `SPONSORSHIP_ADMIN_TOKEN` (at least 32 characters, separate from the v1 admin token). Routes return 404 when unset | `/v2/admin/*` |
| Credential | Project server key `ppk_...`, or client token `ppt_...` from an allowed origin, plus a Privy access token for the free tier | `/v2/sponsor`, `/v2/paymaster/:token` |

The full matrix is on [Credential Matrix](auth.md).

## Route summary

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v2/config` | Public | Service and contract configuration |
| `GET /v2/contract` | Public | Paymaster address, chain id, EntryPoint and ABI |
| `GET /v2/free-tier` | Public | Free-pool state and limits. 503 if the chain is unreadable |
| `GET /v2/auth/nonce` | Public | Issue a single-use SIWE nonce (5 minutes) |
| `POST /v2/auth/login` | Public | Verify a SIWE message and signature, open a session |
| `POST /v2/auth/logout` | Session | Revoke the session |
| `GET /v2/me` | Session | The session address |
| `POST /v2/projects/verify` | Session | Prove control of a Privy app, receive a signed ownership attestation |
| `POST /v2/projects/prepare` | Session | Encode a transaction for the owner's wallet |
| `POST /v2/projects` | Owner | Index a claimed project and issue its credentials |
| `GET /v2/projects` | Session | Projects owned by the session address, plus on-chain claims not yet indexed |
| `GET /v2/projects/{projectId}` | Owner | Project state: on-chain balance and limits, off-chain settings, 24h usage |
| `POST /v2/projects/{projectId}/token/rotate` | Owner | New client token |
| `POST /v2/projects/{projectId}/server-key/rotate` | Owner | New server key |
| `PATCH /v2/projects/{projectId}/settings` | Owner | Per-user cap, `requireIdentity`, `allowedOrigins` |
| `GET /v2/projects/{projectId}/usage` | Owner | Spend history, reserved versus actual |
| `GET /v2/projects/{projectId}/events` | Owner | On-chain events for the project |
| `GET /v2/projects/{projectId}/allowlist` | Owner | Current on-chain destination allowlist |
| `POST /v2/sponsor` | Credential | REST sponsorship |
| `POST /v2/paymaster/{appToken}` | Credential | ERC-7677 JSON-RPC. `OPTIONS` answers CORS. See [ERC-7677 Methods](erc7677.md) |
| `GET /v2/admin/overview` | Admin | Free pool, contract totals, reconciler status, usage counts |
| `GET /v2/admin/projects` | Admin | All indexed projects and apps |
| `POST /v2/admin/apps` | Admin | Create a free-tier-only app and its token |
| `POST /v2/admin/projects/{key}/status` | Admin | Suspend or unsuspend a token (kill switch; does not touch funds) |
| `POST /v2/admin/projects/{key}/token/rotate` | Admin | Lost-token recovery |
| `POST /v2/admin/projects/{key}/server-key/rotate` | Admin | Server-key rotation (on-chain projects only) |
| `POST /v2/admin/reconcile` | Admin | Run the on-chain reconciler once |

## Public routes

### GET /v2/config

Returns chain id, paymaster and EntryPoint addresses, `adminChangeDelaySeconds`, the one-way-deposit and ownership notes, `postOpOverheadGas` and its maximum, the contract `owner` and `manager`, `siweDomains`, `sessionTtlSeconds`, `paymasterRpcPath` (`/v2/paymaster/{token}`) and `projectDefaults` (per-user daily default and maximum, wei).

### GET /v2/contract

`{ "address", "chainId", "entryPoint", "abi" }`. Build deposit and settings transactions from this; the SDK helpers do it for you.

### GET /v2/free-tier

Free-tier state: pool balance, per-op cap, per-wallet limit and per-user allowance. There is no chain-wide ceiling. Eligibility is a verified Privy account. The SDK probe `probePaymaster` reads it when exposed.

## The SIWE session

Project owners authenticate with Sign-In With Ethereum (EIP-4361), so no password or API key is needed to manage a project.

1. `GET /v2/auth/nonce` returns `{ "nonce", "expiresAt" }`. The nonce is single use and lasts 5 minutes.
2. Build an EIP-4361 message. Rules the service enforces: the **domain** must be in `SIWE_DOMAINS` (see `GET /v2/config`), the **chain id** must match, `expirationTime` is required and at most 10 minutes after `issuedAt`, and `issuedAt` must be within clock skew. Sign it with the wallet.
3. `POST /v2/auth/login` with `{ "message", "signature" }`. EOA and ERC-1271 (Safe) signatures are accepted. The response is `{ "token", "address", "expiresAt" }`: an opaque 32-byte session token, stored hashed on the server, valid for 1 hour and bound to that address.
4. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on session and owner routes. `POST /v2/auth/logout` revokes it. Ownership is re-checked on chain on every owner call, so a transfer of ownership takes effect immediately.

Failures: `401 login_failed` with a `reason`, or `429` (login and nonce are rate limited per IP). With the SDK, `api.v2.loginWithWallet(sign, { address, domain })` does all four steps.

## POST /v2/projects/verify

Proves that the caller controls a Privy app and returns an EIP-712 `ProjectClaim` attestation for their wallet. This is how a project's on-chain owner is established without PEPU choosing who owns what.

Auth: a session for `ownerAddress`.

```json
{ "appId": "<your Privy app id, exactly as in the dashboard>", "appSecret": "<your Privy app secret>", "ownerAddress": "0x…" }
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `appId` | 1 to 128 characters of `A-Za-z0-9_-`. **Case-sensitive**, used exactly as given (never lower-cased). The project id is `keccak256(bytes(appId))` |
| `appSecret` | At most 512 characters. Used for **exactly one** outbound request to Privy (HTTP Basic plus the `privy-app-id` header, `GET /v1/users?limit=1`) and **never stored, logged or echoed**, including in errors. Extra body fields are rejected |
| `ownerAddress` | Must equal the session address |

Success (200):

```json
{
  "projectId": "0x…",
  "appId": "…",
  "ownerAddress": "0x…",
  "action": "claimProject",
  "attestation": { "appId": "…", "newOwner": "0x…", "nonce": "…", "deadline": "…", "signature": "0x…" },
  "expiresAt": "…",
  "note": "…"
}
```

`action` is `claimProject` when the project is unclaimed and `reclaimProject` when it already has an owner. `takesEffect` is `immediately` for the claim of an empty project and `after_admin_change_delay` for a re-claim or for the first claim of a project that already holds deposited funds (the `note` says so; finish that claim with `executeReclaim` after the delay). The attestation is EIP-712 `ProjectClaim(string appId,address newOwner,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)` in the domain `PepuSponsoredPaymaster` version `1`, bound to the chain and the paymaster address, **single use**, and valid for at most **1 hour** (the contract rejects a deadline further out; the service default is 10 minutes). Submit it on chain with `prepare` (below) or the SDK's `encodeClaimFromVerification`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 400 | Malformed body (fixed message; the secret is never echoed) |
| 403 | `ownerAddress` is not the session address, or Privy rejected the credentials |
| 409 | This wallet already owns the project |
| 429 | Rate limited. Per IP on every request, plus a failure budget per (app id, signed-in address) charged **only** when Privy rejects the credentials, so a stranger cannot lock the real owner out |
| 501 | Not configured on this deployment |
| 502 | Privy could not be reached |

Rotate the Privy secret in the dashboard afterwards if you wish. Use a dedicated Privy app for sponsorship where you can. A holder of the secret can replace a pending re-claim with their own, so rotate the secret after any recovery.

## POST /v2/projects/prepare

Encodes a transaction for the owner's wallet to sign and send. **It sends nothing.** Owner-gated actions are checked against the project's current on-chain owner. There are no withdrawal actions, because none exist.

| `action` | Fields | Contract function |
|---|---|---|
| `claimProject` | `attestation` | `claimProject`. First claim; sets the owner only. Immediate for an empty project; **pending for the admin change delay (at least 48 hours) when the project already holds funds** |
| `reclaimProject` | `attestation` | `reclaimProject`. Timelocked re-claim (48 hours or more), cancellable by the owner once per new owner |
| `depositFor` | `projectId`, `amountWei` | `depositFor`. Open to anyone, one-way |
| `executeReclaim`, `cancelReclaim`, `acceptProjectOwnership` | `projectId` | the same-named function |
| `setTargets` | `projectId`, `targets[]`, `allowed` | The destination allowlist |
| `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit` | `projectId`, `limitWei` | Project and per-wallet daily limits |
| `setPaused` | `projectId`, `paused` | Pause or resume. Pausing is a project's exit |
| `proposeProjectOwner` | `projectId`, `newOwner` | Voluntary two-step handover. The zero address withdraws a pending nomination |

`claimProject` takes `attestation` only. The former `targets` and `limits` fields are rejected with 400: the claim sets **only** the owner, so afterwards the owner must call `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit`. Nothing is sponsorable until all three have run.

Response (200):

```json
{ "chainId": 97741, "to": "0x…", "data": "0x…", "value": "0", "function": "setDailyLimit(bytes32,uint112)", "description": "…" }
```

Errors: 400 invalid, 403 not the on-chain owner.

## Project routes (owner)

### POST /v2/projects

Indexes an on-chain claimed project and issues credentials. The session address must be the project's current on-chain owner.

```json
{
  "appId": "…",
  "perUserDailyCapWei": "200000000000000000000",
  "requireIdentity": false,
  "allowedOrigins": ["https://app.example.com"]
}
```

Give `projectId` or `appId` (the id is `keccak256(appId)`). `allowedOrigins` are plain origins (`scheme://host[:port]`, no paths or wildcards, `http` only for localhost), at most 20. A project with none can be spent only with its server key; its client token is refused with `project_origin_not_allowed`. Success is `201` with:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `token` | The publishable **client token** `ppt_...`, **shown once** |
| `paymasterUrl` | `https://<host>/v2/paymaster/<token>`, the value for Privy's "Paymaster URL" field. Spends the project's budget only from `allowedOrigins` |
| `serverKey` | The secret **server key** `ppk_...`, **shown once**. Backend only |

`409` means the project is not claimed on chain yet (a pending claim counts as not claimed until `executeReclaim`), or is already indexed. `403` means not the owner. `400 app_id_mismatch` means `appId` does not hash to `projectId`: the service takes the app id from the chain, and uses a request-supplied one only if `keccak256(appId) == projectId`.

### GET /v2/projects

`{ "projects": [...], "onchainUnindexed": [...] }`: projects owned by the session address plus on-chain claims not yet indexed.

### GET /v2/projects/{projectId}

On-chain state (`balance`, `spendable` which is balance minus signed-but-unsettled approvals, `outstandingApprovals`, `paused`, `dailyLimit`, `senderDailyLimit`, `spentToday`, `dailyRemaining`), `adminChangeDelaySeconds`, the allowlist, off-chain settings (credential prefixes, `allowedOrigins`, per-user cap, `requireIdentity`, status), `usage24h` (ops, project-funded and free-tier-funded wei) and the contract address.

### Credentials and rotation

| Route | Effect |
|---|---|
| `POST /v2/projects/{projectId}/token/rotate` | New client token and `paymasterUrl`. **The old one stops working immediately.** Update the URL in the Privy Dashboard |
| `POST /v2/projects/{projectId}/server-key/rotate` | New server key. **The old one stops working immediately** |

Both are shown once. When the on-chain owner changes (an executed re-claim or a voluntary transfer), the engine revokes the previous owner's server key and client token, clears the previous allowed origins and denies requests with `project_owner_changed`. The new owner rotates to get fresh ones.

### PATCH /v2/projects/{projectId}/settings

Off-chain settings; any subset of:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `perUserDailyCapWei` | Per-user daily cap, within the admin maximum (default 200 PEPU; maximum 5,000 PEPU). 400 if out of range |
| `requireIdentity` | Opt in to refusing wallets without a verified Privy token |
| `allowedOrigins` | The client token's origin allowlist, at most 20 |

### Origins

A **client token** is publishable, so it is visible to anyone using the app. It therefore spends the project budget only when the request's `Origin` is in `allowedOrigins`. A project with no allowed origins cannot be spent with its client token at all. The **server key** has no origin restriction and must never reach a browser. Honest limit: browsers enforce `Origin`, but a non-browser client can forge it. Origin binding stops drive-by browser abuse and casual copying of the URL, not a determined holder of the token. The contract's own limits (allowlist, per-wallet and daily limits) are the backstop either way.

### Read routes

| Route | Query | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v2/projects/{projectId}/usage` | `limit` (max 500), `before` | Spend history: reserved versus actual (reconciled from on-chain `UserOpSettled`), project- versus free-funded |
| `GET /v2/projects/{projectId}/events` | `fromBlock`, `limit` (max 1000) | Deposits, claims, settlements and configuration events |
| `GET /v2/projects/{projectId}/allowlist` | none | `{ projectId, source, targets }`, replayed from `TargetSet` events |

## Sponsorship routes

### POST /v2/sponsor

REST sponsorship. Headers: `X-Api-Key` carries the project's server key (any wallet) or client token (needs an allowed `Origin`); `Authorization: Bearer <Privy access token>` is **required for the free tier**. Body: `{ "userOp": { ... } }` as for [v1](rest-api-v1.md#post-sponsor).

Approval (200) returns the paymaster fields, `userOpHash`, a `sponsor` object (`kind` `project` or `free`, `sponsorId`, `projectKey`) and `maxCostWei`. A denial returns `{ "status": "denied", "reason", "message", "detail"? }`, where `detail` can carry the reason for each tier tried (`{ project?, free? }`).

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Approved |
| 400 | Malformed body (`malformed_request`, `invalid_json`), or a bounded-input denial: undecodable calldata, gas or fee out of bounds, fee above the on-chain cap, op above the free pool's cap |
| 401 | Invalid app or Privy credential (unknown credentials are throttled per IP and not written to the audit log) |
| 403 | Forbidden: suspended, origin not allowed, identity required, destination not allowed, project has no per-wallet limit on chain, account deployment disabled |
| 413 | Body larger than 256 KiB (`body_too_large`) |
| 429 | Per-IP request limit (`rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`, checked before the body is read), or cap, balance or per-wallet limit reasons |
| 503 | Chain unreadable (fail closed) |

### POST /v2/paymaster/{appToken}

ERC-7677. `appToken` is the client token (project budget only from allowed origins) or server key. `context.privyAccessToken` is required for the free tier. Full detail on [ERC-7677 Methods](erc7677.md).

## Admin routes

All need `X-Admin-Token`; 401 if wrong, 404 if the admin API is disabled. They are per-IP rate limited. `POST /v2/admin/apps` takes `{ label, perUserDailyCapWei?, allowedDestinations? }` and creates a free-tier-only app (no on-chain project; use the real Privy app id as `label` so identity resolves), returning 201, or 409 if the label exists. The status route takes `{ "status": "active" | "suspended" }`. Server-key rotation returns 400 for free-tier-only apps, which have no server key.

## Free tier

The free tier is funded by the chain's free pool and is for **verified Privy users only** (from PEPU's own Privy app; a third-party app's own Privy token is ignored for billing): 100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per hour as enforced by the live service (the older spec numbers were 50 a day and 30 an hour), with count caps of 40 ops a day and 20 an hour, at most 40 PEPU per operation, no chain-wide ceiling. A request without a verified Privy token is denied with `free_tier_identity_required`. The free tier never pays for a project's non-Privy wallets. See [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md).

## Denial reason catalog

These are the values of `reason` in REST denials and in `error.data.reason` on the ERC-7677 route. The HTTP status comes from the reason. The SDK constant `PAYMASTER_DENIAL_REASONS` and `mapPaymasterReason` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`) mirror this list, and each maps to a typed SDK error; see [Error Reference](../../reference/errors.md).

| Reason | HTTP | Meaning and fix |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_or_expired_token` | 401 | Privy token missing, expired or invalid. Send a fresh one |
| `unknown_or_invalid_app_credential` | 401 | Server key or client token unknown or rotated. Check the URL or key |
| `app_suspended` | 403 | The token was suspended by an admin |
| `sender_not_owned_by_token_user` | 403 | The sender is not an account of the token's Privy user. Two things count as owned: the ZeroDev Kernel v3.1 account (ECDSA validator, index 0) derived from one of the user's own Privy embedded wallets, which is what the SDK combo and session flows create and needs no Smart Wallets setting, or a Privy Smart Wallet linked to the user. The check also fails closed when Privy or the RPC cannot be reached right now, so a retry can succeed |
| `target_not_allowed_onchain` | 403 | A target is not on the sponsor's on-chain allowlist. The owner runs `setTargets` |
| `destination_not_allowed_for_app` | 403 | A target is outside a free-tier-only app's allowed destinations |
| `project_identity_required` | 403 | The project set `requireIdentity` and no verified Privy token came with the request |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | 403 | Client-token request from an origin not in `allowedOrigins` (or none configured) |
| `free_tier_identity_required` | 403 | Free tier needs a verified Privy token |
| `project_paused` | 403 | The owner paused the project |
| `project_not_claimed_onchain` | 403 | The project has no on-chain owner yet. Deposits to it are not spendable until claimed |
| `project_owner_changed` | 403 | The on-chain owner changed; credentials were revoked. The new owner rotates |
| `calldata_decode_failed` | 400 | Not a Kernel v3 `execute` single or batch call |
| `malformed_request` | 400 | Body failed validation |
| `free_pool_op_too_large` | 400 | Worst-case cost exceeds the free pool's per-op cap (40 PEPU) |
| `gas_limits_out_of_bounds` | 400 | A gas field exceeds the service bounds (`preVerificationGas` 1,000,000, `verificationGasLimit` 1,500,000, `callGasLimit` 3,000,000 by default) |
| `fee_out_of_bounds` | 400 | `maxFeePerGas` above the lower of 3 times the current base fee and 40,000 gwei, or the priority fee above the base fee |
| `fee_above_onchain_cap` | 400 | `maxFeePerGas` above the sponsor's on-chain cap, so the contract would reject it |
| `chain_read_failed` | 503 | The service could not read on-chain state (fail closed). Retry |
| `project_balance_exhausted` | 429 | The project cannot cover the worst-case cost. Deposit more |
| `project_daily_limit_reached` | 429 | The project's daily limit (counting in-flight approvals) |
| `project_sender_limit_reached` | 429 | The per-wallet daily limit |
| `project_sender_limit_not_set` | 403 | The project has no per-wallet daily limit on chain (the contract rejects every op until the owner runs `setSenderDailyLimit`) |
| `account_deployment_disabled` | 403 | The service switched off sponsoring new-account deployment (`factory` / `factoryData` present) |
| `project_user_cap_exceeded` | 429 | The off-chain per-user daily cap |
| `free_tier_disabled` | 429 | The owner disabled the free tier |
| `free_tier_user_daily_exceeded`, `free_tier_user_hourly_exceeded`, `free_tier_count_exceeded` | 429 | Free-tier per-user caps |
| `free_tier_sender_limit_reached` | 429 | The free pool's per-wallet limit |
| `free_pool_empty` | 429 | The free pool cannot cover the operation |
| `reservation_cap_exceeded` | 429 | Too many live unexecuted approvals for a client token (2 per wallet, 5% of budget per IP, 25% in total). Retry shortly |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Per-IP limit on client-token requests (default 30 a minute). Respect `Retry-After` |
| `destination_not_globally_allowed`, `user_*_cap_exceeded`, `app_*_spend_cap_exceeded`, `global_circuit_breaker_tripped` | v1 | v1-only reasons; see [REST API v1](rest-api-v1.md) |

The design spec names one reason `project_not_registered_onchain`; the code (and the SDK) uses `project_not_claimed_onchain`. The code is authoritative.

## Rate limits and proxies

In-memory sliding windows, single process: per IP on nonce and login (strict), per address on owner routes, per IP on admin routes, per token and IP on the ERC-7677 route, 30 per minute per IP on client-token evaluations, 600 per minute per IP on `POST /v2/sponsor` (checked **before** the body is read; `RATE_LIMIT_SPONSOR_PER_IP_PER_MIN`), and 60 per minute per IP on ERC-7677 requests whose URL token matches no credential (`RATE_LIMIT_RPC_UNKNOWN_TOKEN_PER_IP_PER_MIN`; junk tokens used to get a fresh bucket each). Denials for an unknown or missing credential are **not written to the audit log** (they are counted in memory and shown by the admin overview as `unauthenticated`); the audit log is pruned after `SPONSORSHIP_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30) by the reconciler timer. `verify` has its own per-IP limit (10 a minute by default) and the per-(app id, address) failure budget. Set `TRUST_PROXY=true` behind a reverse proxy so limits see real client IPs; the client IP is then the `X-Forwarded-For` entry `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` (default 1) from the right, never the client-controlled leftmost entry.

CORS: auth, owner and admin routes send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` only for origins in `SPONSORSHIP_API_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (default none). The ERC-7677 route keeps its open default; project origin binding is a separate check inside the engine.

## Using the SDK

```ts
import { createPaymasterApi, assertApproved } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";

const api = createPaymasterApi(); // defaults to https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com
const free = await api.v2.freeTier();
const result = await api.v2.sponsor(userOp, { apiKey: process.env.PEPU_SERVER_KEY!, privyAccessToken });
const approval = assertApproved(result); // throws a typed PepuPaymasterError on denial
```

`api.v2` covers every route above: `config`, `contract`, `freeTier`, `auth`, `loginWithWallet`, `me`, `projects.{prepare, register, list, get, rotateClientToken, rotateServerKey, updateSettings, usage, events, allowlist}`, `sponsor`, `erc7677Url` and a low-level `request`. See [/paymaster](../../sdk/paymaster.md) and [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](v2-register-deposit-claim.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `login_failed` | SIWE domain not in `SIWE_DOMAINS`, wrong chain id, expired nonce or message | Take the domain from `GET /v2/config`; request a fresh nonce |
| `403` from `verify` | Wrong app secret, or `ownerAddress` is not the session wallet | Check both; the secret is never echoed back |
| `409` from `POST /v2/projects` | Not claimed on chain yet | Submit the claim transaction first, then index |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` in the browser | The page origin is not in `allowedOrigins` | `PATCH` the settings to add it |
| Everything denied right after claiming | The claim sets only the owner | Run `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit` (a project with no per-wallet limit is `project_sender_limit_not_set`) |
| `409` / `project_not_claimed_onchain` after submitting a claim | The project already held funds, so the claim is pending for the admin change delay | Wait for `executableAt` (event `ProjectClaimProposed`), then `prepare {action: "executeReclaim"}` |
| `429` on `POST /v2/sponsor` before any other check | Per-IP request limit (`RATE_LIMIT_SPONSOR_PER_IP_PER_MIN`, default 600) | Back off; send from the backend that holds the server key, or raise the limit |
| `AA33` at the bundler | Bundler executor not allowlisted in the v2 contract | Use the PEPU bundler |

# Paymaster Credential Matrix

Which credential applies to which paymaster call, how to obtain it, and how to rotate it. Read this before putting any key or URL into a browser, a Privy Dashboard field or a backend.

The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`); there is no tokenless default. A project server key (`ppk_`) is a secret and stays server-side. A client token (`ppt_`) works only from the project's allowed origins and is refused with `project_origin_not_allowed` when none are set. The free tier needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app (`context.privyAccessToken`, REST `Authorization: Bearer`); a third-party app's own Privy token is ignored for billing. v1 credentials no longer apply because the v1 paymaster is retired.

## Credential types

| Credential | Format | Who holds it | Browser-safe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Privy access token | JWT from Privy | The signed-in user | Yes |
| v1 app key | Raw key; the service stores only `sha256(key)` in `config/apps.json` | The operator and the app | The URL embedding it is a secret |
| Server key | `ppk_...`, secret | A project's backend | **No** |
| Client token | `ppt_...`, publishable | A project's frontend or Privy Dashboard | Yes, spends only from allowed origins |
| SIWE session | Opaque bearer, 1 hour | A project owner's browser | Yes |
| Admin token | `ADMIN_TOKEN` (v1), `SPONSORSHIP_ADMIN_TOKEN` (v2, 32 or more characters) | PEPU operators | **No** |
| Privy app secret | From the Privy dashboard | The developer | **No**, one call only |

`credentialKind(credential)` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster` tells `"client"` from `"server"` by prefix and never inspects more.

## Matrix by call path

| Call | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | none | none |
| `GET /v2/config`, `/v2/contract`, `/v2/free-tier` | n/a | none |
| `POST /sponsor` | Privy token (`Authorization: Bearer`) **and** app key (`X-Api-Key`) | n/a |
| `POST /v2/sponsor` | n/a | `X-Api-Key` server key (any wallet) or client token (allowed `Origin`); Privy token required for the free tier |
| `pm_getPaymasterStubData` | none: the URL credential is not resolved (spec-compliant) | none: URL token only picks the sponsor id for the stub |
| `pm_getPaymasterData` | app key in the URL | `ppt_` or `ppk_` in the URL; `context.privyAccessToken` for the free tier |
| `/v2/auth/nonce`, `/v2/auth/login` | n/a | none (login is a SIWE signature) |
| `/v2/me`, `/v2/auth/logout` | n/a | SIWE session |
| `POST /v2/projects/verify` | n/a | SIWE session for `ownerAddress` plus the Privy app secret in the body |
| `POST /v2/projects/prepare` | n/a | SIWE session |
| `POST/GET /v2/projects...`, rotation, settings, usage, events, allowlist | n/a | SIWE session whose address is the **current on-chain owner** |
| `POST /admin/circuit-breaker/reset` | `X-Admin-Token` | n/a |
| `/v2/admin/*` | n/a | `X-Admin-Token`; 404 if unset, and not exposed on the hosted host (404) |

What each unlocks on the sponsorship path:

| Credential | Sponsors | Free tier | Origin check | On a leak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Server key `ppk_` | Any wallet, from the project's budget | No (needs a Privy token) | None | Rotate at once; bounded by the project's on-chain limits |
| Client token `ppt_` | Any wallet, only from `allowedOrigins` | With a Privy token | Yes; none configured means it cannot spend the project | Rotate; spend limited to the project's allowlist and daily limits |
| v1 app key | Registered app's budget | n/a | Optional `PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (speed bump) | Operator rotates; anyone with the URL can request sponsorship under the app's caps |

## How to obtain each

| Credential | How |
|---|---|
| Privy access token | From the signed-in Privy session, for example `getAccessToken()` in the Privy client |
| v1 app key | An operator generates a raw key, runs `npm run hash-api-key -- <key>` in the policy service and stores the hash in `config/apps.json`. There is no self-serve path in v1 |
| SIWE session | `api.v2.loginWithWallet(sign, { address, domain })`, or nonce then login by hand |
| Attestation | `requestClaimAttestation` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server` (server or CLI only) |
| Server key and client token | `POST /v2/projects` on a claimed project (`api.v2.projects.register`), **shown once** |
| Admin token | Set in the service environment by the operator |

## Rotation

| Credential | Rotate with | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Client token | `POST /v2/projects/{id}/token/rotate` (`rotateClientToken`) | Old token stops immediately. Update the URL in the Privy Dashboard and any frontend |
| Server key | `POST /v2/projects/{id}/server-key/rotate` (`rotateServerKey`) | Old key stops immediately |
| Both, on ownership change | Automatic revocation when the on-chain owner changes (denial `project_owner_changed`) | The new owner rotates to get fresh ones |
| Lost token | `POST /v2/admin/projects/{key}/token/rotate` (admin) | Recovery |
| Suspend | `POST /v2/admin/projects/{key}/status` | Kill switch; does not touch funds |
| v1 app key | Operator replaces the hash in `apps.json` and restarts | Old URL dies |
| Privy app secret | Rotate in the Privy dashboard after verifying | The service never stored it |

## Rules

- A `ppk_` key never goes into a browser, a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable or a Privy Dashboard field. `buildErc7677Url` throws `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` for a server key in a browser.
- Origin binding is a browser guard: non-browser clients can forge `Origin`. The contract's limits are the real backstop.
- Never log or commit any of these. Only `sha256(rawKey)` goes in `apps.json`.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `unknown_or_invalid_app_credential` | Rotated, mistyped or wrong environment | Re-copy the credential, check which service it belongs to |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | Client token used from an unlisted origin | Add the origin with `PATCH /v2/projects/{id}/settings` |
| `free_tier_identity_required` | No Privy token with a free-tier request | Pass `Authorization: Bearer` or `context.privyAccessToken` |
| `403` on an owner route | Session address is not the on-chain owner | Sign in with the owner wallet |
| Pasted URL stopped working | The token was rotated, or a tunnel URL changed | Re-issue and update the Dashboard |

## Related

- [Paymaster Overview](overview.md)
- [REST API v1](rest-api-v1.md), [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md)
- [ERC-7677 Methods](erc7677.md)
- [Privy Dashboard Settings](../../privy/dashboard-settings.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/infra/paymaster/policy-and-caps

# Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker

What the policy service checks before it signs a sponsorship: the destination allowlist, per-user, per-app and per-project caps, the free-tier numbers and the global circuit breaker, plus how spend is booked. Read it to size caps correctly and to understand a denial.

Rules are served by the policy service at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. The v1 rules belonged to the retired v1 paymaster and no longer apply.

## v1 pipeline

Enforced in this order; every step, approved or denied, writes an audit row. **A denied request never consumes budget.**

1. Token verification (Privy JWT on `/sponsor`; sender-keyed stand-in on the ERC-7677 route) then `invalid_or_expired_token`.
2. Sender ownership (`/sponsor` only) then `sender_not_owned_by_token_user`.
3. App resolution by hashed key then `unknown_or_invalid_app_credential`.
4. Call data decode (Kernel v3 `execute`, single or batch only) then `calldata_decode_failed`.
5. Destination allowlist.
6. Per-user count caps.
7. Per-user spend caps.
8. Per-app spend caps.
9. Global circuit breaker.
10. Validity window encoded into the approval (90 seconds).
11. Sign, atomically with the cap-recording write.

## Allowlist

- **v1:** a destination must be on **both** the global list (`config/allowlist.json`, a hard backstop) and the app's own `allowedDestinations` (`"*"` defers to global). An app can only narrow, never widen. The global list currently holds only TapScore (`0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`). Empty means everything is denied. Denials: `destination_not_globally_allowed`, `destination_not_allowed_for_app`.
- **v2:** the allowlist lives **on chain** per sponsor (`setTargets`), decoded from Kernel call data inside the contract, so it binds even a compromised signer. An empty list sponsors nothing. Account self-calls are denied unless the owner allowlists the account. Denial: `target_not_allowed_onchain`. A project can also pin the sender's account codehash (`setRequiredAccountCodehash`) so that only that account code is sponsored.

## Caps

All figures are configurable; spend is measured at the **worst case** (five gas limits times `maxFeePerGas`), not the eventual actual cost.

| Cap | v1 default | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| Per-user count (hour, day, lifetime) | 20, 100, 2,000 | free tier: 20 an hour, 40 a day |
| Per-user spend (hour, day, lifetime) | 25, 100, 1,000 PEPU | free tier, as enforced by the live service: **50 PEPU an hour, 100 PEPU a day** (the spec design numbers are 30 an hour and 50 a day) |
| Per-app | daily and lifetime per app in `apps.json` | per project: service per-user daily cap, default 200 PEPU, adjustable up to 5,000 PEPU |
| Per-operation | none | free pool: 40 PEPU (`free_pool_op_too_large`) |
| Per-wallet daily (on chain) | none | project: required, above 0. Free pool: default 100 PEPU per smart account per day |
| Project daily (on chain) | none | project `dailyLimit`, above 0 |
| Gas price | none | on-chain `maxFeePerGas` cap per sponsor (deploy default 40,000 gwei) plus service bounds against the live base fee |
| Global daily ceiling | 1,000 PEPU code default (deployment: 500) | none for the free pool; bounded by the pool balance |

Per-user caps use a **trailing window** (cannot reset by waiting for midnight); per-app spend and the global ceiling use calendar-day UTC.

### Free-tier numbers (v2)

Live allowance: 100 PEPU per Privy user per rolling day and 50 PEPU per hour (the spec design number is 50 PEPU a day), enforced by the service. Privy users only (a verified access token is required; there is no anonymous tier), 40 PEPU maximum per operation, **no chain-wide daily ceiling**. The first operation (deploying the account) is about 12 PEPU worst case and later operations about 3 PEPU, so the daily allowance covers a deployment plus many operations. Note that N Privy accounts get N times the daily allowance, bounded by the pool balance. See [Sponsorship Tiers](../../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md).

### Size caps above the cheapest legitimate action

A user's first operation deploys their account and costs about 12 PEPU. A per-user cap smaller than that denies every sponsorship, so it is an outage, not a safety margin. Raise caps above the deployment cost and re-check them whenever gas limits or account mechanics change. The session flow is costlier: the first operation of a sponsored session (deploy plus enabling the permission) reserved about 20.5 PEPU and later ones about 6.9 PEPU.

## Spend accounting

- Booked at signing at worst-case cost. **Idempotent by `userOpHash`**: a duplicate `pm_getPaymasterData` for a live approval is not booked twice (Privy can call twice in parallel).
- Approvals that expire unexecuted stop counting (the signature is dead after `validUntil`). Trade-off: in v1, until a reconciler marks executed operations, an executed operation also drops out of the sums after the window, so v1 caps are effectively a rate limit on signatures per window, with the deposit and the circuit breaker as hard stops.
- v2 reconciles from on-chain `UserOpSettled`, replacing worst-case with the actual charge, and subtracts outstanding approvals from the chain balance so concurrent requests cannot all pass on one balance. Client-token reservations are capped: 2 live approvals per wallet, 5% of budget per IP, 25% in total (the server key is exempt).

## Circuit breaker

`GLOBAL_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_WEI` sums spend over every app, user and sender (calendar-day UTC, or since the last manual reset). When it trips, **all** sponsorship stops with `global_circuit_breaker_tripped` (HTTP 503). It is the last defence against a fleet of fresh sender addresses, each with fresh per-sender caps (Kernel factories are permissionless, so the ERC-7677 path cannot tell an attacker's own account from a real user's). Worst case is denial of service, bounded and resettable, never fund theft, because each call still has to clear the allowlist. Clear it with `POST /admin/circuit-breaker/reset` (`X-Admin-Token`) or `npm run reset-circuit-breaker` in the policy service, which works directly on the database file. `npm run reset-spend-counters` clears per-user and per-app history without touching the audit log.

`PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOW_ACCOUNT_DEPLOYMENT` (default `true`) controls whether the public ERC-7677 route sponsors new-account deployments. Turning it off raises the cost of a sybil fleet and breaks sponsored first transactions.

## Draw order (v2)

1. Project path if the credential is a project's and it can pay (`balance - outstanding` covers worst case, within limits).
2. Otherwise the free tier, only with a verified Privy token and allowance.
3. Otherwise denied, with the reason per tier in `detail`. An operation is never split between tiers, and the free tier never pays for a project's non-Privy wallets.

## Reason codes

The full catalog with HTTP statuses is in [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md#denial-reason-catalog) (v2) and [REST API v1](rest-api-v1.md#status-and-reason-table) (v1). The SDK maps them to typed errors; see [Error Reference](../../reference/errors.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every first transaction denied on spend cap | Cap below the account deployment cost | Raise per-user caps above about 12 PEPU (session flow about 20.5) |
| `global_circuit_breaker_tripped` | Daily ceiling reached | Wait for UTC rollover or reset; investigate for a sybil fleet |
| Cap errors persist after raising caps | Old event rows still count in the window | `npm run reset-spend-counters` (optionally `-- --user` or `-- --app`) |
| `project_daily_limit_reached` early in the day | In-flight approvals count at full worst case | Raise the daily limit or wait for approvals to expire |

## Related

- [Paymaster Overview](overview.md)
- [REST API v1](rest-api-v1.md), [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md)
- [PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract](contracts.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../../concepts/trust-and-security.md)

# Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project

Step-by-step procedure for a developer to fund and take ownership of a tiered-paymaster [project](../../reference/glossary.md): derive the project id, deposit, claim with a Privy-verified attestation, configure the allowlist and limits, issue credentials, plug them into your app, and know the rotation and re-claim rules. It uses the SDK (`@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster` and `/paymaster/server`) and has an agent and MCP route for the parts a tool can do. You need a project for any sponsored template that is not PEPU's own app: this is where the "paymaster token" in the quickstart comes from.

The v2 contract is deployed at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` and the policy service is hosted at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. Deposits are **one-way**: nobody can withdraw them, so deposit only what your project needs.

## The whole procedure at a glance

| # | Step | Who does it | SDK | MCP or agent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Derive the project id from your Privy app id | Anyone | `computeProjectId` | `pepu_project_balance` computes it |
| 2 | Sign in to the policy service with the owner wallet (SIWE) | Owner wallet, in a script | `api.v2.loginWithWallet` | Not possible: needs the wallet's signature |
| 3 | Prove you control the Privy app (attestation) | Your script, with the Privy secret | `requestClaimAttestation` | Not possible: the secret must not pass through a tool |
| 4 | Claim the project on-chain | Owner wallet | `encodeClaimFromVerification`, `sendPaymasterCalls` | `pepu_prepare_project_tx` with `claim` returns the calldata |
| 5 | Set targets and both daily limits | Owner wallet | `configureProject` | `pepu_prepare_project_tx` with `configure` |
| 6 | Deposit PEPU (one-way) and register the project | Any wallet deposits; the owner session registers | `depositFor`, `api.v2.projects.register` | `pepu_prepare_project_tx` with `deposit`; registering needs the SIWE session |
| 7 | Put the right credential in your app and check | You | `checkSponsorship`, `readProject` | `pepu_project_balance`, `pepu_sponsorship_status` |

Do the steps in this order. Claim before anyone deposits, or the claim waits 48 hours. (The numbered sections below split the same work into finer steps.)

## Prerequisites

- The deployed v2 paymaster address, `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (the SDK registry has it as `paymasterV2`; `resolvePaymasterV2Address` throws rather than guess on a chain without one).
- The hosted service, `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default base). The ERC-7677 URL you end up with is `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, with `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` holding the complete URL.
- Your **Privy app id** and app secret (server only; dedicated app recommended).
- An owner wallet that will control the project's settings (an EOA, or a Safe, which can sign SIWE via ERC-1271). Use a fresh wallet used only for this; its private key goes in an environment variable, never in code or a commit.
- Native PEPU in that wallet for deposits and for the configuration transactions' gas (a transaction costs a fraction of a cent; the deposit is whatever budget you want, start small).
- A scratch Node project to run the steps: `npm init -y && npm i @pepu-chain/sdk viem && npm i -D tsx`, then `npx tsx project.ts` with the variables below exported. The complete runnable version is the [Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](../../recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md) recipe.
- The SIWE domain the hosted service accepts: `paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (the `siweDomains` entry of `GET https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/config`). Export it as `PEPU_SIWE_DOMAIN`.

| Variable | Value | Secret? |
|---|---|---|
| `PRIVY_APP_ID` | Your Privy App ID, exactly as the dashboard shows it | No |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Your Privy App Secret | Yes, server or CLI only |
| `PROJECT_OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY` | The owner wallet's key (the recipe's variable name) | Yes |
| `PEPU_SIWE_DOMAIN` | `paymaster.pepeunchained.com` | No |

## 1. Derive the project id

```ts
import { computeProjectId } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";

const projectId = computeProjectId(process.env.PRIVY_APP_ID!); // keccak256(bytes(appId))
```

Use the app id **exactly** as the Privy dashboard shows it. It is case-sensitive: a different case is a different project.

## 2. Check who owns the project, then deposit (anyone can)

Depositing needs no approval and works before anyone claims the project. Funds in an unclaimed project are not spendable until it is claimed. Read the owner first: `address(0)` means unclaimed.

```ts
import { depositFor, readProject } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";

const state = await readProject(publicClient, projectId, { paymaster });
// state.claimed is false for an unclaimed project

const hash = await depositFor({
  walletClient,
  publicClient,
  appId: process.env.PRIVY_APP_ID!,
  amountWei: 10n ** 18n,
  paymaster,
  // requireClaimed defaults to true: refuses an unclaimed project, which catches a mistyped app id.
  // Pass requireClaimed: false to fund a project before its owner claims it.
});
```

**One-way.** Nothing, not the owner, the contract owner nor the manager, can take a deposit back. It can only pay gas. A stranger funding your project cannot hurt you; they only add budget under your settings. Funds in a project that is never claimed stay locked.

## 3. Sign in and request an attestation (server or CLI only)

The attestation proves you control the Privy app. The service checks your secret against Privy once and never stores, logs or echoes it.

```ts
import { createPaymasterApi } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";
import { requestClaimAttestation } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server"; // server only

const api = createPaymasterApi({ baseUrl: process.env.PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL! });

await api.v2.loginWithWallet((message) => account.signMessage({ message }), {
  address: account.address,
  domain: "paymaster.pepeunchained.com", // must be in the service's SIWE domains; see GET /v2/config
});

const verified = await requestClaimAttestation(api, {
  appId: process.env.PRIVY_APP_ID!,
  newOwner: account.address, // must equal the signed-in address
  privyAppSecret: process.env.PRIVY_APP_SECRET!,
});
// verified.action is "claimProject" (unclaimed) or "reclaimProject" (already owned)
```

Never call this from a browser; never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable for the secret. Rotate the secret in the Privy dashboard afterwards if you want to. The attestation expires within an hour and can be used once.

## 4. Claim on chain

```ts
import { encodeClaimFromVerification, sendPaymasterCalls } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";

const claim = encodeClaimFromVerification(verified, { paymaster });
await sendPaymasterCalls(walletClient, [claim], { publicClient });
```

Anyone may submit the claim transaction; the attestation fixes the owner. **A project that holds no funds is claimed immediately. A project that already holds deposited funds is pending for the admin change delay (at least 48 hours):** the claim emits `ProjectClaimProposed`, the contract owner or manager can cancel it, and you (or anyone) finish it with `encodeExecuteReclaim(projectId)` after the delay (and within 30 days). To avoid the wait, claim before anyone funds the project. **The claim sets only the owner.** The project starts with an empty allowlist and a zero daily limit, so nothing is sponsorable yet. The MCP tool `pepu_prepare_project_tx` encodes the same transactions without sending anything.

## 5. Configure the allowlist and limits

```ts
import { configureProject, sendPaymasterCalls } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";

const { calls } = configureProject({
  appId: process.env.PRIVY_APP_ID!,
  paymaster,
  targets: [tapScore],                 // 1 to 50 contracts to sponsor calls to
  dailyLimitWei: 100n * 10n ** 18n,     // project daily budget
  senderDailyLimitWei: 25n * 10n ** 18n, // per-wallet daily budget (above the ~21 PEPU first-operation reservation)
});
await sendPaymasterCalls(walletClient, calls, { publicClient });
```

That is `setTargets(allowed = true)`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit`, in order. All three must run before anything is sponsored: **a project with no per-wallet limit is rejected by the contract** (`ZeroDailyLimit`) however it is otherwise configured. A smart account can batch them into one operation. Size the per-wallet limit above the worst-case reservation of a user's first operation, which also deploys their account: about 12 PEPU for a plain sponsored send and about 21 PEPU (20.5) for the first operation of a Kernel session, or new users are denied on their first action. The project balance must also cover at least one reservation, so deposit at least about 25 PEPU before the first test; unused gas is refunded to the project. You can also set a gas-price cap (`setMaxFeePerGas`), pin the account codehash (`setRequiredAccountCodehash`) and pause (`setPaused`, instant; pausing is a project's exit). See [PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract](contracts.md).

## 6. Index the project and get credentials

```ts
const created = await api.v2.projects.register({
  appId: process.env.PRIVY_APP_ID!,
  allowedOrigins: ["https://app.example.com"],
});
// created.token (ppt_, publishable), created.paymasterUrl, created.serverKey (ppk_, secret): each shown once
```

**Save all three values immediately: each is shown once** (`rotateClientToken` and `rotateServerKey` issue new ones if you lose them). Paste `paymasterUrl` into Privy's "Paymaster URL" field if you use Privy Smart Wallets. Put the server key only in your backend. Without `allowedOrigins`, the client token cannot spend the project at all (`project_origin_not_allowed`). If Privy calls the URL from its own servers and that error appears, use the server key in the dashboard URL and keep it secret. Check state any time with `api.v2.projects.get(projectId)` and `readProject`.

## 7. Plug the credential into your app and check it

| Template | Credential | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| `sponsored-session-app` (and any server or bot using `/combo` or `createPepuSponsoredClient`) | The server key (`ppk_`) | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>` in `.env.local`, server only. Leave `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` as `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` |
| `sponsored-demo` (Privy Smart Wallets) | The client token (`ppt_`) | The `paymasterUrl` from step 6 in the Privy dashboard, Smart Wallets, chain 97741. Allowed origins must include your app's origin |
| A browser using `useDirectSponsoredSend` | The client token (`ppt_`) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, with allowed origins set |

Restart the dev server, then check:

```ts
// Check that a paymaster project is ready to sponsor: reachable services, claimed, limits set, funded.
// Read-only: sends nothing and needs no secrets. See docs/infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md
import { checkSponsorship, getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { computeProjectId, readProject } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";

export async function verifyProject(appId: string) {
  const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);
  const report = await checkSponsorship({ publicClient });
  if (!report.available) console.log(report.reason, report.fixes);

  const state = await readProject(publicClient, computeProjectId(appId));
  console.log(state.claimed, state.limitsConfigured, state.balance); // true, true, a positive balance
  return { available: report.available, ready: state.claimed && state.limitsConfigured && state.balance > 0n };
}
```

Success looks like `claimed: true`, `limitsConfigured: true` and a positive `balance`. Then a first sponsored transaction from a fresh account holding 0 PEPU goes through: the result's `paymaster` field is the v2 contract, and your project's balance drops by the gas it paid.

## Do it with an AI agent (MCP)

The MCP server (`@pepu-chain/mcp`) never signs and never sees your Privy secret. It does the parts that are pure encoding or reading, and tells you which steps still need your wallet or your script.

1. Ask: "Using the pepu MCP tools, walk me through claiming and funding a paymaster project for Privy app `<app id>`." The agent follows the `pepu-paymaster-projects` skill.
2. `pepu_project_balance` with your `appId` shows whether the project exists, who owns it and its balance. A zero-address owner means unclaimed.
3. Run the SIWE login and the attestation (steps 2 and 3) with the recipe script: they need your wallet and your Privy secret. The agent can write and set up the script from `pepu_sdk_snippet` (`v2-deposit-and-claim`), but you export the secrets.
4. `pepu_prepare_project_tx` with `action: "claim"` and the attestation, then `"configure"` (targets, `dailyLimitPepu`, `senderDailyLimitPepu`), then `"deposit"` (`amountPepu`) returns an unsigned `{ to, data, value }` for each. You send them from the owner wallet. The tool sends nothing.
5. Register (step 6) with the script, save the keys, then ask the agent to run `pepu_sponsorship_status` and `pepu_project_balance` for the final check.

## Rotation and the re-claim timelock

| Action | How | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Rotate the client token | `api.v2.projects.rotateClientToken(projectId)` | Old token stops immediately; update the Dashboard URL |
| Rotate the server key | `api.v2.projects.rotateServerKey(projectId)` | Old key stops immediately |
| Change origins, per-user cap, `requireIdentity` | `api.v2.projects.updateSettings(projectId, ...)` | Off-chain settings |
| Lost the owner wallet | Repeat steps 3 and 4 from a new wallet: the result is `reclaimProject` | **Timelocked at least 48 hours**, announced by `ProjectReclaimProposed`, cancellable by the current owner (`encodeCancelReclaim`) **once per new owner** (a second attested re-claim by the same wallet cannot be cancelled), finished by anyone with `encodeExecuteReclaim`; lapses 30 days after it becomes executable |
| Hand over to a multisig | `encodeProposeProjectOwner`, then the new owner calls `encodeAcceptProjectOwnership` | Voluntary two-step transfer; clears any pending re-claim that the owner has not already vetoed once. A nomination can be withdrawn by proposing the zero address (prepare API) |
| Owner changed | Automatic | The previous owner's credentials are revoked (`project_owner_changed`); the new owner rotates |

Watch `ProjectReclaimProposed` (and the contract's `AdminChangeProposed`) and pause if something looks wrong. A re-claim proposed before a signer was removed never executes, even if that signer is re-added. Because ownership follows the Privy secret, rotate the secret after any recovery.

## What to expect

- Nothing is sponsored until step 5 is complete and the project has balance.
- Money leaves only as gas paid for sponsored operations.
- The policy signer is the ownership gatekeeper. A compromised signer could claim an **empty** unclaimed project immediately, and a funded one after the admin delay unless the contract owner or manager cancels it, so claim before anyone funds the project. It can never withdraw funds, because none can be withdrawn.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` about the v2 paymaster address | A chain with no deployed v2 entry (testnet) | On mainnet use the registry address; elsewhere pass one explicitly |
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED` from `depositFor` | Project unclaimed, or the app id is mistyped (case-sensitive) | Check spelling; pass `requireClaimed: false` only on purpose |
| `403` from `verify` | Wrong secret, or `newOwner` is not the signed-in address | Fix and retry |
| Claim reverts with an expired or used claim | Attestation older than an hour, or already used | Request a new one |
| All denials after a claim | Allowlist and limits not set | Run step 5 |
| `409` from `register` | Not claimed on chain yet, or already indexed | Claim first; list with `api.v2.projects.list()` |
| `401 login_failed` at sign-in | The SIWE domain is not one the service accepts | Use `paymaster.pepeunchained.com`, or read `siweDomains` from `GET /v2/config` |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` in the app | A client token (`ppt_`) with no allowed origins, or used from a server | Pass `allowedOrigins` at register or `updateSettings`, or use the server key from a backend |
| Lost the keys shown at register | They are shown once | `rotateClientToken` or `rotateServerKey`, then update the app |

# PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract

Reference for the paymaster contracts: v2 `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` (live on mainnet) and v1 `PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7` (retired): functions, events, errors, roles and timelocks. Names come from the SDK's `pepuSponsoredPaymasterV2Abi` and the spec; the contract source is `services/paymaster/contracts/src`.

The v2 paymaster is at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (about block 10537341). Owner `0x5966…4A1`, manager `0x063A…aBb0`; the free pool was seeded with 300 PEPU. The v1 paymaster at `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` is retired: its EntryPoint deposit was withdrawn (0), so it cannot sponsor anything. Never deposit to it.

## v1: PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7

A fork of Pimlico's singleton verifying paymaster with ERC-20 mode removed. Its job is narrow: check that `paymasterAndData` carries a valid ECDSA signature from an authorised signer over an approved time window, then pay gas from its EntryPoint deposit.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Address | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` (retired) |
| Stake and deposit | Retired. The EntryPoint deposit is withdrawn (0) |
| Signed prefix | `paymaster(20) ‖ verificationGasLimit(16) ‖ postOpGasLimit(16) ‖ mode(1)=0x00 ‖ validUntil(6) ‖ validAfter(6)`, then the 65-byte signature |
| Hash | keccak of sender, nonce, account gas limits, preVerificationGas, gas fees, hashes of initCode, callData and the prefix, then with `chainid`, EIP-191 signed. A frozen cross-language test vector pins both sides |
| Signers | Multi-signer (`MultiSigner`): a manager can add or remove signers without a redeploy |
| Caps | **None on chain.** Every economic safeguard is in the policy service |
| Bundler gate | Not enforced |

The main risk is signer-key compromise: any signature from an authorised signer is honoured up to the deposit. The mitigation is keeping the float small and rotating signers. See [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md).

## v2: PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7

One contract that is both paymaster and vault. All PEPU sits in its EntryPoint deposit; an internal ledger records which sponsor owns what, with `totalLiabilities` equal to the sum of ledgers and `totalLiabilities` at most the EntryPoint balance. Deployed at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`.

### How it validates

`paymasterData` is `mode(1)=0x02 ‖ validUntil(6) ‖ validAfter(6) ‖ sponsorId(32) ‖ signature(65)` (97 bytes signed, `sponsorId` inside the hash). `sponsorId` is `0x00..00` for the free pool or `keccak256(bytes(appId))` for a project. Validation, in order:

1. Caller is the EntryPoint. The mode byte must be exactly `0x02`, and the **bundler gate is unconditional**: `tx.origin` must be an allowlisted bundler (`address(0)` is allowlisted so estimation works).
2. Signature exactly 65 bytes, low-s, from an authorised signer, otherwise `SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED` with no state change (so stubs never revert or charge).
3. `validUntil` non-zero; paymaster post-op gas limit at least 40,000; the op's `maxFeePerGas` at most the sponsor's cap.
4. The sponsor must be claimed and not paused; for the free pool, enabled and under `freeMaxOpCost`. A **project must also have a non-zero per-wallet daily limit** (`ZeroDailyLimit` otherwise); only the free pool may run with 0 = off.
5. Every Kernel `execute` target (single `0x00` or batch `0x01`) must be on the sponsor's allowlist. Empty means nothing.
6. Daily limit (projects) and per-wallet daily limit, keyed on the signed `validAfter` day.
7. The sponsor's balance covers `maxCost`. The full `maxCost` is deducted; `postOp` refunds `maxCost - charge` to the **same** sponsor. `charge` includes a post-op overhead (20,000 gas at deploy, floor 18,000) plus the worst case of the EntryPoint's 10% unused-gas penalty, so the ledger can never be short. Both are **snapshotted into the context at validation**, so `postOp` makes no cold storage read of the overhead and an owner changing it mid-flight cannot change an in-flight op's charge (worst-case postOp 13,918 gas against the 18,000 floor).

Because the gate uses `ORIGIN`, which ERC-7562 bans, v2 is supported only behind a self-run bundler with safe mode off whose executor is allowlisted. See [Bundler Overview](../bundler/overview.md).

### Functions

| Group | Functions | Who |
|---|---|---|
| ERC-4337 | `validatePaymasterUserOp`, `postOp`, `getHash` | EntryPoint (hash view for anyone) |
| Deposits (one-way) | `depositFor(projectId)`, `fundFreePool()`, `creditSurplusToFreePool()` | **Anyone** |
| Claims | `claimProject(Claim)`, `reclaimProject(Claim)`, `executeReclaim`, `cancelReclaim`, views `claimDigest`, `domainSeparator`, `claimUsed`, `signerRemovedAt`, `pendingReclaim`, `vetoedReclaimant`, `PENDING_EXPIRY` | Claim: anyone with a signer attestation. Execute: anyone after the delay and within 30 days. Cancel: the current project owner, **once per new owner**; for a pending **first claim** of a funded, unowned project, the contract owner or manager |
| Project settings | `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`, `setMaxFeePerGas`, `setRequiredAccountCodehash`, `setPaused`, `proposeProjectOwner`, `acceptProjectOwnership` | The project's own owner only |
| Free pool | `setFreeTier`, `setFreeMaxFeePerGas` (owner); `pauseFreePool`, `setFreeTargets` (owner or manager) | Owner, manager |
| Governance | `proposeAdminChange`, `executeAdminChange`, `cancelAdminChange` (kind 1 signer, 2 bundler; `address(0)` allowed as a bundler only), `removeSigner`, `removeBundlers`, `setManager`, `setPostOpOverheadGas` (can only lower), `addStake` (delay at most 30 days), `unlockStake`, `withdrawStake` (stake only) | Owner, manager (stake functions and `setManager`, `setPostOpOverheadGas` are owner only) |
| Ownership | OpenZeppelin `Ownable2Step`: `transferOwnership`, `acceptOwnership`, `renounceOwnership` | Owner |
| Views | `getProject`, `getSenderSpend`, `isTargetAllowed`, `projectIdOf`, `effectiveMaxFeePerGas`, `requiredAccountCodehash`, `pendingAdminChange`, `surplus`, `totalLiabilities`, `adminChangeDelay`, `defaultMaxFeePerGas`, `postOpOverheadGas`, `maxPostOpOverheadGas`, `freeEnabled`, `freeMaxOpCost`, `manager`, `entryPoint`, `signers`, `isBundlerAllowed` | Anyone |

There is no `receive()` or plain `deposit()`, and **no withdrawal function of any kind** for ledger funds. The contract never calls `entryPoint.withdrawTo` (a test scans the bytecode for that selector). `withdrawStake` moves only the separate EntryPoint stake balance. `claimProject` sets only the owner, so the owner follows with `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit`. A claim of a project with **no deposited funds is immediate**; the claim of a project that **already holds funds is pending** for `adminChangeDelay` (event `ProjectClaimProposed`), signer-bound, cancellable by the contract owner or manager, and finished by anyone with `executeReclaim`. `setMaxFeePerGas` and `setFreeMaxFeePerGas` cannot exceed `defaultMaxFeePerGas`; `setFreeTier` rejects a non-zero per-wallet limit below the per-op cap (`InvalidFreeTierConfig`); `proposeProjectOwner(id, address(0))` withdraws a nomination.

### Events

`ProjectClaimed`, `ProjectClaimProposed` (pending first claim; the contract owner and manager should watch), `ProjectReclaimProposed` (owners should watch), `ProjectReclaimCancelled`, `Deposited`, `TargetSet`, `DailyLimitSet`, `SenderDailyLimitSet`, `PausedSet`, `ProjectOwnershipTransferStarted`, `ProjectOwnershipTransferred`, `FreeTierConfigured`, `SurplusCreditedToFreePool`, `ManagerSet`, `PostOpOverheadGasSet`, `BundlerAllowlistUpdated`, `SignerAdded`, `SignerRemoved`, `AdminChangeProposed` (projects should watch), `AdminChangeCancelled`, `MaxFeePerGasSet`, `RequiredAccountCodehashSet`, OpenZeppelin `OwnershipTransferStarted` and `OwnershipTransferred`, `SponsorReserved` and `UserOpSettled`.

### Errors

`NotEntryPoint`, `NotOwnerOrManager`, `NotProjectOwner`, `NotPendingProjectOwner`, `InvalidOwner`, `OwnableInvalidOwner`, `OwnableUnauthorizedAccount`, `ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall`; validation: `PaymasterModeInvalid`, `PaymasterAndDataLengthInvalid`, `PaymasterConfigLengthInvalid`, `PaymasterSignatureLengthInvalid`, `BundlerNotAllowed`, `InvalidValidityWindow`, `PostOpGasLimitTooLow`, `MaxFeePerGasTooHigh`, `AccountCodehashMismatch`, `UnknownSponsor`, `SponsorPaused`, `FreeTierDisabled`, `OpCostTooHigh`, `CostTooLarge`, `UnsupportedCallData`, `TargetNotAllowed`, `DailyLimitExceeded`, `SenderDailyLimitExceeded`, `InsufficientSponsorBalance`; claims: `InvalidAppId`, `InvalidClaimSignature`, `ClaimExpired`, `ClaimAlreadyUsed`, `ClaimDeadlineTooFar`, `ProjectAlreadyClaimed`, `ProjectNotClaimed`, `NoPendingReclaim` (also an expired claim), `ReclaimNotReady`, `ReclaimSignerRemoved`, `ReclaimNotCancellable`; config: `ZeroAmount`, `ZeroDailyLimit`, `ZeroFeeCap`, `DelayTooShort`, `DelayTooLong`, `OverheadOutOfBounds`, `InvalidAdminChange`, `AdminChangeAlreadyProposed`, `AdminChangeNotProposed`, `AdminChangeNotReady`, `InvalidFreeTierConfig`, `NothingToCredit`. The SDK exposes `decodePaymasterRevert` to decode revert data.

### Roles

| Role | Held by | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anyone | | Deposit, fund the free pool, submit claims, execute re-claims, credit surplus to the free pool | Withdraw |
| Project owner | Established by an attested claim | Settings, pause, voluntary transfer, cancel a re-claim (once per new owner) | Touch any other project or the free pool; withdraw |
| Owner | The deployer by default; two-step transfer, renounce supported | Free-tier parameters, manager, lower overhead, `addStake`, `unlockStake`, `withdrawStake`, cancel a pending first claim | Reach any ledger money or a project's settings |
| Manager | Should be a different address (the deploy script refuses owner = manager without an explicit override) | Propose and execute signer and bundler additions (timelocked), instant removals, free-pool targets and pause, cancel a pending first claim | Withdraw, change a project, touch the stake |
| Signer(s) | The policy service key | Approve ops and **attest claims** (one shared set) | Withdraw; pay itself unless it is an allowlisted bundler |

### Timelocks

| Change | Delay |
|---|---|
| Signer or bundler **addition** | `adminChangeDelay`: immutable, constructor-enforced between 48 hours and 30 days (deploy default 48 hours) |
| **Re-claim** of an owned project, and the **first claim of a project that holds funds** | The same delay; announced, cancellable (the current owner once per new owner; the contract owner or manager for a first claim), void if its attesting signer was removed since |
| Any pending claim, re-claim or admin addition | Lapses 30 days after it becomes executable (`PENDING_EXPIRY`) |
| Removals (signer, bundler), pause, limit and fee-cap changes | Instant |
| Attestation validity | At most 1 hour (`ClaimDeadlineTooFar`) |

A project's defence during a timelock window is to pause and tighten its limits.

### Size and pinned build

Runtime size is 23,722 bytes against the 24,576-byte EIP-170 limit (854 bytes of headroom), so any further change needs a size check. It fits only because this contract is compiled with **8,000 optimizer runs** (25,115 bytes at 1,000,000), which costs about 0.2% on validation and 0.5% on `postOp`; `foundry.toml` applies that to this contract only, so the deployed v1 build is unchanged. The deploy script pins the creation-bytecode hash `0x86153ab5c7faa3a83ea9949b2a44ebba196ce367227d376b9a28290e3a468164`, which reproduces only from LF line-ending sources (enforced by `.gitattributes`).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `AA33` with `BundlerNotAllowed` | Executor not on the v2 allowlist | Use the PEPU bundler |
| `TargetNotAllowed` | Call goes outside the allowlist | Owner runs `setTargets` |
| `UnknownSponsor` | Project not claimed (or its claim is still pending) | Claim it, and `executeReclaim` after the delay if the project already held funds; deposits are not spendable before |
| `ZeroDailyLimit` at validation | The project never called `setSenderDailyLimit` | Run `setSenderDailyLimit` |
| `PaymasterModeInvalid` | v1-layout data sent to v2 | Use v2 paymaster data from the v2 route |

# Address Map

Every contract address in the SDK registry for Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet (chain `97741`), with a source and a do-not-substitute note for each. Use this as the one table to copy from. In code, read the registry instead of pasting: `getContract`, `listContracts`, `getPepuAddresses` (an array of rows; `getPepuAddressMap` returns the same rows keyed by name) and `isDeployed` from `@pepu-chain/sdk`.

Mainnet only; the testnet (97740) is not supported. `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` re-checks every address below with `eth_getCode`. The v1 paymaster is retired.

## Verify an address

1. Run `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` from the repository root. It calls `eth_getCode` on each registry address and prints the byte count; it also confirms the canonical Multicall3 address has no code.
2. By hand, `cast code <address> --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz`, or the MCP tool `pepu_check_contract_deployed`.
3. Deployed code does not by itself confirm behavior; see the notes for each entry.

## Core infrastructure

| Name | Address | Bytes | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CREATE2 deterministic deployer (`create2Factory`) | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | 69 | Canonical Nick's-method deployer | Used to deploy Multicall3 and Permit2. See [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md) |
| Multicall3 (`multicall3`) | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | 3808 | PEPU-specific deployment from `mds1/multicall3` source via CREATE2, zero salt | **Not the canonical address.** `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` has no code here and never can. ## PepuSwap (third party)

PepuSwap is not in `pepuContracts`; it has its own registry (`getPepuSwapContract`, `listPepuSwapContracts`). Its addresses, including the **non-canonical** multicall and Permit2 that must not replace the ones above, are on [PepuSwap Addresses](pepuswap.md).

| Contract | Canonical address used on PEPU? |
|---|---|
| CREATE2 deployer | Yes |
| Permit2 | Yes |
| EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7 | Yes |
| Multicall3 | **No.** PEPU-specific at `0x9CE19273…01bd` |
| Kernel contracts | ZeroDev's standard addresses for these versions (no canonical-address trick; use the registry) |
| Paymaster, TapScore | Project-specific |

## Do-not-substitute checklist

- Never use `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` as Multicall3 on PEPU. `assertNotCanonicalMulticall3` throws `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS`.
- Never use PepuSwap's `0xB461…8b4B` as Permit2 or its `0x927a…383B` as Multicall3.
- Never use call policy v0.0.5.

# Deployed Contracts Reference

The complete, current answer to "does standard contract X exist on Pepe Unchained V2, and where." Every address below is on **mainnet (chain `97741`)** unless stated otherwise — see [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md#testnet-out-of-scope-today) for why testnet isn't covered here.

Check this page, not a canonical-address list you already have memorized, before hardcoding anything for PEPU. Multicall3 is live at an unusual address, and read the notes, not just the address column.

## Core infrastructure

| Contract | Address | Deployment | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CREATE2 deterministic deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | **Deployed**, canonical address | Standard "Nick's method" deterministic deployer. Multicall3 and Permit2 were deployed through it. See [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md). |
| Multicall3 | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | **Deployed — NOT at the canonical address** | Read [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md) before using this. The canonical address (`0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11`) is structurally unreachable on this chain. This deployment was built from canonical `mds1/multicall3` source (solc `0.8.12`, optimizer `10,000,000` runs), deployed via the CREATE2 deterministic deployer above with a zero salt, and verified on pepuscan. Deployed in block 10521048. |
| Permit2 | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` (canonical) | **Deployed**, canonical address | Deployed via ordinary CREATE2 at the canonical address (9,152 bytes of bytecode). Deployment details: [Permit2](permit2.md) and `contracts/permit2/`. |

Some first-party PEPU apps deployed their own small, purpose-built contracts that are easy to mistake for general infrastructure because of their name. They are **not** Multicall3- or Permit2-compatible and are not a substitute for the canonical registry above — they're sized for one app's own needs.

| PepuSwap Permit2 | `0xB461c05f76d7f919FF7A3Df2B0D2593F56538b4B` | PepuSwap | PepuSwap's own Permit2 deployment, not the canonical Permit2. If a library assumes canonical Permit2 (most `permit2-sdk`-style tooling does), pointing it at this address will not behave the same way. |

To re-check every registry entry on chain, run `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check`.

## Where this table comes from

Every address above is also encoded in [`@pepu-chain/sdk`'s contract registry](../sdk/core.md#contract-and-dex-registries) (`getContract`, `listContracts`, `isDeployed`), which is the machine-readable version of this page — use it in code instead of copy-pasting addresses out of Markdown. A registry entry that is not deployed has no `.address` field, so code that reads the registry cannot treat an undeployed contract as real.

If you find infrastructure not listed here on PEPU, check it directly (`eth_getCode`, or `pepu_verify_contract_status` if you have the [PEPU MCP server](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md) connected) before relying on it.
