Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/contracts/multicall3

# The Multicall3 Trap

This is the single most important gotcha on Pepe Unchained V2. Read it before you wire up any tooling that reads multiple contracts at once — viem's `multicall()`, wagmi's `useReadContracts`, or anything built on top of either.

## The short version

**Multicall3 is deployed on PEPU mainnet — but not at the address almost every EVM tool assumes.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Canonical Multicall3 address (works on nearly every other EVM chain) | `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` — **has no code on PEPU. It is permanently unreachable here — see why below.** |
| PEPU's actual Multicall3 address | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` — deployed, verified on pepuscan, and works with viem's `multicall()`. |

If your chain configuration doesn't explicitly set this address, or if a library you're using hardcodes the canonical one, batched reads will either throw a confusing "no code at this address" error or silently fail — not something an unfamiliar developer will trace back to "wrong Multicall3 address" quickly.

## Why the canonical address is unreachable here — not just unused

Other canonical contracts could be recovered on PEPU because they were deployed through CREATE2: the deterministic deployer is live, so the same source deployed the same way reproduces the canonical address (that is how Permit2 was deployed; see [Permit2](permit2.md)). Multicall3 is different.

Multicall3's canonical deployment on other chains was **not** done via CREATE2. It used a plain `CREATE` from a specific burn EOA, via a **pre-signed transaction with a hardcoded 1,000,000 gas limit**. That transaction is replayed, unmodified, on every new chain to get Multicall3 at the same address everywhere.

Arbitrum Nitro chains — including PEPU — need roughly **14.3 million gas** to deploy the same Multicall3 bytecode. The pre-signed transaction's fixed 1,000,000 gas limit means it **cannot execute here**, on this chain, ever, using that original signed transaction. There is no version of "just run the deploy script again" that fixes this — the transaction that would recreate the canonical address doesn't have enough gas headroom for this chain's execution costs, and it can't be re-signed with a higher limit without changing its hash (and therefore its resulting address).

The only way to get Multicall3 at the canonical address on PEPU would be for Conduit to add it as a **predeploy** at genesis — something only the chain operator can do, and not something that helps a chain that has already launched.

## What PEPU did instead

A PEPU-specific Multicall3 was deployed:

1. Built from the canonical [`mds1/multicall3`](https://github.com/mds1/multicall3) source, compiled with solc `0.8.12`, optimizer runs set to `10,000,000` — matching the canonical build as closely as possible so the bytecode's behavior is identical.
2. Deployed via the CREATE2 deterministic deployer (`0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C`) with a zero salt, which is why the resulting address (`0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`) is reproducible from the same inputs, just not equal to the canonical one (different deployment method → different resulting address, by construction).
3. Verified on pepuscan.
4. Compatible with viem's `multicall()` action.

It behaves exactly like Multicall3 everywhere else — it's simply at a different address, and every tool that talks to it needs to be told that explicitly.

## Deployment details

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` (in the SDK registry as `multicall3`) |
| Deployer contract | CREATE2 deterministic deployer `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C`, salt all zeros |
| Transaction | `0xf9d8f45010e2a2020871af9a677d134e9b43e039a0a73c09bcd22d1825f99241` |
| Block | 10521048 (`0xa089d8`), the `blockCreated` used in the chain definition |
| Gas used | 874,693 (`0xd58c5`) |
| Runtime size | 3,808 bytes |
| Source | `contracts/multicall3/src/Multicall3.sol`, solc 0.8.12, optimizer 10,000,000 runs (`contracts/multicall3/foundry.toml`) |
| Receipt and script | `deploy/multicall3-receipt.json`, `deploy/deploy-multicall3.sh`, `deploy/verify-multicall3.sh` |

`pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` also confirms that the canonical `0xcA11bde0…CA11` has no code. See [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md) for reproducing the address.

## What to do about it

**If you're using `@pepu-chain/sdk`:** nothing extra — `pepuMainnet.contracts.multicall3` is already set to the correct address. `getPublicClient(pepuMainnet)` and any wagmi config built from `pepuChains` pick it up automatically, and viem's `multicall()` action just works. See [`@pepu-chain/sdk` Reference](../sdk/reference.md).

**If you're hand-rolling a chain definition**, set the address explicitly rather than relying on a default:

```ts
import { defineChain } from "viem";

export const pepuMainnet = defineChain({
  id: 97741,
  name: "Pepe Unchained V2",
  nativeCurrency: { name: "Pepe Unchained", symbol: "PEPU", decimals: 18 },
  rpcUrls: { default: { http: ["https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz"] } },
  contracts: {
    multicall3: {
      address: "0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd",
      blockCreated: 10521048,
    },
  },
});
```

**Never substitute the canonical `0xcA11bde0…` address for PEPU.** It has no code here — any call against it returns empty data, and viem/wagmi's batching will fail for every read routed through it.

**If you omit `contracts.multicall3` entirely**, viem and wagmi fall back to individual per-call requests instead of batching. This is safe — you lose batching performance, not correctness — but it's strictly worse than setting the correct address above, since PEPU does have a working Multicall3 today.

## Don't confuse it with PepuSwap's "multicall"

PepuSwap (PEPU's native DEX, a Uniswap V3 fork) deployed its own small, non-canonical multicall-named contract at `0x927af2a6B76d2d8206d93004463F8C122701383B`. It is **not** Multicall3-compatible — it's a router-adjacent contract sized for PepuSwap's own needs, not general-purpose batching. Don't point generic tooling at it. See [Deployed Contracts Reference](deployed-contracts.md) for the full list of these app-specific, easy-to-confuse addresses.

## Recipe

Once your chain definition has the right address, batching reads is exactly the same code you'd write on any chain with Multicall3 — see [Batch Reads with Multicall3](../recipes/batch-reads-with-multicall3.md) for a copy-pasteable example.

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/contracts/permit2

# Permit2

Uniswap's Permit2 is deployed on PEPU mainnet at its canonical address. This page gives the address and the deployment details, the EIP-712 domain, typed-data examples with the SDK builders, and how it differs from PepuSwap's separate Permit2. Read it before signing a Permit2 permit or pointing a library at a Permit2 address.

Permit2 on PEPU was deployed by PEPU, not by Uniswap.

## Address and deployment

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` (canonical) |
| Deployer | CREATE2 deterministic deployer `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` |
| Salt | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000d3af2663da51c10215000000` (Uniswap's upstream salt) |
| Transaction | `0xbb0a23420f47dd4dbb524d96f46115011a66fc88bbdf0963cd24a50feb6f7c93` |
| Block | 10521367 (`0xa08b17`) |
| Gas used | 2,025,730 (`0x1ee902`) |
| Runtime size | 9,152 bytes, matching Permit2's known bytecode size |
| Files in the repo | `contracts/permit2/` (`initcode.hex`, `salt.txt`, `predicted.txt`, `permit2-receipt.json`, `prove-address.sh`, `deploy-permit2.sh`, `compute-domain-separator.sh`) |

Why it works: Permit2's canonical address is a CREATE2 address, so the exact upstream creation bytecode plus the upstream salt through the live deployer reproduces it. `prove-address.sh` recomputes the address independently with `cast create2` and by hand from `keccak256(0xff ++ deployer ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode))`. Compare [Multicall3](multicall3.md), which could not be recovered at its canonical address. How to reproduce: [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md).

## Domain and typed data

The EIP-712 domain is `{ name: "Permit2", chainId: 97741, verifyingContract: <the address above> }`. There is no `version`. `permit2Domain()` builds it:

```ts
import { permit2Domain, getPermit2 } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const domain = permit2Domain(); // { name: "Permit2", chainId: 97741, verifyingContract }
const { address } = getPermit2();
```

The registry ABI (`permit2Abi`) covers `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR`, `allowance`, `approve`, `nonceBitmap` and `invalidateNonces`.

## Examples

AllowanceTransfer `PermitSingle`:

```ts
import { buildPermitSingleTypedData, readPermit2Allowance } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const { nonce } = await readPermit2Allowance(publicClient, { owner, token, spender });

const typed = buildPermitSingleTypedData({
  token,
  amount: 1_000_000n,
  expiration: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600,
  nonce,
  spender,
  sigDeadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600),
});
const signature = await walletClient.signTypedData({ account, ...typed });
```

SignatureTransfer `PermitTransferFrom`:

```ts
import { buildPermitTransferFromTypedData } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const typed = buildPermitTransferFromTypedData({
  token,
  amount: 1_000_000n,
  spender,
  nonce: 0n, // a fresh unordered nonce; check nonceBitmap
  deadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600),
});
const signature = await walletClient.signTypedData({ account, ...typed });
```

The user still needs a normal ERC-20 `approve` of the token to Permit2 once. See [Sign a Permit2 Permit](../recipes/permit2-permit.md).

## Versus PepuSwap's Permit2

PepuSwap deployed its own Permit2 at `0xB461c05f76d7f919FF7A3Df2B0D2593F56538b4B` and its frontend overrides the address for chain 97741. The two have different EIP-712 domains (`DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` returns different values), so a signature for one is invalid on the other. Libraries that assume canonical Permit2 will not work against PepuSwap's copy, and PepuSwap's UI will not honour approvals made to the canonical one. Use the canonical address for your own contracts and PepuSwap's only when integrating with PepuSwap itself. See [PepuSwap Addresses](pepuswap.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `InvalidSigner` or signature rejected | Signed against the wrong domain (PepuSwap's Permit2, or wrong chain id) | Use `permit2Domain()`; confirm the verifying contract |
| `InvalidNonce` | Reused or stale nonce | Read `allowance` (AllowanceTransfer) or `nonceBitmap` (SignatureTransfer) |
| Transfer reverts after a valid permit | The token was never approved to Permit2 | Send the one-time ERC-20 `approve` |
| `SignatureExpired` | `sigDeadline` or `deadline` passed | Re-sign with a later deadline |

- [PepuSwap Addresses](pepuswap.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/contracts/entrypoints-and-kernel

# EntryPoints and Kernel

The ERC-4337 contracts on PEPU mainnet: EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7, the ZeroDev Kernel v3.1 account stack (factory, meta-factory, implementation, ECDSA validator and signer) and the session-key policies, with the ABIs the SDK ships. Read it to know which address does what and which versions to pin.

These contracts were deployed by ZeroDev's one-click Conduit Marketplace integration; mainnet only. `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` re-checks every address with `eth_getCode`. See [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## EntryPoints

| Version | Address | Bytes | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | 16035 | Kernel v3.x, the PEPU paymaster, Privy's smart-wallet integration. Use this one |
| v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | 23689 | Deployed and served by the bundler; nothing in the dev kit targets it |

Both are at the canonical addresses. The paymaster, the bundler and the policy service all use v0.7. The SDK ships `entryPointV07Abi` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk`); the paymaster deposit is read through it (`getPaymasterDeposit` in `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`).

## Kernel account stack

| Component | Address | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel v3 factory | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` | Creates accounts; `getAddress(...)` returns the counterfactual address, so never re-implement the CREATE2 hash |
| Kernel MetaFactory | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` | Factory of factories |
| Kernel v3.1 implementation | `0xbAC849bB641841b44E965fb01A4Bf5F074F84B4d` | What the factory's `implementation()` resolves to; accounts are proxies to it |
| Kernel ECDSA validator | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` | Default root validator: one ECDSA key (for example a Privy embedded wallet) authorises the account |
| Kernel ECDSA signer module | `0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF` | Signer used inside permission-validator session keys |

The SDK pins Kernel v3.1 (`KERNEL_VERSION` in `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel`). Accounts are deployed on the user's first UserOperation (the operation carries `factory` and `factoryData`), which is why a first transaction costs about 12 PEPU worst case against about 3 PEPU afterwards.

## Session-key policies

| Policy | Address | What it enforces |
|---|---|---|
| Call policy **v0.0.4** | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` | Only the listed targets and selectors, with a native value no larger than the limit (default 0) |
| Timestamp policy | `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` | The permission is invalid outside `validAfter` to `validUntil` |

**Why v0.0.4, not v0.0.5.** ZeroDev's call policy v0.0.5 is not deployed on PEPU. The SDK pins `CallPolicyVersion.V0_0_4` and exports the address as `CALL_POLICY_V0_0_4_ADDRESS` (and `TIMESTAMP_POLICY_ADDRESS`) from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel`. An out-of-scope UserOperation is rejected by the EntryPoint itself, whoever relays it. Do not configure a newer policy version or a client default that selects v0.0.5; it will point at an address with no code. See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md).

## ABIs in the SDK

| Export | Covers |
|---|---|
| `entryPointV07Abi` | EntryPoint v0.7 |
| `kernelFactoryAbi`, `kernelEcdsaValidatorAbi` | Kernel factory and validator. `KERNEL_V3_1_IMPLEMENTATION_ADDRESS` and `ERC7579_MODULE_TYPE` are exported alongside |
| `multicall3Abi`, `permit2Abi` | The two infrastructure contracts, [Multicall3](multicall3.md) and [Permit2](permit2.md) |
| `pepuSponsoredPaymasterV2Abi` (from `/paymaster`) | The v2 paymaster |

Registry access: `getContract(97741, "entryPoint07")`, `getContract(97741, "kernelFactory")` and so on; `isDeployed` narrows the type so an undeployed entry can never be read as an address. Names: `entryPoint06`, `entryPoint07`, `kernelFactory`, `kernelMetaFactory`, `kernelImplementation`, `ecdsaValidator`, `kernelEcdsaSignerModule`, `kernelCallPolicyV004`, `kernelTimestampPolicy`.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Session key setup reverts or the policy has no code | A client defaulted to call policy v0.0.5 | Pin v0.0.4 |
| Counterfactual address differs from the deployed one | Different Kernel version, validator or index | Use the factory's `getAddress` with the SDK's pinned version |
| Operation rejected during account creation | Wrong factory or init data | Build the account with `toPepuKernelAccount` / `getKernelAddress` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel` |
| Bundler says EntryPoint unsupported | Sent v0.6 | Use v0.7 |

## Related

- [Address Map](address-map.md)
- [/aa](../sdk/aa.md), [/session/kernel](../sdk/session-kernel.md)
- [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md)
- [Bundler Overview](../infra/bundler/overview.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/contracts/create2-and-deterministic-deployment

# CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment

How PEPU used its deterministic deployer to put Multicall3 and Permit2 on chain, what salt and init code each used, and how to reproduce the addresses. Read it to deploy your own contract at a predictable address or to verify these deployments.

## The deployer

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` |
| What it is | The standard "Nick's method" deterministic deployer, at the same address as on every chain that has it |
| Registry key | `create2Factory` |
| Calling convention | Send a transaction **to** the deployer whose data is `salt (32 bytes) ‖ initCode`. It runs `CREATE2` and the new contract's address is not returned (compute it) |
| Address formula | `address = last 20 bytes of keccak256(0xff ‖ deployer ‖ salt ‖ keccak256(initCode))` |

Anything deployed through it with the same salt and init code lands at the same address on any chain that has the deployer. The Alto bundler also uses it to deploy its own simulation contracts.

## What was deployed this way

| Contract | Salt | Init code | Address | Transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multicall3 (PEPU-specific) | all zeros | `contracts/multicall3/initcode.hex`, from `mds1/multicall3` source, solc 0.8.12, optimizer 10,000,000 runs | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` (`contracts/multicall3/predicted.txt`) | `0xf9d8f45010e2a2020871af9a677d134e9b43e039a0a73c09bcd22d1825f99241`, block 10521048 |
| Permit2 (canonical) | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000d3af2663da51c10215000000` (`contracts/permit2/salt.txt`) | `contracts/permit2/initcode.hex`, the exact upstream creation bytecode | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` (`contracts/permit2/predicted.txt`) | `0xbb0a23420f47dd4dbb524d96f46115011a66fc88bbdf0963cd24a50feb6f7c93`, block 10521367 |

Permit2 reproduces its **canonical** address because that address was itself produced by CREATE2 with Uniswap's salt. Multicall3's canonical address was not produced by CREATE2 (it came from a plain `CREATE` by a burn key through a pre-signed 1,000,000-gas transaction), so no salt can reproduce it, and that transaction cannot run on this chain. PEPU's Multicall3 is therefore at a different, but reproducible, address. See [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md).

## Reproduce an address

With upstream Foundry (not `foundry-zksync`, which can shadow `forge` and `cast` on `PATH`; check `forge --version`):

```bash
cast create2 \
  --deployer 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C \
  --salt 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000d3af2663da51c10215000000 \
  --init-code "$(cat contracts/permit2/initcode.hex)"
# expect 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3
```

By hand: `keccak256(0xff ++ deployer ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode))`, take the last 40 hex characters. `contracts/permit2/prove-address.sh` does both and prints `RESULT: MATCH`.

Check on chain, read-only:

```bash
cast code 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz
```

## Deploy your own contract deterministically

1. Compile and keep the creation bytecode (`initcode`).
2. Pick a salt and compute the predicted address as above.
3. Check the predicted address has no code.
4. Send a transaction to `0x4e59…956C` with data `salt ‖ initCode`. Set an explicit gas limit: Arbitrum Nitro charges differently from L1, and a bytecode that fits in 1,000,000 gas elsewhere can need far more here (Multicall3 needed about 14.3 million for the plain-`CREATE` route; the CREATE2 deploy used 874,693).
5. Re-check `eth_getCode` at the predicted address.

## Scripts

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `deploy/deploy-multicall3.sh` | Deploys Multicall3. Idempotent: exits if code already exists at the predicted address |
| `deploy/verify-multicall3.sh` | Verification checks |
| `contracts/permit2/deploy-permit2.sh` | Rebuilds, compares the creation bytecode to `initcode.hex`, refuses to broadcast on drift, deploys |
| `contracts/permit2/prove-address.sh` | Independent address computation, read-only |
| `contracts/permit2/compute-domain-separator.sh`, `estimate-gas.sh` | Domain and gas checks |
| `deploy/deploy-tapscore.sh`, `deploy/fund-paymaster.sh`, `deploy/allow-bundler.sh` | TapScore deploy and paymaster operations (not CREATE2) |

These read private keys and the RPC key from gitignored env files. Do not paste keys anywhere.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Computed address does not match | Different init code (compiler version, optimizer runs, constructor args or line endings) | Reproduce the exact build settings; `forge build --force` and compare to `initcode.hex` |
| Deployment transaction succeeds but no code at the address | Wrong salt or init code, or the call reverted inside the deployer (it returns no data) | Recompute; raise the gas limit |
| Out of gas on a plain `CREATE` replay | Nitro needs far more gas than the replayed transaction allows | Use CREATE2 through the deployer instead |
| `forge` behaves oddly | `foundry-zksync` first on `PATH` | Use upstream Foundry |

## Related

- [Address Map](address-map.md)
- [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md)
- [Permit2](permit2.md)
- [Deploy and Verify a Contract](deployment.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/contracts/pepuswap

# PepuSwap Addresses

PepuSwap is PEPU's main DEX, operated by a third party (0sum.io): a white-labelled Uniswap V3 fork. Several of its contracts sit at non-canonical addresses, and two of them (a multicall and a Permit2) are easy to mistake for general infrastructure. This page lists them and the do-not-substitute rules.

Addresses are in the SDK's PepuSwap registry (`getPepuSwapContract`, `listPepuSwapContracts`). These are third-party contracts: PEPU does not operate them and they are outside this repository's security policy. `live-check` covers `pepuContracts` only, so confirm a contract with `pepu_check_contract_deployed` before relying on it. Mainnet only.

## Address table

| Registry key | Name | Address | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v3Factory` | UniswapV3Factory | `0x5984B8BF2d4dB9C0aCB1d7924762e4474D80C807` | Source verified on pepuscan; other PepuSwap contracts' `factory()` return it |
| `swapRouter02` | SwapRouter02 | `0x150c3F0f16C3D9EB34351d7af9c961FeDc97A0fb` | `factory()` and `WETH9()` resolve to the factory and WPEPU |
| `universalRouter` | UniversalRouter | `0x0dE72b751b77d3c74fB96C5fAd0320Cd8d133d36` | No public getters |
| `positionManager` | NonfungiblePositionManager | `0xe2060CbdE18b5e765c86e5Cd6EE68AF209a9faa7` | LP NFTs list as "Launchpad V3 Positions NFT" / UNI-V3-POS |
| `quoterV2` | QuoterV2 | `0xd647b2D80b48e93613Aa6982b85f8909578b4829` | Quote with `eth_call` or `simulateContract` only; never send a real transaction |
| `tickLens` | TickLens | `0x4EB8aA84c066f9bf210eAfE33B30AE49BfafD9a6` | Stateless |
| `v3Migrator` | V3Migrator | `0xFE406d6c3fc0BB3a6D195b089eFADfc8658206D5` | No dedicated ABI in the SDK |
| `v3Staker` | V3Staker | `0x0a875d1C72cb4e1CD61401c3C49f85Df45071f83` | Uniswap LP incentive staking, unrelated to "stake PEPU". No dedicated ABI in the SDK |
| `multicallNonCanonical` | UniswapInterfaceMulticall | `0x927af2a6B76d2d8206d93004463F8C122701383B` | **Not Multicall3** |
| `permit2NonCanonical` | PepuSwap Permit2 | `0xB461c05f76d7f919FF7A3Df2B0D2593F56538b4B` | **Not the canonical Permit2** |

Tokens it trades (also in `@pepu-chain/sdk` tokens): WPEPU `0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8` (18 decimals), USDT `0x06f69A40C33C5A4Cd038BBE1DA689D4D636Ec448` (6 decimals), USDC `0x20fB684Bfc1aBAaD3AceC5712f2Aa30bd494dF74` (6), WETH `0x7CCC51754216C04D4Bb1210630cCA16e5430Aa70` (18). Get PepuSwap's token list from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0sum-io/tokens/refs/heads/main/pepu-mainnet2.json` rather than hardcoding more.

## Do-not-substitute table

| If you want | Use | Never use |
|---|---|---|
| Batched reads (Multicall3 `aggregate3`) | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` ([Multicall3](multicall3.md)) | PepuSwap's `0x927a…383B` (a Multicall2-style contract with a different function set), and not `0xcA11…CA11`, which has no code |
| Permit2 for your own contracts and libraries | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` ([Permit2](permit2.md)) | PepuSwap's `0xB461…8b4B` |
| Integrating with PepuSwap's UI or routers | PepuSwap's own addresses above | The canonical Permit2 (its frontend overrides `PERMIT2_ADDRESS` for chain 97741) |

The two Permit2 deployments respond to `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` with different values, so signatures are not interchangeable. The SDK ships separate ABIs (`pepuSwapMulticallAbi`, `pepuSwapPermit2Abi`) so the confusion is visible in types.

## Using the registry

```ts
import { getPepuSwapContract, listPepuSwapContracts } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const router = getPepuSwapContract(97741, "swapRouter02");
const all = listPepuSwapContracts(97741);
```

Other PepuSwap ABIs shipped: router, quoter, position manager, V3 factory, V3 pool, tick lens and universal router.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Batched calls to `0x927a…` revert or return the wrong shape | It is not Multicall3 | Use PEPU's Multicall3 |
| Permit2 signature rejected by PepuSwap | Signed for the canonical domain | Sign against PepuSwap's Permit2 domain |
| Quoter call spends gas | Sent as a transaction | Use `eth_call` or `simulateContract` |

## Related

- [Address Map](address-map.md)
- [Deployed Contracts Reference](deployed-contracts.md)
- [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md)
- [Permit2](permit2.md)

# Deploy & Verify a Contract

This page takes you from nothing to a deployed, verified contract on Pepe Unchained V2 **mainnet**. Foundry is the primary path below; a complete Hardhat path follows it for anyone who prefers that toolchain. Each path is complete on its own; pick one.

If you haven't already, skim [V1 vs V2](../get-started/v1-vs-v2.md) first: the chain ID and RPC URL below are for the current chain (V2). An older, dead chain shares the project name and gets confused with this one constantly.

**Looking for the fastest path to a running app instead of a bare contract?** See [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](../get-started/quickstart-app.md) — it scaffolds a Next.js app with sign-in and a wallet, no Solidity required. This page is for when you specifically want to write and deploy a contract.

## Why mainnet, not testnet

Testnet (chain `97740`) has no public faucet, no indexed explorer, and none of the infrastructure on this page deployed to it — see [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md#testnet-out-of-scope-today). It is out of scope for development today. Mainnet is the actual "try it" chain: a deployment costs a fraction of a cent, so use a dedicated development key with minimal funds and deploy there directly. Everything below targets mainnet only.

## What you'll need

- A wallet with a private key you control (use a dedicated development key with minimal funds — never a key holding meaningful value).
- Either [Foundry](https://getfoundry.sh) or Node.js 18+ with a package manager, depending on which path you follow.
- A small amount of PEPU to pay gas (see "Get funds" below).

## Network parameters

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Chain ID | `97741` |
| RPC URL | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Currency | PEPU (18 decimals) |
| Explorer | `https://pepuscan.com` |

Full parameters, an "Add to Wallet" JSON snippet, and the complete deployed-contracts reference are on [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md).

## Get funds

Buy PEPU on an exchange, or bridge existing PEPU from Ethereum L1 via [pepubridge.com](https://pepubridge.com). Gas on this chain is a fraction of a cent per transaction (see the gas note on [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md)), so a very small amount funds a long testing session.

## The contract

Both paths below deploy the same minimal contract. Save it as `src/Counter.sol` (Foundry) or `contracts/Counter.sol` (Hardhat):

```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.24;

contract Counter {
    uint256 public count;

    function increment() external {
        count += 1;
    }
}
```

---

## Path 1: Foundry (primary)

### Install and confirm your toolchain

```bash
curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash
foundryup
```

This guide targets upstream Foundry `v1.5.1-stable`.

> **Check which `forge` you're running before you go further.** If [`foundry-zksync`](https://github.com/matter-labs/foundry-zksync) is installed on the same machine, the `forge` binary on your `PATH` may resolve to the zkSync fork instead of upstream Foundry. The zkSync fork compiles and deploys differently and is the wrong tool for an Arbitrum Orbit chain like this one. Run:
>
> ```bash
> forge --version
> ```
>
> The zkSync fork announces itself in the version string (it will mention `zksync`). If you see that, reinstall or switch to upstream Foundry via `foundryup` before continuing.

Confirm the RPC is reachable and returns the chain ID you expect:

```bash
cast chain-id --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz
# 97741
```

### Set up the project

```bash
forge init pepu-quickstart
cd pepu-quickstart
```

`forge init` scaffolds its own default `src/Counter.sol`. Replace it with the contract from [above](#the-contract) so the rest of this walkthrough matches exactly.

Add an RPC alias to `foundry.toml`:

```toml
[profile.default]
src = "src"
out = "out"
libs = ["lib"]

[rpc_endpoints]
pepu_mainnet = "https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz"
```

### Build

```bash
forge build
```

### Deploy

Set your development private key as an environment variable (never commit it):

```bash
export PRIVATE_KEY=0xyourdevelopmentprivatekey
```

```bash
forge create src/Counter.sol:Counter \
  --rpc-url pepu_mainnet \
  --private-key $PRIVATE_KEY \
  --broadcast
```

Foundry estimates gas automatically — you don't need to override gas price to work around PEPU's ~12,500 gwei-equivalent base fee; that's a real, expected value, not something to fight (see [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md)). Note the deployed contract address `forge create` prints — you'll need it to verify.

### Verify

Verify against pepuscan directly, using Foundry's Blockscout verifier:

```bash
forge verify-contract \
  --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz \
  --verifier blockscout \
  --verifier-url https://pepuscan.com/api \
  <DEPLOYED_ADDRESS> \
  src/Counter.sol:Counter
```

This is Blockscout's own documented Foundry verification pattern (`--verifier blockscout` pointed at a self-hosted instance's `/api` path). It works against pepuscan. Most self-hosted Blockscout instances, pepuscan included, don't require an API key for this.

Don't just trust the CLI's exit code — confirm the verification actually landed:

```bash
curl -s "https://pepuscan.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/<DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>" | grep -o '"is_verified":[a-z]*'
```

If you have the `pepu` MCP server connected, `pepu_verify_contract_status` does this same check and also distinguishes "unverified contract" from "not a contract at all" — see [Agent Tooling](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md).

Conduit's Sourcify-compatible service (`--verifier sourcify --verifier-url https://contracts.conduit.xyz`) is a documented fallback if the Blockscout route doesn't pick up the verification for some reason — but Blockscout against pepuscan is the confirmed, primary path.

### View it

Open `https://pepuscan.com/address/<DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>`. You should see the contract, its verified source, and a "Read/Write Contract" tab once pepuscan.com picks up the verification.

---

## Path 2: Hardhat (alternative)

Foundry is primary for PEPU work, but Hardhat is a fully documented alternative — use it if the project already standardized on Hardhat, or if Foundry genuinely isn't available on the machine.

### Install

```bash
mkdir pepu-quickstart && cd pepu-quickstart
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev hardhat @nomicfoundation/hardhat-toolbox dotenv
npx hardhat init
```

Choose "Create a TypeScript project" (or JavaScript, adjusting file extensions below) when prompted.

### Configure

Create a `.env` file:

```
DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY=0xyourdevelopmentprivatekey
```

Replace `hardhat.config.ts` with:

```ts
import type { HardhatUserConfig } from "hardhat/config";
import "@nomicfoundation/hardhat-toolbox";
import "dotenv/config";

const DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY = process.env.DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY;

const config: HardhatUserConfig = {
  solidity: "0.8.24",
  networks: {
    pepuMainnet: {
      url: "https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz",
      chainId: 97741,
      accounts: DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY ? [DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY] : [],
    },
  },
  sourcify: {
    enabled: true,
    apiUrl: "https://contracts.conduit.xyz",
    browserUrl: "https://pepuscan.com",
  },
};

export default config;
```

The `sourcify` block is the fastest way to get one-command verification working on Hardhat 2 + `hardhat-toolbox` today (it runs against Conduit's Sourcify-compatible service). If your project has moved to **Hardhat 3**, its newer `@nomicfoundation/hardhat-verify` plugin has first-class Blockscout support instead — configure a `verify.blockscout` block and run `npx hardhat verify blockscout --network pepuMainnet <address>` for the same pepuscan-verified result the Foundry path above gets directly. Either produces a verified contract on pepuscan; they're two different plugins' paths to it, not competing sources of truth.

### Write the contract and compile

Save the contract from [above](#the-contract) as `contracts/Counter.sol`, then:

```bash
npx hardhat compile
```

### Deploy

Create `scripts/deploy.ts`:

```ts
import { ethers } from "hardhat";

async function main() {
  const Counter = await ethers.getContractFactory("Counter");
  const counter = await Counter.deploy();
  await counter.waitForDeployment();
  console.log("Counter deployed to:", await counter.getAddress());
}

main().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
```

```bash
npx hardhat run scripts/deploy.ts --network pepuMainnet
```

### Verify

With the `sourcify` block above in place, Hardhat's standard verify command runs against Conduit's Sourcify-compatible service:

```bash
npx hardhat verify --network pepuMainnet <DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>
```

### View it

Same as the Foundry path: `https://pepuscan.com/address/<DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>`.

- [Social Login & Embedded Wallets (Privy)](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) — wiring up user-facing wallets instead of a raw private key.

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/contracts/paymaster-v2-spec

# Paymaster v2 Spec Summary

A readable summary of the tiered gas-sponsorship specification (`services/paymaster/SPONSORSHIP-SPEC.md`): model, invariants, security considerations and design decisions. The full spec is the source of truth; this page is the map. Read it to understand what v2 guarantees and where its limits are.

Deployed at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`. The numbers below are the spec's design numbers; the live per-user free allowance is 100 PEPU per day and 50 PEPU per hour, enforced by the policy service. The v1 paymaster is retired.

## Model

| Tier | Funded by | Who draws | Bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free tier | The chain: a free pool anyone can fund | **Verified Privy users only** | 100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per hour (service). Spec design numbers: 50 PEPU per day, 40 PEPU max per operation. On-chain per-wallet backstop, the pool balance. **No chain-wide ceiling** |
| Project tier | A project, funded by anyone depositing on chain | **Any wallet** the project sponsors | Project balance, daily limit, per-wallet limit, destination allowlist, gas-price cap |

Per operation, atomically and never split: the project pays if it can; otherwise the free tier, only for a verified Privy account with allowance; otherwise denied. The free tier never pays for non-Privy wallets, even when a project is empty.

One contract is both paymaster and vault. All PEPU sits in its EntryPoint deposit and an internal ledger records each sponsor's share (`sponsorId` 0 is the free pool; otherwise `keccak256(bytes(appId))`). Validation deducts the full `maxCost` from the sponsor; `postOp` refunds `maxCost - charge` to that same sponsor.

## Decisions

| | Decision |
|---|---|
| Deposits | **One-way.** Anyone deposits into any project (claimed or not) or the free pool; **nothing can withdraw**, not project owners, the contract owner or the manager. The only outflow is gas settlement |
| Project identity | `projectId = keccak256(bytes(appId))`: one canonical project per Privy app, case-sensitive |
| Ownership | Privy-verified. The policy service checks the Privy app secret, issues an EIP-712 attestation, the developer calls `claimProject`. **The claim sets only the owner**; the owner then calls `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit` (all three are required: a project with no per-wallet limit is rejected on chain). An **empty** project is claimed immediately; a project that **already holds funds** is pending for the admin delay (cancellable by the contract owner or manager) |
| Re-claim | Of an owned project: timelocked at least 48 hours, announced on chain, cancellable by the current owner **once per new owner** (a second attested re-claim by the same new owner is final), void if the attesting signer was removed, lapses 30 days after it becomes executable |
| Exit | **Pausing is the exit**, instant. Funds cannot leave |
| Contract owner | The deployer by default; `Ownable2Step`, renounce supported. Nothing a project needs depends on the owner |
| Free tier numbers | 50 PEPU per user per day, 40 PEPU per operation |
| Surplus | Unused prepay returns to the exact sponsor that was charged; unattributable residue (and donations) can only go to the free pool, never to the owner |
| Governance | Signer and bundler **additions** wait an immutable `adminChangeDelay` (at least 48 hours, at most 30 days); removals instant; manager separate from owner |
| Gas-price cap | On-chain per-sponsor cap on `maxFeePerGas` (deploy default 40,000 gwei; a sponsor can only tighten it) plus service bounds |
| Bundler gate | Unconditional on-chain `tx.origin` allowlist; mode byte must be exactly `0x02` |
| Credentials | Server key `ppk_` (secret, any wallet) or client token `ppt_` (publishable, origin-bound) |
| Stranded funds | Accepted: an abandoned project's money stays locked, no escape hatch |

## Differences from v1

| | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| Caps | Off-chain only | Off-chain plus on-chain allowlist, limits and fee cap per sponsor |
| Accounting | One shared deposit | Per-sponsor ledger, actual-cost settlement and refunds |
| Who funds | One operator | Anyone, per project, plus a free pool |
| Onboarding | Manual registration | Self-serve claim |
| Mode byte | `0x00` | `0x02` only (sponsor id in the signed data) |
| Bundler gate | None | Required allowlisted bundler |

## Invariants

- Ledgers sum to `totalLiabilities`, and `totalLiabilities` is at most the EntryPoint deposit; balances never underflow.
- **No function of any role moves ledger funds out of the EntryPoint deposit**; the contract never calls `entryPoint.withdrawTo` (a test scans the bytecode). Only stake, a separate balance, can be withdrawn by the owner.
- The deposit plus gas paid to the beneficiary equals everything ever deposited, over random sequences of claims, deposits, donations, pauses, stake moves and operations.
- On the real EntryPoint v0.7 sources, the ledger charge is at least the EntryPoint's true debit for every operation, including the worst-case slot-restoring attack at the overhead floor (post-op overhead floor 18,000 gas, deployed 20,000; measured worst case 13,918 gas with cold state, after the overhead is snapshotted at validation).
- Day counters track charges exactly; one sponsor's operation never moves another sponsor's ledger.

## Security considerations

- The policy signer is the **ownership gatekeeper** for projects as well as the sponsorship signer (one shared signer set). A compromised signer can claim an **empty unclaimed** project immediately, claim a funded one after the admin delay unless the contract owner or manager cancels it (or the signer is removed), or start a re-claim of an owned one, but can never withdraw funds. Its spending is bounded on chain: only claimed sponsors, only allowlisted targets, only within the daily and per-wallet limits, only paid to an allowlisted bundler, at no more than the fee cap. The free pool's worst case is its balance, because a signer can invent wallets.
- A hot manager cannot quickly add itself as signer and bundler: additions are timelocked, so projects that watch `AdminChangeProposed` can pause first.
- Re-claims and the first claim of a funded project are visible, timelocked, cancellable and die with a removed signer; credentials follow the on-chain owner and are revoked on change. The owner can veto a re-claim once per new owner, so a hostile owner cannot block recovery forever.
- The `tx.origin` gate means v2 works only behind a bundler with safe mode off and an allowlisted executor, which is how the hosted PEPU bundler runs; a conformant public-mempool bundler rejects it.
- Design limitations:
  - Free-tier sybil: N Privy accounts get N times the per-user free allowance a day, bounded by the pool balance.
  - A many-address attacker can hold up to 25% of a client token's reservation pool.
  - The contract is immutable and holds third-party deposits that cannot be withdrawn.
  - Destination decoding supports Kernel accounts only.
  - Runtime size is 23,722 of 24,576 bytes, built with 8,000 optimizer runs.

## Full detail

- Full spec: `services/paymaster/SPONSORSHIP-SPEC.md` (sections: model, architecture, contract, accounting, free tier, sybil resistance, invariants, claims, API, threat model T1 to T22, migration, decisions D1 to D22 and open questions).
- Contract reference: [PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract](../infra/paymaster/contracts.md).
- API: [REST API v2](../infra/paymaster/rest-api-v2.md). Procedure: [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md).
- User-facing model: [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md).

## Related

- [Security Reviews](audits.md)
- [Paymaster Overview](../infra/paymaster/overview.md)
- [Address Map](address-map.md)

# Security Reviews

How each PEPU contract was reviewed, which contracts are upstream code, and how to report a vulnerability.

## Contracts

| Contract | Address | Provenance | Reviews and tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paymaster v2 `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` | Authored by PEPU. Source in `services/paymaster/contracts` | Three internal reviews (below). 195 Foundry tests (unit, fuzz, six invariants, a harness on the real EntryPoint v0.7 sources, reentrancy and cross-language vectors) and 328 policy-service tests |
| Paymaster v1 `PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7` | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` | Authored by PEPU; a fork of Pimlico's singleton paymaster with ERC-20 mode removed. Retired: its EntryPoint deposit was withdrawn and it cannot sponsor anything | 18 Foundry tests |
| Multicall3 | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | Built from canonical `mds1/multicall3` source with canonical settings; source verified on pepuscan | Upstream code, no PEPU changes |
| Permit2 | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` | Exact upstream creation bytecode, deployed at the canonical address | Upstream code, no PEPU changes |
| EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7, Kernel v3.1, validator, signer, call and timestamp policies | See [Address Map](address-map.md) | ZeroDev deployments through Conduit Marketplace | ZeroDev's own audits apply to the upstream code. Call policy v0.0.4 is used because v0.0.5 is not deployed on PEPU |
| TapScore | `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` | Demo contract used by the templates | For demonstration only; do not use it to hold value |
| CREATE2 deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | Standard deterministic deployer | Widely used upstream |

"Source verified" means the source is published on pepuscan or reproducible from the repository. `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` confirms that bytecode exists at each registry address.

## Internal reviews of the v2 paymaster

The review reports are in `services/paymaster/audits/`. Each file begins with a table of findings and their resolution.

| Report | Scope |
|---|---|
| `2026-10-internal-review.md` | Commit `dafc259`: the contract, its EntryPoint interaction, the deploy script and the signing service. Includes a harness built on the real EntryPoint v0.7 sources. |
| `2026-10-delta-review.md` | The deposit-only and attested-claim changes (`f55527f..c354508`). |
| `2026-10-review-3.md` | Commit `4882bd3`, reviewed along three axes: economics and accounting; access control and governance; ERC-4337 conformance and the signer service. All on the real EntryPoint v0.7. |

The reviews follow the [pashov](https://github.com/pashov/skills) `solidity-auditor` methodology. They are internal and do not replace an independent audit.

## Design notes

- The v2 contract is immutable and holds project deposits. Deposits are one-way and cannot be withdrawn, so deposit only what your project needs.
- The `tx.origin` bundler gate in v2 requires a self-run bundler with safe mode off. The hosted bundler is configured accordingly.
- The contract size margin is 854 bytes at 8,000 optimizer runs. Any change to the contract needs a size re-check.
- The harness uses vendored EntryPoint sources on a local EVM. The 18,000-gas post-op floor is a design value, not a measurement from the PEPU chain's gas schedule.

## Report a vulnerability

Do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. Follow [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md): email contact@pepeunchained.com with a description, reproduction steps, the affected package or file and whether it touches deployed contracts. The policy covers this repository's code (the paymaster contracts and services live here too; if in doubt, send it). It does not cover the chain, Conduit, pepuscan or third-party contracts such as Kernel.

# Recipe: Read a Contract

Call a read-only (`view` or `pure`) function on a deployed contract with the SDK's public client, in a script or a React app.

TapScore (`0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`) is the sample contract.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk` and `viem`. For the React variant, a wagmi config built on `pepuMainnet`.

## Steps

`getPublicClient(pepuMainnet)` returns an ordinary viem `PublicClient` on PEPU's RPC. Everything after it is plain viem. Take well-known addresses from the SDK registry (`getContract`, narrowed with `isDeployed`) instead of pasting them, so a pending contract cannot be read by accident.

```ts
// Read a contract with the SDK's public client. See docs/recipes/read-a-contract.md
import { getContract, getPublicClient, isDeployed, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { parseAbi } from "viem";

const client = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

// TapScore is in the SDK registry; getContract returns a pending-or-deployed union.
const tapScore = getContract(pepuMainnet.id, "tapScore");
if (!isDeployed(tapScore)) throw new Error("TapScore is not deployed on this chain");
const tapScoreAddress = tapScore.address;

const abi = parseAbi(["function scores(address) view returns (uint256)"]);

export async function readScore(player: `0x${string}`): Promise<bigint> {
  return client.readContract({
    address: tapScoreAddress,
    abi,
    functionName: "scores",
    args: [player],
  });
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/read-contract.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

### In a React app (wagmi)

```tsx
import { useReadContract } from "wagmi";
import { parseAbi } from "viem";
import { pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const abi = parseAbi(["function scores(address) view returns (uint256)"]);

function Score({ address }: { address: `0x${string}` }) {
  const { data: score, isLoading } = useReadContract({
    chainId: pepuMainnet.id,
    address: "0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078",
    abi,
    functionName: "scores",
    args: [address],
  });

  if (isLoading) return <p>Loading</p>;
  return <p>Score: {score?.toString()}</p>;
}
```

This needs a `WagmiProvider` configured with a PEPU chain. `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` from [/privy/wagmi](../sdk/privy-wagmi.md) does it.

### Don't know the ABI

`createPepuscanClient(pepuMainnet).getVerifiedAbi(address)` returns a verified contract's ABI from pepuscan, or `null` if it is unverified. The MCP tool `pepu_verify_contract_status` does the same from an agent.

## What to expect

- The result is typed from the ABI. A `uint256` is a `bigint`.
- Reads cost no gas and need no wallet.
- The public RPC is rate limited. For volume pass an authenticated transport: `getPublicClient(pepuMainnet, { transport: http(url) })`.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Property 'address' does not exist on type 'ContractEntry'` | Skipped `isDeployed` | Narrow first, then read `.address` |
| `returned no data ("0x")` | Wrong address, or the contract is not deployed on chain 97741 | Check the address with `pepu_check_contract_deployed` or the explorer |
| Many sequential reads are slow | One request per call | Batch them: [Batch Reads with Multicall3](batch-reads-with-multicall3.md) |

## Related

- [Batch Reads with Multicall3](batch-reads-with-multicall3.md)
- [Core](../sdk/core.md)
- [MCP Server and Skills (overview)](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/send-a-transaction

# Recipe: Send a Transaction

Send native PEPU from a key you control (scripts, backend jobs), or from a Privy embedded wallet in a React app (the flow a real user goes through).

These transactions cost real gas in PEPU paid by the sender. For gas the user does not pay, see [Send a Sponsored Transaction](sponsored-send.md).

A base fee around 12,500 gwei is normal on this chain, not an error. `formatPepu` and `estimateTransactionCost` show costs in a readable form.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk` and `viem`. A funded sender. For React, [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md).

## From a private key (scripts, backend)

Estimate first, check the balance covers amount plus gas with `maxSendableAmount`, send, wait, then link the result.

```ts
// Estimate, send and link a native PEPU transfer from a script.
// See docs/recipes/send-a-transaction.md
import {
  estimateTransactionCost,
  formatPepu,
  getPublicClient,
  maxSendableAmount,
  pepuMainnet,
  txUrl,
} from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { createWalletClient, http, parseEther } from "viem";
import type { Hex } from "viem";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

// SCRIPT ONLY. Never ship a private key in a browser bundle.
const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env["DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY"] as Hex);
const walletClient = createWalletClient({ account, chain: pepuMainnet, transport: http() });

export async function sendPepu(to: `0x${string}`, amountPepu: string): Promise<string> {
  const value = parseEther(amountPepu);

  const estimate = await estimateTransactionCost(publicClient, { account: account.address, to, value });
  console.log(`Estimated cost: ${estimate.costFormatted}`);

  const balanceWei = await publicClient.getBalance({ address: account.address });
  const max = await maxSendableAmount({ client: publicClient, from: account.address, to, balanceWei });
  if (max.status !== "ok") throw new Error(max.reason);
  if (value > max.amountWei) throw new Error("Amount leaves too little PEPU for gas");

  const hash = await walletClient.sendTransaction({ to, value });
  await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });
  console.log(`Sent ${formatPepu(value)}`);
  return txUrl(pepuMainnet, hash);
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/send-transaction.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

The key comes from the environment. Never a key that holds real value in a script like this, and never in a browser bundle.

## From a Privy embedded wallet (React)

The embedded wallet is a normal wagmi connector once you use `@privy-io/wagmi`'s config, which `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` does for you.

```tsx
import { useSendTransaction, useWaitForTransactionReceipt } from "wagmi";
import { parseEther } from "viem";
import { pepuMainnet, txUrl } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { useState } from "react";

export function SendPepuForm() {
  const [to, setTo] = useState("");
  const [amount, setAmount] = useState("");
  const { sendTransaction, data: hash, isPending } = useSendTransaction();
  const { isLoading: isConfirming, isSuccess } = useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });

  return (
    <form
      onSubmit={(e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        sendTransaction({ to: to as `0x${string}`, value: parseEther(amount) });
      }}
    >
      <input value={to} onChange={(e) => setTo(e.target.value)} placeholder="0x..." />
      <input value={amount} onChange={(e) => setAmount(e.target.value)} placeholder="0.01" />
      <button type="submit" disabled={isPending || isConfirming}>
        {isPending ? "Confirm in wallet" : isConfirming ? "Confirming" : "Send PEPU"}
      </button>
      {hash && <a href={txUrl(pepuMainnet, hash)}>View on pepuscan</a>}
      {isSuccess && <p>Sent.</p>}
    </form>
  );
}
```

This is the pattern the `consumer-app` template's send form uses. Privy's confirmation modal runs its own balance check before signing and can refuse an amount `maxSendableAmount` sized correctly, which is why the template has no "Max" button.

## Calling a contract function

Use `useWriteContract` in React or `walletClient.writeContract` in a script. Take the address from the registry:

```tsx
import { useWriteContract } from "wagmi";
import { parseAbi } from "viem";

const abi = parseAbi(["function tap() external"]);

export function TapButton() {
  const { writeContract, isPending } = useWriteContract();
  return (
    <button
      disabled={isPending}
      onClick={() =>
        writeContract({ address: "0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078", abi, functionName: "tap" })
      }
    >
      Tap
    </button>
  );
}
```

## What to expect

- `receipt.status` is `"success"` or `"reverted"`. A revert still costs gas.
- The cost shown by `estimateTransactionCost` excludes the L1 data fee, which reads as 0 on PEPU today (see `explainDualFeeModel`).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Transaction stuck | A hardcoded gas price below the base fee | Let viem or the SDK estimate it. Never hardcode a low price |
| `insufficient funds for gas` | Amount plus gas exceeds the balance | Use `maxSendableAmount` to size it |
| Wrong account sends | An extension became wagmi's active account | Keep the active-wallet pin on |
| Privy modal refuses a valid amount | Its own over-conservative balance check | Send a smaller amount, or sign without Privy's modal |

## Related

- [Send a Sponsored Transaction](sponsored-send.md)
- [Grant a Session](grant-a-session.md) for repeated actions with no popup
- [Sign with Privy, Broadcast Yourself](sign-with-privy-broadcast-yourself.md)
- [Core](../sdk/core.md#gas-and-fees)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/sign-with-privy-broadcast-yourself

# Sign with Privy, Broadcast Yourself

**Recipe:** submit a transaction on a user's behalf from your backend, using a Privy session signer, on Pepe Unchained V2. Ask Privy to **sign**, then broadcast the signed transaction yourself through PEPU's RPC.

This is the supported pattern on PEPU. It is not a workaround for a bug in your code: the one-call alternative does not work on this chain.

The SDK implements the pattern as `signAndBroadcast` and `privySessionSigner`.

## Why not `eth_sendTransaction`

Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` asks Privy to construct, sign, broadcast and track the transaction in a single call. On PEPU it fails:

```
400 { "error": "Unsupported chain with id 97741", "code": "invalid_data" }
```

That is not a malformed request. Privy groups chain support into tiers, and "send transactions" (Tier 3) means Privy's own managed infrastructure handles the whole lifecycle. PEPU, an Arbitrum Orbit chain operated by Conduit, is not one of the chains that infrastructure covers. There is no self-serve way to register a custom chain for it; Privy's own docs point to contacting Privy support to request a chain.

It is also different from what already works on PEPU. Client-side signing in the embedded wallet works fine, because the browser broadcasts through the RPC you configured in your chain definition. Privy only has to produce a signature, which is chain-agnostic. The server-side send flow broadcasts through Privy's RPC, which is where the chain allowlist lives.

## The pattern

`eth_signTransaction` takes no chain parameter, so there is nothing for an allowlist to reject, and Privy's policy engine evaluates the same conditions against it (`ethereum_transaction` and `ethereum_calldata` field sources work for both methods). Your backend then broadcasts the raw signed transaction.

One consequence: Privy does not fill in missing nonce or gas fields for signing the way it can for a send on a chain it manages. Resolve them yourself first.

The SDK implements all three steps. `signAndBroadcast` resolves the pending nonce, gas (plus 20 percent) and gas price against PEPU's RPC, builds the legacy transaction, calls your `sign` callback (Privy `eth_signTransaction`), and broadcasts the result. `privySessionSigner` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/server` wraps it for a session wallet.

```ts
// Sign with Privy on the server, broadcast to PEPU yourself.
// SERVER ONLY. See docs/recipes/sign-with-privy-broadcast-yourself.md
import { getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { createPrivyServer, privyEnvVar } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server";
import { privySessionSigner } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/server";
import { signAndBroadcast } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

const privy = createPrivyServer();

// Easiest: the SDK's signer for a session wallet.
export async function tapWithSigner(walletId: string, address: `0x${string}`): Promise<`0x${string}`> {
  const signer = privySessionSigner({ privy, walletId, address });
  return signer.signAndBroadcast({ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" });
}

// Lower level: you own the sign callback.
export async function tapWithCallback(walletId: string, address: `0x${string}`): Promise<`0x${string}`> {
  const authorizationKey = privyEnvVar("authorizationKey");
  if (!authorizationKey) throw new Error("PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY is not set");

  return signAndBroadcast({
    client: getPublicClient(pepuMainnet),
    from: address,
    to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS,
    abi: tapScoreAbi,
    functionName: "tap",
    chainId: pepuMainnet.id,
    sign: (transaction) =>
      privy
        .wallets()
        .ethereum()
        .signTransaction(walletId, {
          params: { transaction },
          authorization_context: { authorization_private_keys: [authorizationKey] },
        }),
  });
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/sign-and-broadcast.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

What `signAndBroadcast` does, so you can reason about failures:

1. Resolve everything Privy will not fill in, against PEPU's own RPC: `getTransactionCount` (pending), `estimateGas` and `getGasPrice`.
2. Ask Privy to sign. The attached session policy is evaluated here.
3. Broadcast the raw signed transaction with `sendRawTransaction`.

Notes on the choices above:

- **Legacy `type: 0` with a single `gas_price`.** PEPU is an Arbitrum Nitro chain with a single-component L2 execution price, and legacy transactions are accepted everywhere without depending on EIP-1559 fee-estimation RPC methods. See [`@pepu-chain/sdk`'s gas helpers](../sdk/core.md#gas-and-fees) for the dual-fee model.
- **Do not hardcode a lower gas price.** Use `getGasPrice()`. PEPU's base fee is about 12,500 gwei and a lower value gets your transaction stuck. See [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md).
- **Hex quantities.** Privy's quantity fields take `0x`-prefixed hex strings. Convert `bigint` values with `toHex`; do not squeeze them through `Number`.
- **Optional authenticated RPC.** The public RPC is rate-limited. Pass a Conduit URL with your API key to `getPublicClient` through a custom transport if you expect volume. See [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md#authenticated-rpc).
- **Never set `sponsor: true`.** It belongs to the same managed-chain infrastructure and does nothing here. Gas is paid by the user's embedded wallet.

## The policy must target `eth_signTransaction`

The session signer's policy rule must use `method: "eth_signTransaction"`. A rule written for `eth_sendTransaction` never matches a sign request, so every call would be denied. The scope is otherwise unchanged:

```ts
{
  name: "Allow tap() on TapScore, 0 value, expires",
  method: "eth_signTransaction",
  action: "ALLOW",
  conditions: [
    { field_source: "ethereum_transaction", field: "to", operator: "eq", value: contractAddress },
    { field_source: "ethereum_calldata", field: "function_name", abi: [tapFunctionAbi], operator: "eq", value: "tap" },
    { field_source: "ethereum_transaction", field: "value", operator: "eq", value: "0x0" },
    { field_source: "system", field: "current_unix_timestamp", operator: "lte", value: String(expiresAtUnixSeconds) },
  ],
}
```

Policy and rule names must be at most 49 characters. Privy's published spec says `maxLength: 50`, but its live validator rejects names of 50 characters or more ("must be fewer than 50 characters"), so treat 49 as the limit. `buildSessionPolicy` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session` enforces it (also exported from `@pepu-chain/sdk/server`), and `signAndBroadcast` implements the sign-then-broadcast flow above. The full policy rules, the consent screen and the safety caveats are on [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md).

## What changes compared to a managed send

- **No pre-signing simulation.** On a chain it manages, Privy can simulate before signing, so an obviously reverting call is rejected before it is ever signed. Pure signing has no such step. A call that would revert is discovered when you broadcast it, as an ordinary on-chain revert. The policy still enforces contract, function, value and expiry before Privy signs; only the place a simulation failure surfaces moves.
- **You own nonce management.** Two rapid requests for the same wallet can race. Use `blockTag: "pending"` as above, and serialize requests per wallet if a user can trigger them quickly (a double tap, for example). A broadcast failure from a nonce race is a failed transaction, not evidence that the session is gone, so do not send the user back to the consent screen.
- **You own failures.** A policy denial and a broadcast error both come back as errors from your route. Surface them as failed transactions.

## Reference implementation

The `game-app` template does exactly this. Its tap route, `app/api/game/tap/route.ts`, carries the full investigation in a long comment, and `lib/tap-transaction.ts` builds the unsigned transaction with unit tests. `lib/session-policy.ts` is the only place a policy is built.

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-game --template game-app
```

(See the [Quickstart](../get-started/quickstart-app.md) for more on `create-pepu-app`.)

## Related

- [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md)
- [Privy Setup](../onboarding/privy-setup.md)
- [Send a Transaction](send-a-transaction.md): the client-side path, where the user's own browser signs and broadcasts.

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet

# Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account

Two things go wrong between "the user signed in with Google" and "the user's wallet is the account the app acts on". This recipe covers both. It is what the `consumer-app` template uses, now as SDK exports.

1. **The embedded wallet may not exist yet.** Privy's own "Creating your wallet / Please wait..." modal can hang forever for an app whose Dashboard mixes TEE execution with a stale on-device recovery setting. The fix is to create the wallet yourself, server-side.
2. **The wrong wallet can become the active account.** An installed browser extension (MetaMask, Phantom) can auto-connect and become wagmi's active account, so balance reads and sends silently go to the extension's address, not the embedded wallet the user was just shown.

The SDK ships all three pieces, ported from the `consumer-app` template: `createEnsureWalletRoute`, `WalletGate` and the active-wallet pin.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@privy-io/node` (server) and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` plus `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`. For wagmi also `@privy-io/wagmi`, `wagmi` and `@tanstack/react-query`.

## Part 1: provision the wallet server-side

### The config

Set `createOnLogin: "off"` so Privy's login modal never attempts wallet creation. `createPepuPrivyConfig` does this by default, and `PepuPrivyProvider` and `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` call it for you:

```tsx
import { createPepuPrivyConfig } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";

export const privyConfig = createPepuPrivyConfig({ loginMethods: ["email", "google", "wallet"] });
```

**The Privy Dashboard setting wins.** The `createOnLogin` value in code is very likely inert at runtime: the resolved app config takes it from the Dashboard's embedded wallet settings. Keep the code value for intent, but check the Dashboard when behavior does not match. See [Privy Setup](../onboarding/privy-setup.md#automatically-create-embedded-wallets-on-login).

### The route: `POST /api/wallet/ensure`

One line from the SDK. The route:

1. Refuses with `500` (`CONFIG_MISSING_ENV`) if `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is not set. The secret is server-only and must never be a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable.
2. Verifies the caller's Privy access token and takes the user id from it, never from the request body.
3. Returns `{ address, created: false }` if the user already has an Ethereum embedded wallet.
4. Otherwise creates one with `owner: { user_id }` and returns `{ address, created: true }`.
5. If the create fails, re-checks for a concurrent request that already created it, so a double submit never makes a second wallet.

**Custody.** The wallet is owned by the user. Your backend holds no signing authority over it. Do not add a session signer in this route.

```ts
// Pillar 1, server: provision the embedded wallet and authenticate requests.
// SERVER ONLY (reads PRIVY_APP_SECRET). See docs/sdk/privy-server.md
import { createEnsureWalletRoute, requireUser } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server";

// app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts
export const { POST } = createEnsureWalletRoute();

// Any other authenticated route handler. The user id comes only from the
// verified Privy access token, never from the request body.
export async function whoAmI(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const auth = await requireUser(request);
  if (!auth.ok) return auth.response; // ready-made JSON error with the right status
  return Response.json({ userId: auth.user.userId, address: auth.user.address });
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/ensure-wallet-route.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

### The component: `WalletGate`

`WalletGate` wraps the signed-in part of the app. For an authenticated user with no embedded wallet it calls your ensure route with a bounded timeout, refreshes the user so the wallet appears without a reload, and shows `loading`, `error` (with retry) or `stalled` (wallet exists but this session has not synced it; offers a reload) through render props. It gates on the **embedded** wallet, never on "any wallet": `useWallets()` can be non-empty for a user with no wallet in their Privy account, because an extension can be tracked without being linked.

## Part 2: pin the embedded wallet as the active account

An installed extension (MetaMask, Phantom) can become wagmi's active account, so balance reads and sends silently go to the extension's address. `useActiveWalletPin` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi` re-asserts the embedded wallet whenever the active account drifts. `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` already mounts it.

```tsx
// Provision the embedded wallet and keep it the active account.
// See docs/recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { useActiveWalletPin } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi";
import { WalletGate, useEmbeddedWallet, useEnsureWallet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react";

// Inside PepuPrivyWagmiProvider the pin is already mounted. Call this yourself only when you
// built your own provider tree.
export function Pin(): null {
  useActiveWalletPin();
  return null;
}

// The hook behind WalletGate, for custom UI.
export function Custom({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const { status, address, error, retry } = useEnsureWallet({ endpoint: "/api/wallet/ensure" });
  const { external } = useEmbeddedWallet();

  if (status === "error") return <button onClick={retry}>{error?.message}</button>;
  if (status !== "ready") return <p>{status}</p>;
  return (
    <div>
      <p>Embedded wallet {address}. External wallets tracked by Privy: {external.length}</p>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

// Or the finished component.
export const Gated = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => <WalletGate>{children}</WalletGate>;
```

Source: `docs/snippets/provision-and-pin.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

Details that matter:

- **The guard prevents a render loop.** `shouldPinEmbeddedWallet` only says yes when the active address differs from the embedded one.
- **It runs continuously, not once.** An extension can auto-connect or switch accounts well after first render.
- **No embedded wallet means no action.** A user who signed in with an external wallet keeps it.
- **Opt out deliberately** with `pinEmbeddedWallet={false}` or `useActiveWalletPin({ enabled: false })`.

Never label wagmi's `useAccount()` address "your embedded wallet" without comparing it to `useEmbeddedWallet().address`.

## What to expect

After sign-in a new user sees a short "setting up" state, then the app with `useEmbeddedWallet().address` set. Returning users skip straight through.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Privy's "Creating your wallet" modal hangs | Dashboard creation setting is on or stale, and Privy's client-side creation hangs | Keep `createOnLogin: "off"` and turn automatic creation off in the Dashboard; provision server-side |
| `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN` from the ensure route | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is for a different app | Use the secret from the same app as the app id |
| Balance or sends use the wrong address | An extension became the active account | Keep the pin on |
| `WalletGate` stays on the reload prompt | The wallet exists but this session has not synced | Reload |

## Related

- [/privy/react](../sdk/privy-react.md), [/privy/wagmi](../sdk/privy-wagmi.md), [/privy/server](../sdk/privy-server.md)
- [Privy Setup](../onboarding/privy-setup.md)
- [Social Login & Embedded Wallets (Privy)](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md)
- [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md): "Creating your wallet..." never finishes

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/batch-reads-with-multicall3

# Recipe: Batch Reads with Multicall3

Read many values in one request. PEPU has Multicall3, but not at the canonical address, so this recipe uses the SDK to pin the right one.

PEPU's Multicall3 is `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`. The canonical `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` has no code on PEPU.

Read [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md) first if you have not.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk` and `viem`.

## Steps

`pepuMulticall(client, calls, { allowFailure?, blockNumber? })` is viem's `multicall` pinned to PEPU's address. It goes through `getMulticall3`, which throws `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` rather than ever use the canonical one.

```ts
// Batch reads through PEPU's own Multicall3. See docs/recipes/batch-reads-with-multicall3.md
import { erc20Abi, getAddress } from "viem";
import { getPublicClient, pepuMainnet, pepuMulticall, pepuTokenList } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const client = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

export async function readTokens(holder: `0x${string}`) {
  const tokens = pepuTokenList.tokens.map((t) => getAddress(t.address));

  // pepuMulticall pins the Multicall3 address; the canonical one has no code on PEPU.
  const results = await pepuMulticall(
    client,
    tokens.flatMap(
      (address) =>
        [
          { address, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "symbol" },
          { address, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "balanceOf", args: [holder] },
        ] as const,
    ),
    { allowFailure: true },
  );

  return results.map((r) => (r.status === "success" ? r.result : null));
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/multicall-batch-reads.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

Plain viem works too, because `pepuMainnet.contracts.multicall3` already holds PEPU's address: `client.multicall({ contracts })` on a client from `getPublicClient(pepuMainnet)` batches correctly. Use `pepuMulticall` when you want the guard.

In React with wagmi see [Batch Reads with Multicall3 in React](multicall-in-react.md).

### Calling `aggregate3` yourself

For per-call failure control, `encodeAggregate3(calls)` and `decodeAggregate3Result(data)` wrap the `aggregate3` ABI. The contract is a normal Multicall3 deployment; only the address differs from other chains.

### Without the SDK

Set `contracts.multicall3` explicitly in your chain definition, with `address: "0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd"` and `blockCreated: 10521048`. Never substitute the canonical address.

## What to expect

- One RPC round trip for all calls. Results are in order, each with a `status`.
- With `allowFailure: false` a failing call rejects the whole batch.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every batched call fails | Routed through the canonical address | Use `pepuMainnet` or `pepuMulticall` |
| `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` | The canonical address reached `getMulticall3` | Use the registry entry, never a literal |
| `UNKNOWN` "Multicall3 is not deployed" | A non-mainnet chain ID | Use chain 97741 |

## Related

- [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md)
- [Batch Reads with Multicall3 in React](multicall-in-react.md)
- [Gate Content by Token Balance](gate-content-by-token-balance.md)
- [Core](../sdk/core.md#multicall3-and-permit2)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/add-pepu-to-a-wallet

# Recipe: Add PEPU to a Wallet

A one-click "Add Network" for Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet, using the SDK instead of a hand-written `wallet_addEthereumChain` payload.

`toAddEthereumChainParameter` produces the standard EIP-3085 payload (`chainId` `0x17dcd` for 97741) and `switchOrAddPepuChain` implements the EIP-3326 fallback.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk` and an injected EIP-1193 wallet (MetaMask and compatible).

## Steps

`switchOrAddPepuChain(provider, chain)` tries `wallet_switchEthereumChain` and, on error `4902` (chain not recognized), adds the chain with `wallet_addEthereumChain`. viem's own `switchChain` does not add a missing chain. Any other error, such as the user rejecting the prompt, is rethrown unchanged. `toAddEthereumChainParameter(chain)` builds the payload if you want to send it yourself.

```ts
// Add PEPU to an injected wallet. See docs/recipes/add-pepu-to-a-wallet.md
import { pepuMainnet, switchOrAddPepuChain, toAddEthereumChainParameter } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import type { EIP1193Provider } from "viem";

export function manualParameter() {
  // The exact object wallet_addEthereumChain expects (chainId is "0x17dcd").
  return toAddEthereumChainParameter(pepuMainnet);
}

export async function addAndSwitch(): Promise<void> {
  const provider = (window as unknown as { ethereum?: EIP1193Provider }).ethereum;
  if (!provider) throw new Error("No injected wallet found");
  await switchOrAddPepuChain(provider, pepuMainnet);
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/add-pepu-to-wallet.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

### React button

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { addAndSwitch } from "./add-pepu-to-wallet";

export function AddPepuButton() {
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  return (
    <>
      <button
        onClick={() =>
          addAndSwitch().catch((e: unknown) => setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Failed to add network"))
        }
      >
        Add Pepe Unchained to Wallet
      </button>
      {error && <p role="alert">{error}</p>}
    </>
  );
}
```

### With wagmi

If the wallet is connected through wagmi, `useSwitchChain` adds the chain automatically when it is in your config's `chains`:

```tsx
import { useSwitchChain } from "wagmi";
import { pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

export function SwitchToPepuButton() {
  const { switchChain } = useSwitchChain();
  return <button onClick={() => switchChain({ chainId: pepuMainnet.id })}>Switch to Pepe Unchained</button>;
}
```

## Manual entry

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Network Name | Pepe Unchained V2 |
| RPC URL | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Chain ID | `97741` |
| Currency Symbol | PEPU |
| Block Explorer URL | `https://pepuscan.com` |

Do not offer testnet here: it is out of scope. See [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md#testnet-out-of-scope-today).

## What to expect

A wallet that already has the chain switches silently. One that does not asks the user to approve adding it, then switches.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "No injected wallet found" | No extension, or a mobile browser without one | Offer manual entry or a WalletConnect-style flow |
| The helper rethrows | The user rejected, or the wallet uses a non-standard error code | Show the message; offer manual entry |
| `switchChain` errors in wagmi | The chain is not in `createConfig`'s `chains` | Add `pepuMainnet` |

## Related

- [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md)
- [Core](../sdk/core.md#chains-and-clients)
