Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/deploy-an-erc20

# Recipe: Deploy an ERC-20

A standard OpenZeppelin-based ERC-20, deployed and verified on Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet with Foundry.

This is the standard Foundry flow against PEPU mainnet. It uses the Foundry toolchain, so there is no SDK code to type-check; the SDK helps after deployment. If you haven't deployed anything here yet, do [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md) first — this recipe assumes a working Foundry project and a funded development key.

## The contract

```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.24;

import "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol";

contract MyToken is ERC20 {
    constructor(uint256 initialSupply) ERC20("My Token", "MTK") {
        _mint(msg.sender, initialSupply);
    }
}
```

Save as `src/MyToken.sol`.

## Install OpenZeppelin

```bash
forge install OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts
```

Add a remapping in `foundry.toml` if `forge install` didn't add one automatically:

```toml
remappings = ["@openzeppelin/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/"]
```

## Deploy

Constructor takes the initial supply in the token's smallest unit (18 decimals is OpenZeppelin's ERC-20 default, so `1_000_000e18` for one million whole tokens):

```bash
forge create src/MyToken.sol:MyToken \
  --rpc-url pepu_mainnet \
  --private-key $PRIVATE_KEY \
  --broadcast \
  --constructor-args 1000000000000000000000000
```

(That's `1,000,000 * 10^18` — one million tokens at 18 decimals.)

## Verify

Same Blockscout verification pattern as any other contract on this chain, with constructor args passed through so pepuscan can reproduce the exact deployed bytecode:

```bash
forge verify-contract \
  --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz \
  --verifier blockscout \
  --verifier-url https://pepuscan.com/api \
  --constructor-args $(cast abi-encode "constructor(uint256)" 1000000000000000000000000) \
  <DEPLOYED_ADDRESS> \
  src/MyToken.sol:MyToken
```

## Add it to the wallet the deploying key belongs to (optional, for testing)

Most wallets support `wallet_watchAsset` for this:

```ts
await window.ethereum.request({
  method: "wallet_watchAsset",
  params: {
    type: "ERC20",
    options: {
      address: "0xYourTokenAddress",
      symbol: "MTK",
      decimals: 18,
    },
  },
});
```

## Things this recipe deliberately does not cover

- **Listing on PepuSwap or any DEX** — that's a liquidity/business decision, not a deployment step, and out of scope for developer docs.
- **A canonical token list entry.** `@pepu-chain/sdk`'s token list (see [`@pepu-chain/sdk` Reference](../sdk/core.md#contract-and-dex-registries)) only includes addresses that clear a high independent-verification bar. Deploying your own token doesn't add it there automatically, and it shouldn't — that list is for chain-level infrastructure tokens, not every token anyone deploys.
- **Permit2.** The canonical Permit2 is deployed on PEPU (`getPermit2()`), so a freshly deployed ERC-20 can use signature-based approvals after one ordinary `approve(permit2, amount)`. See [Sign a Permit2 Permit](permit2-permit.md).


## After deployment, with the SDK

- Link the deployment: `txUrl(pepuMainnet, hash)` and `addressUrl(pepuMainnet, address)` ([Explorer Links](explorer-links.md)).
- Read it: [Read a Contract](read-a-contract.md), and gate content on it: [Gate Content by Token Balance](gate-content-by-token-balance.md).
- For gas the user does not pay, the contract must be on the paymaster allowlist: [Send a Sponsored Transaction](sponsored-send.md).

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/gate-content-by-token-balance

# Recipe: Gate Content by Token Balance

Show or hide something based on whether the signed-in wallet holds at least some amount of a token, and enforce it on the server where it matters.

The `token-gated-app` template implements this with Multicall3-batched balance reads.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk`, `viem`, and for the UI a wagmi setup on `pepuMainnet` with the embedded wallet pinned as the active account. See [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md).

## Steps

### Gate by native PEPU balance (UI)

```tsx
import { useAccount, useBalance } from "wagmi";
import { parseEther } from "viem";

const MINIMUM = parseEther("100");

export function GatedContent({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const { address } = useAccount();
  const { data: balance, isLoading } = useBalance({ address });

  if (!address) return <p>Sign in to check access.</p>;
  if (isLoading) return <p>Checking balance</p>;
  if (balance === undefined || balance.value < MINIMUM) return <p>You need at least 100 PEPU to view this.</p>;
  return <>{children}</>;
}
```

### Gate by an ERC-20 balance (UI)

```tsx
import { useAccount, useReadContract } from "wagmi";
import { erc20Abi, parseUnits } from "viem";
import { pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const TOKEN = "0xYourTokenAddress" as const;
const MINIMUM = parseUnits("1000", 18);

export function GatedByToken({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const { address } = useAccount();
  const { data: balance, isLoading } = useReadContract({
    chainId: pepuMainnet.id,
    address: TOKEN,
    abi: erc20Abi,
    functionName: "balanceOf",
    args: address ? [address] : undefined,
    query: { enabled: !!address },
  });

  if (!address) return <p>Sign in to check access.</p>;
  if (isLoading) return <p>Checking balance</p>;
  if (balance === undefined || balance < MINIMUM) return <p>You need at least 1000 tokens to view this.</p>;
  return <>{children}</>;
}
```

`erc20Abi` is viem's, re-exported by `@pepu-chain/sdk` so every ABI imports from one place. Token decimals differ: WPEPU has 18, USDT has 6.

### Enforce on the server

A client check decides what to show, not what to authorize. Verify at the point of use:

```ts
// Gate access by token balance on the server. See docs/recipes/gate-content-by-token-balance.md
import { erc20Abi } from "viem";
import { formatUnitsCompact, getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const client = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

export async function holdsEnough(
  token: `0x${string}`,
  holder: `0x${string}`,
  minimum: bigint,
): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; shown: string }> {
  const [balance, decimals] = await Promise.all([
    client.readContract({ address: token, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "balanceOf", args: [holder] }),
    client.readContract({ address: token, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "decimals" }),
  ]);
  return { allowed: balance >= minimum, shown: formatUnitsCompact(balance, decimals) };
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/gate-by-balance.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

For an NFT use `erc721Abi`: `balanceOf(address)` is a count, so `balance > 0n` is "owns one". For ERC-1155, `balanceOf(address, tokenId)` takes a token id.

## What to expect

- The UI check is fast and advisory. The server check is the real gate and must run on every privileged request.
- Take the wallet address on the server from the verified Privy token (`requireUser` from [/privy/server](../sdk/privy-server.md)), never from the request body.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The gate shows another wallet's balance | An extension is wagmi's active account | Keep the active-wallet pin on |
| Wrong threshold on USDT | Assumed 18 decimals | Read `decimals()`; USDT has 6 |
| Gate bypassed | Client-only check | Add the server check |

## Related

- [Batch Reads with Multicall3](batch-reads-with-multicall3.md) for checking many addresses at once
- [Token-Gated App template](../templates/token-gated-app.md)
- [Core](../sdk/core.md)

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/grant-a-session

# Recipe: Grant a Session

Grant your app a scoped session so it can act for a signed-in user with no popup per action. Two modes exist: Privy mode (this page, in full) and Kernel mode (on-chain scope, see the end of the page and [Sponsored Session in One Flow](sponsored-session.md)).

Privy mode: the scope is enforced by Privy's policy engine, off-chain, and the user pays gas. Kernel mode: the scope is enforced on-chain and, with the paymaster, the user pays no gas.

## Prerequisites

- Google to wallet working (see [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md)).
- A Privy authorization key and key quorum, with `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` set. See [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md). Generate the key with `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` from [/doctor](../sdk/doctor.md).
- The one contract and function the session may call. This recipe uses TapScore's `tap()`.

## Steps

### 1. Server: mount the routes

`createSessionRoutes` gives you `grant`, `status` and `revoke`. `createSessionActionRoute` is the one action the session may perform. The action route signs with Privy `eth_signTransaction` and broadcasts the raw transaction itself, because Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` rejects chain 97741.

```ts
// Pillar 2 (Privy mode), server: grant, status, revoke and one scoped action.
// SERVER ONLY (reads PRIVY_APP_SECRET and PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY).
// See docs/sdk/session.md and docs/recipes/grant-a-session.md
import { createSessionActionRoute, createSessionRoutes } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/server";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapFunction } from "./tapscore";

const scope = { contractAddress: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, functions: [tapFunction] } as const;

const routes = createSessionRoutes({ scope });

// app/api/session/grant/route.ts
export const grant = routes.grant;
// app/api/session/status/route.ts
export const status = routes.status;
// app/api/session/revoke/route.ts
export const revoke = routes.revoke;

// app/api/game/tap/route.ts: signs with Privy eth_signTransaction and broadcasts itself,
// because Privy's server-side eth_sendTransaction rejects chain 97741.
export const tap = createSessionActionRoute({
  scope,
  parse: () => ({}),
  buildCall: () => ({ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: [tapFunction], functionName: "tap" }),
  rateLimit: { perMinute: 60 },
});
```

Source: `docs/snippets/session-privy-server.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

Put each handler in its own route file (`app/api/session/grant/route.ts` exports `const { POST } = routes.grant`, and so on).

### 2. Client: grant, act, revoke

```tsx
// Pillar 2 (Privy mode), client: grant once, then act with no popup.
// See docs/sdk/session.md and docs/recipes/grant-a-session.md
import { useSessionAct, useSessionGrant, useSessionRevoke, useSessionStatus } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/react";

export function Session() {
  const { state, secondsLeft, loading } = useSessionStatus({ pollMs: 30_000 });
  const { grant, status: grantStatus, error: grantError } = useSessionGrant();
  const { revoke } = useSessionRevoke();
  const { act, status: actStatus, error: actError } = useSessionAct<Record<string, never>, { hash: string }>({
    endpoint: "/api/game/tap",
  });

  // Avoid flashing the consent screen on reload.
  if (loading) return <p>Checking session</p>;

  if (state !== "active") {
    return (
      <button onClick={() => void grant()} disabled={grantStatus === "creating-policy" || grantStatus === "awaiting-consent"}>
        {state === "expired" ? "Session expired, start a new one" : "Start session"}
        {grantError ? ` (${grantError.code})` : ""}
      </button>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <p>{secondsLeft}s left</p>
      <button onClick={() => void act({}).then((r) => console.log(r.hash))} disabled={actStatus === "pending"}>
        Tap
      </button>
      <button onClick={() => void revoke()}>End session</button>
      {actError ? <p>{actError.code === "SESSION_NONE" ? "No active session" : actError.message}</p> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/session-privy-react.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

`useSessionGrant` asks the server for a fresh scoped policy, then asks the user to approve it with Privy's `addSigners`. Show the user what they approve with `describeSessionScope` and `SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE["privy-offchain"]`.

## What to expect

- One consent for the whole session, then each `act` returns `{ hash, address, explorerUrl }` with no popup.
- The session length defaults to 15 minutes (`SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES`, clamped 1 to 1440).
- The user still pays gas from their embedded wallet. Privy mode does not sponsor gas.
- Privy mode limits are enforced by Privy's backend, not on-chain. Say so on the consent screen.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every action returns an error right after grant | The policy was built for `eth_sendTransaction` | Use `buildSessionPolicy`, which targets `eth_signTransaction` |
| `SESSION_NONE` (HTTP 409) | No signer attached | Send the user to the grant button. Any other failure is a failed transaction, not a lost session |
| 401 "No valid authorization keys" | The server key is not the key whose quorum the user granted | Match `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` to `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` as JSON from every route | The contract address variable is unset | Set it. Routes answer at request time naming the variable |
| "Duplicate signer" | `addSigners` called twice | Use the hook; it skips `addSigners` on `alreadyGranted` |

## Kernel mode: on-chain scope

When the limit must hold even if your backend is compromised, and you want no gas for the user, use the on-chain session from [/session/kernel](../sdk/session-kernel.md), wired up by [/combo](../sdk/combo.md). The owner signs one EIP-712 message with no gas, and ZeroDev's call and timestamp policies enforce the scope during UserOperation validation. The primitives:

```ts
// Pillar 2 (Kernel mode), the low-level primitives behind /combo.
// Most apps use createSponsoredSessionRoutes instead (see combo-server.ts).
// See docs/sdk/session-kernel.md
import { getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import {
  approveKernelSession,
  buildKernelSessionPolicies,
  checkApproval,
  describeKernelSessionScope,
  expectedPermissionId,
  generateSessionKey,
  isCallInScope,
  loadKernelSessionAccount,
} from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel";
import type { KernelOwner, KernelSessionCall } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel";
import { encodeFunctionData } from "viem";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

const calls: KernelSessionCall[] = [{ target: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }];
const validUntil = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 15 * 60;

// --- SERVER: create the session key. The private key never leaves the server. ---
export const sessionKey = generateSessionKey();
export const policies = buildKernelSessionPolicies({ calls, validUntil });

// Consent-screen data, plain JSON.
export const scope = describeKernelSessionScope({ calls, validUntil });

// --- BROWSER: the owner signs ONE EIP-712 message. No gas, no private key leaves the wallet. ---
export function grant(owner: KernelOwner) {
  return approveKernelSession({ publicClient, owner, sessionKeyAddress: sessionKey.address, policies });
}

// --- SERVER: verify the approval before storing it, then act with the session key. ---
export async function activate(approval: string, kernelAddress: `0x${string}`) {
  const permissionId = await expectedPermissionId({ publicClient, sessionKeyAddress: sessionKey.address, policies });
  const check = checkApproval(approval, { kernelAddress, permissionId });
  if (!check.ok) throw new Error(check.reason);
  return loadKernelSessionAccount({ publicClient, approval, sessionPrivateKey: sessionKey.privateKey });
}

// Pure, fails fast before sponsoring. The chain enforces the real limit.
export const tapIsAllowed = isCallInScope(scope, {
  to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS,
  data: encodeFunctionData({ abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }),
  value: 0n,
});
```

Source: `docs/snippets/session-kernel.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## Related

- [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md)
- [/session](../sdk/session.md), [/session/kernel](../sdk/session-kernel.md)
- [Sign with Privy, Broadcast Yourself](sign-with-privy-broadcast-yourself.md)
- [Sponsored Session in One Flow](sponsored-session.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/sponsored-send

# Recipe: Send a Sponsored Transaction

Send a transaction from a smart account whose gas is paid by a paymaster, from a script or from a React component.

A zero-balance Kernel smart account can transact with gas paid by the v2 paymaster `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`, through the hosted bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and paymaster `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>`. The bundler is the SDK default; you supply a project token. Local development defaults for your own services are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`.

## Prerequisites

- The hosted bundler and paymaster (the SDK defaults), plus a project of yours that is claimed, configured and funded (see [Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](v2-deposit-and-claim.md)) and its token. The free tier needs a Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app and is not available to third-party apps.
- `@pepu-chain/sdk`, `viem`, and for the script path `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`.
- The destination contract must be on the paymaster's allowlist. TapScore is the sample.

## Steps

1. Check the services are reachable with `checkSponsorship`. It never throws for an unreachable service and returns `fixes`.
2. Build the Kernel account with `toPepuKernelAccount`. Two addresses exist: the owner (signs) and the smart account (sends, holds assets). See [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md).
3. Create the client with `createPepuSponsoredClient`.
4. Send with `sendSponsored`. It encodes the calls, sends one UserOperation, waits for the receipt and reports who paid.

### Script

```ts
// Pillar 3: a sponsored transaction from a script (direct transport).
// Needs a bundler and a paymaster: set PEPU_BUNDLER_URL and PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL
// (the bundler defaults to https://bundler.pepeunchained.com; the ERC-7677 URL is https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>).
// Local dev defaults are http://localhost:4337 and http://localhost:8788 for your own services.
// See docs/sdk/aa.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-send.md
import { buildPaymasterContext, checkSponsorship, explorerLinks, getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { createPepuSponsoredClient, sendSponsored, toPepuKernelAccount } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel";
import type { Hex } from "viem";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

// SCRIPT ONLY: the owner key stays in your environment.
const owner = privateKeyToAccount(process.env["OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY"] as Hex);

export async function sponsoredTap(privyAccessToken?: string) {
  // 1. Is sponsorship reachable? Never throws for an unreachable service.
  const status = await checkSponsorship({ publicClient });
  if (!status.available) throw new Error(`${status.reason} ${status.fixes.join(" ")}`);

  // 2. The Kernel smart account that sends and holds assets. The owner EOA only signs.
  const account = await toPepuKernelAccount({ publicClient, owner });

  // 3. A client that sends through your bundler and has gas paid by your paymaster.
  const client = createPepuSponsoredClient({
    account,
    // The v2 free tier wants the user's Privy access token (from PEPU's own Privy app).
    ...(privyAccessToken ? { paymasterContext: buildPaymasterContext({ privyAccessToken }) } : {}),
  });

  // 4. One UserOperation: encode, send, wait for the receipt, report who paid.
  const result = await sendSponsored({
    client,
    calls: [{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }],
  });

  return { ...result, links: explorerLinks({ tx: result.transactionHash, sender: account.address }) };
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/sponsored-send.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

### React

There are two hook entries. `useSponsoredSend` from `/aa/react` uses Privy's smart-wallet client with the bundler and paymaster URLs set in the Privy dashboard, and never needs ZeroDev. `useDirectSponsoredSend` from `/aa/react-direct` builds a Kernel account for the embedded wallet and uses the hosted endpoints (override with `PEPU_*`), passing the Privy access token as paymaster context (it only unlocks the free tier for PEPU's own Privy app) (it needs `@zerodev/sdk` and `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`).

```tsx
// Pillar 3, client: send with gas sponsored from a component.
// See docs/sdk/aa.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-send.md
import { usePepuSmartAccount, usePepuSponsorship, useSponsoredSend } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

export function SponsoredTap() {
  const { smartAccount } = usePepuSmartAccount();
  // "privy-smart-wallets" uses the bundler and paymaster URLs from the Privy dashboard.
  // For your own bundler and paymaster, use useDirectSponsoredSend from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct".
  const { send, status, result, error } = useSponsoredSend({ transport: "privy-smart-wallets" });
  const sponsorship = usePepuSponsorship({ pollMs: 0 });

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Smart account: {smartAccount}</p>
      <button
        disabled={status === "signing" || status === "submitting"}
        onClick={() => void send([{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }])}
      >
        Tap, no gas
      </button>
      {status === "confirmed" && result ? <a href={result.explorerUrl}>Paid by {result.paymaster}</a> : null}
      {error ? (
        <p>
          {error.code}: {error.hint}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {!sponsorship.loading && !sponsorship.available ? <p>{sponsorship.reason}</p> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/sponsored-send-react.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

## What to expect

- The smart account balance can be zero. `result.paymaster` is the paymaster address and `result.actualGasCostWei` is what it paid.
- A bundle can carry several operations. Use `userOpEventsFromReceipt` from `/aa` to inspect them all.
- pepuscan has no UserOperation page. Link the bundle transaction and the sender with `explorerLinks` (see [Explorer Links](explorer-links.md)).
- The first operation of a new account is larger because it deploys the account. The paymaster reserves about 20.5 PEPU for it and about 6.9 PEPU for later operations.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "No bundler or paymaster URL is configured" | No paymaster token or `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` was supplied (the ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token) | Pass `paymasterToken` or set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | A client token (`ppt_`) was used with no allowed origins or from another origin | Set the project's allowed origins, or use the server key (`ppk_`) from a backend |
| `PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE` | The project's balance cannot cover the operation | Deposit PEPU into the project (`depositFor`). `checkSponsorship({ publicClient })` reports `depositWei` |
| `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | The contract is not on the allowlist | Add it to the project's targets |
| `PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED` | The v2 free tier needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app | Pass `buildPaymasterContext({ privyAccessToken })`, or use a project instead |
| `BUNDLER_AA_FAILED` with an `AAxx` code | The EntryPoint rejected the operation | `error.hint` names the fix; `describeUserOpFailure` mapped it |
| `zd_getUserOperationGasPrice` not found | ZeroDev's default fee estimator against Alto | Use `createPepuSponsoredClient`, which wires the Alto-compatible one |

## Related

- [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)
- [/aa](../sdk/aa.md), [/paymaster](../sdk/paymaster.md)
- [Sponsored Session in One Flow](sponsored-session.md)
- [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/sponsored-session

# Recipe: Sponsored Session in One Flow

Google sign-in, one owner signature that grants an on-chain session, then actions with no popup and no gas for the user. This is the combination of all three pillars, and `@pepu-chain/sdk/combo` is the whole backend plus the hook.

An on-chain Kernel session key plus sponsorship runs end to end in the `sponsored-session-app` template. The hosted bundler (the SDK default) and paymaster are available; set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project server key>`. You need your own claimed and funded project.

## Prerequisites

- A Privy app with Google login enabled and your origin allowed. See [Privy Setup Walkthrough](../onboarding/privy-setup.md). Smart Wallets are not needed: the SDK builds its own Kernel account.
- `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (and optionally `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, which defaults to `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`). Treat `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` as a secret: it embeds your project's server key. The routes forward the signed-in user's Privy token as ERC-7677 context (`forwardPrivyToken`, default true; set it false for a paymaster you do not trust with it); a project ignores it for billing.
- The wallet provisioning pieces from [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md).
- The target contract on the paymaster's allowlist.
- Peers: `@privy-io/node`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, and the three `@zerodev/*` packages.

## Steps

### 1. Server: five routes

```ts
// The combination, server: Google login + on-chain session key + sponsored gas.
// SERVER ONLY. See docs/sdk/combo.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-session.md
// Needs PRIVY_APP_SECRET and PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL (https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project server key>).
// PEPU_BUNDLER_URL defaults to https://bundler.pepeunchained.com.
import { createMemoryStore, createSponsoredSessionRoutes } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo";
import type { SessionStore } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

// DEV ONLY. The store holds session private keys: production needs a persistent
// SessionStore with sessionPrivateKey encrypted at rest.
const store: SessionStore = createMemoryStore();

export const routes = createSponsoredSessionRoutes({
  scope: { calls: [{ target: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }] },
  store,
  act: {
    parse: () => ({}),
    buildCalls: () => [{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }],
  },
});

// app/api/session/prepare/route.ts   export const { POST } = routes.prepare;
// app/api/session/activate/route.ts  export const { POST } = routes.activate;
// app/api/session/status/route.ts    export const { GET } = routes.status;
// app/api/session/act/route.ts       export const { POST } = routes.act;
// app/api/session/revoke/route.ts    export const { POST } = routes.revoke;
export const { prepare, activate, status, act, revoke } = routes;
```

Source: `docs/snippets/combo-server.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

Mount `prepare`, `activate`, `status`, `act` and `revoke` at `app/api/session/<name>/route.ts`, the paths the hook expects by default.

### 2. Client: one hook

```tsx
// The combination, client: one owner signature, then actions with no popup and no gas.
// See docs/sdk/combo.md and docs/recipes/sponsored-session.md
import { describeKernelSessionScope } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel";
import type { KernelSessionCall } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel";
import { useSponsoredSession } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo/react";
import type { SponsoredActResult } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo/react";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore";

// The browser rebuilds the policies from the same scope the server uses.
const calls: KernelSessionCall[] = [{ target: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }];
const scope = { calls };

export function SponsoredSession() {
  const { phase, statusLoading, owner, smartAccount, expiresAt, grant, act, revoke, error } = useSponsoredSession<
    undefined,
    SponsoredActResult
  >({ scope });

  if (statusLoading) return <p>Checking session</p>;
  const preview = describeKernelSessionScope({ calls, validUntil: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 15 * 60 });

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Owner (signs once): {owner}</p>
      <p>Smart account (sends, holds assets): {smartAccount}</p>

      {phase === "ready" || phase === "expired" ? (
        <div>
          <p>This session may call: {preview.calls.map((c) => c.signature).join(", ")}</p>
          <button onClick={() => void grant()}>Start session</button>
        </div>
      ) : null}

      {phase === "active" ? (
        <div>
          <p>Active until {expiresAt}</p>
          <button onClick={() => void act().then((r) => console.log(r.explorerUrl))}>Tap, no popup, no gas</button>
          <button onClick={() => void revoke()}>End session</button>
        </div>
      ) : null}

      {error ? (
        <p>
          {error.code}: {error.hint}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/combo-react.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

The browser rebuilds the policies from the same `scope` the server uses. If they differ, the server rejects the approval with `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH`, so share one `scope` module between both sides.

## What to expect

- The user signs once (an EIP-712 message, no gas). Every `act` after that has no popup and costs the user nothing.
- The scope is enforced on-chain: only the listed contract and function selectors, with zero native value, between the grant and its expiry. A call outside it is rejected by the EntryPoint no matter what your backend does.
- `revoke` deletes the key on the server at once. The on-chain grant stays valid until its expiry, but only the deleted key could use it.
- Reserve for gas: about 20.5 PEPU for the first action of a session and 6.9 PEPU after (`SESSION_GAS_RESERVATION_PEPU`). Size spend caps above it.
- `createMemoryStore` is for development. It holds the session private key in process memory. Production needs a `SessionStore` on a database with the key encrypted at rest.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `phase` stuck on `provisioning` | The user has no embedded wallet yet | Wrap the app in `WalletGate` |
| `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH` | Browser and server scopes differ | Share the scope |
| `SESSION_NONE` on act | No live session, or the server restarted with an in-memory store | Grant again; use a persistent store |
| `PAYMASTER_CAP` after the first action | Caps below the reservation | Raise per-user caps |
| `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | The contract is not allowlisted | Add it to the project targets |
| 429 on act | Another action is running for that user | Wait and retry |

## Related

- [Sponsored Session: No Popup, No Gas](../onboarding/sponsored-session.md)
- [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md)
- [/combo](../sdk/combo.md)
- [Sponsored Session App template](../templates/sponsored-session-app.md)

---

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim

# Recipe: Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project

Register an app with the v2 tiered paymaster, claim its project on-chain, configure its limits and fund it. All with SDK helpers.

The v2 paymaster is deployed at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`. The registry entry `paymasterV2` points at it, so the helpers default to it. Deposits are one-way, so deposit only what your project needs.

## Prerequisites

- The v2 paymaster address: the registry default, or read it from the policy service (`api.v2.contract()`).
- A Privy app. The project id is `keccak256(bytes(appId))`, case-sensitive.
- A wallet that will own the project, with PEPU for gas.
- The policy service, hosted at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default; `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` overrides), and a SIWE domain it allows.
- A server or CLI. The claim call sends your Privy app secret to the service. Use a dedicated Privy app for sponsorship if you can, and rotate the secret afterwards.

## What to know first

- **Deposits are one-way.** There are no withdrawals. Pausing a project is the exit.
- **The claim sets the owner only.** Nothing is sponsored until the owner also calls `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit`; the contract rejects a project with no per-wallet limit.
- **Claim before anyone funds the project.** An empty project is claimed at once; a project that already holds deposits is pending for the 48-hour admin delay and finished with `executeReclaim`.
- **A typo is expensive.** A mistyped app id makes a different project nobody can claim. `depositFor` refuses an unclaimed project unless you pass `requireClaimed: false`.
- **Free tier:** 100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per hour, only for users of PEPU's own Privy app, not available to third-party apps (their Privy token is ignored for billing). Your app uses a project.
- **Re-claims** of an owned project are timelocked 48 hours and can be cancelled by the owner once per new owner.

## Steps

1. Sign in to the policy service with the owner wallet (`api.v2.loginWithWallet`).
2. Prove control of the Privy app and get an attestation (`requestClaimAttestation`), then submit the claim (`encodeClaimFromVerification`, `sendPaymasterCalls`).
3. Configure the project with `configureProject`: targets, total daily limit and per-sender daily limit.
4. Fund it with `depositFor`.
5. Register the project with the service to get credentials (`api.v2.projects.register`). The client token (`ppt_`) is browser-safe and works only from the allowed origins you set (otherwise `project_origin_not_allowed`). The server key (`ppk_`) is secret and shown once.
6. Read the state back with `readProject` and build the ERC-7677 URL with `buildErc7677Url`.

```ts
// Register, claim, configure and fund a v2 paymaster project.
// Deposits are one-way; deposit only what your project needs.
// SERVER OR CLI ONLY: requestClaimAttestation sends your Privy app secret to the policy service.
// See docs/sdk/paymaster.md and docs/recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md
import { getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import {
  buildErc7677Url,
  computeProjectId,
  configureProject,
  createPaymasterApi,
  depositFor,
  encodeClaimFromVerification,
  readProject,
  sendPaymasterCalls,
} from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";
import { requestClaimAttestation } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server";
import { createWalletClient, getAddress, http, parseEther } from "viem";
import type { Hex } from "viem";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
import { TAPSCORE_ADDRESS } from "./tapscore";

const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);
const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env["PROJECT_OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY"] as Hex);
const walletClient = createWalletClient({ account, chain: pepuMainnet, transport: http() });

// The registry's paymasterV2 entry is the deployed paymaster; the helpers default to it. It is passed explicitly here
// (GET /v2/contract on the service returns it too). Override with PEPU_PAYMASTER_V2_ADDRESS.
const paymaster = getAddress(process.env["PEPU_PAYMASTER_V2_ADDRESS"] ?? "0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D");
const appId = process.env["PRIVY_APP_ID"] as string;
const projectId = computeProjectId(appId); // keccak256(bytes(appId)), case-sensitive

export async function registerClaimConfigureFund() {
  // The paymaster service defaults to https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com (override with PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL).
  const api = createPaymasterApi();

  // 1. Sign in with the wallet that should own the project (SIWE, 1 hour session).
  await api.v2.loginWithWallet((message) => account.signMessage({ message }), {
    address: account.address,
    domain: process.env["PEPU_SIWE_DOMAIN"] as string,
  });

  // 2. Prove control of the Privy app, then submit the claim on-chain. The claim sets the owner ONLY.
  const verified = await requestClaimAttestation(api, {
    appId,
    newOwner: account.address,
    privyAppSecret: process.env["PRIVY_APP_SECRET"] as string,
  });
  const claim = encodeClaimFromVerification(verified, { paymaster });
  await sendPaymasterCalls(walletClient, [claim], { publicClient });

  // 3. Nothing is sponsored until the owner sets targets and both daily limits.
  const { calls } = configureProject({
    appId,
    paymaster,
    targets: [TAPSCORE_ADDRESS],
    dailyLimitWei: parseEther("100"), // project budget per day
    senderDailyLimitWei: parseEther("25"), // per wallet; must exceed one first-operation reservation (about 21 PEPU)
  });
  await sendPaymasterCalls(walletClient, calls, { publicClient });

  // 4. Deposits are ONE-WAY. depositFor refuses an unclaimed project by default (catches a mistyped app id).
  await depositFor({ walletClient, publicClient, appId, amountWei: parseEther("25"), paymaster });

  // 5. Index the project to get credentials (client token is browser-safe, the server key is not).
  const registered = await api.v2.projects.register({ appId, allowedOrigins: ["https://app.example.com"] });

  const state = await readProject(publicClient, projectId, { paymaster, checkTargets: [TAPSCORE_ADDRESS] });
  return {
    claimed: state.claimed,
    limitsConfigured: state.limitsConfigured,
    balance: state.balance,
    // Paste into the Privy "Paymaster URL" field, or pass to a viem paymaster client.
    erc7677Url: buildErc7677Url({ baseUrl: api.baseUrl, token: registered.token }),
  };
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/v2-deposit-and-claim.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## What to expect

- After step 3, `readProject` reports `claimed: true` and `limitsConfigured: true`.
- Sponsorship then draws on the project's balance first, within the daily limits you set.
- A denied request returns a mapped `PepuPaymasterError` (`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED`, `PAYMASTER_CAP`, `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED`, and so on).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` "No v2 paymaster address" | An old SDK without the deployed registry entry, and no address was passed | Update the SDK, or pass `paymaster` |
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED` on deposit | Not claimed, or the app id is mistyped | Check the id's case; claim first |
| Claimed, but sponsorship is denied | `setTargets` or a limit was never set | Run `configureProject` |
| `PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED` | The SIWE session expired (one hour) | Call `loginWithWallet` again |
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED` | A re-claim completed | Check `readProject().owner` |

## Related

- [/paymaster](../sdk/paymaster.md)
- [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md)
- [Paymaster v2 Spec Summary](../contracts/paymaster-v2-spec.md)
- [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md)

# Recipe: Sign a Permit2 Permit

Sign an EIP-712 Permit2 `PermitSingle` so a spender can pull a token without a separate `approve` transaction per spender, using the SDK's typed-data builders and the canonical Permit2 deployed on PEPU.

The SDK provides the Permit2 domain and typed data. Submitting the permit to a spender contract depends on that contract and is not covered here.

## Prerequisites

- A token that is an ordinary ERC-20. A one-time ordinary `approve(permit2, amount)` from the owner to Permit2 is still required once per token, because Permit2 pulls through the token's allowance.
- A connected wallet client that can `signTypedData` (a wagmi `useWalletClient`, or a viem `WalletClient`).
- The canonical Permit2 address `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3`. Use `getPermit2()` rather than typing it.

PepuSwap also ships its own, separate Permit2 (`pepuSwapContracts` name `permit2NonCanonical`). It is a different contract with a different domain and does not interoperate with the canonical one. `buildPermitSingleTypedData` always targets the canonical one.

## Steps

1. Read the current allowance and nonce with `readPermit2Allowance`. The nonce lives in Permit2, so do not guess it.
2. Build the typed data with `buildPermitSingleTypedData`. It sets the domain (`name: "Permit2"`, no version, chain 97741, the canonical address) and the `PermitSingle` and `PermitDetails` types.
3. Sign with `walletClient.signTypedData`.
4. Hand the signature to the spender contract, which calls `permit` on Permit2 and then `transferFrom`.

```ts
// Sign a Permit2 AllowanceTransfer permit. See docs/recipes/permit2-permit.md
import {
  buildPermitSingleTypedData,
  getPermit2,
  getPublicClient,
  pepuMainnet,
  readPermit2Allowance,
} from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import type { WalletClient } from "viem";

const client = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

export async function signPermit(
  walletClient: WalletClient,
  token: `0x${string}`,
  spender: `0x${string}`,
  amount: bigint,
): Promise<{ signature: `0x${string}`; permit2: `0x${string}` }> {
  const owner = walletClient.account?.address;
  if (!owner) throw new Error("Connect a wallet first");

  // The nonce lives in Permit2; read it rather than guessing.
  const current = await readPermit2Allowance(client, { owner, token, spender });

  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const typed = buildPermitSingleTypedData({
    token,
    amount,
    expiration: now + 60 * 60, // allowance lifetime
    nonce: current.nonce,
    spender,
    sigDeadline: BigInt(now + 30 * 60), // how long this signature may be submitted
  });

  const signature = await walletClient.signTypedData({
    account: owner,
    domain: typed.domain,
    types: typed.types,
    primaryType: typed.primaryType,
    message: typed.message,
  });
  return { signature, permit2: getPermit2().address };
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/permit2-permit.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

For signature-based one-off transfers use `buildPermitTransferFromTypedData` (SignatureTransfer `PermitTransferFrom`) the same way, with `nonce` and `deadline` as `bigint` and an unordered nonce of your choosing.

## What to expect

- The wallet shows a typed-data signing prompt with no gas. With a Privy embedded wallet and the active-wallet pin, the prompt belongs to the embedded wallet.
- `expiration` is when the allowance lapses. `sigDeadline` is how long the signature may be submitted. Keep both short.
- `amount` is a `uint160`. Do not use `maxUint256`.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `getPermit2` throws `UNKNOWN` | The chain is not mainnet | Use chain 97741 |
| The spender reverts with an invalid signer | Wrong nonce, expired `sigDeadline`, or the wrong Permit2 | Re-read the nonce; check you did not sign for PepuSwap's own Permit2 |
| `TransferFrom` fails with insufficient allowance | The token was never approved to Permit2 | Send an ordinary `approve(permit2, amount)` once |
| `amount` rejected | Above `uint160` | Use a bounded amount |

## Related

- [Permit2](../contracts/permit2.md)
- [Core](../sdk/core.md#multicall3-and-permit2)
- [Deployed Contracts Reference](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/multicall-in-react

# Recipe: Batch Reads with Multicall3 in React

Read many values in one request from a React component with wagmi, using PEPU's own Multicall3. No Multicall3 configuration is needed when you use the SDK's chain.

The token-gated template batches balance reads this way.

## Prerequisites

- A wagmi config that uses `pepuMainnet`, ideally `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` from [/privy/wagmi](../sdk/privy-wagmi.md) or `pepuWagmiConfig`.
- Read [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md): the canonical Multicall3 address has no code on PEPU. PEPU's is `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`.

## Steps

1. Use `pepuMainnet` as the chain. It carries `contracts.multicall3` at PEPU's address, so wagmi's `useReadContracts` batches into one `aggregate3` call automatically.
2. Build the contract list. Pass `chainId: pepuMainnet.id` on each item.
3. Read the native PEPU balance separately with `usePepuBalance`, because a native balance is not a contract call.

```tsx
// Batched reads in React with wagmi. See docs/recipes/multicall-in-react.md
import { useReadContracts } from "wagmi";
import { erc20Abi, formatUnits } from "viem";
import { pepuMainnet, pepuTokenList } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { usePepuBalance } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/react";
import { getPublicClient } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

export function Balances({ holder }: { holder: `0x${string}` }) {
  // pepuMainnet carries contracts.multicall3 at PEPU's own address, so wagmi batches these into one call
  // with no extra configuration.
  const { data, isLoading } = useReadContracts({
    allowFailure: true,
    contracts: pepuTokenList.tokens.flatMap(
      (t) =>
        [
          { chainId: pepuMainnet.id, address: t.address as `0x${string}`, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "symbol" },
          {
            chainId: pepuMainnet.id,
            address: t.address as `0x${string}`,
            abi: erc20Abi,
            functionName: "balanceOf",
            args: [holder],
          },
        ] as const,
    ),
  });

  // The native balance is not a contract call; usePepuBalance polls it.
  const native = usePepuBalance(publicClient, { address: holder, pollingInterval: 15_000 });

  if (isLoading) return <p>Loading</p>;
  return (
    <ul>
      <li>PEPU {native.data !== undefined ? formatUnits(native.data, 18) : "..."}</li>
      {pepuTokenList.tokens.map((t, i) => {
        const symbol = data?.[i * 2];
        const balance = data?.[i * 2 + 1];
        return (
          <li key={t.address}>
            {symbol?.status === "success" ? String(symbol.result) : t.symbol}{" "}
            {balance?.status === "success" ? formatUnits(balance.result as bigint, t.decimals) : "..."}
          </li>
        );
      })}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/multicall-in-react.tsx`, type-checked against the SDK.

Outside React, use `pepuMulticall(client, calls)`. See [Batch Reads with Multicall3](batch-reads-with-multicall3.md).

## What to expect

- One RPC request for all contract reads. Results come back in order, each `{ status, result }` or `{ status, error }` when `allowFailure` is true.
- A failing token (not an ERC-20, for example) returns a failure entry for that call and does not fail the batch.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Reads return nothing or the batch errors | A hand-written chain definition uses the canonical address | Use `pepuMainnet` from the SDK |
| The embedded wallet's balance is not shown | Wagmi's active account is an extension | Keep the active-wallet pin on ([Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md)) |

## Related

- [Batch Reads with Multicall3](batch-reads-with-multicall3.md)
- [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md)
- [Core](../sdk/core.md#multicall3-and-permit2)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/recipes/explorer-links

# Recipe: Explorer Links

Build pepuscan links for transactions, addresses, tokens and blocks, and link a sponsored UserOperation correctly.

pepuscan is PEPU mainnet's Blockscout explorer at `https://pepuscan.com`.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk` and `pepuMainnet`. No React, no network call: link building is pure.

## Steps

Use the shorthand for the resource you have: `txUrl`, `addressUrl`, `tokenUrl`, `blockUrl`, or `explorerUrl(chain, type, value)` for the generic form. For a bundle of links at once use `explorerLinks`.

A UserOperation has no page of its own on pepuscan. Link its bundle transaction (`result.transactionHash`) and its sender (the smart account address). `SponsoredResult.explorerUrl` and the combo `act` response already carry the bundle transaction URL.

```ts
// Build pepuscan links. See docs/recipes/explorer-links.md
import { addressUrl, blockUrl, explorerLinks, explorerUrl, pepuMainnet, tokenUrl, txUrl } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import type { SponsoredResult } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa";

export const single = {
  tx: (hash: string) => txUrl(pepuMainnet, hash),
  address: (a: string) => addressUrl(pepuMainnet, a),
  token: (a: string) => tokenUrl(pepuMainnet, a),
  block: (n: number) => blockUrl(pepuMainnet, n),
  generic: (hash: string) => explorerUrl(pepuMainnet, "tx", hash),
};

// A UserOperation has no page of its own on pepuscan: link its bundle transaction
// and its sender (the smart account).
export function userOpLinks(result: SponsoredResult, smartAccount: string) {
  return explorerLinks({ tx: result.transactionHash, sender: smartAccount });
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/explorer-links.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## What to expect

- `txUrl(pepuMainnet, hash)` gives `https://pepuscan.com/tx/<hash>`.
- `explorerLinks({ tx, sender })` returns only the keys you passed.
- `explorerUrl` throws for a chain with no explorer (`pepuTestnet`). Wrap the call if you need a soft failure.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `explorerUrl: no block explorer is configured` | You passed `pepuTestnet` | Use `pepuMainnet` |
| A link to `/userop/...` 404s | Blockscout on PEPU has no UserOperation page | Link the transaction and sender instead |
| Block link by hash fails | Hash passed as a number | Pass the hash as a string |

## Related

- [Core](../sdk/core.md#explorer-links)
- [Send a Sponsored Transaction](sponsored-send.md)
- [Send a Transaction](send-a-transaction.md)

# Endpoints


Every endpoint the dev kit talks to, in one table: the public RPC and explorer, and the bundler and paymaster. Docs elsewhere write `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` as placeholders and point here for what they mean. This page is generated from the SDK, so it cannot disagree with `resolvePepuEndpoints()`.

The SDK uses the hosted bundler and paymaster service by default (`PEPU_HOSTED`); the environment variables below override them. Bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. The ERC-7677 paymaster URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`), so it is never a default: set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to it.

## Prerequisites

- Nothing for the RPC and explorer. Sponsored transactions also need a bundler and a paymaster, see [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## Endpoint table

| Service | Value | Environment variable | Local development default |
|---|---|---|---|
| RPC (chain `97741`) | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` | `PEPU_RPC_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_RPC_URL`) | none, use the public RPC |
| Explorer (PepuScan) | `https://pepuscan.com` | none | none |
| Explorer API (Blockscout) | `https://pepuscan.com/api` | none | none |
| Bundler (ERC-4337, EntryPoint v0.7) | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) | `http://localhost:4337` |
| Paymaster service (REST API, health, free-tier state) | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` | base of `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `http://localhost:8788` |
| Paymaster ERC-7677 URL | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`) | `http://localhost:8788/v2/paymaster/<your-token>` |

The ERC-7677 paymaster URL carries a credential in its path (`/v2/paymaster/<token>`). A project **client token** (`ppt_`) is publishable but only works from the project's allowed origins: with none set, or from another origin, the service refuses it with `project_origin_not_allowed`. A project **server key** (`ppk_`) is a secret: keep it on the server and never put it in a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable. The **free tier** (100 PEPU/day and 50 PEPU/hour per user, TapScore as the only target for now) needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app sent as `context.privyAccessToken` in the ERC-7677 request; it is not available to apps on their own Privy app. See [Credential Matrix](../infra/paymaster/auth.md).

## How the SDK resolves them

`resolvePepuEndpoints()` picks each value in this order: an explicit option, then the environment (the server variable, then the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable), then the hosted default in `PEPU_HOSTED`. A malformed URL throws `CONFIG_BAD_URL` naming the variable, never its value. It returns `bundlerUrl`, `paymasterUrl` (the complete ERC-7677 URL, `null` unless you configured one, because it needs a token) and `paymasterBaseUrl` (the service base: the hosted base unless `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` points elsewhere, in which case the `/v2/paymaster/<token>` tail is stripped). `createPaymasterApi`, the probes, `checkSponsorship` and `pepu doctor` default to the base; `createPepuPaymasterClient` needs the complete URL or a `paymasterToken`. `hostedErc7677Url(token)` builds `<hosted base>/v2/paymaster/<token>` and `hostedFreeTierUrl()` the public free-tier state route. `isHostedSponsorshipLive()` is `true` only when the hosted bundler and paymaster base are both set.

| Value | Explicit option | Server variable | Browser variable | Hosted default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RPC | `rpcUrl` | `PEPU_RPC_URL` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_RPC_URL` | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Bundler | `bundlerUrl` | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` |
| Paymaster ERC-7677 URL | `paymasterUrl` | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | none (needs your token) |
| Paymaster service base | `baseUrl` (`createPaymasterApi`) | base of `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | base of `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` |

## Contract registry

Deployed addresses in the SDK registry (`getPepuAddresses()`), for quick copying. Notes, bytecode sizes and do-not-substitute warnings are on [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md). PepuSwap's own non-canonical contracts are on [PepuSwap Addresses](../contracts/pepuswap.md).

| Key | Name | Address |
|---|---|---|
| `create2Factory` | CREATE2 Deterministic Deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` |
| `multicall3` | Multicall3 | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` |
| `permit2` | Permit2 | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` |
| `entryPoint06` | ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` |
| `entryPoint07` | ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` |
| `kernelFactory` | Kernel v3 Account Factory | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` |
| `kernelMetaFactory` | Kernel MetaFactory | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` |
| `ecdsaValidator` | Kernel ECDSA Validator | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` |
| `paymaster` | Sponsored Paymaster v2 (PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7, alias of paymasterV2) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` |
| `kernelImplementation` | Kernel v3.1 Implementation | `0xbAC849bB641841b44E965fb01A4Bf5F074F84B4d` |
| `kernelEcdsaSignerModule` | Kernel ECDSA Signer (permission signer module) | `0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF` |
| `kernelCallPolicyV004` | ZeroDev Call Policy v0.0.4 | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` |
| `kernelTimestampPolicy` | ZeroDev Timestamp Policy | `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` |
| `tapScore` | TapScore | `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` |
| `paymasterV1` | Verifying Paymaster v1 (PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7) - RETIRED | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` |
| `paymasterV2` | Sponsored Paymaster v2 (PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` |

## Hosted-URL swap (maintainers)

The only place the hosted URLs are set is `PEPU_HOSTED` in `packages/sdk/src/endpoints.ts`. To change them: edit it, rebuild the SDK, run `node scripts/gen-docs.mjs`, run `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/mcp snapshots`, then release the SDK and the MCP server together. See `RELEASING.md`.

## What to expect

- `pepu_health_check` and `pepu_sponsorship_status` report "not configured" for the bundler and paymaster until you set the variables or the hosted URLs exist.
- `node scripts/check-docs-parity.mjs` verifies the addresses and counts on the docs pages against the SDK registry.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_BAD_URL` | A URL variable is not a valid http(s) URL | Fix the variable the message names |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` for the paymaster | No complete ERC-7677 URL: it always embeds a token, so there is no tokenless default | Set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, or pass `paymasterToken` |
| Browser calls to the bundler fail with CORS errors | The bundler does not allow your origin | See [Operating the Bundler](../infra/bundler/operating.md) |

## Related

- [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md)
- [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md)
- [Environment Variables](env-vars.md)
- [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md)

# Environment Variables

Every environment variable used by the templates, the SDK, the MCP server and the services: which component reads it, whether it is required, whether it is secret, and a placeholder. Never put real values in docs, commits or chat.

Derived from `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS`, `PRIVY_ENV`, `PEPU_ENV`, the templates' `.env.example` files and the services' `.env.example` files.

## Prerequisites

None. `npm run doctor` in a template checks its own variables.

## App and SDK variables

| Name | Read by | Required | Secret | Example placeholder |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (alias `PRIVY_APP_ID`) | Provider, `/privy/server`, doctor | All templates | No (public) | `<privy-app-id>` |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | `/privy/server`, `/session/server`, `/combo` | All templates | **Yes** | `<privy-app-secret>` |
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | `/session/server` | `game-app` | **Yes** | `<base64-pkcs8-private-key>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (alias `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`) | `createSessionRoutes` | `game-app` | No | `<key-quorum-id>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `game-app` scope | `game-app` | No | `0x<contract>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC20_ADDRESS` | `token-gated-app` | One of the two gate addresses | No | `0x<erc20>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC721_ADDRESS` | `token-gated-app` | One of the two | No | `0x<erc721>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `nft-mint` | `nft-mint` | No | `0x<nft>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMASTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `sponsored-demo` (deposit proof) | Optional; defaults to the v2 paymaster `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` | No | same |
| `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `resolvePepuEndpoints`, `/combo`, `/aa`, MCP, doctor | `sponsored-session-app`; any sponsorship | **Yes** (treat as a credential) | Optional; defaults to `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (local: `http://localhost:4337`) |
| `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | Same | Same | **Yes** (embeds a token) | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project server key>` (local: `http://localhost:8788/paymaster/<your-app-key>`). The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token, so there is no tokenless default; the hosted base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` is the default for the REST client and probes |
| `PEPU_RPC_URL` | SDK server entries, doctor, MCP | Optional; default is the public RPC | Only if it embeds a key | `<authenticated-rpc-url>` |
| `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` | `/session/server`, `/combo` | Optional; default 15, clamped 1 to 1440 | No | `15` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_RPC_URL` | `resolvePepuEndpoints` (browser variants) | Optional | Visible to every visitor | Avoid for credentials |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_NETWORK` | Doctor shape check only | Optional | No | `mainnet` (the only valid value) |

Precedence in `resolvePepuEndpoints`: explicit option, then the server variable, then the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variant, then the hosted default (`PEPU_HOSTED`: the bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and the paymaster base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; the complete ERC-7677 URL is `null` until you supply a token). The names are exported as `PEPU_ENV`, `PEPU_PUBLIC_ENV` and `PRIVY_ENV`.

## Per-template matrix

| Template | Required | Optional |
|---|---|---|
| `consumer-app` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | none |
| `game-app` | the two above, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES`, `PEPU_RPC_URL` |
| `token-gated-app` | the two Privy vars, plus at least one of the gate addresses | both gate addresses |
| `nft-mint` | the two Privy vars, `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | none |
| `sponsored-demo` | the two Privy vars | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMASTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` |
| `sponsored-session-app` | the two Privy vars, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES`, `PEPU_RPC_URL` |

## MCP server

No API key. Optional: `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (sponsorship tools) and `PEPU_RPC_URL`. Everything else uses public PEPU RPC and pepuscan's public REST API.

## Services (operators)

| Name | Component | Secret | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ALTO_RPC_URL` | Bundler | **Yes** (embeds the RPC key) | RPC for Alto |
| `ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS` | Bundler | **Yes** | Funded submitter key or keys |
| `PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Paymaster policy service | secret: the second | Verify user tokens |
| `PAYMASTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`, `CHAIN_ID`, `ENTRY_POINT_ADDRESS`, `PORT`, `DB_PATH` | Policy service | No | Chain and paymaster config |
| `PAYMASTER_SIGNER_PRIVATE_KEY` | Policy service (loaded from a gitignored keys file) | **Yes** | Signs approvals |
| `USER_HOURLY_SPEND_CAP_WEI`, `USER_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_WEI`, `USER_LIFETIME_SPEND_CAP_WEI`, count caps, `GLOBAL_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_WEI` | Policy service | No | Caps; size above the first-operation reservation |
| `ADMIN_TOKEN` | Policy service | **Yes** | Enables the circuit-breaker reset endpoint |
| `PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOW_ACCOUNT_DEPLOYMENT` | Policy service | No | ERC-7677 endpoint controls |
| `SPONSORSHIP_V2_ENABLED` and the `SPONSORSHIP_V2_*`, `FREE_TIER_*`, `PROJECT_*`, `SPONSORSHIP_*` family | Policy service v2 (on in the hosted service; off by default in a fresh run) | `SPONSORSHIP_ADMIN_TOKEN` is secret | Tiered paymaster |

Full lists: [Operating the Bundler](../infra/bundler/operating.md), [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](../infra/paymaster/policy-and-caps.md), [Paymaster Overview](../infra/paymaster/overview.md).

## Public versus secret rules

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_` means bundled into client JavaScript. Use it only for the App ID, the quorum id and contract addresses.
- Server-only code never reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_` secrets.
- `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` are credentials in practice: keep them server-side.
- Restart the dev server after editing `.env.local`; Next.js reads it once.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` | A required variable is empty | Set it, restart |
| `CONFIG_BAD_URL` | A URL variable is not http(s) | Fix the value (the message names the variable, not its value) |
| Doctor says `placeholder` | Value like `your-app-id` | Replace it |

## Related

- [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md)
- [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md)
- [Error Reference](errors.md)
