Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/reference/errors

# Error Reference


Every error code the SDK, the MCP server and the paymaster client can return: what it means, why it happens, how to fix it, the HTTP status route handlers use and whether a retry can help. Each code has a stable anchor, so the `docsUrl` on a `PepuError` (`https://docs.pepeunchained.com/reference/errors#<CODE>`) lands on its entry. Paste an error into [`explainError`](../sdk/errors.md) or the MCP tool `pepu_explain_error` to get its entry directly.

## Prerequisites

- None. For the SDK functions that produce these errors, see [SDK Error Catalog](../sdk/errors.md).

## Index

| Code | HTTP | Retryable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`CONFIG_BAD_URL`](#CONFIG_BAD_URL) | 500 | no | Invalid endpoint URL |
| [`CONFIG_MISSING_ENV`](#CONFIG_MISSING_ENV) | 500 | no | Missing environment variable |
| [`CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH`](#CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH) | 500 | no | Origin is not allowed by Privy |
| [`CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN`](#CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN) | 500 | no | Embedded wallet never appears after login |
| [`CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD`](#CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD) | 500 | no | Privy dashboard misconfiguration |
| [`CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY`](#CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY) | 500 | no | Server-only module imported in the browser |
| [`AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`](#AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN) | 401 | no | Invalid or missing Privy access token |
| [`WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN`](#WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN) | 400 | no | Coinbase Smart Wallet does not support PEPU |
| [`WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE`](#WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE) | 400 | no | An injected browser wallet is the active account |
| [`WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED`](#WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED) | 409 | yes | User has no embedded wallet yet |
| [`PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741`](#PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741) | 502 | no | Privy rejects server-side eth_sendTransaction on PEPU |
| [`PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH`](#PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH) | 500 | no | Privy authorization key does not match the wallet owner |
| [`POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG`](#POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG) | 400 | no | Privy policy or rule name is too long |
| [`POLICY_UNSCOPED`](#POLICY_UNSCOPED) | 400 | no | Session policy is not scoped |
| [`SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH`](#SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH) | 409 | no | Session approval does not match |
| [`SESSION_EXPIRED`](#SESSION_EXPIRED) | 410 | no | Session expired |
| [`SESSION_NONE`](#SESSION_NONE) | 409 | no | No active session |
| [`BUNDLER_AA_FAILED`](#BUNDLER_AA_FAILED) | 502 | no | EntryPoint rejected the UserOperation |
| [`BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE`](#BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE) | 502 | yes | Bundler or paymaster is unreachable |
| [`PAYMASTER_API_ERROR`](#PAYMASTER_API_ERROR) | 502 | no | Paymaster API request failed |
| [`PAYMASTER_CAP`](#PAYMASTER_CAP) | 429 | yes | Sponsorship cap reached |
| [`PAYMASTER_DENIED`](#PAYMASTER_DENIED) | 403 | no | Paymaster denied the sponsorship |
| [`PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED`](#PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED) | 403 | no | Paymaster refused the call destination |
| [`PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`](#PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE) | 429 | yes | Free tier cannot sponsor this operation |
| [`PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](#PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED) | 401 | no | A verified Privy account is required |
| [`PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE`](#PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE) | 429 | yes | Sponsorship project has no balance |
| [`PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`](#PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED) | 403 | no | Paymaster refused the request origin |
| [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED`](#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED) | 409 | no | Sponsorship project is not claimed on-chain |
| [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED`](#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED) | 403 | no | Project owner changed since the credentials were issued |
| [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED`](#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED) | 403 | no | Sponsorship project is paused |
| [`PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED`](#PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED) | 429 | yes | Paymaster API rate limit |
| [`PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED`](#PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED) | 401 | no | Paymaster owner session missing or expired |
| [`PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE`](#PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE) | 502 | yes | Paymaster service is unreachable |
| [`MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS`](#MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS) | 500 | no | Canonical Multicall3 address used on PEPU |
| [`TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT`](#TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT) | 502 | yes | Gas limit too low |
| [`TX_NONCE_RACE`](#TX_NONCE_RACE) | 409 | yes | Nonce conflict |
| [`TX_REVERTED`](#TX_REVERTED) | 502 | no | Transaction reverted |
| [`UNKNOWN`](#UNKNOWN) | 500 | no | Unknown error |

## Configuration

<a id="CONFIG_BAD_URL"></a>

### CONFIG_BAD_URL

**Invalid endpoint URL**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** A configured bundler, paymaster or RPC URL is not a valid http(s) URL.
- **Fix:** Use a full URL such as https://bundler.example.com.

<a id="CONFIG_MISSING_ENV"></a>

### CONFIG_MISSING_ENV

**Missing environment variable**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** A required environment variable is not set.
- **Fix:** Set the listed variables (see .env.example) and restart the process.

<a id="CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH"></a>

### CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH

**Origin is not allowed by Privy**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The page origin (scheme, host and port) is not in the Privy app's allowed origins. A different dev port is the usual cause.
- **Fix:** Add the exact origin, including the port, to Privy dashboard Allowed origins.

<a id="CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN"></a>

### CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN

**Embedded wallet never appears after login**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The dashboard's automatic embedded wallet creation is off, so createOnLogin never resolves.
- **Fix:** Create the wallet server-side with the ensure-wallet route (createEnsureWalletRoute), or enable creation in the Privy dashboard.

<a id="CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD"></a>

### CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD

**Privy dashboard misconfiguration**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** A required Privy dashboard setting is missing.
- **Fix:** Run checkPrivyDashboardConfig() and follow its fix list.

<a id="CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY"></a>

### CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY

**Server-only module imported in the browser**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** A server entry point was bundled into client code.
- **Fix:** Import server entries only from route handlers, server actions and scripts.

## Auth and wallet

<a id="AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN"></a>

### AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN

**Invalid or missing Privy access token**

- **HTTP status:** 401
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The request carried no bearer token, or Privy could not verify it.
- **Fix:** Send Authorization: Bearer <getAccessToken()> and verify the token server-side.

<a id="WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN"></a>

### WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN

**Coinbase Smart Wallet does not support PEPU**

- **HTTP status:** 400
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** Coinbase Smart Wallet is a smart-contract wallet on chains it knows; PEPU (97741) is not one of them, and it floods the console with unsupported-chain errors.
- **Fix:** Pin Coinbase to eoaOnly via createPepuPrivyConfig() from @pepu-chain/sdk/privy.

<a id="WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE"></a>

### WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE

**An injected browser wallet is the active account**

- **HTTP status:** 400
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** wagmi's active account is a browser extension rather than the Privy embedded wallet.
- **Fix:** Pin the embedded wallet with useActiveWalletPin() from @pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi.

<a id="WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED"></a>

### WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED

**User has no embedded wallet yet**

- **HTTP status:** 409
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** The user is signed in but no embedded Ethereum wallet exists.
- **Fix:** Call the ensure-wallet route (useEnsureWallet or WalletGate) before acting.

## Privy

<a id="PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741"></a>

### PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741

**Privy rejects server-side eth_sendTransaction on PEPU**

- **HTTP status:** 502
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** Privy's server-side send path does not know chain 97741 and rejects it. Signing works; sending does not.
- **Fix:** Sign with eth_signTransaction on the server and broadcast the raw transaction yourself (signAndBroadcast from @pepu-chain/sdk/session).

<a id="PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH"></a>

### PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH

**Privy authorization key does not match the wallet owner**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** Privy returned 401 'No valid authorization keys or user signing keys available': the server's PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY is not a signer on the wallet, or the key quorum id differs from the one the user granted.
- **Fix:** Make sure PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY is the private half of the key whose quorum id is NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID, and that the user granted that quorum as a signer.

## Session keys and policies

<a id="POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG"></a>

### POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG

**Privy policy or rule name is too long**

- **HTTP status:** 400
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** Privy rejects policy and rule names of 50 or more characters (the real limit is 49).
- **Fix:** Shorten the policy or rule name to 49 characters or fewer.

<a id="POLICY_UNSCOPED"></a>

### POLICY_UNSCOPED

**Session policy is not scoped**

- **HTTP status:** 400
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** A session policy needs a target contract, at least one function and an expiry.
- **Fix:** Pass contractAddress, functions and expiresAtUnixSeconds to buildSessionPolicy().

<a id="SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH"></a>

### SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH

**Session approval does not match**

- **HTTP status:** 409
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The approval was made for another account, permission id or mode.
- **Fix:** Re-run prepare, have the owner sign again, then activate.

<a id="SESSION_EXPIRED"></a>

### SESSION_EXPIRED

**Session expired**

- **HTTP status:** 410
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The session's expiry has passed.
- **Fix:** Grant a new session.

<a id="SESSION_NONE"></a>

### SESSION_NONE

**No active session**

- **HTTP status:** 409
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The user has not granted a session, or it was revoked.
- **Fix:** Ask the user to grant a session first.

## Bundler

<a id="BUNDLER_AA_FAILED"></a>

### BUNDLER_AA_FAILED

**EntryPoint rejected the UserOperation**

- **HTTP status:** 502
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The EntryPoint reported FailedOp with an AAxx code during validation or execution.
- **Fix:** Read the AAxx code: AA21 prefund missing, AA23 signature or validation reverted, AA25 invalid nonce, AA31/AA33/AA34 paymaster problems.

<a id="BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE"></a>

### BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE

**Bundler or paymaster is unreachable**

- **HTTP status:** 502
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** The request to the bundler or paymaster URL failed before any response.
- **Fix:** Check PEPU_BUNDLER_URL and PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL. Use checkSponsorship() to see which one failed.

## Paymaster and sponsorship

<a id="PAYMASTER_API_ERROR"></a>

### PAYMASTER_API_ERROR

**Paymaster API request failed**

- **HTTP status:** 502
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The paymaster API returned an error that has no more specific PEPU code.
- **Fix:** Read error.details (HTTP status and the service's error code) and the OpenAPI spec for that route.

<a id="PAYMASTER_CAP"></a>

### PAYMASTER_CAP

**Sponsorship cap reached**

- **HTTP status:** 429
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** A daily, per-sender or per-operation sponsorship cap was hit.
- **Fix:** Wait for the cap window to reset, or raise the project's daily and sender limits.

<a id="PAYMASTER_DENIED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_DENIED

**Paymaster denied the sponsorship**

- **HTTP status:** 403
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The paymaster rejected the credential or the sender (for example unknown_or_invalid_app_credential or sender_not_owned_by_token_user).
- **Fix:** Check the app credential or token, and that the smart account belongs to the user whose access token you sent.

<a id="PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED

**Paymaster refused the call destination**

- **HTTP status:** 403
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The UserOperation targets a contract that is not on the project's target allowlist.
- **Fix:** Add the contract to the project's targets, or sponsor only calls to allowed targets.

<a id="PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE"></a>

### PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE

**Free tier cannot sponsor this operation**

- **HTTP status:** 429
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** The free tier is disabled, its pool is empty, or the operation is larger than the per-op cap.
- **Fix:** Deposit into your own project and use its credentials, or retry later.

<a id="PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED

**A verified Privy account is required**

- **HTTP status:** 401
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The free tier (and any project with requireIdentity on) only sponsors users with a verified Privy access token.
- **Fix:** Send the user's Privy access token as Authorization: Bearer (or context.privyAccessToken for ERC-7677).

<a id="PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE"></a>

### PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE

**Sponsorship project has no balance**

- **HTTP status:** 429
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** The project's paymaster deposit cannot cover this operation.
- **Fix:** Deposit more PEPU to the project, then retry.

<a id="PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED

**Paymaster refused the request origin**

- **HTTP status:** 403
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The request Origin is not on the project's allowlist.
- **Fix:** Add the exact origin (scheme, host and port) to the project's allowed origins.

<a id="PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED

**Sponsorship project is not claimed on-chain**

- **HTTP status:** 409
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** Deposits can sit in an unclaimed project, but nothing is sponsored until its owner has claimed it on-chain (the contract reports ProjectNotClaimed, the service project_not_claimed_onchain).
- **Fix:** Prove the Privy app (requestClaimAttestation from @pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server), call claimProject, then configureProject (setTargets, setDailyLimit, setSenderDailyLimit).

<a id="PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED

**Project owner changed since the credentials were issued**

- **HTTP status:** 403
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The on-chain owner of the project is no longer the address the off-chain credentials were issued to (an ownership transfer or re-claim completed).
- **Fix:** As the new owner, sign in with SIWE, register the project again and rotate the client token and server key.

<a id="PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED

**Sponsorship project is paused**

- **HTTP status:** 403
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The project owner paused sponsorship on-chain.
- **Fix:** The owner can resume it with setPaused(projectId, false).

<a id="PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED

**Paymaster API rate limit**

- **HTTP status:** 429
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** Too many requests to the paymaster API from this IP or account.
- **Fix:** Back off for the Retry-After interval (error.details.retryAfterSeconds when present).

<a id="PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED"></a>

### PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED

**Paymaster owner session missing or expired**

- **HTTP status:** 401
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** Owner endpoints need a SIWE session token (1 h lifetime) for the project's current on-chain owner.
- **Fix:** Call loginWithWallet() on the paymaster API client, then retry.

<a id="PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE"></a>

### PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE

**Paymaster service is unreachable**

- **HTTP status:** 502
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** The request to the paymaster service failed before any response (network error, DNS failure or timeout).
- **Fix:** Check PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL and your network. The hosted service is https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com; run checkSponsorship() or probePaymaster() for detail.

## Transactions and chain

<a id="MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS"></a>

### MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS

**Canonical Multicall3 address used on PEPU**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** PEPU's Multicall3 is not at the canonical 0xcA11...CA11 address.
- **Fix:** Use getMulticall3() or pepuMulticall() from @pepu-chain/sdk, or the pepuMainnet chain object, which carries the right address.

<a id="TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT"></a>

### TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT

**Gas limit too low**

- **HTTP status:** 502
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** Nitro gas estimation undershoots on PEPU: the L1 data component is not covered by the plain estimate.
- **Fix:** Add headroom to the estimate, 20% via withGasLimitBuffer() from @pepu-chain/sdk/session.

<a id="TX_NONCE_RACE"></a>

### TX_NONCE_RACE

**Nonce conflict**

- **HTTP status:** 409
- **Retryable:** yes
- **Cause:** Two transactions raced for one nonce, or a replacement was underpriced.
- **Fix:** Serialize sends per account (a lock), re-read the pending nonce, and retry.

<a id="TX_REVERTED"></a>

### TX_REVERTED

**Transaction reverted**

- **HTTP status:** 502
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The contract call reverted.
- **Fix:** Decode the revert reason with explainError(<revert data>) and check arguments, allowances and balances.

<a id="UNKNOWN"></a>

### UNKNOWN

**Unknown error**

- **HTTP status:** 500
- **Retryable:** no
- **Cause:** The error did not match any known PEPU failure.
- **Fix:** Read the original message. Run pepu_known_gotchas in the MCP server, or search the docs.

## Paymaster denial reasons

The policy service answers a denied request with a `reason` string. The SDK maps every reason to one of the codes above with `mapPaymasterReason(reason)` and `paymasterReasonToError(reason, message)` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`. An unknown reason (a newer service) maps to `PAYMASTER_DENIED`. Reasons marked v1 come from the v1 paymaster; the rest come from the v2 policy service, which is built but not deployed.

| Reason | Service | Maps to | Retryable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unknown_or_invalid_app_credential` | v2 | [`PAYMASTER_DENIED`](#PAYMASTER_DENIED) | no |
| `app_suspended` | v2 | [`PAYMASTER_DENIED`](#PAYMASTER_DENIED) | no |
| `invalid_or_expired_token` | v2 | [`AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`](#AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN) | no |

## Bundler and AA failures

A bundler rejection surfaces as `BUNDLER_AA_FAILED` with the EntryPoint's `AAxx` code in the message (for example `AA21 didn't pay prefund`, `AA25 invalid account nonce`, `AA33 reverted` for a paymaster revert). A network or CORS failure surfaces as `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE`. The JSON-RPC error table for the bundler is on [Bundler JSON-RPC API](../infra/bundler/api.md); the paymaster HTTP error table is on [REST API v1](../infra/paymaster/rest-api-v1.md) and [REST API v2](../infra/paymaster/rest-api-v2.md).

## What to expect

- `pepu_health_check` and `pepu_sponsorship_status` probe the hosted bundler and the paymaster service base by default; set the variables to point elsewhere.
- `node scripts/check-docs-parity.mjs` verifies the addresses and counts on the docs pages against the SDK registry.

## Common failures

- You see a code that is not on this page: you are on an older SDK. Upgrade `@pepu-chain/sdk`, or run the error text through `pepu_explain_error`.
- You see `UNKNOWN`: nothing in the catalog matched. Read the original `cause`, and see [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md).

- [MCP Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md)

# Glossary

Terms used across the PEPU docs, alphabetical.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Alto | The open-source ERC-4337 bundler PEPU hosts at `bundler.pepeunchained.com`, configured with `--chain-type arbitrum`. |
| Approval | The owner's enable signature plus policy parameters for a Kernel session. Holds no secret. |
| Authorization key | A P-256 key whose public half is registered in Privy; the server signs signing requests with the private half. See [Authorization Keys](../privy/authorization-keys.md). |
| Bundler | A service that accepts UserOperations and submits them through the EntryPoint. |
| Call policy | A ZeroDev policy contract limiting a session to listed targets, selectors and value. PEPU has v0.0.4. |
| Chain ID | `97741` for mainnet. `3409` is the dead V1 chain. |
| Client token | A project's publishable paymaster credential (`ppt_`). Works only from the project's allowed origins. Used in the Privy Smart Wallets dashboard URL. See [Credential Matrix](../infra/paymaster/auth.md). |
| Combination | Google login plus one on-chain session plus sponsorship. See [End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md). |
| Embedded wallet | The EOA Privy creates for a user at login. |
| EntryPoint | The ERC-4337 singleton. v0.7 is `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032`. |
| `eoaOnly` | The Coinbase Wallet preference that avoids Coinbase Smart Wallet, which does not support chain 97741. |
| ERC-4337 | Account abstraction through UserOperations, bundlers and paymasters. |
| ERC-7677 | The paymaster JSON-RPC interface: `pm_getPaymasterStubData`, `pm_getPaymasterData`. |
| Free tier | v2: 100 PEPU per Privy user per day and 50 PEPU per hour, funded by the chain, for PEPU's own Privy app only. |
| Kernel | ZeroDev's smart account. PEPU uses v3.1. |
| Key quorum | A group of authorization keys Privy accepts as a signer; its id is `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`. |
| Multicall3 | Batch-read contract. PEPU's is `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`, not the canonical address. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md). |
| Owner | The embedded wallet that controls a Kernel account. Also, the owner of a v2 paymaster project. |
| Paymaster | A contract plus policy service that pays UserOperation gas. v2 is `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`; v1 `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` is retired. |
| Permission id | The id the chain derives for a session key plus policies; the server compares it with the approval. |
| Permit2 | Uniswap's token approval contract, at the canonical address on PEPU. |
| Policy (Privy) | A Privy rule set attached to a session signer; names at most 49 characters. |
| Policy service | The off-chain ERC-7677 service deciding sponsorship. |
| Privy Smart Wallets | Privy's dashboard feature that builds and manages a Kernel account for the embedded wallet and sends from the browser. Path 2. Needs the Smart Wallets dashboard setting. |
| Project (v2) | A paymaster budget keyed by `keccak256(bytes(appId))`. |
| Server key | A project's secret paymaster credential (`ppk_`), for backends, scripts and the session routes. Never in a browser. |
| Session key | A key allowed to act within limits without a popup. Privy mode or Kernel mode. |
| Session signer | Privy's delegated-actions mechanism on an embedded wallet. |
| SessionStore | The SDK interface storing Kernel session records. `createMemoryStore()` is dev-grade. |
| Smart account | A contract account. Here, a Kernel account with a different address from its owner. See [Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md). |
| Smart account paths | Path 0 plain embedded wallet, Path 1 ZeroDev-native (the SDK builds the Kernel account), Path 2 Privy Smart Wallets (Privy builds it). See [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md). |
| TEE execution | Privy's `user-controlled-server-wallets-only` mode, reassembling keys in an enclave. |
| Timestamp policy | A ZeroDev policy limiting a permission to a validity window. |
| UserOperation | The ERC-4337 transaction-like object a smart account sends. |
| WalletGate | SDK component that renders children once the embedded wallet exists, provisioning it first. |

## Related

- [FAQ](faq.md)
- [The Three Pillars](../get-started/pillars.md)
- [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)

# FAQ

Short answers to questions builders ask first, with links to the page that has the detail.

## Chain and network

**Which chain do I build on?** Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet, chain ID `97741`. Testnet `97740` is out of scope (no faucet, no indexed explorer, no deployed infrastructure). `3409` is the dead V1 chain. See [V1 vs V2](../get-started/v1-vs-v2.md).

**Why is gas so high in gwei?** PEPU is a low-value token; the base fee is around 12,500 gwei and a transfer still costs a fraction of a cent. Do not hardcode a lower price. See [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md).

**Is Multicall3 at the usual address?** No. PEPU's is `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`; the canonical address has no code. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md).

## Privy and login

**Login fails with a blocked iframe or 403.** The origin, including the port, is not in Allowed origins. Next.js may have moved to 3001. See [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

**"Creating your wallet..." never ends.** Use `PepuPrivyProvider` and `WalletGate`, which provision the wallet server-side. See [Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md).

**Do I need Smart Wallets in the Privy dashboard?** Only for the Privy Smart Wallets sponsorship transport. Not for login, Privy sessions or the combination.

**Which smart account setup should I use: ZeroDev-native or Privy Smart Wallets?** ZeroDev-native (the SDK builds the Kernel account) if you want sessions, the free tier, a server or a bot; Privy Smart Wallets for one gasless button in a client-only app. Users who just pay their own gas need neither. See [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md).

**Why does my users' balance show 0 but they transacted?** With a smart account there are two addresses. See [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md).

## Sessions and sponsorship

**Privy session or Kernel session?** Privy: least setup, scope enforced by Privy, user pays gas. Kernel: scope enforced on-chain, usually sponsored, uses the hosted bundler and a funded project. See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md).

**Is gas sponsorship available?** Yes. The hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) are live on mainnet. You bring a project (claim, set targets and limits, deposit, token); the free tier is only for PEPU's own Privy app. Check live with `pepu_sponsorship_status`, or run your own from `services/`. See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md).

**Why did the second tap fail with `trailing-hour spend ... would exceed cap`?** Per-user caps are below the worst-case reservation (about 20.5 PEPU for a session's first operation, 6.9 later). Raise them.

**What is the tiered paymaster?** v2: a free tier (100 PEPU per Privy user per day and 50 PEPU per hour, PEPU's own Privy app only) plus project deposits. Deployed on mainnet as deployed. See [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md).

**Does revoking a Kernel session uninstall it on-chain?** No. The server key is deleted at once; the grant lapses at expiry. Keep sessions short.

## Agents and MCP

**How do I give my coding agent PEPU facts?** Install the MCP server (`npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`) and, for Claude Code, the plugin. See [Build with an AI Coding Agent](../get-started/ai-assisted.md).

**Can the agent set up Privy?** It can scaffold, write env keys without printing secrets, generate the authorization key and check config. You must create the Privy app, copy the App ID and secret, and register the public key in the dashboard.

## Related

- [Glossary](glossary.md)
- [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md)
- [Error Reference](errors.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/reference/changelog

# Changelog

Dated changes to the dev kit packages and docs, newest first. Each entry lists what a builder can now do, not the commit log. Versions are those in the repository on the date of each entry.

## 2026-10-22: @pepu-chain/mcp 0.2.8, plugin 0.4.4

- **Decode any transaction's events in one call.** The new `pepu_decode_tx_logs` tool takes a transaction hash and returns each log with its event name, signature and named arguments, with big integers as decimal strings, without you supplying an ABI. Each log is resolved from your optional ABI fragments, then the verified ABI of the emitting contract on pepuscan (proxy implementations included), then pepuscan's own decoding re-checked locally against the raw log, then a built-in set of standards (ERC-20 and ERC-721, WPEPU, the ERC-4337 EntryPoint, Uniswap V2 and V3 pools), and finally a public signature database that names the event and infers its indexed parameters. Every result records its `source` and a `lookups` summary shows what was consulted; logs that nothing decodes are listed with their `topic0` and candidate signatures. Pass `offline: true` to skip every network lookup when pepuscan is unreachable.
- **Decode the call as well.** The top-level input is decoded the same way, from your function fragments, the verified ABI of the target contract, pepuscan's decoded call, the built-in functions and a public signature database, so an EntryPoint `handleOps` bundle or a contract call arrives as named arguments. For a `handleOps` bundle the result points to the decoded `UserOperationEvent` logs; inner account calldata is not decoded.
- **UserOperation hashes work too.** With `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` set, a UserOperation hash is resolved to its bundle transaction, the same way `pepu_explain_tx` does it.
- **The MCP server now has 33 tools.** The tool reference, the plugin description and the `pepu-debug-transaction` skill describe the new tool, and `pepu_explain_tx` points to it for decoded event arguments.

## 2026-10-19: @pepu-chain/sdk 0.2.4, @pepu-chain/mcp 0.2.7, create-pepu-app 0.1.5, plugin 0.4.3

Fixes from a clean-room test of the published packages.

- **The hosted paymaster is reported healthy.** `probePaymaster` used to POST `pm_getPaymasterStubData` to the service root, which the v2 service answers with a REST 404, so `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` was reported `ok: false` and `pepu_paymaster_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status` and `checkSponsorship` said it was down. The probe now checks `GET /health`, `GET /v2/free-tier` and the v2 ERC-7677 route `POST /v2/paymaster/<token>` (a placeholder token and empty params when only the service base is given; nothing is sent on chain). A structured JSON-RPC error such as invalid params or an unknown credential counts as responding (`erc7677: "needs-credential"`); only network errors, non-JSON answers and 5xx are `"not-responding"`. The result gains `freeTierOk` and `erc7677Route`.
- **New error code `PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE`.** A paymaster probe or REST call that cannot reach the service now fails with `PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE` instead of `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE`, with a hint that names the hosted base and the `/v2/paymaster/<client token>` endpoint. A reachable host whose ERC-7677 route does not answer JSON-RPC is `PAYMASTER_API_ERROR`.
- **`probePaymaster()` and `probeBundler()` default to the hosted services** and accept `string | null | undefined`, so `probePaymaster(resolvePepuEndpoints().paymasterBaseUrl)` type-checks under strict mode.
- **`PEPU_MISSING_PEER` messages are complete.** Every React entry now lists `react-dom` with `react`, the message points to `npx create-pepu-app` as the zero-config path, and, for entries that use `@privy-io/react-auth`, `permissionless` or ZeroDev, it shows the `"overrides": { "viem": "$viem" }` entry that resolves a viem peer conflict (the templates already carry it). The install tables in the SDK README and the SDK reference follow `scripts/peer-requirements.mjs`.
- **Windows clones from deep folders.** Unused vendored Solidity sources (OpenZeppelin governance, token extensions, proxy and access-control extensions, and others that nothing imports) are removed from `services/paymaster/contracts/lib`. The longest tracked path went from 126 to 112 characters, and CI fails above 112. The compiled paymaster bytecode is unchanged: the pinned creation-code hashes for v1 and v2 are identical, verified from a `git archive` extraction. The clone instructions add `git clone -c core.longpaths=true`.
- **Stale text.** The `sponsored-session-app` description no longer says the hosted services are not public; it states that the hosted bundler and paymaster are the defaults. Status wording is removed from the template READMEs and agent files.
- **`create-pepu-app` no longer prints the Node 24 `DEP0190` warning.** Installs and `npm view` run through a single command string on Windows and a direct spawn elsewhere, never `shell: true` with an args array.
- **`PepuError` documents its positional constructor**, `new PepuError(code, message?, options?)`.
- **Docs links point at `docs.pepeunchained.com`.** Error hints (`errorDocsUrl`, `PEPU_ERRORS_DOCS_URL`), Privy requirement fixes, the MCP `pepu_get_docs` tool, package homepages, the plugin manifest, skills and template READMEs all use the published docs domain.
- **`create-pepu-app` checks npm for the exact SDK version it bundles** before writing `^<version>` to `package.json`, and uses the bundled copy when that version is not published yet.

## 2026-10-18: @pepu-chain/sdk 0.2.3, @pepu-chain/mcp 0.2.6, create-pepu-app 0.1.4, plugin 0.4.2

Documentation and wording release. Guides, READMEs, templates, skills and MCP text are rewritten in a reference-documentation voice, the docs gain diagrams and live-demo screenshots, and the GitBook site configuration (`gitbook-docs.yaml`) is added. No API changes.

## 2026-10-15: @pepu-chain/mcp 0.2.5, plugin 0.4.1

New guide: [Smart account paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md) explains ZeroDev-native accounts built by the SDK versus Privy Smart Wallets versus plain embedded wallets, with a decision table. The quickstart is now a 10-minute zero-to-sponsored-transaction guide, the paymaster project guide is step by step with SDK and MCP routes, and the skills link the new guide. The MCP server bundles the refreshed docs and skills.

## 2026-10-15: create-pepu-app 0.1.3, @pepu-chain/mcp 0.2.4

Every template's `.env.example` now carries the full Privy dashboard checklist (allowed origins, login methods, embedded wallets, Coinbase `eoaOnly`, Smart Wallets status, authorization keys for game-app, paymaster credentials). `docs/privy/dashboard-settings.md` gains per-template requirements and the Smart Wallets table (Kernel v3.1, chain 97741, hosted bundler, paymaster URL with a project client token). The MCP server bundles the refreshed docs.

## 2026-10-15

### Fresh-account fixes for the combination: `@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.2, `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.3, `create-pepu-app` 0.1.2

Fixes for two failures that a first-time Google account hit on `sponsored-session-app` and an existing account did not.

- **First sign-in showed a red error.** The embedded wallet exists in the browser a moment before Privy's server lists it, so `status` answered 409 `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED`. The combo routes now look the user up again a few times (`provisioningWait`, default 3 retries), and `status` answers `{ active: false, provisioning: true }` (a normal 200) if the wallet is still not visible. `useSponsoredSession` keeps `statusLoading` true and re-checks with backoff (0.5 s to 5 s, about 30 s), and `grantKernelSession` retries `prepare` for about 6.5 s. Neither shows an error for this state.
- **The first tap was denied.** The paymaster service only recognized Privy Smart Wallets as "the user's account", but the combo flow creates a ZeroDev Kernel v3.1 account that Privy has never seen, so the service denied the first operation with `sender_not_owned_by_token_user`, before it even chose between the project and the free tier. The service now also accepts the Kernel v3.1 account (ECDSA validator, index 0) derived from one of the token user's own Privy embedded wallets (derivation via the factory's `getAddress`, pinned by a test vector from the SDK), and still denies any other sender. This is a service-side change; no app change is needed. A new user's first operation (about 20 PEPU reserved, because it deploys the account) now falls back to the free tier when the project balance cannot cover it.
- **The error named the wrong thing.** viem reports the service's denial as the generic "Missing or invalid parameters." `describeUserOpFailure` now reads the real denial and says, for example, `Paymaster denied the operation (sender_not_owned_by_token_user): ...`, with the matching catalog code and a specific hint.

`create-pepu-app` 0.1.2 vendors the 0.2.2 SDK and scaffolds `@pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.2`; the `sponsored-session-app` README and `.env.example` now describe the project-first, free-tier-fallback behaviour accurately. `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.3 pins exactly SDK 0.2.2.

## 2026-10-14

### Browser flow for the combination

Documented the browser flow for the Google login, on-chain Kernel session key and gas sponsorship combination in `sponsored-session-app`, against the hosted bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and the v2 paymaster `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`: Google sign-in to the embedded wallet, one Privy `eth_signTypedData_v4` signature on chain 97741, sponsored taps with no popup while the smart account stays at 0 PEPU, and revoke. The docs, skills, MCP text and READMEs describe the flow. The MCP server text changed (known gotcha and prompt), so it ships in `@pepu-chain/mcp@0.2.2`.

### `create-pepu-app` 0.1.1

Label fix only; the `features` vocabulary (`login`, `session`, `sponsor`) and `--list --json` shape are unchanged. The picker and `--list` showed every template's `login` feature as "Google login", but `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint` and `game-app` enable email, Google and wallet sign-in, and `sponsored-demo` and `sponsored-session-app` enable Google and email. The feature is now labelled "sign-in + embedded wallet", and the `consumer-app` and `sponsored-session-app` descriptions name the methods they enable. The vendored SDK is 0.2.1 and `--sdk npm` scaffolds `@pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.1`.

### `@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.1 and `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.1

Patch release with clean-room install fixes for the public packages. `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.1 depends on exactly `@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.1. `create-pepu-app` stays at 0.1.0, which ships the 0.2.0-era templates and scaffolds `@pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.1`.

- **Windows clone fixed.** `git clone` of the repository failed on Windows with "Filename too long" under the vendored Solidity libraries, which also broke `/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit`. Vendored test, docs, audit, certora, mock and sample files that the build never compiles were removed; the longest tracked path went from 150 to 126 characters, and CI fails above 130 (`scripts/check-path-length.mjs`). The compiled paymaster bytecode is unchanged: the pinned creation-code hashes for v1 and v2 are identical.
- **Clear errors for missing optional peers.** Importing a peer-dependent subpath (for example `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react` without `react` or `@privy-io/react-auth`) now throws `PEPU_MISSING_PEER` naming the subpath and the exact `npm i` command, instead of Node's "Cannot find package 'react' imported from dist/chunk-XXXX.js". Under Node the ESM entries load through a small guard (`node` export condition only; bundlers and browsers get the plain entry); CJS entries carry the guard inline. The SDK README and [SDK Reference](../sdk/reference.md#install-peers-per-subpath) gained an Install table (subpath, peers, one-line `npm i`) and a bundle command; `create-pepu-app` remains the recommended path because it scaffolds every peer.
- **Accurate health probes.** `probeBundler` and `pepu_bundler_health` reported `eth_sendUserOperation`, `eth_estimateUserOperationGas` and `eth_getUserOperationReceipt` as unsupported on the live Alto bundler, because Alto answers bad params of a known method with code `-32601` ("Validation error: ..."). Support is now judged from the message (only "method not found" and Alto's "Invalid discriminator value" mean unsupported), the calls still use deliberately invalid params so nothing is sent on-chain, and the verdict is only healthy when the chain, EntryPoint v0.7 and the three required methods are present (`missingRequiredMethods` lists any gap). `probePaymaster` and `pepu_paymaster_health` add `erc7677: "stub-ok" | "needs-credential" | "not-responding"`; without a client token the stub check is reported as not applicable (`erc7677StubOk` is `null`) instead of `false`, and a service that does not speak ERC-7677 JSON-RPC is no longer called healthy.
- **`getPepuAddresses()` shape.** The docs and TSDoc now say plainly that it returns an array of rows (`.find((r) => r.key === "paymaster")`). New `getPepuAddressMap()` returns the same rows keyed by contract name.
- **Docs.** The root README and the CLI page describe the packages on npm.

### Hosted endpoints live, v2 paymaster deployed, v1 retired

- **Hosted endpoints are live.** Bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) and paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default base for `createPaymasterApi`, the probes, `checkSponsorship` and `doctor`). The `/v2` routes are public (free-tier state, config, SIWE, projects, verify); `/v2/admin` is not exposed. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token, `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, so there is no tokenless default: `PEPU_HOSTED` is `{ bundlerUrl, paymasterBaseUrl, paymasterUrl: null }` and `isHostedSponsorshipLive()` returns true.
- **v2 paymaster deployed.** `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` is on PEPU mainnet at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (about block 10537341). The registry keys `paymasterV2` and `paymaster` point at it. Owner `0x5966dFaB11c8AEe767e0739083417D02f4a634A1`, manager `0x063Ab6C16c38D19A4bC76E7c39A4A0A73afCaBb0`, free pool seeded with 300 PEPU. Free tier per user: 100 PEPU a day and 50 PEPU an hour; free-tier targets are TapScore only for now.
- **v1 paymaster retired.** `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` has an EntryPoint deposit of 0, so it cannot sponsor anything. The registry entry `paymasterV1` has `retired: true`, and `getPepuAddresses` rows carry `retired`.
- **New SDK helpers.** `PEPU_HOSTED.paymasterBaseUrl`; `resolvePepuEndpoints()` also returns `paymasterBaseUrl`; `paymasterBaseOf(url)`; `hostedErc7677Url(token)` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`); `hostedFreeTierUrl()` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk`); `createPepuPaymasterClient` and `createPepuSponsoredClient` accept `paymasterToken`; `requirePaymasterUrl(explicit?, token?)`; `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` accepts `endpoints.paymasterToken` and `forwardPrivyToken` (default true: forwards the request's Bearer Privy token as ERC-7677 `context.privyAccessToken`; set false for a paymaster you do not trust with it).
- **MCP.** `pepu_project_balance` and `pepu_prepare_project_tx` default to the registry's deployed v2 paymaster (an explicit `paymaster` overrides). `pepu_paymaster_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status` and `pepu_health_check` probe the hosted bundler and the paymaster service base by default.
- **Token behaviour.** A project client token (`ppt_`) is publishable and works only from the project's allowed origins (otherwise `project_origin_not_allowed`); a server key (`ppk_`) is secret. The free tier needs a verified Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app; a third-party app's Privy token is ignored for billing, and the Privy Smart Wallets dashboard URL cannot attach one.
- **Docs.** The sponsorship pages, templates, recipes and style guide now describe the live endpoints; "Sponsorship Tiers (Upcoming)" is now "Sponsorship Tiers".

## 2026-10-03

### `@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.0

Additive release: every 0.1 export remains. See [Migration Notes](../sdk/migration.md).

**New subpaths**

| Subpath | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `/privy`, `/privy/react`, `/privy/wagmi`, `/privy/server` | Google to wallet: typed Privy config for PEPU, `PepuPrivyProvider` and `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`, `WalletGate`, `useEnsureWallet`, the active-wallet pin, `createEnsureWalletRoute`, `requireUser`, the Privy requirements table and dashboard checker |
| `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react` | Privy-mode session keys: `buildSessionPolicy`, `createSessionRoutes`, `createSessionActionRoute`, `privySessionSigner`, `signAndBroadcast`, `useSessionGrant`, `useSessionStatus`, `useSessionAct`, `useSessionRevoke` |
| `/session/kernel` | On-chain session keys with ZeroDev Kernel permissions (call policy v0.0.4 plus timestamp policy) |
| `/aa`, `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react`, `/aa/react-direct` | Sponsored transactions: bundler and paymaster clients, the Alto-compatible fee estimator, `toPepuKernelAccount`, `createPepuSponsoredClient`, `sendSponsored`, `describeUserOpFailure`, probes, `useSponsoredSend`, `usePepuSponsorship`. `/aa/react` serves Privy Smart Wallets and never references `@zerodev/*`; the direct transport lives in `/aa/react-direct` (`useDirectSponsoredSend`, `useDirectSmartAccount`) |
| `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server` | The policy service REST client (v1 and v2), v2 on-chain helpers (claim, configure, deposit, read), the Privy claim attestation, denial reason mapping |
| `/combo`, `/combo/react` | The combination: `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` (five routes) and `useSponsoredSession` |
| `/doctor` | `runDoctor`, `checkPepuEnv`, `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS`, `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` |
| `/server` | Kept as a stable server-only alias for the pure session policy helpers |

**New on the core entry:** the error model (`PepuError` and seven subclasses, a code catalog, `explainError`, `toPepuError`, `toErrorResponse`); endpoint resolution (`resolvePepuEndpoints`, `PEPU_ENV`, with `PEPU_HOSTED` as the single swap point for the hosted URLs); `checkSponsorship` (live bundler and paymaster probe); `pepuMulticall`, `getMulticall3` and `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` guard; `getPermit2` and Permit2 typed-data builders; `explorerLinks`; `getPepuAddresses`; `formatUnitsCompact`; `erc20Abi` and `erc721Abi`; the ERC-7677 request builders; registry entries for the Kernel implementation, signer module, call policy v0.0.4, timestamp policy, `tapScore`, `paymasterV1` and `paymasterV2` (pending at the time; deployed 2026-10-14).

**Deprecated:** `getSponsorshipStatus` and `useSponsorshipStatus`. They always report unavailable. Use `checkSponsorship` and `usePepuSponsorship`.

**Boundaries:** five server-only entries throw `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` in a browser bundle. `/privy/wagmi` is ESM only. Each optional peer is imported only from its own subpaths, enforced by test.

**Also included:** `WalletGate` `stalled` render prop, `useSessionStatus().loading`, `useSponsoredSession().statusLoading`, `SponsoredActResult`, route factories that answer `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` at request time instead of throwing at load, the pure `session/scope` helpers that need no `@zerodev/*`, `encodeKernelExecute`, `userOpEventsFromReceipt`, and a `usePepuSmartAccount` fallback through Privy's `getClientForChain`.

### `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.0

The MCP server was rebuilt on `@pepu-chain/sdk`. It now serves 32 tools, 6 prompts and resources, so an agent reads the same registry, error catalog and requirements table that apps import. New tools cover probing the bundler and paymaster, explaining errors and transactions, checking environment and Privy configuration, generating an authorization key, encoding calls, scaffolding, listing SDK exports and fetching docs. The health check uses the live `checkSponsorship` probe, not a hard-coded answer. See [MCP Server Overview](../mcp/index.md) and [Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md).

### Claude Code plugin `pepu-devkit` 0.4.0

Rewritten around the SDK and the MCP server: 12 skills (including `pepu-sdk`, `pepu-session-keys`, `pepu-sponsored-session`, `pepu-sponsored-transactions`, `pepu-paymaster-projects`), 6 slash commands (`/pepu-new-app`, `/pepu-add-login`, `/pepu-add-session`, `/pepu-add-sponsorship`, `/pepu-add-sponsored-session`, `/pepu-doctor`) and a builder subagent. See [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md) and [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md).

### `create-pepu-app` 0.1.0

An interactive arrow-key flow (template, project name, package manager, install, git), with a non-interactive mode for CI and agents: `--yes`, `--json` (one JSON document on stdout), `--list`, `--sdk <vendor|npm>`, `--skip-agent-files`. Six templates: `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint`, `game-app`, `sponsored-demo`, `sponsored-session-app`. Templates are built on the SDK subpaths, ship `.mcp.json`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, and pre-fill environment files. See [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md) and [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md).

### Docs

- A page per SDK subpath, a pillar-to-subpath decision table, a server and client boundary section, and a complete export index. See [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md).
- Type-checked sample code under `docs/snippets`, embedded in the recipes. Fifteen recipes now use SDK functions instead of hand-rolled code, including seven new ones: grant a session, sponsored send, sponsored session, v2 deposit and claim, Permit2 permit, multicall in React and explorer links.

## Earlier

Before 0.2.0 the SDK was 0.1: chain definitions, the contract and DEX registries, ABIs, gas helpers, explorer helpers, the token list, and the `/react`, `/privy` and `/server` entries, with `getSponsorshipStatus` as an always-unavailable placeholder. There is no dated history before 2026-10-02.

# Troubleshooting

Symptoms you can hit while building on Pepe Unchained V2, grouped by the three pillars (Google to wallet, session keys, sponsored transactions), their combination, and the infrastructure underneath. Every entry names the cause and the fix, and links to the error code the SDK raises for it. Start with the section that matches what you were doing.

Error codes link to the generated [Error Reference](reference/errors.md), which is checked against the code in CI. Mainnet only (chain `97741`).

## Prerequisites

- Paste the error text into the MCP tool `pepu_explain_error` (or `explainError` from `@pepu-chain/sdk`) to get its catalog entry directly. `pepu_known_gotchas` lists the chain-level traps below.
- Run `npm run doctor` in a scaffolded app, or the MCP tools `pepu_check_env` and `pepu_check_privy_config`, before debugging by hand. They check the env, the RPC and the Privy dashboard settings without printing secrets.

## How to read an error code

A `PepuError` carries `code`, `hint` and `docsUrl`; the URL is `https://docs.pepeunchained.com/reference/errors#<CODE>`. The codes in this page link to the same entries.

| Area | Codes |
|---|---|
| Configuration | [`CONFIG_MISSING_ENV`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_MISSING_ENV), [`CONFIG_BAD_URL`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_BAD_URL), [`CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY) |
| Pillar 1, Google to wallet | [`CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD), [`CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH), [`CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN), [`WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED`](reference/errors.md#WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED), [`WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE`](reference/errors.md#WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE), [`WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN`](reference/errors.md#WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN), [`AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`](reference/errors.md#AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN) |
| Pillar 2, session keys | [`POLICY_UNSCOPED`](reference/errors.md#POLICY_UNSCOPED), [`POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG`](reference/errors.md#POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG), [`SESSION_NONE`](reference/errors.md#SESSION_NONE), [`SESSION_EXPIRED`](reference/errors.md#SESSION_EXPIRED), [`SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH`](reference/errors.md#SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH), [`PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH`](reference/errors.md#PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH), [`PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741`](reference/errors.md#PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741) |
| Pillar 3, sponsored transactions | [`PAYMASTER_DENIED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_DENIED), [`PAYMASTER_CAP`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_CAP), [`PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE), [`PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED), [`PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED), [`PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED), [`PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED), [`PAYMASTER_API_ERROR`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_API_ERROR) |
| v2 projects | [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED), [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED), [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED), [`PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE), [`PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED) |
| Infrastructure | [`BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE`](reference/errors.md#BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE), [`PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE), [`BUNDLER_AA_FAILED`](reference/errors.md#BUNDLER_AA_FAILED) |
| Transactions and chain | [`TX_REVERTED`](reference/errors.md#TX_REVERTED), [`TX_NONCE_RACE`](reference/errors.md#TX_NONCE_RACE), [`TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT`](reference/errors.md#TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT), [`MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS`](reference/errors.md#MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS), [`UNKNOWN`](reference/errors.md#UNKNOWN) |

## Chain, RPC and tooling

### "My batched reads are failing or returning nothing"

Code: [`MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS`](reference/errors.md#MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS).

**You are almost certainly hitting the Multicall3 trap.** PEPU has Multicall3 deployed, but not at the canonical address (`0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11`) that viem, wagmi and most tooling assume by default. That address has no code on this chain; calls routed through it return empty data or a "no code" error that never mentions Multicall3.

Fix: use `@pepu-chain/sdk`'s `pepuMainnet`, which already points at PEPU's Multicall3 (`0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`), or set `contracts.multicall3.address` to that value. Full explanation: [The Multicall3 Trap](contracts/multicall3.md).

### "The gas price looks insane: thousands of gwei"

Code: [`TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT`](reference/errors.md#TX_GAS_UNDERSHOOT) when you under-set it.

**Expected, not a bug.** PEPU's base fee normally sits around 12,500 gwei, versus roughly 0.01 to 0.1 gwei on Arbitrum One. PEPU's per-token USD price is very low, so the chain needs a much larger wei-per-gas number to recover the same real-dollar cost, including the L1 data-posting cost every Orbit chain pays.

Do not hardcode a lower gas price: your transactions will get stuck and look like a different, harder failure. Let automatic gas estimation work (Foundry and Hardhat both do), and add headroom with `withGasLimitBuffer()` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session` when you submit your own transactions. A simple transfer still costs a fraction of a cent.

### "My RPC calls are rate-limited or rejected"

The public RPC (`https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz`) rate-limits (`-32017`) and gates `debug_*` and `trace_*` methods behind an authenticated Conduit API key (`-32401`). It also caps `eth_getLogs` to a **2,000-block range**; a wider range throws `-32602`, so paginate.

For `debug_traceCall`, `eth_simulateV1` or higher limits, use an authenticated Conduit RPC URL (`https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz/<API_KEY>`). See [Network Reference](get-started/network-reference.md#authenticated-rpc). There is no WebSocket RPC, even on the authenticated tier, so do not build an `eth_subscribe` flow.

### "`forge` behaves strangely or compiles differently than expected"

**Check whether your `forge` is upstream Foundry.** [`foundry-zksync`](https://github.com/matter-labs/foundry-zksync) installs to the same `~/.foundry` location and overwrites the `forge` and `cast` binaries on `PATH`. If a machine has ever run `foundryup-zksync`, `forge` may be the zkSync fork, which produces wrong results against an Arbitrum Orbit chain.

```bash
forge --version
```

If the output mentions zksync anywhere, reinstall upstream Foundry (`foundryup`) or point your scripts at an upstream binary. See [Deploy and Verify a Contract](contracts/deployment.md).

### "I cannot find or fund a wallet on testnet"

**Testnet (chain `97740`) is out of scope.** There is no public faucet, no indexed explorer and none of PEPU's deployed infrastructure there. Build against mainnet; a transaction costs a fraction of a cent. See [Network Reference](get-started/network-reference.md#testnet-out-of-scope-today).

### "Am I looking at the right chain?"

Two unrelated chains share the "Pepe Unchained" name. **V1** (chain ID `3409`, OP Stack) is dead; its legacy claims portal closed 2026-01-31. **V2** (chain ID `97741` mainnet, Arbitrum Orbit) is the current chain and the only one these docs cover. If you found chain ID `3409` or an OP Stack reference, you are reading V1 history. See [V1 vs V2](get-started/v1-vs-v2.md).

### "The explorer does not have the data I expect"

`pepuscan.com` is a fully indexed Blockscout instance: use it for address history, token analytics, contract verification and its API. The Conduit-bundled `explorer-pepu-v2-*.t.conduit.xyz` explorer self-reports no indexer and shows only single blocks and transactions by hash. Point explorer-API tooling at `pepuscan.com`. See [Endpoints](reference/endpoints.md).

### "npx create-pepu-app or npm install says the package was not found"

Check the spelling. The scope is `@pepu-chain` (not `@pepu`), the CLI is the unscoped `create-pepu-app`, and the MCP server is `@pepu-chain/mcp`. Use `npx create-pepu-app@latest` to bypass a stale npx cache, confirm `npm config get registry` is the public npm registry, and use Node.js 18.17 or newer. See [Quickstart](get-started/quickstart-app.md).

### "Missing environment variable" or "Invalid endpoint URL"

Codes: [`CONFIG_MISSING_ENV`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_MISSING_ENV), [`CONFIG_BAD_URL`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_BAD_URL), [`CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY).

Set the variables the message names (it names them, never their values) in `.env.local` and restart the dev server, since Next.js reads the file once at startup. A bundler, paymaster or RPC URL must be a full http(s) URL. `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` means a server entry (for example `/privy/server`) was imported into client code; import it only from route handlers and scripts. See [Environment Variables](reference/env-vars.md).

## Pillar 1: Google to wallet

Full explanations are on [Privy Setup Walkthrough](onboarding/privy-setup.md) and [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](privy/dashboard-settings.md).

### "Login fails: the login iframe is blocked, OAuth returns 403"

Codes: [`CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_ORIGIN_MISMATCH), [`CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_PRIVY_DASHBOARD).

**Almost always the allowed origin, and specifically the port.** Privy's **Allowed origins** list matches the full origin including the port. `http://localhost:3000` matches; `http://localhost` does not. If port 3000 is busy, Next.js silently starts on 3001 and login fails with errors that never mention the port. Free port 3000, or add the exact origin you run on. The doctor checks this when you pass an origin: `npm run doctor` uses `http://localhost:3000` (set `PEPU_APP_ORIGIN` for another port), and `runDoctor({ origin })` does the same in code.

### "Creating your wallet..." never finishes, or the user has no wallet

Codes: [`CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN`](reference/errors.md#CONFIG_PRIVY_CREATE_ON_LOGIN), [`WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED`](reference/errors.md#WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED).

Turn on **Automatically create embedded wallets on login** in the Privy Dashboard; the `createOnLogin` value in your code does not override it. Check that `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is set (the templates create the wallet server-side as a fallback) and restart after any `.env.local` change. See [Privy Setup Walkthrough](onboarding/privy-setup.md#automatically-create-embedded-wallets-on-login). If Privy's own modal hangs, set `createOnLogin: "off"` and provision the wallet yourself: [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md).

### "The configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741"

Code: [`WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN`](reference/errors.md#WALLET_COINBASE_UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN).

Coinbase's smart wallet does not support chain 97741. Pin the connector to `eoaOnly` with `createPepuPrivyConfig()` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy`, or set `externalWallets: { coinbaseWallet: { config: { preference: { options: "eoaOnly" } } } }`.

### "A browser extension wallet is the active account"

Code: [`WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE`](reference/errors.md#WALLET_INJECTED_ACTIVE).

wagmi picked an injected wallet instead of the Privy embedded wallet. Pin the embedded wallet with `useActiveWalletPin()` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi`. See [Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md).

### "401 from my API route after login"

Code: [`AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`](reference/errors.md#AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN).

The request carried no bearer token, or Privy could not verify it. Send `Authorization: Bearer <getAccessToken()>` and verify the token server-side with the app secret.

### "Unable to fetch token price" in the browser console

Harmless. Privy cannot fetch a fiat price for PEPU. It does not affect login, wallets or transactions.

### "Privy refuses a transfer my wallet can afford"

Privy's pre-flight gas estimate in its confirmation modal is conservative, and PEPU's base fee makes it large enough to block a transfer the wallet could pay for. You cannot change that check from your app. The `consumer-app` template has no "Max" button for this reason. If your app submits transactions itself, `maxSendableAmount` in [`@pepu-chain/sdk`](sdk/core.md#gas-and-fees) sizes a transfer correctly.

### "Unsupported chain with id 97741" from Privy's server-side API

Code: [`PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741`](reference/errors.md#PRIVY_CHAIN_REJECTED_97741).

Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` does not support PEPU. This is a platform limitation, not a mistake in your request. Sign with `eth_signTransaction` and broadcast through PEPU's RPC (`signAndBroadcast` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session`). See [Sign with Privy, Broadcast Yourself](recipes/sign-with-privy-broadcast-yourself.md).

### "The address I see in Privy is not the address on pepuscan"

With sponsorship, the account that transacts is a Kernel smart account at a different address from the embedded wallet. See [The Two-Address Model](onboarding/two-address-model.md).

## Pillar 2: Session keys

See [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](onboarding/session-keys.md) and [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](privy/authorization-keys.md).

### "My session signer's transactions are all denied"

Codes: [`POLICY_UNSCOPED`](reference/errors.md#POLICY_UNSCOPED), [`POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG`](reference/errors.md#POLICY_NAME_TOO_LONG), [`SESSION_EXPIRED`](reference/errors.md#SESSION_EXPIRED), [`PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH`](reference/errors.md#PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH).

A denial comes back as an error from your signing route, not a popup, and it is a failed transaction, not proof the session is gone. Work through these in order.

1. **Policy mismatch.** The rule's `method` must be `eth_signTransaction` (a rule written for `eth_sendTransaction` never matches), and the `to` address, function and `value` must equal what you are signing. A call to any other contract or function, or with a nonzero value, is denied by design. `buildSessionPolicy()` refuses an unscoped policy with `POLICY_UNSCOPED`.
2. **Expiry.** The policy's `current_unix_timestamp` condition denies every request after the expiry (`SESSION_EXPIRED`). Grant a new session.
3. **Policy name length.** Policy and rule names must be at most 49 characters. Privy's published spec says 50, but the live validator rejects 50 or more. This fails when the policy is created (a 400 from your grant route), so the signer is never attached.
4. **Key quorum mismatch.** The signer belongs to a key quorum, and your server must sign each Privy request with that quorum's authorization key. Check that `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` is the quorum you registered and that `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` is the private half of that same key pair. The symptom is `401 "No valid authorization keys or user signing keys available"`.

See [Session Keys](onboarding/session-keys.md#common-failures).

### "No active session" or "session approval does not match" (Kernel session)

Codes: [`SESSION_NONE`](reference/errors.md#SESSION_NONE), [`SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH`](reference/errors.md#SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH).

The user has not granted a session, or it was revoked (`SESSION_NONE`): ask them to grant one. If the approval was made for another account, permission id or mode (`SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH`), run prepare again, have the owner sign again, then activate. The scope on the server and the client must match. See [Session Keys](onboarding/session-keys.md) and the [Grant a Session](recipes/grant-a-session.md) recipe.

## Pillar 3: Sponsored transactions

### "Is gas sponsorship available?"

**Yes, through the hosted endpoints.** A Kernel smart account holding 0 PEPU can send a project-sponsored operation through `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>`. The SDK uses the hosted bundler and paymaster base by default; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` override them. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token, so you need a project of your own (claim, set targets and limits, deposit, token); the free tier needs a verified Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app and is not available to third-party apps. The v1 paymaster is retired. See [Endpoints](reference/endpoints.md), [Sponsored Transactions](onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md) and [Infrastructure Map](infra/overview.md). The tiered v2 model is documented on [Sponsorship Tiers](onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md). If you want no popup and no sponsorship at all, [Session Keys](onboarding/session-keys.md) need none of this.

### "The paymaster denied my UserOperation"

Codes: [`PAYMASTER_DENIED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_DENIED), [`PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED), [`PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED), [`PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED).

The reason is in the JSON-RPC error's `data.reason`, not in the HTTP status and not always in the headline message. Read `error.data.reason` first, then look it up in [Paymaster denial reasons](reference/errors.md#paymaster-denial-reasons), which maps every reason to a code. `pm_getPaymasterStubData` succeeding proves nothing: it is unauthenticated by spec, and only `pm_getPaymasterData` enforces the policy. See [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](infra/paymaster/policy-and-caps.md).

### "Sponsorship stopped: cap reached, no balance or rate limited"

Codes: [`PAYMASTER_CAP`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_CAP), [`PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE), [`PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED), [`PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE).

All four are retryable. A cap resets with its window; no balance means the project's paymaster deposit cannot cover the operation (deposit more; v2 deposits are one-way); rate limiting wants a back-off for `Retry-After`. The v2 free tier is 100 PEPU per Privy user per day and 50 PEPU per hour, for PEPU's own Privy app only.

### "My v2 project is not claimed, paused or owned by someone else"

Codes: [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED), [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED), [`PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED), [`PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_SESSION_REQUIRED).

These apply to the deployed v2 paymaster. A claim sets the owner only; after it the owner must call `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit` before anything is sponsored. See [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md) and [Credential Matrix](infra/paymaster/auth.md).

### "The sponsored transaction reverted or the EntryPoint rejected it"

Codes: [`BUNDLER_AA_FAILED`](reference/errors.md#BUNDLER_AA_FAILED), [`TX_REVERTED`](reference/errors.md#TX_REVERTED), [`TX_NONCE_RACE`](reference/errors.md#TX_NONCE_RACE).

Read the `AAxx` code in the message: `AA21` prefund missing, `AA23` signature or validation reverted, `AA25` invalid nonce, `AA31`, `AA33`, `AA34` paymaster problems. For a plain revert, `explainError(<revert data>)` decodes the reason. Serialize sends per account to avoid nonce races. See [Bundler JSON-RPC API](infra/bundler/api.md).

## The combination: Google, session and sponsorship together

See [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md) and the `sponsored-session-app` template.

- **Set up screen instead of the app.** No Privy app id: run `npm run doctor` and fill `.env.local`. See [Sponsored Session App](templates/sponsored-session-app.md).
- **Session works, sponsorship does not.** The session is enforced on-chain by the Kernel; sponsorship is the paymaster. Check them separately: `pepu_sponsorship_status` for the paymaster side, and the session scope for the other.
- **Spend caps reject the first operation.** Size caps above the gas reservation (the first operation deploys the account and reserves more than later ones). See [Sponsored Session in One Flow](recipes/sponsored-session.md).
- **State is lost on restart.** `createMemoryStore()` is for development only; use a durable store in production. See [Trust and Security Model](concepts/trust-and-security.md).

## Infrastructure: bundler and paymaster services

### "Bundler or paymaster is unreachable"

Codes: [`BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE`](reference/errors.md#BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE) (bundler) and [`PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE`](reference/errors.md#PAYMASTER_UNREACHABLE) (paymaster).

The request failed before any response. Check `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; the SDK defaults to `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`, so an unreachable error with neither set points at the network or the hosted service. `checkSponsorship()` and the MCP tools `pepu_bundler_health` and `pepu_paymaster_health` tell you which side is down. A service bound to `localhost` is unreachable from a teammate's machine or a deployed app. See [Endpoints](reference/endpoints.md).

### "The bundler returns HTTP 500 on eth_sendUserOperation"

If you run your own Alto bundler on `@pimlico/alto` 0.0.21, this is almost certainly `safe-mode: true`, which cannot complete `eth_sendUserOperation`. Set `safe-mode` to `false` and restart. Gas estimation succeeding while sending fails is the tell. See [Operating the Bundler](infra/bundler/operating.md).

### "Failed to fetch" or a CORS error calling the bundler from the browser

Privy's smart-wallet client calls the bundler directly from the browser, and a missing CORS preflight response shows up as a bare `Failed to fetch`. Set `enable-cors` to `true` on the bundler. Because that exposes the bundler to any web page, put it behind a filtering proxy in production. See [Operating the Bundler](infra/bundler/operating.md).

### "Setting up your smart wallet..." never clears

Smart Wallets is off, or is not configured for chain 97741 in the Privy Dashboard (provider Kernel, plus your bundler and paymaster URLs). Use the hosted URLs `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project token>`. See [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](privy/dashboard-settings.md) and [Sponsored Transactions](onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md).

### "A pasted bundler or paymaster URL stopped working"

The URL pasted into the Privy Dashboard points at a host that changed address, or the token in it was rotated. Use a stable hostname for any service the Dashboard calls, and update the Dashboard when you rotate. See [Credential Matrix](infra/paymaster/auth.md).

## What to expect

- Every entry here either resolves the issue or points to the page that explains it.
- If a code is not listed above, search the [Error Reference](reference/errors.md); it lists all of them.

## Related

- [Error Reference](reference/errors.md)
- [SDK Error Catalog](sdk/errors.md)
- [MCP Tool Reference](mcp/tools.md) (`pepu_explain_error`, `pepu_known_gotchas`, `pepu_check_privy_config`)
- [FAQ](reference/faq.md)

Source: https://docs.pepeunchained.com/CONTRIBUTING-DOCS

# Docs Style Guide and Page Template

Rules for writing and editing pages in this folder. The docs are the single source of truth for the PEPU dev kit, so accuracy outranks polish.

## Voice

- Present tense. State facts as facts, with no hedging.
- Imperative steps: say what to do, then why.
- Plain and precise. No hype words, no emoji, no marketing adjectives, no exclamation marks.
- No work-log language: no session history ("earlier", "now fixed"), no first person ("we did"), no internal process notes.
- Describe what the product does, not how far its development has progressed. Do not cite proof transactions or the dates something was checked.
- Include a caveat only when it changes what the developer does, for example "Deposits are one-way; they can't be withdrawn." or "Sessions are stored in memory in the template; use a persistent store in production."
- Every page must make it easier to build or to use. If it does not, cut it.
- PEPU is a chain, not "an AI chain". Agent tooling is described as tooling that helps builders get PEPU facts right.

Security guidance belongs in [Trust and Security Model](concepts/trust-and-security.md) and [Security Reviews](contracts/audits.md), written neutrally.

## Facts to respect

- Mainnet only: chain ID `97741`. The testnet `97740` is not supported. Chain ID `3409` is the retired V1 chain.
- Hosted endpoints: bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. They are the SDK defaults; keep the env var names `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` as overrides. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`), so there is no tokenless default; write `<token>` and never a real one. Local development defaults (`http://localhost:4337`, `http://localhost:8788`) may stay for people running their own services. Never write a tunnel URL (no ngrok, no trycloudflare) anywhere.
- The v2 paymaster is `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7`. The v1 paymaster is retired. Deposits to v2 are one-way.
- Multicall3 is at a PEPU-specific address, never the canonical one. Give full addresses, never truncated ones, in tables meant for copying.
- Never state a feature is available if it is not live.

## Code samples use real SDK exports

- Import only symbols that exist in `@pepu-chain/sdk` and its documented subpaths: `/privy`, `/privy/react`, `/privy/wagmi`, `/privy/server`, `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react`, `/session/kernel`, `/aa`, `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react`, `/aa/react-direct`, `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server`, `/combo`, `/combo/react`, `/doctor`.
- If a symbol is not exported, do not invent it. Check `packages/sdk/src` and the exports test, or call the `pepu_sdk_exports` MCP tool.
- Prefer SDK functions over hand-rolled infrastructure. Use raw viem or JSON-RPC only where the SDK has no equivalent, and say so.
- Server-only code (Privy app secret, authorization key, claim attestation) is labeled server-only and never reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables.
- Never print or embed secrets, keys or real tokens. Use obvious placeholders.
- Samples meant to compile live under `docs/snippets/` and are type-checked in CI. Pages include them and do not diverge from them.

## Page template

````markdown
# Page Title

One paragraph: what this page is for and who needs it.

## Prerequisites
## Steps or reference body
## What to expect
## Common failures
## Related
````

Rules:

- One H1 per page, title case, matching the `SUMMARY.md` entry.
- Reference pages use tables; procedures use numbered steps.
- Every failure symptom names the cause and the fix.
- Link with relative paths, for example from the docs root `[Session Keys](onboarding/session-keys.md)`.
- Add every new page to `SUMMARY.md` in the same change.
- Do not put Markdown link syntax inside `TODO` comments; the link checker reads them.

## Stubs and ownership

New pages start as stubs: a title, a one-paragraph purpose and a `TODO(Dn)` comment listing the required sections. The owner replaces the stub and removes the TODO.

| Writer | Folders |
|---|---|
| D2 | `get-started/`, `onboarding/`, `concepts/`, `privy/`, `reference/env-vars.md`, glossary, FAQ |
| D3 | `sdk/`, `recipes/`, `snippets/`, changelog |
| D4 | `mcp/`, `agent-tooling/`, `templates/`, `cli/` |
| D5 | `infra/`, `contracts/` |
| D6 | generated pages (`reference/errors.md`, `reference/endpoints.md`, `sdk/errors.md`), `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `troubleshooting.md` |

## Checks

- `node scripts/check-links.mjs` must report 0 broken links.
- `docs/llms.txt` assumes each page URL mirrors its path; D6 keeps it current.
